h1: IB Tutors in Sector 102, Gurugram
heroSubtitle: An academic year here does not stay still. What a student needs in August is not what they need by February, and the tutoring plan should move with it. This page maps that year for families around Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens and the sectors nearby.
introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 102 Gurugram are matched around two things: the point the student has reached in the academic year, and the fact that this sector sits well north of the main international school belt. Support is available from Grade 1 to Grade 12 across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes. Home sessions depend on which tutors are free nearby in a given term. Online sessions usually offer a wider choice at higher level, particularly for evening slots.

contentBlocks.heading: How one academic year unfolds for an IB student in Sector 102
contentBlocks.body:
August feels manageable. New subjects, new folders, a timetable that has room in it. Nothing is due yet, and most families see no reason to think about tutoring.

By the middle of October the picture changes. The first substantial internal assessment brief has landed, Middle Years students have met their first proper criterion-marked task, and the gap between understanding a lesson and producing assessed work is suddenly visible. This is when the first calls usually come.

November and December bring mocks for the older cohort, and with them the uncomfortable discovery that knowing a subject and writing a paper against the clock are separate abilities. January and February are dominated by deadlines: extended essay drafts, internal assessments moving towards submission, coursework that has been quietly slipping since October. By March, students preparing for the May 2026 session are revising rather than learning, and the honest scope of what tutoring can still change has narrowed considerably.

The practical conclusion for a family in Sector 102 is simple enough. Support that starts in October has options. Support that starts in March has techniques. Both are worth having, but they are not the same thing, and no tutor can turn the second into the first.
items: August: no pressure, and no urgency to arrange anything
October: first criterion-marked tasks expose the real gaps
November and December: mocks separate knowledge from technique
January and February: extended essay and IA deadlines cluster
March onwards: revision only, with scope genuinely reduced

contentBlocks.heading: Why online tutoring often works better on this side of Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 102 sits along the Dwarka Expressway, in the northern band of Gurugram sectors. Most tutors with deep higher level Diploma experience are based further south, near the older international school belt around Golf Course Road, the DLF phases and Sohna Road. That is a real distance, and at six in the evening it is a real hour of driving.

The consequence is worth saying plainly rather than dressing up. Home tutoring here is thinner on weekday evenings than it is in Sector 57 or DLF Phase 5. Where it does work, it tends to be an afternoon slot, a weekend morning, or a tutor who already lives on this side of the city. Home tutoring may be available in Sector 102 depending on tutor schedules, and that phrasing is deliberate: it is checked per request rather than promised.

Online changes the arithmetic completely. The tutor pool stops being a radius and becomes a subject list. A Math AI HL specialist or a Chemistry tutor comfortable with internal assessment design can teach a Sector 102 student at eight in the evening without either party losing an hour to the expressway.

For younger children the balance tips the other way, and a nearby tutor in the room usually beats a better one on a screen.
items: Sector 102 lies north of the main tutor concentration
Weekday evening home slots are genuinely limited here
Afternoon and weekend home sessions are more realistic
Online removes travel from higher level subject matching
Younger students still do better with a tutor present

contentBlocks.heading: Subject requests that come out of Sector 102 households
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics dominates, as it does everywhere, but the two Diploma routes generate different conversations. Math AA HL requests usually surface after a calculus test, and the underlying issue is often algebraic speed rather than the calculus itself. Math AI HL requests come later in the year and centre on modelling: choosing a function that fits a context, justifying that choice, and using technology without hiding behind it.

Physics and Chemistry follow the internal assessment calendar. Physics enquiries cluster around mechanics early and around fields and circuits later, while the recurring pain point is the long multi-part question where one wrong assumption in part b quietly ruins parts c and d. Chemistry enquiries peak when the internal assessment investigation has to be designed, because school laboratories limit what can genuinely be measured and students frequently choose something unworkable.

Economics support is heavily seasonal, rising before mocks, and focuses on diagram accuracy and on evaluation that weighs something rather than listing advantages. English A work concentrates on the individual oral and on written commentary, where the difficulty is almost never comprehension.

Middle Years requests span sciences, individuals and societies, and language. Primary Years requests are mostly reading and number confidence.
items: Math AA HL: algebraic speed underneath calculus problems
Math AI HL: model choice, justification and sensible technology use
Physics: multi-part questions where an early error cascades
Chemistry: IA designs that a school laboratory can actually support
Economics: diagram accuracy and weighted evaluation
English A: individual oral and written commentary

contentBlocks.heading: Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens and the sectors around 102
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 102 is largely a residential sector of high-rise condominium communities, and the tutoring pattern reflects that. Requests come from Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph and ATS Kocoon, and a tutor already visiting one of those towers will frequently take a second student in the same complex or the one next door. Two families in the same community sharing a tutor's travel is common here and often improves the slot each of them gets.

The neighbouring Dwarka Expressway sectors behave similarly. Movement within this band is quick outside peak hours, which is why a four o'clock session is easy and a seven o'clock one is not.

The older Gurugram pockets, Nirvana Country, South City 1, DLF Phase 1 and Phase 4, Sector 50 and Sector 65, sit on the far side of the city from here. A tutor teaching there will rarely add a Sector 102 slot on the same day.

Proximity to Delhi is the compensating advantage. Some tutors travelling from the Dwarka side reach this sector more easily than they reach Golf Course Road, and families with a parent working in Delhi, Noida or Faridabad usually find the evening online session the only reliable option.
items: Sobha City and Puri Diplomatic Greens requests are frequent
ATS Triumph and ATS Kocoon families often share a tutor visit
Movement along the expressway is easy outside peak hours
Sector 50, Sector 65 and the DLF phases are the far side of town
Delhi-side tutors sometimes reach here faster than Golf Course Road

contentBlocks.heading: Ages three to nineteen: what each IB programme asks of a tutor
contentBlocks.body:
A single tutor is rarely right across all three programmes, and the reasons are worth understanding before choosing one.

The Primary Years Programme runs from ages three to twelve and is built around inquiry. A tutor here needs patience and restraint. The temptation is to drill, and drilling a seven-year-old who is learning to ask questions removes the very thing the programme is developing. Reading fluency, number confidence and the ability to explain a method aloud are the useful targets.

The Middle Years Programme covers ages eleven to sixteen and marks against criteria rather than percentages. A tutor without criterion literacy will teach the content well and leave the marks unchanged, which is the single most common complaint parents raise about tutoring at this stage.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, needs genuine subject specialism at the level being taught, plus familiarity with internal assessment structure, extended essay supervision, theory of knowledge and command-term language. Past-paper practice, review of school assignments and a plan aimed at the May 2026 or November 2026 session make up most of the work.

Support across Grade 1 to Grade 12 is possible, but it usually means more than one tutor over the years rather than one for all of them.
items: PYP, ages three to twelve: fluency and confidence, not drilling
MYP, ages eleven to sixteen: criterion literacy is the difference
DP, ages sixteen to nineteen: subject specialism at the exact level
IA, EE, TOK and command terms handled as specific skills
Different tutors at different stages is normal, not a failure

contentBlocks.heading: From first message to first session for a Sector 102 family
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is short and it is worth knowing what each stage is for.

You send the requirement: year group, subjects with levels, what has gone wrong, and the hours in the week that are actually free. An advisor reads it and asks follow-up questions, usually about the assessment calendar and about whether the difficulty is content, technique or organisation. Those three need different tutors.

Availability is then checked against the sector. This is the stage where a home request in Sector 102 sometimes turns into an online recommendation, and you are told why rather than quietly redirected. If a strong nearby tutor exists for that subject and level, they are offered. If they do not, saying so is more useful than proposing a weak local match.

Two or three profiles follow, each with levels taught, an outline of how they run a session, and what times they currently have open. Availability is confirmed at that moment and stays subject to tutor schedules.

Then a trial session, at a time you choose, in the mode you prefer. Afterwards you continue, ask for a different profile, or stop. There is no obligation attached to the trial itself.
items: Send year group, levels, the problem and free hours
Content, technique and organisation need different tutors
Local availability checked before any promise is made
An honest online recommendation instead of a weak local match
Trial session first, decision afterwards

contentBlocks.heading: What progress looks like by week four, and what to refuse outright
contentBlocks.body:
Refuse anything that promises a specific final score, a percentage improvement, or a particular grade by a particular month. Boundaries shift between examination sessions, and the paper is still written by a teenager on a morning nobody controls. A promise of that kind tells you something about the seller rather than about the student.

Progress that can actually be observed by week four looks different and less dramatic. The student can explain a method rather than recite the steps. A marked piece of work shows fewer repeats of the same error, even if the overall mark has not moved much. The tutor can describe next month's plan and say how it differs from last month's, which means they have been paying attention. And the student stops describing the subject as impossible, which sounds soft but is usually the earliest real signal.

If none of that has happened after a month, change something. Waiting until the next report card wastes a term.

On cost: rates depend on level, subject and mode, and travel to Sector 102 affects home session pricing more than it would closer to the school belt. Confirm the rate, the notice period and the exam-season position before the second session.
items: No promised grades, percentages or point improvements
Week four: a method explained, not a procedure recited
Fewer repeats of the same error in marked work
A revised plan proves the tutor is actually tracking
Rates, notice periods and travel costs settled early

contentBlocks.heading: The Gurugram IB school run from Sector 102, and what it costs in hours
contentBlocks.body:
Most established international schools in the region sit south and east of here. Pathways World School lies in the wider Gurugram region, Lancers International School is on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School is in Sector 57, and GD Goenka World School is towards Sohna Road. Families in Sector 102 attending any of these are already spending a meaningful part of the day on the road.

That commute is the strongest argument for online tutoring here, and it has nothing to do with teaching quality. A student who reaches home at half past five after an hour in a bus has a limited amount of usable concentration left. Spending twenty minutes of it waiting for a tutor stuck near a toll plaza is a poor trade. A session that begins the moment the student sits down protects the part of the evening that still works.

Some families choose a weekend home session for exactly this reason and keep weekdays online, which tends to hold up across a full term.

contentBlocks.heading: Vetting a tutor, and why it matters differently for online sessions
contentBlocks.body:
Checks cover identity, qualification, level history and reliability. Government identity documents are verified before any introduction. Claims about teaching a specific level are matched against actual history at that level, since a strong degree says little about whether someone has taught Math AA HL to examination standard. Assessment literacy, meaning familiarity with internal assessment criteria, extended essay supervision and command-term language, is treated as a distinct competence. Feedback from families is reviewed, and a pattern of cancellations or unexplained absences counts against a tutor.

Online sessions shift the risk profile rather than removing it. A parent cannot glance into the room, so the checks that matter most become punctuality, whether the camera is on at both ends, and whether the tutor produces work that can be shown to someone else afterwards. Ask for the shared documents or annotated papers from the first fortnight. If nothing exists in writing, the sessions are probably conversational rather than structured.

For home sessions in Sector 102, the practical additions are ordinary and worth insisting on: sessions in a common area rather than a bedroom, and a parent within earshot for the first few weeks.

No vetting process is complete on its own. The trial session and the four-week review carry the rest of the weight.
items: Identity verified before any introduction is made
Level history checked, not just the qualification
Assessment criteria literacy assessed separately
Online: cameras on, written artefacts from every session
Home: common area, parent within earshot early on

contentBlocks.heading: Finding an IB tutor in Sector 102 for the term ahead
contentBlocks.body:
The best time to ask is roughly a term before you think you need to. October enquiries get a wider choice of tutors than March ones, for the plain reason that the same specialists are being asked for by everyone at the same time.

Send the year group, the subject list with levels, a sentence on what has gone wrong, and the hours that are genuinely free in your week. Mention your community, whether that is Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph, ATS Kocoon or a neighbouring sector, since a tutor already teaching in the same complex changes what is possible.

An advisor checks who is available at that level, tells you honestly whether a home match exists nearby or whether online gives a better tutor, and shares two or three profiles with current availability.

A trial session follows at a time you choose. Watch it. Then decide whether to continue with that tutor, try a different one, or leave it for now. Availability is confirmed only at the point of matching, because it genuinely changes month to month.
items: Ask a term earlier than feels necessary
Name your community, not just the sector
Say whether the problem is content, technique or organisation
Home or online recommended honestly, not by default
Trial session before any commitment

faqs.question: Are there IB tutors who will actually travel to Sector 102 on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Some will, and it depends entirely on who is teaching nearby that term. Afternoon slots are far easier to fill than evening ones, because the return journey towards the older parts of Gurugram after seven is slow. Tutors already visiting Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens or a neighbouring condominium community are the most likely to take an additional student here. If no suitable local tutor is free at your level, you will be told rather than offered a weaker match.

faqs.question: We are moving into Sector 102 mid-year. How disruptive is changing tutors?
faqs.answer: Less disruptive than most families fear, provided the handover is deliberate. Ask the outgoing tutor for a short written summary: topics covered, what the student still finds difficult, and what work has been set recently. A new tutor who reads that begins from the right place instead of spending three sessions rediscovering it. Online arrangements often survive a move entirely, which is one practical reason families relocating within the region keep them.

faqs.question: When in the year should we start tutoring for the best result?
faqs.answer: October is usually the sensible point for a Diploma student. The first internal assessment briefs have landed, early marked work exists to diagnose from, and there is still a full year of runway before the May session. Starting in the second half of the school year narrows what is possible to technique, timing and targeted revision, which has value but is a smaller job. Middle Years students benefit from starting whenever criterion marks stop matching classroom understanding.

faqs.question: My son studies well but freezes in exams. Is that a tutoring problem?
faqs.answer: Partly. A good deal of what looks like exam anxiety is actually an absence of rehearsed process: no plan for reading a paper, no rule for when to abandon a question, no habit of writing the first line of an answer before deciding it is too hard. Those are teachable and respond to timed practice under realistic conditions. If the freezing extends beyond examinations into ordinary classwork, that is worth raising with the school counsellor rather than treating as a revision problem.

faqs.question: Can two families in the same condominium share a tutor and split the fee?
faqs.answer: Shared sessions between two students at the same level are sometimes workable and can be discussed with the tutor directly. They work best when both students are close in ability and studying the same subject at the same level. They work badly when one is revising for final papers while the other is repairing foundations, because the tutor ends up teaching neither properly. Rates for shared sessions are agreed with the tutor rather than set centrally.

faqs.question: How long should a session be, and how many a week are sensible?
faqs.answer: Sixty to ninety minutes suits most students, with ninety reserved for Diploma subjects where a full past paper needs working through. Two sessions a week in one subject is usually the practical ceiling before returns drop, since the student needs time between them to attempt work independently. Younger children do better with shorter and more frequent sessions. Adding a third weekly hour rarely helps as much as making the existing two more demanding.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for practical subjects like Chemistry?
faqs.answer: For theory, mark-scheme technique and internal assessment design, yes, and often better than home sessions because the specialist pool is larger. For the laboratory work itself, no, and nobody should claim otherwise. The experiment belongs to the school. What a tutor can genuinely do online is help choose a variable that can be measured with the equipment available, check the method for controlled variables, and work through uncertainty and evaluation before the write-up begins.

faqs.question: What is included in the fee, and what is charged separately?
faqs.answer: The session itself, planning for it and the marking of work set are normally covered by the hourly rate agreed with the tutor. Longer written feedback on full essays or extended essay drafts is sometimes charged separately, since it can take as long as a session. Home tutoring in Sector 102 may carry a travel element in the rate given the distance from the main tutor concentration. Confirm all of this in writing before the second session.

faqs.question: Do you help students preparing for the November session as well as May?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions are supported. November candidates work to a calendar offset by about six months, with internal assessment deadlines falling mid-year and final revision running through a period when much of the peer group has already finished. That isolation makes a fixed weekly session more valuable than it is for May candidates. Availability for either is checked at the point of matching and remains subject to tutor schedules.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is good but my child still is not doing the work?
faqs.answer: Then the problem is organisation, and a subject specialist is the wrong tool for it. Some students need a weekly planning session more than another hour of content: a review of what is due, a realistic split across the week, and a check the following week on what actually happened. Say this openly when describing the requirement, because the tutor best suited to structure and accountability is not always the strongest subject expert available.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Tutoring Fee in Sector 103, Gurugram Actually Pays For
contentBlocks.body:
Most parents here start with a number. Two names get passed around a Sobha City residents group, one quotes a monthly figure, the other quotes per session, and neither quote says anything about what the hour contains. That is a poor place to begin a decision. It is also where nearly every conversation begins, so it is worth being blunt about the economics.

An IB hour is priced by scarcity more than by effort. A tutor who can read a Math AI HL exploration against the actual assessment criteria is harder to find than a competent secondary maths teacher, and the fee reflects that difference. Travel is the second driver. A tutor coming from Sector 57 or Sushant Lok to Puri Diplomatic Greens gives up close to ninety minutes on the road for a ninety-minute session, and that time sits inside your fee whether anyone itemises it or not.

What the hour should buy is narrower than parents expect. One agreed target for the fortnight. Work marked before the session rather than read out during it. Two lines at the end naming what the student attempts alone.

On IB Gram, fees for IB tutors in Sector 103 Gurugram depend on level, subject and schedule, and get discussed openly before any trial is booked.

HL specialists are scarcer than SL generalists, and priced that way
Drive time from Sector 57 or Sushant Lok sits inside the fee

Trial session first, longer commitment afterwards

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Tutors in Sector 103 Gurugram Are Shortlisted
contentBlocks.body:
A request from this pocket of Gurugram is not treated as a subject name plus a pin code. Five things get asked before any name is put forward, and the order matters.

First the school and the year group, because a Grade 9 MYP student two terms from personal project work needs something different from a Grade 11 student who has just picked HL subjects. Then the exact subject and level, written the way the school writes it: Math AA HL and Math AI HL are not interchangeable, and a tutor strong in one can be mediocre in the other. Then the immediate pressure, whether that is a criterion C investigation, a lab report backlog, or a Paper 2 that went badly. Then the honest weekly window, including the day the school bus actually reaches home. Then the mode you can sustain, which is where travel realism enters.

Only after that does a shortlist get built, usually two or three names rather than a long list. A trial session follows. If the fit is wrong, saying so in the first fortnight costs nothing and saves a term.

Requests can be reviewed for Grade 1 to Grade 12, subject to tutor availability for the level and slot you need.

Exact subject and level, written as the school writes it
The immediate pressure: IA draft, lab backlog, weak paper
Realistic weekly window after school bus arrival
Two or three names, then a trial

contentBlocks.heading: Math AA HL, Chemistry and the Subjects Hardest to Staff
contentBlocks.body:
Requests from the Dwarka Expressway sectors cluster tightly around six subjects, and they do not all behave the same way in a tutoring market.

Math AA HL is the heaviest single request. Students who coped through MYP often hit a wall in the proof and calculus sections, and what they need is technique under time pressure rather than fresh explanation. Physics and Chemistry requests usually arrive with an internal assessment attached, and the useful help is around variable control, uncertainty handling and evaluation, not chapter revision. Scarcity follows those needs. HL science and HL maths tutors who mark against criteria are in shorter supply than the request volume, so a home slot near Sobha City in those subjects is harder to fill than an online one.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: Three Different Reasons to Call
contentBlocks.body:
The three IB programmes generate three very different requests, and the fee conversation looks different in each.

PYP families in the newer towers usually want reading fluency and number sense supported without the session collapsing into worksheet drilling. That work is slower to show results and easier to get wrong. Sessions tend to be shorter, more frequent, and cheaper per hour than Diploma work. MYP is where most of the confusion sits. A child can understand a concept and still score poorly, because the marks live in criterion language: inquiring and analysing, communicating, reflecting. A good MYP tutor spends part of every session on how the task is worded. Diploma Programme work is the most specialised and the most time-bound. Internal assessments, the extended essay, theory of knowledge and past-paper practice all compete for the same weeks.

Support runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, with May 2026 and November 2026 exam sessions shaping the DP calendar and earlier planning suggested for younger DP cohorts.

One honest limitation: a student arriving in February of the second DP year with three weak subjects cannot be given back a lost year. Priorities have to be chosen, and something gets left.

contentBlocks.heading: At Home in Sector 103 or Online Across Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Both modes work. They fail in different ways, and knowing which failure you can tolerate is the real decision.

Home tutoring gives you presence. A younger PYP or early MYP student sits down because someone is physically at the dining table, and a parent can hear whether the session is teaching or babysitting. The cost is rigidity. One fixed slot, one tutor, and an evening lost to rain on the expressway is simply lost. Online reverses that. The pool widens to the whole city and beyond, so an IB online tutor in Sector 103 Gurugram is usually findable for HL Chemistry or Math AA HL at nine in the evening, when no home tutor would agree to travel. Screen-shared past papers and annotated PDFs work well for exam technique. What online does not do well is force a distracted fourteen-year-old to concentrate.

A hybrid pattern suits many families here: one home session a week for accountability, one online session for specialist depth, and doubt-solving by message in between.

For late evenings, rare subjects or urgent DP revision, online generally produces the stronger specialist match.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Name Reaches You
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a process, not a badge. Here is what it involves, described plainly so you can judge whether it is enough.

Identity and qualification documents are collected first. Then subject evidence at the specific level claimed, which matters because teaching Chemistry to Grade 10 and teaching HL Chemistry with an internal assessment attached are different jobs. Then references where available, and past tutoring history on the platform where it exists.

None of that predicts chemistry between a particular tutor and a particular teenager. It reduces the odds of an obviously poor match, which is a smaller promise than most platforms make and a more accurate one.

contentBlocks.heading: Four Weeks In: What You Should Be Able to See
contentBlocks.body:
Parents rarely have a way to judge tutoring except by their child's mood, which is unreliable. So set a checkpoint at four weeks and look for evidence instead.

By then you should be able to see marked work carrying written comments, not just ticks. You should hear your child use assessment vocabulary without prompting, saying that a question wants evaluation rather than description. You should see a short plan for the coming fortnight that survives contact with school deadlines. And you should be able to ask the tutor one question, which is what specifically has improved and what has not, and get a specific answer rather than a reassuring one.

What you should not expect at four weeks is a jump in marks. Nobody can promise that, and any quote arriving attached to a promised score is telling you something about the seller rather than the service. Marks in the Diploma Programme move on the back of technique repeated over months.

If the checkpoint fails, change something. A different tutor, a different mode, or a narrower target for the term.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Sector 103 usually depend on?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and any page quoting one figure for every subject is simplifying. The fee moves with three things. The level, because HL work with an internal assessment attached takes preparation time outside the session. The subject, because Math AA HL and the HL sciences have fewer available specialists than Economics or English A. And the schedule, because a late evening slot or a home visit involving a long drive costs the tutor more of their day. Frequency matters too. Fees are shared before a trial, not after it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor actually come home to Sobha City or ATS Kocoon?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends almost entirely on whether a tutor is already working inside the Dwarka Expressway sectors that evening. Someone finishing a session in Puri Diplomatic Greens can often take a second one nearby. A tutor coming from Sector 57 or Sohna Road is a harder ask, because the return drive can outlast the lesson. faqs.question: My child is in MYP and understands the topic but keeps losing marks. Why?
faqs.answer: That gap is usually about criterion language rather than knowledge. MYP tasks are marked against strands with specific verbs, and a student who explains well but never analyses will lose marks while sounding confident at home. The fix is unglamorous. The tutor reads the task sheet with the student, identifies which criterion is being assessed, and rewrites one paragraph together to hit the wording. Repeated across a term, that shifts scores more reliably than covering extra content does.

faqs.question: How quickly can sessions start after we send an enquiry?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the slot. Common requests such as MYP maths or DP Economics can often be shortlisted quickly. A narrow request, for example HL Chemistry at nine in the evening with a home visit inside Sector 103, takes longer because very few tutors satisfy all three conditions at once. Being flexible on one condition, usually mode, shortens the wait considerably. An advisor will say honestly if a request looks difficult to fill rather than leaving it open indefinitely.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely effective for Diploma Programme subjects?
faqs.answer: For most DP work it is, and for some of it online is better. Past papers, mark-scheme walkthroughs, exploration drafts and essay feedback all work well on a shared screen, and the annotated file can be revisited later. Where online struggles is with students who need physical presence to stay on task, and with practical laboratory intuition, which needs the school laboratory anyway. A reasonable test: if your child can work alone for twenty minutes, online will hold up.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not the right fit for my child?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than waiting for the term to end. Two or three sessions is usually enough to tell whether the tutor explains at the right pace and whether your child talks during the lesson. A replacement can be requested and a different profile suggested, subject to availability for your level and time slot. Be specific about what did not work, because moving from a patient explainer to a brisk drill-focused tutor is a different change from moving to another subject specialist.

faqs.question: We are starting late in the Diploma Programme. Is it worth beginning now?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but with narrowed expectations, and this is where families deserve straight talk. Starting in the final months means choosing between depth in one weak subject and thin coverage across three. Past-paper technique and command-term precision give the fastest return, because they recover marks the student has already half-earned. Rebuilding two years of missing foundations in eight weeks is not realistic. A good tutor will tell you which of your three worries is actually fixable in the time left.

faqs.question: Do you handle extended essay and theory of knowledge support?
faqs.answer: Yes, as mentoring alongside the school supervisor rather than instead of them. Extended essay help is mostly about question narrowing, source selection and structure, since a broad research question is the most common reason an essay stalls. Theory of knowledge support usually focuses on how a claim is framed and how counterclaims are handled. The written work must remain the student's own, and the school supervisor stays the primary authority on deadlines and academic honesty requirements.

faqs.question: How does support differ for a Grade 4 PYP child compared with Grade 11?
faqs.answer: Almost entirely. PYP sessions are shorter, more frequent, and built around reading fluency, number sense and curiosity, and they go wrong when they turn into worksheet factories. A Grade 11 session is time-bound and specialised: one internal assessment, one weak paper, one set of command terms. The tutor profile differs too. Warmth and patience matter most for the younger child, while subject depth at the exact level matters most for the older one. Requests across Grade 1 to Grade 12 can be reviewed.

contentBlocks.heading: Changing Tutors Mid-Course in Sector 104, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor leaves in October. The student has a half-finished exploration, a folder of loose notes, and a working style the old tutor understood and nobody wrote down. Three weeks later the replacement is still asking questions the previous tutor could have answered in five minutes.

That lost time is the real cost of a change, and it is almost never the fee difference that families were worried about. So the useful question is not whether to switch, but what has to move across with the student.

Four things do. The exact subject and level as the school writes it. The current draft of any internal assessment, with the supervisor's comments still attached. The school calendar, including mock dates and internal deadlines. And a plain description of what went wrong, because a student who disengaged from a lecturing tutor needs a different replacement from one who was left behind on content.

Parents around Sobha City often apologise for switching, as though it reflects badly on them. It usually does not. Fit is partly unpredictable, and two or three sessions is the honest window in which to judge it.

Requests for IB tutors in Sector 104 Gurugram can be reviewed on that basis, subject to tutor availability.

contentBlocks.heading: Which Subjects Survive a Tutor Change and Which Do Not
contentBlocks.body:
Not every subject takes a handover equally well, and knowing the difference changes how urgently you act.

Economics and English A move across relatively cleanly. The content is stable, the skills are visible in written work, and a new tutor can read three past essays and see the problem within a session. Physics and Chemistry are harder, because a science internal assessment carries a design decision made months earlier. If the variable was chosen badly, a replacement tutor may have to say so, and that conversation is unpleasant but better held in November than in February. Math AA HL is the least forgiving. The syllabus is cumulative, and a gap left in the calculus or proof sections tends to surface repeatedly, so a new tutor usually spends the first fortnight diagnosing rather than teaching. Math AI HL handovers stall on a different point: the modelling work is only as good as the justification, and that habit takes time to rebuild.

An IB science tutor Sector 104 families take on mid-year should be asked directly how much of the earlier work they intend to revisit.

Subject requests here run across Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A.

contentBlocks.heading: Continuity Looks Different in PYP, MYP and DP
contentBlocks.body:
The cost of a change rises sharply as a student moves up the programmes, which is why the same decision can be trivial at Grade 3 and serious at Grade 12.

For a PYP child, continuity is mostly emotional. A seven-year-old who has built trust with one adult will take a fortnight to relax with another, and during that fortnight very little content lands. The remedy is overlap and patience, not a faster syllabus. In MYP the loss is procedural. Criterion-based tasks are marked against strands, and a tutor who has spent a term learning how a particular school interprets those strands carries knowledge that is genuinely hard to transfer. A new MYP tutor should ask to see two marked tasks with the rubric attached before deciding anything.

In the Diploma Programme the loss is calendar loss. Internal assessments, the extended essay, theory of knowledge and past-paper drilling are all sequenced against May 2026 and November 2026, and four wasted weeks in the second year cannot be recovered later.

Support runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12. Younger DP cohorts benefit from planning earlier than most families expect.

contentBlocks.body:

A home tutor in Sector 104 is chosen partly for geography. When that person leaves, the replacement has to satisfy the same geography, and the pool of tutors willing to drive into the Dwarka Expressway sectors on a weekday evening is not large. Replacing a home tutor mid-term can therefore take longer than replacing an online one, sometimes considerably. Online removes that constraint. An IB online tutor in Sector 104 Gurugram is drawn from across the city and beyond, so a like-for-like replacement in HL Chemistry or Math AA HL can usually be found faster, and a recorded or annotated session file gives the next tutor something concrete to read.

Home tutoring still wins on attention for younger students and for anyone who quietly stops working when unsupervised. That is a real advantage and worth paying the flexibility cost for.

Many families here settle on a mix: home sessions for the school-week routine, online for specialist depth and for the weeks before mocks when late slots are the only ones left.

contentBlocks.heading: Briefing a New IB Tutor in Sector 104, Gurugram Properly
contentBlocks.body:
Matching runs as a short sequence, and a replacement request skips none of it. Here is the order.

One, the school and year group, since campuses in this region sequence units differently and set internal deadlines months apart. Two, the subject and level exactly as written on the report card, because HL and SL are separate teaching jobs and the request often arrives blurred. Three, the deadline that is closest, whether that is an exploration draft, a lab write-up or a mock paper. Four, the weekly window that works after the school bus reaches the tower, which in this part of Gurugram is later than families in central sectors assume. Five, the history: how long the previous arrangement ran and why it ended.

That fifth point is the one families skip, and it is the one that most improves the second match. Saying that the earlier tutor talked for fifty minutes of every hour is more useful than saying it did not work out.

A shortlist of two or three names follows, then a trial session. Availability for a given level and slot can be reviewed before anything is committed.

contentBlocks.heading: Evidence a Replacement Tutor Should Be Able to Show
contentBlocks.body:
A second tutor gets less benefit of the doubt than the first, and that is reasonable. Screening is designed around evidence rather than assertion.

Qualification and identity documents are collected before a profile is shown. Subject capability is checked at the exact level, so HL Physics and general school-level physics are treated as separate claims. Familiarity with IB assessment is checked directly: whether the tutor can separate analyse from evaluate as command terms, whether they have marked against criteria descriptors, and how they would handle an internal assessment where the school supervisor has already given feedback. A teaching sample or structured discussion follows, focused on how they would open with a student who has just lost momentum. References are taken where available.

What screening cannot do is predict rapport. It narrows the field to people who can do the academic job, and leaves the rest to the trial session, which is why the trial exists.

If the second arrangement also proves wrong, ask for a third profile rather than persisting. Replacement is subject to availability for your subject, level and slot, and being flexible on timing usually speeds it up.
items: Documents checked before any profile is shared
Level-specific subject evidence, HL claims tested separately
Command-term and criterion knowledge probed directly
Sample teaching focused on a student who has stalled
A third profile is a normal request, not a complaint

Weekend mornings are frequently the better slot for heavy subjects, particularly during internal assessment season.

Calendars matter more than campus reputation for a replacement tutor. Mock exam weeks, internal draft deadlines and report cycles differ between these schools by several weeks, and a tutor planning against the wrong calendar will schedule revision at the wrong time. Ask any new tutor to record the next three school deadlines before the second session.

contentBlocks.heading: Signals That the Second Tutor Is Working Out
contentBlocks.body:
After a switch, parents tend to watch anxiously for a week and then stop watching. A better approach is to fix two review points and use them.

At two weeks, the question is diagnostic. Can the tutor tell you, without hedging, what the specific weakness is? Someone who says your child needs to work harder has not looked at the work. Someone who says the evaluation paragraphs consistently describe rather than judge has.

At six weeks, the question is directional. Is there marked work with written comments? Has the internal assessment moved from where it was stuck? Does your child now use the language of the criteria when explaining a task? Small changes in vocabulary are a better early indicator than marks, which lag behind by roughly a term and can hide real progress in the meantime.

One honest caution. A switch made close to the final exam sessions rarely produces a dramatic recovery, and anyone suggesting otherwise is selling. What a good second tutor can do late is protect the marks the student can still reach, and stop the panic revision that wastes the last month.

Six-week check: marked work and a moved IA draft
Criteria vocabulary appearing in ordinary conversation
Marks lag behind technique by roughly a term
Late switches protect marks rather than transform them

Say whether you want a home slot, an online one, or a mix, and whether weekend mornings are open, because for the heavier HL subjects that answer often decides how quickly a name can be suggested.

faqs.question: Our tutor left in the middle of an internal assessment. What should we collect before they go?
faqs.answer: Ask for three things in writing, ideally by message so it is recorded. The current draft file with any comments the tutor added. A one-paragraph note on what stage the work is at and what the next step was going to be. And any past-paper or practice material the student was working through, so the sequence is not restarted from scratch. Most tutors will send this readily. The absence of it costs the replacement roughly two sessions of guesswork that you end up paying for.

faqs.question: Will a new tutor make my child repeat topics that were already covered?
faqs.answer: Some rechecking is unavoidable and healthy, because a tutor cannot plan against work they have not seen. Expect the first session or two to include diagnostic questions across recent topics rather than new teaching. What is not reasonable is a full restart of the syllabus. If a tutor proposes going back to the beginning of the year in November, ask them to justify it against the exam calendar. A good answer names specific gaps. A vague answer about building foundations usually means they have not diagnosed anything yet.

faqs.question: Is it a mistake to change tutors three months before the final exams?
faqs.answer: It is a risk, and it depends on what is broken. If the problem is rapport or reliability, changing is usually better than enduring, because a student who has stopped listening gains nothing from continuity. If the problem is that marks have not moved, a change alone will not fix it and the target needs narrowing instead. Late in the cycle, ask any new tutor for a written plan covering the remaining weeks before the second session. If they cannot produce one, that answers the question.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor continue if we move from Sector 104 to another part of Gurugram?
faqs.answer: For online sessions, yes, a move changes nothing. For home tutoring it depends entirely on the new distance. A shift within the Dwarka Expressway sectors is usually manageable. A move towards Sohna Road or the DLF phases often means the existing tutor cannot keep the slot, since the evening drive becomes the deciding factor rather than willingness. Where that happens, switching the same arrangement to online is worth trying before replacing the tutor, since the teaching relationship is already established.

faqs.question: How many tutors is it reasonable to try before settling?
faqs.answer: Most families settle on the first or second, and a third is not unusual for a narrow HL requirement. Beyond that, the problem is often the brief rather than the tutors. If three capable specialists have all struggled with the same student, look again at timing, workload and whether the sessions are placed after the point in the evening where concentration has gone. Changing the slot sometimes fixes what changing the person does not. Trials exist precisely so this can be tested cheaply.

faqs.question: What should a tutor leave behind at the end of an engagement?
faqs.answer: A short handover is normal professional practice, though few parents ask for it. Useful contents include the topics covered with dates, the work marked and where those files sit, the current position on any internal assessment, and an honest note on what still needs attention. Two paragraphs is enough. Ask for it at the time of notice rather than afterwards, because response rates drop sharply once the arrangement has ended and nobody is obliged to reconstruct months of work from memory.

faqs.question: Do we pay for the trial session, and what happens during it?
faqs.answer: The trial is a working session rather than a sales call, and its terms are confirmed by the advisor before it is booked so there are no surprises. Expect the tutor to look at recent work, ask the student to attempt something while they watch, and then describe what they saw. A good trial ends with a specific plan for the next fortnight. A weak one ends with general encouragement. That difference alone is usually enough to decide whether to continue.

faqs.question: Can two siblings in different grades share one tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: Rarely with good results, unless they are close in level and taking the same subject. A Grade 6 MYP student and a Grade 11 DP student have almost nothing in common in what a session needs to do, and splitting an hour halves the attention each receives while saving less than expected. Where siblings genuinely overlap, a tutor may agree to consecutive sessions on the same visit, which reduces travel and is often easier to arrange in these towers than two separate evenings.

faqs.question: What if the new tutor keeps cancelling or shifting the session time?
faqs.answer: Raise it after the second occurrence rather than the fifth. Irregular sessions do more damage in the Diploma Programme than a slightly weaker tutor does, because the schedule is what holds the internal assessment work together. Report the pattern with dates through the advisor so it is on record, and ask whether the slot itself is the problem, since a tutor who has overcommitted their evenings will keep slipping. If the pattern continues, request a replacement rather than negotiating repeatedly.

contentBlocks.heading: Working Backwards From the Exam Date in Sector 106, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Most tutoring enquiries from these towers arrive in the same fortnight. A report card lands, or an internal assessment draft comes back covered in supervisor comments, and suddenly everyone in the building wants the same Physics specialist for the same Tuesday evening.

That bunching is avoidable, because the Diploma calendar is not a surprise. Written exams sit in May and November. Mock papers usually fall two to four months earlier. Internal assessment drafts, the extended essay and the theory of knowledge essay have school deadlines set at the start of the year, and those dates are printed in a calendar the school has already given you.

So the practical move is to plan the year the other way round. Take the earliest hard deadline, count back six to eight weeks, and that is when the relevant tutoring should begin rather than when the panic starts.

Done that way, the request also becomes specific enough to match well. Asking for help with a Chemistry internal assessment due in seven weeks produces a far better shortlist than asking for a chemistry tutor.

IB tutors in Sector 106 Gurugram can be matched against that calendar for Grade 1 to Grade 12, subject to availability.

Mocks typically two to four months ahead of finals

contentBlocks.heading: Assessment Milestones by Programme, From PYP to DP
contentBlocks.body:
Each programme has its own rhythm, and confusing them is the commonest planning error parents make.

The Primary Years Programme has no external examination. Its milestones are the units of inquiry and, at the end, the PYP exhibition, which asks a Grade 5 child to sustain an independent piece of work for the first time. Support here is about reading stamina, questioning and number confidence rather than exam drilling. The Middle Years Programme is marked continuously against four criteria per subject, with the personal project standing out in the final year. A student can be strong in class and still lose marks because the reflection is thin or the sources are unevaluated.

The Diploma Programme is where dates dominate. Each subject carries an internal assessment, the extended essay runs to four thousand words, the theory of knowledge essay responds to a prescribed title in about sixteen hundred words, and all of it competes with revision for the written papers.

Students in these towers are typically working across Grade 1 to Grade 12, and the earlier a DP cohort starts mapping deadlines, the less the final year turns into triage.

Distance outward is the constraint. During IA season, when demand peaks, that gap widens further.

contentBlocks.heading: Paper Structures and Internal Assessments, Subject by Subject
contentBlocks.body:
What a tutor should be doing depends on which assessment is closest, and that varies by subject in ways worth knowing before you call.

In Math AA HL and Math AI HL, the internal assessment is an exploration the student chooses themselves, and a poorly chosen topic is the single biggest cause of a weak mark. Good help arrives at the topic-selection stage, not at the writing stage. The written papers reward timed practice and command-term precision, particularly on the longer response paper. In Physics and Chemistry, the internal assessment is an individual investigation where marks hang on the research question, control of variables, uncertainty treatment and evaluation. The papers combine multiple-choice and data-based work with extended response, depending on the syllabus version your school follows.

Economics students write commentaries linking real articles to syllabus theory, and the marks are lost in weak evaluation far more often than in weak content. English A brings the individual oral and, at higher level, a written essay on a studied text.

An IB science tutor Sector 106 families approach in October is usually needed for investigation design, not revision.

Sciences: research question, variables, uncertainty, evaluation
Economics: commentaries where evaluation carries the marks
English A: individual oral plus the higher level essay
Timed paper practice separate from coursework support

Each sets its own internal calendar, and the differences are large enough to matter. One campus may want a complete internal assessment draft before the winter break while another accepts it well into the new year. Mock weeks can sit a month apart. A tutor planning against a generic timetable will therefore be revising the wrong thing at the wrong time, which is why the school calendar should be shared in the first session rather than the fifth.

The commute also compresses the working evening. A student reaching home from Sector 57 after five has limited useful attention left, so heavy coursework sessions often land better on weekend mornings, especially in the weeks before a draft deadline.

contentBlocks.heading: Turning a Deadline List Into a Tutor Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Matching works better when the request carries dates. The sequence is short and every step removes guesswork.

Start with the subject and level written as the school writes it, since HL and SL differ in paper structure as well as depth. Add the assessment that is closest, named specifically: an exploration draft, a lab investigation, three economics commentaries, a prescribed title essay. Add its deadline. Add the school and year group, so the tutor can align to the right internal calendar. Then give the weekly windows that genuinely exist once travel from the campus is accounted for.

From that, a shortlist of two or three profiles is built, weighted towards tutors who have worked on that specific assessment rather than only taught the subject. A trial session follows, and it should end with the tutor stating what they would do in the first four weeks.

One caveat worth saying plainly. A request made two weeks before a hard deadline narrows the field sharply, because the tutors best suited to that work are usually already committed. Earlier requests get better matches, not just more of them.

contentBlocks.heading: Timetabling Home and Online Sessions in Sector 106, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Mode is a scheduling decision as much as a teaching one, and during coursework season that becomes obvious.

Home sessions hold their value for younger students and for anyone whose attention drifts without an adult present. They are also the easier setting for long, messy work sessions where papers are spread across a table. The limitation is supply. A weekday evening home slot inside these towers depends on a tutor already being in the area, and in the weeks before a draft deadline those slots go first.

Online changes the arithmetic. An IB online tutor in Sector 106 Gurugram can be found for narrow requirements such as HL Physics uncertainty analysis or a mathematics exploration review, at hours no travelling tutor would accept. Draft feedback in particular works well on screen, since annotated comments arrive in the document itself and can be reread later.

A common arrangement here runs one home session weekly through the term for routine, and adds short online reviews in the fortnight before a deadline. For urgent revision or rare subject combinations, online usually produces the stronger specialist match.

contentBlocks.heading: Reading Progress From the Draft, Not the Mood
contentBlocks.body:
Judging whether tutoring is working is easier during coursework season than at any other time, because there is a document to look at.

Open the draft. Compare it with the version from three weeks earlier. Has the research question narrowed? Have the sources been evaluated rather than listed? Is there a section that actually weighs one interpretation against another? Those are visible changes, and they do not depend on your child's account of how the session went.

For paper work, the equivalent evidence is a marked past paper with the lost marks categorised. A tutor who can tell you that most marks went in the extended response section on evaluation, rather than saying the paper was tough, is doing the job.

And one limitation to keep in view. Coursework improvements show up in a draft within weeks, but paper marks tend to move slowly, because timing and accuracy under pressure rebuild over months rather than sessions. Nobody should promise a grade, and a plan that depends on one is not a plan. Ask instead for the two specific weaknesses being worked on this month, then check the same two next month.

contentBlocks.heading: The Checks Behind Every Profile We Send
contentBlocks.body:
Because so much of this work is assessment-specific, screening looks at what a tutor has actually handled rather than at general teaching experience alone.

Identity and qualifications are documented first. Subject capability is then checked at the precise level, since HL and SL papers differ in structure and an SL-only background is a poor fit for higher level extended response work. Assessment familiarity is probed directly: whether the tutor has supported an exploration or an individual investigation before, whether they can explain how a criterion descriptor is applied, and whether they understand the boundary between supporting a student and doing the work. That boundary is not negotiable, since coursework must remain the student's own and the school supervisor holds the academic honesty responsibility.

A teaching sample or structured conversation follows, usually built around a student stuck on a draft rather than one simply behind on content, and references are taken where available.

What this cannot tell you is whether your child will get on with the person. That is what the trial session is for, and if the answer is no, a different profile can be requested subject to availability for your level and slot.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma student here start internal assessment support?
faqs.answer: Six to eight weeks before the school's first draft deadline is the point where help is most useful, because the topic and research question are still open. Once a draft has been written around a weak question, fixing it means starting again, and few students have the appetite for that in the second year. If the deadline is closer than three weeks, the realistic aim shifts from improving the work to salvaging the strongest parts of it. Earlier requests also get better tutor availability, since IA season creates a queue.

faqs.question: How long is the extended essay, and how much help is a tutor allowed to give?
faqs.answer: The extended essay runs to four thousand words on a research question the student chooses within a subject. A tutor can help with narrowing that question, testing whether sources exist, planning structure and reading a draft critically. What a tutor cannot do is write sections, supply arguments as finished text, or replace the school supervisor, who signs off on the process and holds the academic honesty responsibility. Practically, most essays stall at the question stage, so that is where outside help pays off most.

faqs.question: What is the theory of knowledge essay, and can tutoring help with it?
faqs.answer: It is an essay of roughly sixteen hundred words responding to one of the prescribed titles released by the IB, and it is assessed externally. Students find it hard because it rewards precise handling of knowledge claims rather than content recall, and strong subject students often write vaguely here. Useful support focuses on unpacking the title, choosing areas of knowledge that genuinely fit, and building counterclaims that are more than a token paragraph. The argument and examples must remain the student's own throughout.

faqs.question: Our mock week clashes with an IA draft deadline. What should we prioritise?
faqs.answer: Usually the draft, and for a practical reason. The draft feeds a mark that goes forward, while a mock is diagnostic and can be recovered from. But the answer depends on how far along each is. If the draft is nearly complete and the mock covers a paper the student has failed twice, splitting the fortnight makes sense. Ask the tutor to write the split down as a plan with dates. A verbal agreement in a tired evening rarely survives the week.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma Programme student usually need?
faqs.answer: For one subject, one session a week is the common pattern through the term, rising to two in the weeks around a deadline or a mock. Taking three subjects at two sessions each is where families overload, because homework and coursework still have to happen somewhere. Watch total hours rather than per-subject hours. A student with no unscheduled evening left will start missing sessions, and that pattern damages the schedule more than dropping one subject's tutoring would have.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue during study leave before the May exams?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that period often suits short, frequent sessions better than long ones. Study leave removes the school timetable, so the day can be structured around timed paper practice in the morning and a review session later. Availability during that stretch is tighter than usual because many students want the same weeks, which is another argument for booking ahead. Online tends to work better than home visits then, since slots move around as the exam timetable dictates.

faqs.question: Does the Middle Years Programme need the same kind of deadline planning?
faqs.answer: Less rigid, but not none. MYP assessment is continuous rather than concentrated in a final exam series, so the pressure points are unit task deadlines and, in the last year, the personal project. Planning matters most around the personal project, where students are asked to manage a long piece of independent work for the first time and often underestimate the process journal. Support there is largely about milestones and reflection quality rather than subject content.

faqs.question: What is the difference between support for Paper 1, Paper 2 and Paper 3?
faqs.answer: They test different things, so the practice looks different. Paper 1 typically rewards speed and accuracy across shorter items, and improves with repeated timed sets rather than discussion. Paper 2 involves longer structured responses where command terms decide how much is written and in what form. Where a subject has a Paper 3, it usually draws on options or data handling and needs targeted preparation late in the course. A tutor should say which paper a session is aimed at.

faqs.question: Our child is in Grade 10 and has not chosen higher level subjects yet. Too early to start?
faqs.answer: Not at all, and this is arguably the most useful moment to get advice. Subject choice shapes the next two years more than any tutoring decision does, and a student who picks Math AA HL on reputation rather than aptitude will struggle for a long time. Sessions at this stage can test whether the higher level version of a subject is realistic, strengthen the specific skills it assumes, and avoid a change of level in the first term, which is disruptive.

h1: IB Tutors in Sector 107, Gurugram: Begin With One Honest Diagnostic Hour
heroSubtitle: Most families here have already tried a well-meaning tutor who taught for an hour and changed nothing. A first session should instead read the student work, name the exact place marks are being lost, and leave behind a plan for the next four weeks that fits school deadlines.
introSummary: Parents looking for IB tutors in Sector 107 Gurugram usually want one question settled quickly: will the first session tell us anything useful. It should. A good first hour reads marked work, identifies where the marks are actually going, and ends with a four-week plan rather than a promise. IB Gram takes requests from Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph and ATS Kocoon, checks what the student needs at PYP, MYP or DP level, and suggests tutors who can realistically reach this end of the Dwarka Expressway or teach online.

contentBlocks.heading: What the First Hour With a Tutor Should Actually Produce
contentBlocks.body:
A first session is not a trial lesson in the usual sense. It is a diagnostic hour, and by the end of it a parent should be holding three concrete things: a short account of what the student can already do unaided, the specific place the marks are leaking, and a plan for the next four weeks that fits around school deadlines rather than ignoring them.

Tutors who are any good get there by asking for evidence before they teach. A marked Paper 1. The last two assignments with teacher comments still on them. The criterion sheet the school used. A half-finished internal assessment, however embarrassing its current state.

What should not happen in that hour: general conversation about effort and attitude, reassurance that everything will settle down, or a tutor opening at Chapter 1 because that is where their own notes start.

By the fourth week you should be able to judge the match yourself. Not by a grade jump, which usually takes a full term, but by how the student talks about the subject. Fewer questions about what the question is asking. A faster start on homework instead of forty minutes of avoidance. An IA section that exists.

If none of that has moved, the match is wrong, and changing it is better than defending it.
items: Bring marked scripts, not the report card
Diagnosis before teaching, in that order
A written four-week plan, agreed before the second session
Week four signal: how the student talks about the subject
Wrong match changed, not argued over

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 107 Sits at the Delhi End of Gurugram, and That Changes Timings
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 107 lies along the Dwarka Expressway, on the northern edge of Gurugram rather than in the older Golf Course Road belt. Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph and ATS Kocoon put a large number of school-going children inside a small radius, which is helpful, because a tutor who takes one student in a tower can often take a second in the same complex without adding travel.

The less comfortable fact is distance. A tutor living in DLF Phase 5, Sushant Lok or Sector 57 faces a real cross-city drive to reach this sector, and that drive gets worse between six and eight in the evening, which is exactly when most families want sessions. So the pool of tutors willing to travel here in person is thinner than the pool available to DLF Phase 1 or South City 1.

That has two practical consequences. Home tutoring works best when the slot is early evening or weekend morning, and when the tutor lives on this side of town or in Dwarka. For anything late, urgent, or unusually specialised, online almost always reaches a better teacher.

Requests from Sector 50, Sector 65, Nirvana Country and DLF Phase 4 are reviewed the same way, but their travel maths is different.
items: Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph, ATS Kocoon: dense clusters, short walks
Cross-city drive from DLF Phase 5 or Sector 57 is the main constraint
Early evening and weekend morning slots hold up best
Tutors based in Dwarka or the northern sectors travel more reliably
Late-evening requests: online is the honest recommendation

contentBlocks.heading: Home Visits Near Sobha City Against an Online Slot at Half Past Eight
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring has one advantage nothing online replicates: the student cannot quietly stop paying attention. For younger children, and for anyone who has been avoiding a subject for months, that physical presence does most of the work in the first few weeks.

It also has a failure mode. A tutor stuck on the expressway arrives twenty minutes late, teaches a shortened session, and cancels twice in a bad month. Two reliable online hours beat three unreliable home visits, and a parent who has lived through one term of shifting slots usually agrees.

Online suits three situations in particular. Higher level subjects where the number of genuinely strong teachers is small. Internal assessment work, where sharing a document and marking it live is faster than reading over a shoulder. And the weeks before papers, when a student needs short frequent contact rather than long visits.

Hybrid arrangements are common here and rarely discussed: one weekend session at home for accountability, one midweek online session for the technical work. Families with two children in different programmes often land on this by themselves.

Availability in either mode depends on level, subject and the time slot you can offer, and remains subject to tutor schedules.
items: Home: strongest for PYP and early MYP, and for avoidance habits
Online: better reach for HL specialists and rare subject combinations
IA drafting is faster with a shared screen than a shared table
Hybrid: weekend home session plus midweek online work
Reliability beats format, every time

contentBlocks.heading: Math AA HL and Physics Dominate the Requests From This Part of Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Two subjects account for most of what parents here write in when they first make contact: Mathematics at higher level, and Physics.

Math AA HL and Math AI HL are not one course with two difficulty settings, and treating them as interchangeable is an expensive mistake. AA HL runs deep into proof, calculus and algebraic technique. AI HL leans on modelling, statistics and the interpretation of real data, and its papers reward a different kind of written reasoning. A tutor comfortable with one is not automatically useful for the other, so IB Gram treats them as separate requests.

Physics at higher level usually breaks in one of two places. Either the mathematics underneath a topic was never secure, in which case the fix is partly a maths fix, or the student can complete the calculation but cannot answer the explain and justify questions that carry the marks in Paper 2.

Chemistry, Economics and English A come up steadily as well. Economics requests are almost always about evaluation and diagram use rather than definitions. English A requests are usually about guided analysis and the individual oral, not about reading more books.
items: Math AA HL: proof, calculus, algebraic fluency
Math AI HL: modelling, statistics, data interpretation
Physics HL: a maths gap and an explain-question gap are different problems
Economics: evaluation and diagrams carry the marks
English A: guided analysis and the individual oral
Chemistry: bonding and energetics first, then the practical work

contentBlocks.heading: How a Request for IB Tutors in Sector 107 Gurugram Becomes a Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
The process is deliberately short, because most families make contact after a bad report or a missed deadline and do not want a week of back and forth.

Step one is the request itself: grade, programme, subject and level, the days and times that genuinely work, and whether you want someone at home or online. Step two is a conversation, usually about fifteen minutes, where an advisor asks what the school has actually said. That is where the useful information sits, and it is why we ask for teacher comments rather than your summary of them.

Step three is the match. Tutors are filtered by subject and level first, then by whether they can hold the slot you need, then by the kind of student they teach well. Someone excellent with a confident DP2 student chasing the top band is not always right for a Grade 9 student who has stopped trying.

Step four is the diagnostic session described above, and step five is a check-in after roughly four weeks.

If the shortlist is thin for a particular combination, we say so rather than sending an approximate match and hoping.

Advisor call: what the school said, in the school wording
Filter order: subject and level, then schedule, then student type
Diagnostic session, then a four-week review
A thin shortlist is reported, not padded

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Each Need a Different Kind of First Session
contentBlocks.body:
Support across Grade 1 to Grade 12 does not mean one lesson delivered at three difficulty levels.

With a PYP child the first session is mostly observation. Can the child read fluently enough to work independently, can they explain their thinking out loud, do they have the number sense the current unit assumes. The risk at this stage is turning inquiry-based learning into worksheet drilling, which produces a short-lived improvement and a bored child.

MYP is where most parents in these sectors first feel lost, because marks arrive as criteria rather than percentages. A first session here should put the criterion descriptors side by side with the student work, so the student can see the difference between a level four response and a level six response in their own writing. That comparison does more in one sitting than a month of general advice.

DP is the most time-pressured. A first session covers where the student stands against the syllabus, the state of the internal assessment, the Extended Essay timeline, and how much Theory of Knowledge work is outstanding. Anyone who skips the calendar in a DP first session is teaching, not planning.
items: PYP: reading fluency, spoken reasoning, number sense
MYP: criterion descriptors read against the student own work
DP: syllabus position, IA state, EE timeline, TOK backlog
Grade 1 to Grade 12 supported, with different first-session shapes
Concept-based learning respected, not replaced with drills

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 107 Families Send Their Children to School Across Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Children living in this sector rarely attend a school on the same road. Buses run long routes from the Dwarka Expressway sectors into schools spread across the city, which is why so many students here leave home before seven in the morning and return well after four.

Pathways World School, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and GD Goenka World School towards Sohna Road are among the schools families in the northern sectors commonly consider. Each sets its own internal deadlines, reporting rhythm and house style for assignment feedback, and a tutor who has previously worked with students from a particular school tends to read that feedback faster.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Nothing here is endorsed by them, and no tutor should ever claim inside knowledge of a school marking policy.

What a tutor can do is work from the documents the school gives you: the task sheet, the criterion grid, the teacher comment. Those are enough to plan four weeks properly.

Pathways World School and Lancers International School on the Golf Course Road side

contentBlocks.heading: What Is Checked Before Any Tutor Name Reaches You
contentBlocks.body:
Screening reduces obvious risk. It does not certify brilliance, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. Two things get checked before a tutor is suggested.

The first is identity and background. Government photo identification, claimed qualifications seen as documents rather than described in a message, and the teaching history a tutor puts on record. Where a tutor says they have taught a particular programme, that claim should trace back to a school, a centre or a set of students.

The second is subject competence at the level requested. A degree in Mathematics does not by itself show that someone can teach Math AA HL to the top band, because the course has its own structure and its own examiner expectations. So subject discussion is level-specific and covers assessment mechanics: command terms, criterion wording, paper structure, what an examiner rewards in an evaluation question.

Parent feedback in the early weeks counts as evidence too. A tutor who is repeatedly late, or who cannot say what was covered in the last session, stops being recommended.

We publish no tutor counts and no success percentages, because no honest platform can verify them.

Teaching history recorded, not merely claimed
