AI HL: choosing the right model from a written context
Physics: sketch the situation before reaching for a formula
Chemistry: uncertainty analysis planned, not appended
Economics: diagram used inside the argument, not beside it

contentBlocks.heading: What a study week looks like across PYP, MYP and DP in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Each programme asks for a different weekly shape, and parents comparing notes across age groups often confuse the three.

A Primary Years Programme child needs frequency over length. Three short sessions of reading and number work beat one long Saturday block, because attention at that age is the limiting resource and inquiry collapses when a child is tired. Tutoring here should look like conversation and hands-on tasks. If it looks like a worksheet factory, the programme is being taught wrongly.

Middle Years Programme students need a repeating cycle: understand the concept, attempt the task, compare against the criterion strands, redo one section. The value is in that fourth step, which almost no student does voluntarily. Ages eleven to sixteen is also when self-management can be built without much resistance, and it becomes much harder later.

Diploma Programme students need a calendar more than they need extra teaching hours. Internal assessments across six subjects, the Extended Essay, TOK deadlines and past papers stack into the same weeks. Support aimed at the May 2026 or November 2026 session works when it front-loads the coursework so the final months can hold revision alone. Younger DP cohorts benefit from starting that mapping in DP1.

MYP: attempt, compare against strands, redo one section
DP: coursework front-loaded so revision months stay clear
Self-management is easiest to build between ages eleven and sixteen
EE and TOK deadlines mapped alongside IA dates

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 111 within the Dwarka Expressway belt of Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 111 falls in the northern band of Gurugram that grew along the Dwarka Expressway, a stretch of largely gated high-rise living where Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph and ATS Kocoon anchor the residential population. It is a young-family pocket, which is why demand here skews towards PYP and MYP support alongside the DP requests.

Distance behaves differently than parents expect. The Delhi border is close. Nirvana Country, South City 1, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 feel closer on a map than they do at 6 pm on a Wednesday, and Sector 50 or Sector 65 are a serious journey for a tutor who has already taught two sessions that day.

That has a direct effect on the study week. Because school buses run long routes out of this belt, a student often gets home later than a classmate living near campus. Planning a 6 pm session and a 10 pm bedtime for a Grade 6 child leaves very little room, and families who ignore that end up cancelling more sessions than they attend.

Weekend mornings are underused in this sector and often produce the steadiest attendance of the week.
items: High-rise pocket: Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph, ATS Kocoon
Younger family profile, so PYP and MYP demand runs high
Nirvana Country and DLF phases are nearer on paper than in traffic
Long bus routes shorten the usable weekday evening
Weekend morning slots hold attendance better than late weeknights

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing between a home slot and a screen in Sector 111 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring has one advantage that nothing replaces: a tutor sitting beside a student can see the exact moment the student stops following, before the student admits it. For younger learners and for anyone who drifts easily, that is worth a great deal.

It also has costs that families underweight. The session has to survive traffic, and the pool of tutors willing to travel this far north is smaller than the pool teaching around Golf Course Road or Sector 57. Insisting on home tutoring for a niche HL subject narrows the choice sharply, and the tutor you end up with may be the one who was available rather than the one who was right.

Online flips both. Wider choice, no travel loss, easier rescheduling when a school trip or a family visit disrupts the week. Screen-sharing a mark scheme against a student's script is genuinely better than crowding around one page. But it demands a student who will stay in the session, and a quiet corner in the flat.

Many Sector 111 families settle on a split: home tutoring for the younger child, online for the DP student. That is usually the correct answer rather than a compromise.
items: Home sessions catch the moment comprehension stops
Smaller travelling-tutor pool this far north
Online reschedules more easily around trips and school events
Screen-shared mark schemes beat a shared paper copy
Split arrangement across siblings is common and sensible

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars that shape a Sector 111 study week
contentBlocks.body:
Families in this sector send children across the wider Gurugram region rather than to a single nearby campus. Pathways World School sits in the Gurugram region, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57, and GD Goenka World School in the Sohna Road region. Those journeys are long enough to matter to any weekly plan.

The calendars matter just as much. Unit assessments, MYP interim reports, IA draft deadlines and mock exam blocks fall in clusters, and demand for specialist DP tutors rises steeply at those points. A family requesting a Chemistry HL tutor a fortnight before mocks will find fewer options than one asking in the quieter middle of a term.

There is a habit consequence too. Students who only study in the pressure weeks build a stop-start rhythm that produces exhausted cramming and shallow retention. The steadier pattern, two consistent sessions a week through the term, is less dramatic and considerably more effective.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Naming them here reflects where students in this pocket study, nothing more.
items: Pathways World School, Gurugram region
Lancers International School, Golf Course Road
Scottish High International School, Sector 57
GD Goenka World School, Sohna Road region
Specialist demand peaks around mocks and IA deadlines

contentBlocks.heading: The checks behind every name we send you
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist is only useful if the screening behind it is specific, so here is what is actually confirmed.

Level-specific teaching history. A tutor recommended for Physics HL has to demonstrate having taught Physics HL recently, including the internal assessment. A strong SL background does not automatically transfer, and pretending otherwise wastes a family's term.

Programme literacy. Tutors are asked how they would guide a student through a criterion strand, what they would change in a weak IA research question, and how they explain a command term such as evaluate to a student who keeps describing instead. Answers to those questions separate IB-experienced teachers from capable subject graduates very quickly.

Identity and background verification before any home session is scheduled. For a household in a Sector 111 tower, that check is not paperwork, it is a person entering your home.

Manner and clarity, judged on an unrehearsed explanation, then reassessed through what parents and students report after sessions begin.

No screening process catches everything, and this one does not claim to. It filters out the obvious mismatches and shifts the remaining judgement to where it belongs, which is the first few sessions with your own child.
items: Recent teaching history at the exact level requested
IA, criterion and command-term questions in screening
Identity and background confirmed before home visits
Unrehearsed explanation used to judge clarity
Continuing feedback from families after sessions start

contentBlocks.heading: Honest limits of what tutoring can shift
contentBlocks.body:
Tutoring changes technique, direction and confidence. It does not change a student's timetable, their sleep, or how much they want the subject, and the families who see the biggest gains are usually the ones who fix one of those alongside the sessions.

Starting late limits what is possible, and there is no way to phrase that kindly. A student beginning Chemistry HL support in February of the exam year can rebuild exam technique and target the highest-yield gaps. Rebuilding two years of shaky foundations in the same window is not realistic, and any tutor who promises otherwise is selling comfort. Nobody can guarantee a grade or a percentage improvement.

The reasonable expectation over four weeks is different and quite measurable. A student who can name what the last task lost marks for. Homework attempted before the worked solution is opened. Drafts started earlier than before. A revision method that is not re-reading.

If none of that appears after four weeks, the arrangement is not working, and the right response is a conversation rather than a wait-and-see. Ask for a different tutor or a different approach. That request is expected and carries no friction.
items: Technique and direction shift; motivation and timetable are yours
Late starts mean triage, not full reconstruction
No grade, score or percentage promises from anyone
Four-week markers: naming lost marks, earlier drafts, active recall
Raise a poor fit early rather than waiting for a report card

contentBlocks.heading: Booking IB tuition for a Sector 111 Gurugram student
contentBlocks.body:
Come to the first call with three things and the rest moves quickly. The subjects with their levels, the most recent piece of marked school work, and an honest description of when your child can actually sit down and concentrate.

That third item is the one families guess at, and guessing costs weeks. A slot that looks fine on paper but arrives after a two-hour bus ride and a swimming class will be missed by the third week, and everyone will blame the tutor.

An advisor will talk through whether the need is content, technique or routine, since the answer changes which tutor suits. Where home tutoring in Sector 111 is impractical for a particular subject, that will be said plainly and an online match proposed instead of a booking likely to unravel. Where a short block of focused work would serve better than an open-ended arrangement, that gets said too.

Shortlists follow the call. Availability can be reviewed and depends on tutor schedules, the level requested, and how far ahead of the May 2026 or November 2026 session you are working.
items: Bring subjects with levels and one marked assignment
Describe real concentration windows, not ideal ones
Advisor separates content gaps from routine problems
Short focused blocks offered where they fit better
Shortlist after the call, availability subject to schedules

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Grade 8 MYP student in Sector 111 really need?
faqs.answer: For one struggling subject, two sessions a week is the usual starting point, with a third only if an assessment block is approaching. More than that tends to backfire at this age, because the student stops doing independent work and starts waiting for the tutor to think for them. The MYP gains come from the redo cycle between sessions rather than from contact hours. If two well-used sessions plus honest independent attempts are not shifting anything after a month, the problem is the method, not the quantity.

faqs.question: My son studies for hours but his criterion scores stay flat. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always the studying is passive. Re-reading notes and highlighting feels productive and produces very little retrieval, which is the thing assessments actually test. The second common cause is that he understands the material but is not answering in the form the criterion asks for, so a strong explanation gets marked against a strand about analysis or evaluation. A tutor should be able to identify which of the two it is within one session by watching him attempt a question cold, without notes open beside him.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with planning and deadlines, or only with subject content?
faqs.answer: Both, and for Diploma students the planning half is often worth more. A tutor can map the internal assessment dates, Extended Essay checkpoints and TOK deadlines across the term, then work backwards to sensible draft dates. What a tutor should not do is manage the calendar on the student's behalf indefinitely, because self-management is part of what the programme is teaching. The reasonable goal is a student who maintains the plan themselves by the end of a term, with the tutor checking rather than driving.

faqs.question: What should a parent see after four weeks of tuition?
faqs.answer: Look for changes in behaviour before changes in marks, since marks lag by a reporting cycle. Your child should be able to say what the last assignment lost marks for in specific terms. Homework attempts should be starting before solutions are consulted. Drafts should be appearing earlier than they used to. There should be a plan your child can describe without being prompted. If none of that has appeared in four weeks, ask for a review of the approach or a different tutor rather than waiting for the next report.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring in the middle of DP1?
faqs.answer: No, and mid-DP1 is arguably the best point to start. There is still time to fix the study routine before the exam year, internal assessment work has usually begun so the tutor has real output to diagnose, and the subject choices have settled. Starting here also means coursework can be front-loaded, which protects the final months for revision. Starting in DP2 is still worthwhile, but the work shifts from building foundations to targeting the highest-yield weaknesses within a much tighter window.

faqs.question: Do tutors set homework on top of school work?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, but it should be small and targeted rather than an extra pile. A good tutor sets two or three problems that test the exact weakness discussed, or asks for a redrafted paragraph of a returned task, not a fresh chapter of exercises. If the additional work is regularly crowding out school assignments, tell the tutor. The point of between-session work is to force independent retrieval, and half an hour of the right questions does that better than two hours of the wrong ones.

faqs.question: How does the Extended Essay get supported without the tutor writing it?
faqs.answer: The support sits around the essay rather than inside it. A tutor can pressure-test the research question, check that the scope is narrow enough to be answerable in the word limit, discuss whether the sources will carry an argument, and read a draft to point out where the reasoning thins or the analysis becomes description. What they must not do is supply text, structure the argument for the student, or edit line by line. Your child's school supervisor sets the academic honesty expectations, and tutors work within them.

faqs.question: We travel often. Can sessions move around?
faqs.answer: Online sessions move easily, which is one reason travelling families in the Dwarka Expressway sectors lean that way. A session can run from a hotel room or a grandparent's house with no change to the arrangement. Home tutoring is less flexible, since a rescheduled slot has to fit around a tutor's other travel commitments across Gurugram, and repeated short-notice changes usually end the arrangement. If your calendar is genuinely unpredictable, say so at the start so the mode chosen suits the reality.

faqs.question: Why do rates differ between one tutor and another?
faqs.answer: Level and scarcity, mostly. A tutor who has taught Math AA HL for years and has marked internal assessments is scarcer than a tutor supporting Grade 6 numeracy, and that shows in the rate. Mode matters too, since a home session in Sector 111 carries travel time the tutor cannot use for teaching. Experience with a specific assessment, such as the Extended Essay or a science IA, also moves the figure. Rates are discussed on the advisor call against your actual requirement rather than quoted as one number.

h1: IB Tutors in Sector 112, Gurugram
heroSubtitle: Online tutoring gives a Sector 112 family access to subject specialists who would never drive up the Dwarka Expressway for a single session. It also asks more of the student. This page sets out both sides before you choose a mode.
introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 112 Gurugram work online across the city and, where schedules allow, at home near Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph and ATS Kocoon. Online sessions suit Diploma Programme specialists, past-paper work and families with unpredictable weeks. Home sessions suit younger PYP learners and students who lose focus on a screen. Coverage runs Grade 1 to Grade 12 across all three programmes, and the right mode is decided per child rather than as a policy.

contentBlocks.heading: What online IB tutoring does well for Sector 112 Gurugram families
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the honest case for the screen, because families in this part of Gurugram are often talked out of it for the wrong reasons.

The strongest argument is supply. Sector 112 sits well up the Dwarka Expressway, away from the older tutoring clusters. A tutor who specialises in Economics HL evaluation or Math AI HL modelling has a full week of teaching within a few kilometres of Golf Course Road and no reason to spend ninety minutes travelling here and back. Online, that same person will take a 8:30 pm slot without hesitation. The choice stops being about who is nearby and becomes about who is right.

The second argument is the work itself. Past-paper practice is better on a shared screen than on paper. A tutor can put a mark scheme beside a student's script, annotate both live, and the student keeps the annotated file afterwards. Trying to do that with two people leaning over a printout is genuinely worse.

The third is continuity. Sessions survive rain, a late school bus, a family trip and a tutor's own schedule change.

What online does not do is manufacture attention. That part is covered further down, without spin.
items: Access to level specialists who will not travel this far north
Annotated mark scheme and script side by side on one screen
Session files kept by the student after the call
Continuity through weather, traffic and travel
Attention remains the student's responsibility, not the platform's

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects transfer cleanly to a screen
contentBlocks.body:
Not every subject behaves the same way online, and it is worth knowing which is which before choosing.

Mathematics transfers extremely well. Working through a Math AA HL Paper 3 investigation or an AI HL modelling question is a matter of shared writing space, and a tablet with a stylus on the tutor's end reproduces a whiteboard closely. The exploration benefits too, since the tutor can comment directly in the student's document rather than describing changes verbally.

Economics is similarly comfortable. Diagram work is drawn live, and the 15-mark evaluation paragraphs that decide the grade are best coached by editing a real student paragraph on screen.

English A works well for the guided analysis and the individual oral, where a recorded practice run gives the student something to listen back to. That single feature is hard to reproduce at a dining table.

The sciences are more mixed. Physics and Chemistry theory and calculation work fine. The internal assessment planning works fine. What cannot happen online is standing beside a student at the bench, so IA data collection stays a school responsibility and the tutor works on design, uncertainty and evaluation around it. Support depends on level and schedule.
items: Math AA HL and AI HL: shared writing space works close to a whiteboard
Economics: live diagrams, edited evaluation paragraphs
English A: recorded oral practice the student can replay
Physics and Chemistry theory and IA design, but not bench work
Exploration and IA drafts commented on inside the document

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP on screen: where each one gains and loses
contentBlocks.body:
Age is the biggest variable in whether an online session is a good idea, more than subject and far more than technology.

Primary Years Programme children lose most on a screen. A six-year-old needs manipulatives, eye contact and someone who can redirect attention with a hand on a page. Short online sessions can work for a confident older primary child, particularly for reading practice, but for the youngest learners a home tutor is usually the better recommendation and we will say so rather than sell the convenient option.

Middle Years Programme students sit in the middle. They gain from screen-shared criterion strands and from seeing a task annotated against the descriptors. They lose if nobody is checking whether they are actually in the session, which is why a shared room rather than a bedroom matters at this age.

Diploma Programme students gain the most. The subject specialists they need are scarce, the work is document-based, and a DP2 student preparing for the May 2026 session benefits more from the right Chemistry HL tutor at 9 pm than from an average one at the table at 6 pm. November 2026 candidates follow the same pattern half a year later.
items: PYP ages three to twelve: home tutoring usually recommended
MYP ages eleven to sixteen: workable with a shared room, not a bedroom
DP ages sixteen to nineteen: online generally the stronger match
Criterion strands annotated live for MYP tasks
May 2026 and November 2026 revision runs well on screen

contentBlocks.heading: Online, home and hybrid across Sector 112 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Three arrangements are common here, and each suits a different household.

Fully online is the default for Diploma students and for any subject where the specialist pool is thin. It also suits families whose weeks change, since a slot can be moved without stranding a tutor mid-journey.

Fully at home suits younger children and students who genuinely cannot hold attention without a person in the room. Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and communities nearer to Sector 112, but it depends entirely on tutor schedules, and the further north the address, the shorter the list of tutors who can sustain it week after week. A tutor already teaching inside one of the Dwarka Expressway societies is the best case.

Hybrid is underrated. A weekend home session for the relationship and the harder conceptual teaching, midweek online sessions for problem practice and doubt-solving. Families with two children in different programmes often run this pattern with different tutors, which spreads the travel demand and keeps at least one arrangement stable when a week goes wrong.
items: Fully online: default for DP and scarce specialisms
Fully at home: younger children and attention-limited students
Hybrid: weekend at home, midweek online
Home availability shrinks as the address moves north
Tutors already teaching in the same society are the strongest home option

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 112 request becomes a shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
A request moves through a short sequence, and nothing is proposed before the first step is done properly.

An advisor speaks to you. The school, the programme year, the subjects with levels, the specific difficulty as the teacher described it, and your realistic weekly windows. If you are unsure whether the mode should be online or at home, that conversation settles it, using the age and subject logic set out above rather than a preference.

A shortlist is then built from tutors whose recent teaching matches the exact level. For an online match, the pool covers Gurugram and beyond. For a home match, it narrows to tutors who can sustain the journey, which is a real filter this far along the Expressway.

A first session follows, built around the student's own returned work. The tutor reports what the actual gap is and proposes a plan. Sometimes that report contradicts what the family assumed, and it is more useful when it does.

After a few weeks there is a review. If the fit is wrong, a different tutor is arranged. If the mode is wrong, the mode is changed, and a student who has drifted through four online sessions is moved to a home slot where one is available.
items: Advisor call decides mode as well as subject
Online pool is city-wide; home pool is filtered by travel
First session diagnostic, built on returned school work
Written plan shared with the parent
Mode and tutor both reviewable after the first weeks

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 112 and the northern Gurugram sectors around it
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 112 lies in the newer residential strip that developed along the Dwarka Expressway, with Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph and ATS Kocoon among the towers that most requests come from. The character is different from old Gurugram: fewer independent floors, more gated high-rise, and a resident population that skews towards families who moved in over the past decade.

The geography explains most of the tutoring pattern. Delhi is close, and several families here have a shorter run to South West Delhi than to Sohna Road. The established tutoring belt around DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, South City 1, Nirvana Country, Sector 50 and Sector 65 lies to the south and east, and every one of those is a proper journey during teaching hours.

There is a second-order effect worth naming. Because home tutoring is harder to arrange here, families sometimes accept whichever tutor can travel rather than the one suited to the level. That trade is usually a mistake for a Diploma subject. An online specialist beats a convenient generalist for HL work, and the convenience stops mattering by the second month.

For primary-age children the calculation reverses, and proximity wins.
items: Gated high-rise pocket along the Dwarka Expressway
Delhi border nearer than the Sohna Road belt
DLF phases, South City 1, Nirvana Country all a real drive away
Convenient generalist versus online specialist: level decides
Proximity matters most for primary-age learners

contentBlocks.heading: What is confirmed about a tutor before a session is booked
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is written out here in specifics, since a parent choosing online cannot rely on meeting someone at the door to form an impression.

Teaching history at the requested level is checked first. Physics HL means someone who has taught Physics HL and handled its internal assessment, not a graduate physicist willing to attempt it. The distinction decides whether a DP2 student gains anything in the months before an exam session.

Programme knowledge is probed with questions that cannot be bluffed: how they would tighten a weak IA research question, what they would tell a student who keeps describing when the command term says evaluate, how they explain a criterion strand to a Grade 8 student who has never read the descriptors.

Identity and background verification happens before any tutor is put forward, and before any home visit is arranged.

For online tutors, the practical setup is confirmed as well: a stable connection, a writing surface the student can actually read, and the habit of sending session notes afterwards. A brilliant teacher with an unreadable whiteboard is not a good online tutor.

The process reduces risk. It does not eliminate it, which is why the early review exists and why changing tutors is straightforward.
items: Level-specific teaching history, IA experience included
Unbluffable questions on command terms and criterion strands
Identity and background confirmed before any booking
Online setup checked: connection, writing surface, session notes
Early review because screening reduces risk rather than removing it

contentBlocks.heading: The Gurugram schools behind most Sector 112 requests
contentBlocks.body:
Children from this sector attend IB schools spread across the region rather than one nearby campus. Pathways World School is in the Gurugram region, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57, and GD Goenka World School in the Sohna Road region.

The distance has a specific consequence for mode choice. contentBlocks.heading: Where online tutoring falls short, and what to do about it
contentBlocks.body:
The case against the screen deserves the same space as the case for it.

Attention is the real problem. A teenager with a laptop has every distraction one keystroke away, and a tutor cannot see the second monitor or the phone below the desk. The fix is unglamorous: sessions in a shared room, phone left in another room, camera on. Families who apply those three rules rarely report the problem at all. Families who put the child in a bedroom with the door closed usually do.

Younger children are the second limitation, and it is not solvable by discipline. Attention span at that age is short and physical presence carries much of the teaching.

The third is that a tutor cannot read body language as completely on a screen. A good one compensates by asking the student to explain back rather than asking whether they understood, since students say yes to the second question almost automatically.

And no mode, online or at home, can promise a grade. What can be judged after four weeks is whether the student is attempting work independently, using assessment language, and starting drafts earlier. Those markers are visible to a parent without any report card.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a Grade 3 PYP child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it is rarely the first recommendation. Children of that age learn through handling things, through eye contact, and through an adult who can redirect attention physically. Twenty-minute online sessions focused on reading aloud or number talk can work with a parent sitting nearby for the first few weeks. Beyond that, a home tutor generally achieves more per hour. If home tutoring is impractical at your address, shorter and more frequent online sessions work better than one long one, and expectations should be adjusted accordingly.

faqs.question: What software or setup do we need at home in Sector 112?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect. A laptop or tablet with a working camera, a broadband connection that holds a video call, headphones, and a table in a shared part of the flat. A cheap graphics tablet helps for maths and sciences if your child writes a lot of working, though photographing a page and sharing it also works. The tutor supplies the shared whiteboard or document. No specialist software purchase is required, and any tutor asking you to buy a platform licence is worth questioning.

faqs.question: Are sessions recorded so my daughter can revise later?
faqs.answer: This depends on the individual tutor and is agreed with them at the start rather than assumed. Many are comfortable recording, and for past-paper walkthroughs a recording is genuinely useful because a student can replay the reasoning at their own speed. Others prefer to send written session notes and annotated files instead, which for most subjects covers the same ground more compactly. Ask during the first session. If replaying explanations matters to your child, make it part of the matching request so a suitable tutor is proposed.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor mark a Physics IA properly?
faqs.answer: Yes for everything except the bench work. Research question framing, variable control, the data table structure, uncertainty propagation, graphing choices and the evaluation section can all be worked through on a shared document, and comments sit directly against the text your daughter wrote. What cannot happen remotely is supervising the actual experiment, which is the school's responsibility in any case. The most common IA weakness is a thin evaluation written the night before submission, and that is entirely fixable online if the work starts early enough.

faqs.question: Which is cheaper, online or a tutor coming to Sobha City?
faqs.answer: Online is usually lower for the same subject and level, because a home session prices in travel time the tutor cannot spend teaching, and the journey to the Dwarka Expressway sectors is not short from most of Gurugram. The gap widens for high-demand Diploma subjects. It narrows or disappears if a tutor already teaches inside your society and has no real travel cost. Exact rates are discussed on the advisor call against your specific requirement rather than published as a flat figure.

faqs.question: Our internet drops during the evening. Is that a dealbreaker?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, though it needs planning rather than hoping. A mobile hotspot as a fallback handles most short outages, and audio with a shared document survives a weak connection far better than full video does. Tell the tutor at the start so the session structure allows for it, and agree what happens to a session cut short. If drops are frequent and long, a home tutor is the more sensible arrangement, and it is better to accept that at the beginning than after a month of interrupted sessions.

faqs.question: How do you keep a teenager off other tabs during a session?
faqs.answer: Honestly, the platform cannot, and any claim otherwise would be nonsense. What works is environmental. Run sessions in a shared room where a screen is visible from a doorway, keep the phone in another room, and have the camera on. Ask the tutor to make the student produce work during the session rather than watch. A student who is drifting shows it in the between-session work within a fortnight, and at that point the sensible response is a home slot rather than more rules.

faqs.question: Can we mix online weekday sessions with a home session on Saturday?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this hybrid pattern suits Sector 112 well. Weekend mornings avoid the traffic that makes weekday home sessions fragile this far north, so the in-person session is the one most likely to run reliably. Midweek online slots then cover problem practice and doubt-solving without adding a journey to anyone's evening. Whether the same tutor covers both depends on their schedule, and some families use one tutor for the weekend conceptual work and another for midweek subject practice.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor is genuinely an IB specialist and not just a good graduate?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions in the first session. Which levels of this subject have you taught in the last two years. What would you change about this internal assessment research question. What does this command term require that my child is not currently doing. Someone who has taught the programme answers all three immediately and with specifics. Someone who has not will talk about their subject knowledge instead. Screening covers this before a name reaches you, but your own five minutes of questions remain the best final check.

contentBlocks.heading: IB Tutors in Sector 113 Gurugram: This Week, This Month, This Term
contentBlocks.body:
Almost every parent who searches for IB tutors in Sector 113 Gurugram is working against a date. Sometimes it is Friday's unit test. Sometimes it is a first internal assessment draft due before the month closes. Sometimes it is the whole of DP1 stretching ahead with a quiet worry that the gap widens every week nothing changes.

Those three clocks need three different answers, and naming yours before you speak to anyone saves a great deal of time.

A this-week problem is narrow. One topic, one paper, one command term the student read as describe when the question wanted evaluate. You need a tutor who can start almost immediately and does not spend two sessions warming up. A this-month problem is usually structural: an IA research question that is far too broad, a chemistry lab report losing marks in evaluation every single time, an English A commentary that retells the passage instead of arguing about it. A this-term problem is different in kind. It is pacing, revision habit, and whether the higher level choice made last June still suits the student now.

IB Gram matches against the problem rather than the subject label on the timetable. The first conversation asks which clock you are watching, then narrows to tutors whose specialisation and open evenings genuinely fit. Travel on the Dwarka Expressway side of the city shapes what is possible at home, and we will say so plainly rather than promise a slot that cannot hold.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Support for Sector 113 Families
contentBlocks.body:
The three IB programmes ask for genuinely different teaching, and a tutor who is excellent at one may be wrong for another.

Primary Years Programme work, roughly ages three to twelve, is where families in the newer Sector 113 towers most often ask for reading fluency and number sense. The risk here is obvious and worth naming: turning inquiry learning into a worksheet factory because worksheets feel like progress. Good PYP tutoring keeps the questioning alive and builds the mechanics underneath it, so the child still reasons out loud rather than reciting.

Middle Years Programme students, ages eleven to sixteen, usually stumble on translation. They understand the science but write an answer that never touches the criterion the teacher is marking against. So MYP support tends to be part subject teaching, part decoding of criteria A to D and the language of the task sheet.

Diploma Programme students, ages sixteen to nineteen, carry a heavier and more specific load. Six subjects, higher and standard level split, internal assessments in most of them, an extended essay, theory of knowledge, and a calendar that does not move for anyone. Support here is subject specialist work plus a weekly plan that protects school deadlines instead of competing with them. A DP1 student in Sector 113 usually needs planning; a DP2 student in February usually needs past papers and triage.
items: PYP: reading, inquiry questioning, number sense without rote drilling
MYP: criterion A to D language, task sheet decoding, subject content
DP: HL and SL specialists, IA direction, EE mentoring, TOK
DP1 leans towards planning; DP2 leans towards past papers

Many still keep one foot in Delhi for work, and Noida or Faridabad appear on the weekend map more often than they do for a family settled in old Gurugram.

The practical consequence is distance. The established international school cluster and much of the experienced IB tutoring pool sit south and east of you, around Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and Sohna Road. On paper that is not far. On a weekday evening it can be a long, unpredictable run.

So a Sector 113 parent asking for IB home tuition should expect a smaller realistic pool than a parent in Nirvana Country or South City 1, and a wider one online. Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules, and a tutor already teaching in DLF Phase 4 or Sector 50 that evening is a very different proposition from one starting a fresh journey across the city.

We would rather tell you that upfront than discover it in week three.

contentBlocks.heading: The Sector 113 Subject Requests That Decide a Term
contentBlocks.body:
Requests from this part of Gurugram cluster tightly around a handful of subjects, and each fails in its own way.

Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at higher level is the most common. Students arrive comfortable with procedure and lose marks on proof, on modelling assumptions, and on Paper 3 style extended reasoning where the question keeps unfolding. Mathematics Applications and Interpretation at higher level fails elsewhere: the statistics and technology use are fine, the written interpretation of what a result actually means is thin.

Physics and Chemistry both punish the same habit. A student who can solve the numerical part but writes two lines under an evaluate command term will cap out, and the internal assessment magnifies it, because uncertainty handling and honest limitations carry real weight.

Economics is deceptively pleasant to read and hard to score in. Diagrams get drawn, evaluation gets skipped. English A trips students who write beautifully but summarise rather than analyse a passage.

A request for an IB maths tutor near Sector 113 therefore begins with a short diagnostic rather than a syllabus march. We look at a recent marked script if you have one. It usually shows within ten minutes whether the problem is content, technique, or exam behaviour, and those three need different tutors.

contentBlocks.heading: How a Shortlist Gets Built for a Sector 113 Address
contentBlocks.body:
The process is deliberately unglamorous, and it runs in a fixed order.

Step one is the intake call. We ask for programme, year, subject and level, the deadline you are working against, and the days and times that are genuinely free rather than theoretically free. Step two is the evidence. A recent marked script, a returned IA draft with teacher comments, or a report card tells us more than a description of the problem does, because parents and teachers often diagnose differently.

Step three is filtering. Subject and level first, then assessment experience, then the practical question of whether that tutor can reach your address at that hour or teaches online at that hour. Step four is the shortlist itself, which comes with what each tutor actually teaches and how they prefer to work. Step five is a first session, which should be diagnostic rather than a lecture. Step six, and this is the one families forget to ask about, is a check-in around the four week mark.

By four weeks you should be able to point at something concrete: a paper mark that moved, an IA section the teacher stopped commenting on, a student who now attempts the last question instead of leaving it. If nothing has moved, the honest response is to change the tutor or change the plan, and a request for IB tuition near Sector 113 can be reopened without a fuss.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Both for IB Tuition in Sector 113 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring in Gurugram is most practical when location and timing are realistic, and Sector 113 tests that sentence harder than most sectors do.

In person suits younger students, PYP and early MYP, where attention needs a person in the room and a parent nearby. It suits students who hide confusion well, because a tutor sitting beside them sees the pencil stop. It also suits families who want the routine of a fixed evening and a doorbell.

Online suits the opposite cases. A rare higher level combination, a specialist for extended essay mentoring, a late evening slot after an activity, or the February crunch before a May session when you want three short sessions a week rather than one long one. Screen sharing a past paper and annotating it live is genuinely good for exam technique. For an online tutor in Sector 113 Gurugram the search radius stops mattering, which is why the specialist match is usually stronger.

The honest limitation: online is weaker for a distractible young child, weaker when home internet is unreliable during evening peak, and weaker for a student who needs someone to physically slow their hand down during a proof.

Many families here end up hybrid. One in-person session a week for accountability, one or two online for drill and doubt-solving, and the balance reviewed after the first reporting cycle.

We can tell you that availability depends on level, subject and schedule, and that a request for a higher level specialist at seven in the evening on the Dwarka Expressway side may take longer to fill than the same request online.

And we can tell you when tutoring is the wrong tool. A DP2 student starting in March with three subjects unattended is in triage, not remediation, and pretending otherwise wastes your money and their remaining weeks.

contentBlocks.heading: The Checks Behind Every Sector 113 Tutor Recommendation
contentBlocks.body:
Before a profile is shown to a family, it goes through a set of checks that are boring by design.

Identity and contact details are confirmed. Academic background is reviewed against the subject and level being requested, which matters more in IB than in most systems, because teaching Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at higher level is not the same job as teaching it at standard level. Teaching history is discussed, with attention to which programme the tutor has actually worked in rather than which one they have read about.

Assessment familiarity is checked separately. Has this tutor supervised or supported internal assessments in this subject, and can they explain how a criterion is applied rather than describe it in general terms. For extended essay mentoring we look for someone who has seen drafts through supervision cycles.

Then the practical layer. Which areas the tutor realistically travels to on which days, whether their online setup works for annotating past papers, and whether their stated availability survives contact with a school calendar.

Parent feedback after the early sessions feeds back into future matching, and repeated concerns about punctuality, preparation or communication remove a tutor from recommendation. None of this makes anyone infallible. It does mean that when a name reaches your shortlist, someone has already asked the questions you would have asked in week two.

contentBlocks.heading: Start a Tutor Search for Sector 113 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Send the programme, the year group, the subjects and levels, and the two or three evenings that are actually free. Add the deadline if there is one, because a Friday test and a DP2 May session lead to very different shortlists.

An advisor will come back with tutors whose subject depth, assessment experience and availability fit, and will tell you honestly whether an in-person slot near Sobha City or the ATS communities looks realistic or whether online will get you a better specialist sooner. Matching is subject to tutor availability, and higher level or less common subjects can take longer to place.

If you have a recent marked script or an internal assessment draft with teacher comments, share it. The first session is far more useful when the tutor has already seen where the marks are actually going, and it saves you paying for an hour of introductions.

It also helps to say what you have already tried. A previous tutor who did not work, a peer group that fell away, a self-study plan that lasted two weeks: each of those tells us something about what to avoid this time.

One last practical point. Decide before you call how many hours a week your child can genuinely give without the schedule collapsing, and treat that number as a ceiling rather than a target. Families who book four sessions in a burst of resolve usually drop to one by the third week, and the stop-start pattern does more harm than a smaller plan held steadily.

faqs.question: Are IB home tutors actually available in Sector 113, or only online?
faqs.answer: Both are possible, but they are not equally easy. Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules, and Sector 113 sits further out along the Dwarka Expressway than most of that pool. An in-person match usually works when a tutor already teaches somewhere on that route. Online tutoring stays open across Gurugram for every supported IB subject and generally produces a stronger specialist match at short notice. faqs.question: How quickly can sessions start once I make contact?
faqs.answer: It depends on what you are asking for. A standard level subject at a mid-evening slot, taught online, can usually be arranged quickly. A higher level specialist at a specific hour, in person, on the Dwarka Expressway side of the city, takes longer because two constraints have to line up at once. During peak periods before the May and November sessions, experienced Diploma Programme tutors fill early. Availability is always subject to tutor schedules, so we would rather give you a realistic date than an optimistic one that slips.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1. Is it too early to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: DP1 is often the better time, not the early one. Internal assessments in most subjects begin taking shape during this year, and the difference between a research question that works and one that fights the student for six months is decided in a handful of early conversations. Starting in DP1 also leaves room for lighter, less anxious sessions. Compare that with a March start in DP2, where the honest plan becomes triage across papers rather than proper learning. Earlier support usually costs fewer hours overall.

faqs.question: What do IB tutoring fees in Gurugram depend on?
faqs.answer: Fees vary with programme, subject, level and format. Diploma Programme higher level sciences and mathematics sit at the upper end because the tutor pool is narrower. Primary Years support sits lower. In-person sessions cost more than online because travel time is real time, and a session that requires a long run to Sector 113 in evening traffic reflects that. Session length and frequency matter too. We share indicative ranges during the intake call before any introduction, so you are not comparing tutors without knowing what each will cost.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics and Chemistry at higher level?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being careful about it. There are tutors with genuine depth in both, particularly those who taught across a science department. There are also tutors comfortable in one and merely competent in the other, which shows up around internal assessment supervision and the harder end of Paper 2. For higher level in both, we usually check assessment experience separately for each subject before suggesting a single name. Two specialists often serve a Diploma Programme student better than one generalist, though it does complicate the weekly schedule.

faqs.question: What if my child does not get along with the tutor we choose?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than waiting for the term to end. Fit is not only academic: pace, tone, and how a tutor handles a wrong answer all matter, and a student who has gone quiet in sessions is telling you something. Let the advisor know what is not working, in specific terms if possible, and a different profile can be reviewed. Changing after two or three sessions is normal and costs far less than persisting for a term with someone the student has stopped talking to.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow our school's plan or their own?
faqs.answer: The school's plan comes first. Your child is assessed on their school's schedule, with their teacher's task sheets and their internal deadlines, so a tutor working to a separate syllabus creates conflict. Tutors work from the actual assignments, unit tests and internal assessment stages the school has set. Where a tutor sees a genuine gap, they will add practice around it rather than replace what the school is doing. Support for the extended essay and theory of knowledge also stays within the supervision boundaries the school has defined.

faqs.question: We moved to Sector 113 recently and my child changed schools mid-programme. Where do we begin?
faqs.answer: Begin with the differences rather than the subjects. Schools sequence Middle Years and Diploma units differently, so a transferring student often has genuine gaps in topics the new class covered last term and duplicated ground elsewhere. Send us the previous school's reports and any marked work alongside the new task sheets. A short diagnostic session usually maps the gaps faster than a month of general revision. Command term expectations and criterion wording can also differ in emphasis between schools, and that adjustment catches capable students more often than content does.

faqs.question: How will I know within a month whether this is working?
faqs.answer: Ask for something you can see. Not a feeling of confidence, but a marked paper, a returned draft, an IA section that stopped attracting the same teacher comment, or a student attempting the final question instead of skipping it. Agree at the first session what that evidence will be. At four weeks, look at it honestly. If nothing has moved and the student has been attending and working, the problem is the match or the plan, and both can be changed. Persisting without evidence is how families lose a term.

h1: IB Tutors in Sector 14 Gurugram: Support That Fits a School Night
heroSubtitle: The hardest part of arranging tuition in older Gurugram is rarely the subject. It is the hour. We start from the evening you actually have, then look for tutors whose subject depth, assessment experience and open slots line up with it, in person or online.
introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 14 Gurugram cover Grade 1 to Grade 12 across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes. IB Gram is an independent matching service, not a coaching centre, so the first thing an advisor asks about is your weekday timetable rather than a package. Home tuition around Sector 14 and the older Gurugram sectors depends on tutor travel and schedules. Online sessions run across the city and usually open up a wider choice of higher level subject specialists.

contentBlocks.heading: The Sector 14 Gurugram Evening Problem Nobody Plans For
contentBlocks.body:
Picture a Wednesday. The school bus turns into the sector at around a quarter to seven because the route home from the international school belt is long and the last stretch crawls. The bag lands in the hall. There is dinner, a shower, a football kit to hang up, and somewhere in there a chemistry internal assessment draft that the teacher wants on Monday.

The free window is about seventy minutes, and it is not the same seventy minutes every night.

That is the real constraint for most IB families in Sector 14, and it is the reason so many tuition arrangements quietly fall apart by the second month. The subject was matched. The hour was not. A tutor who can only offer six in the evening is useless to a household whose child is still on the road at that time, however good they are on Mathematics Analysis and Approaches.

So IB Gram begins from the timetable. Which evenings are genuinely usable, how long the child can concentrate after a full school day, whether the weekend carries more capacity than the week does. Only after that does the search narrow by subject, level and assessment experience. It is a less impressive opening question than most agencies ask. It is also the one that decides whether the arrangement is still standing in March.
items: Late bus arrivals shorten the usable weekday window
Evening capacity differs by day, not just by week
Timetable is matched before subject specialism
Grade 1 to Grade 12, PYP through Diploma Programme
Weekend blocks often carry the heavier work

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 14 and the Older Gurugram Sectors Around It
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 14 belongs to the earlier layer of the city. Independent houses and low-rise blocks rather than a single gated tower, a sector market people still walk to, and internal roads laid out long before the current traffic volumes existed. Palam Vihar and the neighbouring established HUDA sectors share that character, and it produces a tutoring pattern quite unlike the one you find in newer developments such as Sobha City or Puri Diplomatic Greens.

Two things follow from it.

First, the trip. Most of the experienced IB tutoring pool works around the newer school corridor to the south and east, near Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and Sohna Road. Home tutoring may be available across those areas and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules, so a Sector 14 request is asking someone to travel against the grain of their usual evening route.

Second, the mix. Households here often have one child in an IB school and a cousin or sibling in a board school, which means the family already has opinions about tutoring formed in a different system. Those opinions do not always transfer. Marks in an IB internal assessment do not respond to the volume of practice papers the way a board pre-board does, and that is worth knowing before you set expectations for a new tutor.

Older internal roads, sector market within walking distance
Tutor pool concentrated in the newer southern and eastern corridor

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing a Format That Survives a Sector 14 Weeknight
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring in Gurugram is most practical when location and timing are realistic. Sector 14 stretches that sentence, and the sensible response is to pick the format per session rather than per family.

A tutor in the room earns its cost when the student is young, when they go quiet instead of asking, or when handwriting and working out need to be watched rather than described. Primary Years and early Middle Years children usually do better face to face. So do students who have been drifting, because a person at the table removes the option of a browser tab.

Online earns its cost differently. It gives you a specialist for Mathematics Applications and Interpretation at higher level or for extended essay mentoring without asking anyone to cross the city at seven. It allows a twenty-five minute doubt-solving session on a Tuesday, which nobody would travel for. It also lets the session start eight minutes after the bag drops, and on a Wednesday evening in Sector 14 those eight minutes are not trivial.

Where online falls down is worth saying plainly. A restless nine-year-old, a shared study space with a television in it, or an unstable connection during evening peak will each undo the format. And a student who needs their hand physically slowed during algebra is better served in person.

Most families here settle on a mix and revise it after the first reporting cycle.

Online: rare higher level combinations, EE mentoring, short doubt sessions
Online removes the cross-city trip for both sides
Poor fit online: restless young learners, noisy shared rooms, weak evening bandwidth
Format reviewed after the first school report, not fixed forever

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Requests That Come From Sector 14 Households
contentBlocks.body:
The subject list from this part of the city is short and repeats itself, which tells you something about where IB actually hurts.

Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at higher level leads. The usual pattern is a student fluent in method who has never been taught to write a proof, or who treats a modelling question as an equation to solve rather than an assumption to justify. Mathematics Applications and Interpretation at higher level produces a different complaint: correct statistics, weak commentary on what the numbers imply.

Physics arrives most often in DP1, around the point where the mathematics inside the physics stops being optional. Chemistry arrives later and almost always attached to the internal assessment, because designing an investigation with a defensible variable and a real uncertainty discussion is a skill nobody teaches in a lesson.

Economics looks manageable until the evaluation marks go missing. English A trips confident writers who explain what the text says and forget to argue about how it works.

An IB science tutor in Sector 14 will usually ask for a marked script before the first session. Reading one is faster than any conversation, because it shows whether the loss is content, exam technique or the student simply running out of time in the last twenty minutes.
items: Math AA HL: proof writing and justified modelling assumptions
Math AI HL: interpretation of statistical results
Physics: the mathematics inside DP1 topics
Chemistry: investigation design and uncertainty in the IA
Economics and English A: evaluation and analysis, not description

contentBlocks.heading: From First Message to First Session for a Sector 14 Family
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is short, and every step exists because skipping it caused a problem for somebody earlier.

You send the programme, the year, the subjects with their levels, and the evenings that work. An advisor calls and asks for detail that a form cannot capture: how the child responds to being corrected, whether the difficulty is recent or long-standing, what the teacher wrote on the last report. Where possible we ask to see marked work, because a parent's account of the problem and the examiner's view of it are often two different problems.

Then filtering. Level and subject depth first. Assessment experience second, which for the Diploma Programme means internal assessment supervision and, where relevant, extended essay drafts. Availability and reachability third, since a name that cannot make Thursday at half past seven is not a candidate however strong the profile.

You receive a shortlist with what each tutor teaches and how they run a session, and you choose. The opening session should map the gap rather than deliver a lesson, and you should hear afterwards what the tutor found.

At about the one month mark, review it against something visible: a returned assignment, a paper score, a draft that came back with fewer structural comments. If there is nothing, we change the plan rather than defend it.

Advisor call goes beyond the form: history, temperament, teacher comments
Marked work reviewed wherever the family can share it
Filter order: subject depth, assessment experience, then availability
One month review against visible evidence

contentBlocks.heading: How PYP, MYP and DP Demands Shift Across a Gurugram School Career
contentBlocks.body:
Parents often ask for the same tutor to follow a child upwards. Occasionally that works. More often the three programmes reward different strengths in a teacher.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, the job is to protect curiosity while quietly fixing mechanics. A child who cannot read fluently will struggle with inquiry regardless of how interesting the unit is, so phonics, reading stamina and number facts still matter. What ruins PYP tutoring is drilling. If a session becomes a stack of worksheets, the child learns to produce answers without thinking, and the school will notice before you do.

The Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, is largely a translation problem. Students know more than their marks suggest and cannot express it in the shape the criteria demand. A capable MYP tutor spends real time on the task sheet itself, on what the criterion strands mean, and on the difference between describing and evaluating.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, is a workload problem wrapped around a content problem. Six subjects, internal assessments across most of them, an extended essay, theory of knowledge, and fixed school deadlines. Tutoring here has to sit inside the school calendar. Adding an ambitious parallel schedule in DP2 usually costs more than it returns.

MYP: criterion language, task sheets, describe versus evaluate
DP: six subjects, IAs, extended essay, theory of knowledge

contentBlocks.heading: IB Schools Sector 14 Students Travel Out To
contentBlocks.body:
Families in this sector generally send children out to the international schools clustered elsewhere in the city, including Pathways World School, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and GD Goenka World School towards Sohna Road. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. They are listed because they explain your commute, nothing more.

That outward journey has a cost the tutoring plan has to absorb.

A student leaving early and returning late has less discretionary time than the timetable suggests, and fatigue is not a moral failing. Two focused half-hour sessions in a week frequently beat one heroic two-hour block that ends with a child asleep over a past paper. Weekend mornings, before the day gets committed, tend to be the strongest slot available to Sector 14 households, and they suit internal assessment work particularly well because that work needs continuous thinking rather than short bursts.

School practice also varies. One school may run mock examinations early and set internal assessment deadlines well ahead of the official ones; another may leave more room and expect greater independence. Tutors work from your school's actual task sheets and dates rather than a generic scheme, so send those across at the start. It prevents the awkward situation where a tutor is teaching a unit the class finished a month ago.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Name Reaches a Sector 14 Family
contentBlocks.body:
Screening happens before you ever see a profile, and it is a series of ordinary questions asked properly.

Identity is confirmed and contact details are verified. Qualifications are reviewed against the specific subject and level, since a strong standard level mathematics tutor is not automatically a higher level one, and the Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation routes need separate confidence. Teaching history is discussed with attention to which IB programmes the person has genuinely worked inside.

Assessment familiarity is treated as its own question. Can this tutor explain how a criterion is applied to a real piece of student work. Have they seen internal assessment drafts through more than one cycle. Do they understand where a supervisor's help stops, which matters for academic honesty as much as for marks.

After that comes the practical screen. Which days and areas they can reach, whether their online setup handles live annotation of a past paper, and whether the availability they claim holds up against a school term rather than a quiet week in June.

Parent feedback in the early weeks feeds back into how a tutor is recommended afterwards. Repeated reports of lateness, thin preparation or poor communication take someone out of rotation. This does not make any tutor perfect. It does mean the obvious questions have been asked before you spend an evening asking them.

contentBlocks.heading: The Promises We Refuse to Make to Gurugram Families
contentBlocks.body:
A lot of tutoring marketing in this city is written to remove doubt. We would rather leave some of it in place, because the doubt is accurate.

Nobody can promise a grade. Not a 7, not a points total, not a percentage jump. The student's own work, the school's teaching, the subject combination, the examiner's paper on the day: none of that is under a tutor's control, and a service that quotes you a number is selling reassurance rather than teaching. We do not publish invented ratings, made-up reviews or student statistics either.

IB Gram has no affiliation with any school, with the International Baccalaureate Organization, or with any examining authority. It is a platform that matches families to independent tutors.

What is fair to describe is the method. How the intake conversation runs, what is checked before a recommendation, what an opening session should look like, and what evidence of progress you should be able to see within a month. Availability can be reviewed but never promised in advance, and it depends on subject, level and the hours you need.

And there is a point at which more tuition is the wrong answer. A student sleeping five hours and attending four sessions a week does not need a fifth. Sometimes the useful advice is to cut something, and we will give it.

contentBlocks.heading: Arrange IB Tuition for Sector 14 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the timetable. Send the days and hours that are realistically free, the year group, and the subjects with their levels. If there is a fixed date pressing on you, an internal assessment deadline, a mock, or a May session ahead, say so, because urgency changes which tutors are worth shortlisting.

An advisor will look at what is available for your part of older Gurugram and answer the awkward question directly: whether a tutor can reasonably reach Sector 14 at the hour you need, or whether online will give you a better subject specialist without the travel risk. Matching is subject to tutor availability, and less common higher level subjects take longer to arrange.

Send marked work if you have it. A returned paper with the examiner's or teacher's comments still on it is worth more than a long description of the difficulty, and it lets the first session begin with something concrete instead of introductions.

One caution before you book. Agree a weekly load the household can actually sustain through a busy term rather than the load that feels right in a worried week. Consistency over two months does more than intensity over two weeks, and it is easier to add a session later than to rescue a plan that collapsed.

Share marked work or a returned draft

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually travel to Sector 14, or should we assume online?
faqs.answer: Assume nothing until you ask, because it varies by day and by subject. Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules, and Sector 14 sits away from that main cluster. In-person matches do happen, usually with tutors who already have an earlier commitment in the same direction. Online is open across Gurugram for every supported subject and normally gives you more choice at the hour you need. The advisor will say which is likely for your request.

faqs.question: We have two children at different IB stages. Can one arrangement cover both?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, though it is worth thinking about carefully. A Middle Years child and a Diploma Programme sibling need different teaching, and the tutor who is right for a criterion-based science assignment is not automatically right for higher level Physics. What often works is scheduling both on the same evening with different tutors, or the same tutor across two adjacent slots if their subject range genuinely covers it. Tell the advisor about both children at intake. Planning it together from the start usually produces a tidier weekly schedule than adding the second child later.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in on the sessions?
faqs.answer: For younger Primary Years children, being nearby helps, particularly in the first few sessions while everyone settles. For Middle Years and Diploma students, sitting in usually backfires. Teenagers perform for an audience rather than admit confusion, and admitting confusion is the point of the hour. A better arrangement is a short update after the session, or a brief note on what was covered and what to practise. If you are worried about what is happening in the room, ask for that update in writing rather than staying in it.

faqs.question: Is group tuition cheaper and does it work for IB?
faqs.answer: Small groups can lower the cost per hour, and for shared content revision before a test they work reasonably well. The difficulty is that IB support is often individual by nature. An internal assessment has a specific research question, a specific data set and a specific supervisor comment, and none of that generalises to the student sitting next to them. Extended essay mentoring is individual by definition. Many families run group sessions for content revision and keep one-to-one time for assessment work. That split usually costs less than making everything individual.

faqs.question: Our child is switching from a board school to IB. How different is it really?
faqs.answer: Different enough to catch strong students. Board preparation rewards accurate recall and volume of practice; IB rewards structured argument, correct use of command terms, and work produced against published criteria. A student used to scoring on completeness may write a full, correct answer and still lose marks because the question asked them to evaluate. The first weeks are usually spent on assessment literacy rather than content: reading task sheets properly, understanding what each criterion strand wants, and learning that a shorter, sharper answer often scores higher.

faqs.question: What happens to tutoring during school holidays?
faqs.answer: Holidays are the most useful and most wasted weeks of the year. For Diploma Programme students they are the natural time to work on internal assessment drafts, read for an extended essay, or repair a topic that went badly in a unit test, because nothing else is competing for attention. For younger children a lighter schedule is usually wiser than an intensive one. contentBlocks.heading: What Sector 15 Gurugram Parents Type, and What Actually Moves the Mark
contentBlocks.body:
The search box gets one kind of request. The returned paper tells a different story.

Families looking for the best IB tutor in Sector 15 usually type a subject: maths, physics, economics. Reasonable, because a subject is what the report card names. But sit with a marked Diploma Programme script for ten minutes and the loss is rarely a gap in content. It is a question that asked the student to evaluate and got a description. It is an internal assessment that gathered good data and never argued about it. It is thirty-two minutes spent on the first long question, leaving the last one blank.

Those are not the same problem, and they do not need the same tutor.

A content gap needs teaching. A command term problem needs someone who will make the student rewrite three answers until the verb in the question controls the shape of the response. An exam pacing problem needs timed practice under a stopwatch and someone willing to be unpleasant about stopping. An internal assessment problem needs a tutor who has supervised drafts and knows where a supervisor's help must end.

So before anyone is recommended, IB Gram asks to see evidence. A returned paper, a draft with teacher comments, or the last report. The subject label is where the search starts. It is almost never where the answer sits.
items: Content gaps and technique gaps look identical on a report card
Command term misreading is the most common quiet cause
Exam pacing is trainable and often ignored
IA marks turn on argument, not on data collection
Evidence is read before a tutor is suggested

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 15 Request Becomes a Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Six steps, in this order, with nothing skipped for speed.

One. You send the year group, the subjects and levels, and the hours that genuinely exist in your week. Two. An advisor calls and asks what the paperwork cannot show: when the difficulty started, whether it appeared in one subject or spread, how the student reacts to correction, and what the school has said.

Three. Evidence. A returned assignment, a mock paper, an internal assessment draft with the supervisor's notes. This is the step families most want to skip and the one that changes the outcome most.

Four. Filtering. Subject and level depth first, then assessment experience appropriate to the diagnosis, then the practical question of availability at the hours you named. A tutor strong on higher level Chemistry content but with no internal assessment supervision behind them is the wrong pick if the internal assessment is the problem.

Five. A shortlist, with what each tutor teaches and how they run sessions, so you can choose rather than be assigned.

Six. An opening session that maps the gap and reports back on what it found.

A month later, you compare against the evidence you started with. Same subject, later paper, better or not. If not, the plan changes rather than continues.

Advisor call captures history and temperament
Returned work reviewed before filtering begins
Filter: depth, then assessment experience, then availability

contentBlocks.heading: Three IB Programmes, Three Different Jobs for a Gurugram Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Treating the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes as one continuum is a common and expensive mistake.

Primary Years work, spanning roughly ages three to twelve, asks a tutor to build fluency without flattening curiosity. Reading stamina, number sense, the confidence to say a wrong answer out loud. A child who has been trained to fill worksheets quietly will look compliant and learn less, and the school notices that pattern before the parent does.

Middle Years work, ages eleven to sixteen, is largely about assessment literacy. Students hold the ideas and lose the marks because the criterion wanted something specific and the answer wandered. Time spent on the task sheet and the criterion strands, unglamorous as it sounds, tends to shift grades faster than another chapter of content.

Diploma work, ages sixteen to nineteen, is where load and depth collide. Six subjects with higher and standard level splits, internal assessments across most of them, an extended essay, theory of knowledge, and a school calendar that does not negotiate. Planning for the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions has to begin well before the panic does, and younger Diploma cohorts benefit from mapping the year early rather than reacting to it.

The useful question is not who is a good tutor. It is who is a good tutor for this stage.
items: PYP: fluency and confidence, ages three to twelve
MYP: criterion strands and task sheet literacy, ages eleven to sixteen
DP: subject depth plus workload management, ages sixteen to nineteen
Assessment support spans IA, EE, TOK and past-paper revision
May 2026 and November 2026 planning starts early

contentBlocks.heading: Face to Face or Online for IB Tuition in Sector 15
contentBlocks.body:
Choose the format from the diagnosis rather than from habit.

If the trouble is attention, a person in the room wins. Younger learners, students who quietly disengage, and anyone who nods along without understanding are all better served by a tutor who can see the pencil stop moving. Home tuition also suits families who want a fixed rhythm to the week and a visible routine.

If the trouble is specialism, online usually wins. A higher level combination with a small teaching pool, extended essay mentoring in a narrow field, or theory of knowledge structuring does not care where the tutor sits. Online also permits short sessions. A twenty minute doubt-solving slot before a test is impossible to justify in person and easy to run on a screen.

If the trouble is exam technique, either works, provided the tutor insists on timed conditions.

The honest limits: online struggles with distractible young children, with a study space that is really the family living room, and with connections that wobble at evening peak. In-person options around Sector 15 and older Gurugram depend on tutor travel, since home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on schedules.
