contentBlocks.heading: The Subjects Behind Most Sector 15 Enquiries
contentBlocks.body:
Six subjects account for the majority of requests from this part of the city, and each fails in a recognisable way.

Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at higher level: students who compute confidently and cannot construct a proof, or who solve a modelling task without ever stating an assumption. The fix is writing practice, not more exercises.

Mathematics Applications and Interpretation at higher level: the calculation is right and the interpretation is a single flat sentence. Examiners want meaning attached to the number.

Physics: usually a mathematics problem wearing a physics uniform, most visible in DP1 when the algebra inside the topics stops being incidental.

Chemistry: the internal assessment dominates. Choosing a variable that can genuinely be controlled, then discussing uncertainty and limitations honestly, is where the marks concentrate.

Economics: diagrams drawn correctly, evaluation absent. The command word carries most of the difference between a middling and a strong answer.

English A: fluent writers who paraphrase the text rather than analyse how it produces its effect.

A request for an IB maths tutor near Sector 15 therefore begins with which of those failures is actually happening, because two students with the same grade in the same subject frequently need opposite kinds of help.
items: Math AA HL: proof construction and stated assumptions
Math AI HL: interpretation attached to the result
Physics: the algebra hidden inside DP1 topics
Chemistry: controllable variables, uncertainty, limitations
Economics and English A: evaluation and analysis over description

contentBlocks.heading: School Deadlines That Shape a Sector 15 Study Week
contentBlocks.body:
Students from this sector attend international schools spread across the city, among them Pathways World School, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and GD Goenka World School towards Sohna Road. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Their calendars matter here only because they set the pressure points.

Schools differ more than parents expect. One sets internal assessment checkpoints months ahead of the official submission and runs early mocks; another leaves the schedule looser and expects the student to self-manage. A tutor working from a generic plan will collide with either approach.

So the practical instruction is simple: send the school's task sheets, checkpoint dates and mock timetable at the start. Tutors then build around those dates instead of running a parallel syllabus that competes with them.

There is a further point about the commute. Students travelling from Sector 15 out to schools on the southern and eastern corridors lose real hours to the road, and the energy left in the evening is not what the timetable implies. Families who front-load heavier work onto Saturday mornings, keeping weekdays for short review and doubt-solving, generally sustain the plan longer than those who schedule two-hour weeknight sessions.

contentBlocks.body:
Sector 15 sits in the older, established part of the city: HUDA-era planning, houses and low blocks rather than a single large complex, a neighbourhood market people reach on foot, and roads that were laid for a much smaller Gurugram. Palam Vihar and the surrounding older sectors share that character, which is quite different from newer builds such as Sobha City or Puri Diplomatic Greens further north.

What that means for tutoring is a question of direction.

The deeper pool of experienced Diploma Programme tutors works around the southern and eastern belt, near Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and Sohna Road, alongside communities such as Nirvana Country, South City 1, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, Sector 50 and Sector 65. Some will. Many cannot without giving up an earlier session, and a tutor who agrees reluctantly tends to become the tutor who cancels in week five.

This section exists because the alternative is the standard tutoring page, and the standard tutoring page overstates.

We cannot promise a grade. Not a 7 in higher level Chemistry, not a points total, not a stated percentage gain. Too much of the outcome belongs to the student's own effort, the school's teaching, the subject combination and the paper that appears in the examination hall. We publish no invented ratings, no manufactured testimonials, and no statistics about past students. What we can be precise about is method: the questions the intake asks, what is checked before a name is put forward, how the opening session should run, and what visible evidence of progress ought to exist after four weeks. contentBlocks.heading: Vetting Carried Out Before a Sector 15 Introduction
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor passes through the same checks before their profile reaches a family, and they are deliberately mundane.

Identity is confirmed and contact details verified. Academic background is examined against the exact subject and level requested, which in IB means distinguishing between the Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation routes, and between higher and standard level, rather than accepting mathematics as a single competence.

Teaching history is reviewed for which programmes the person has actually worked in. Someone with years of board experience and one term of Middle Years exposure is a different proposition from someone who has taught the criteria for five years, and both may be right for different students.

Assessment familiarity is probed separately. Can they walk through how a criterion is applied to a real script. Have they seen internal assessment drafts across more than one cohort. Do they know where legitimate supervision stops, which is an academic honesty question before it is a marks question.

Then logistics: which areas and days they can realistically reach, and whether their online setup allows live annotation of a past paper rather than a static video call.

Parent feedback from early sessions informs later recommendations, and consistent complaints about preparation, punctuality or communication end a tutor's place in the pool.

contentBlocks.body:
Send four things and the first conversation will be worth having: the year group, the subjects with their levels, the hours in the week that are realistically free, and a piece of recent marked work.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to have taught at my child's own school?
faqs.answer: It helps occasionally and is rarely the deciding factor. What matters more is whether the tutor has taught the programme and the level, and whether they understand how the criteria or the examination papers work. School-specific knowledge is mostly about deadlines and teacher preferences, and you can supply both by sending the task sheets and the assessment calendar. A tutor who has supervised internal assessments across several schools often brings wider perspective than one who has only seen a single institution's habits. Ask about assessment experience rather than school names.

faqs.question: My child understands everything in class but blanks in tests. Can tutoring fix that?
faqs.answer: Often yes, though the work looks different from ordinary teaching. Understanding in class is recognition, and a test demands recall plus production under time pressure, which are separate skills. Sessions for this student focus on timed practice, on writing full answers without notes, and on the habit of reading the command word before starting. Marking their own work against a real scheme also helps, because it shows where an answer felt complete but was not. If anxiety is the main driver, the school counsellor may be more useful than extra hours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help improve a predicted grade before university applications?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help the student produce better work, and predicted grades follow from that. What a tutor cannot do is negotiate with the school or promise a particular prediction, since predictions rest on the teacher's judgement of internal evidence. The practical route is to strengthen the assessments the prediction draws on: mock papers, internal assessment drafts and classwork. Timing matters here more than intensity, because a prediction formed in one term is difficult to shift in the next. Starting earlier gives the evidence time to change.

faqs.question: How many hours a week is sensible for a Diploma Programme student?
faqs.answer: For one subject, one session a week with independent practice in between is usually enough. Two subjects can work at two sessions if the school load allows it. Beyond that, the constraint is not the tutor but the student's remaining time, since internal assessments, the extended essay and ordinary homework already consume the evenings. Families sometimes book heavily during an anxious week and then cancel steadily. A smaller schedule kept for three months does more than a large one abandoned in three weeks.

faqs.question: Do you offer trial sessions before we commit?
faqs.answer: The opening session functions as one, and it should be treated that way by both sides. It ought to be diagnostic: the tutor working out where the student actually loses marks, checking how they respond to correction, and forming a view on pace. Afterwards you should receive a summary of what was found and what the plan would be. If that summary is vague, that itself is information. Arrangements can be reviewed after the first session or two, and changing early costs far less than persisting out of politeness.

faqs.question: Is support available for language subjects and less common Diploma options?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and is worth asking about early rather than assuming. Widely taught options are generally easier to arrange than niche language or arts subjects, where the pool of tutors with real Diploma experience is small. For those, online matching is usually the only practical route, because restricting the search to tutors who can reach a specific address removes most of the candidates. Availability is subject to tutor schedules, and requests made close to an examination session have fewer options than earlier ones.

faqs.question: The school says my child does not need a tutor. Should we still arrange one?
faqs.answer: Take the school's view seriously and then look at the evidence yourself. Teachers see a full cohort and may be judging against the class average rather than your child's own trajectory. If recent papers show a steady position and the student is not distressed, extra hours may add pressure without adding marks. If the marks are drifting, or one specific assessment keeps returning with the same comment, that is worth addressing regardless of reassurance. The disagreement usually resolves once you both look at the same returned work.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a tuition centre and a matched private tutor?
faqs.answer: A centre offers a fixed timetable, a shared group and a set curriculum, which suits content revision and costs less per hour. A matched private tutor works to one student's diagnosis, which suits internal assessment supervision, extended essay mentoring and any problem specific to how that student writes or paces themselves. Searching for an IB tuition centre near Sector 15 and searching for a private tutor are really two different requests. Some families use both, keeping group sessions for content and individual time for assessment work.

faqs.question: If my child is retaking a subject in a November session, how does the plan change?
faqs.answer: A retake plan is narrower and more evidence-driven than first-time preparation. The starting point is the previous performance and, where available, the subject breakdown, since retake candidates usually lose marks in a consistent place rather than everywhere. Work concentrates on that pattern, on full timed papers, and on any internal assessment component being carried forward or resubmitted. Fewer months are available, so the schedule tends to be tighter from the outset. Tutor availability around examination periods is limited, which makes early planning more important than usual.

mainEntity.name: Does the tutor need to have taught at my child's own school?

acceptedAnswer.text: It helps occasionally and is rarely the deciding factor. What matters more is whether the tutor has taught the programme and the level, and whether they understand how the criteria or the examination papers work. School-specific knowledge is mostly about deadlines and teacher preferences, and you can supply both by sending the task sheets and the assessment calendar. A tutor who has supervised internal assessments across several schools often brings wider perspective than one who has only seen a single institution's habits. Ask about assessment experience rather than school names.

mainEntity.name: My child understands everything in class but blanks in tests. Can tutoring fix that?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes, though the work looks different from ordinary teaching. Understanding in class is recognition, and a test demands recall plus production under time pressure, which are separate skills. Sessions for this student focus on timed practice, on writing full answers without notes, and on the habit of reading the command word before starting. Marking their own work against a real scheme also helps, because it shows where an answer felt complete but was not. If anxiety is the main driver, the school counsellor may be more useful than extra hours.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help improve a predicted grade before university applications?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tutor can help the student produce better work, and predicted grades follow from that. What a tutor cannot do is negotiate with the school or promise a particular prediction, since predictions rest on the teacher's judgement of internal evidence. The practical route is to strengthen the assessments the prediction draws on: mock papers, internal assessment drafts and classwork. Timing matters here more than intensity, because a prediction formed in one term is difficult to shift in the next. Starting earlier gives the evidence time to change.

mainEntity.name: How many hours a week is sensible for a Diploma Programme student?

acceptedAnswer.text: For one subject, one session a week with independent practice in between is usually enough. Two subjects can work at two sessions if the school load allows it. Beyond that, the constraint is not the tutor but the student's remaining time, since internal assessments, the extended essay and ordinary homework already consume the evenings. Families sometimes book heavily during an anxious week and then cancel steadily. A smaller schedule kept for three months does more than a large one abandoned in three weeks.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer trial sessions before we commit?

acceptedAnswer.text: The opening session functions as one, and it should be treated that way by both sides. It ought to be diagnostic: the tutor working out where the student actually loses marks, checking how they respond to correction, and forming a view on pace. Afterwards you should receive a summary of what was found and what the plan would be. If that summary is vague, that itself is information. Arrangements can be reviewed after the first session or two, and changing early costs far less than persisting out of politeness.

mainEntity.name: Is support available for language subjects and less common Diploma options?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the subject and is worth asking about early rather than assuming. Widely taught options are generally easier to arrange than niche language or arts subjects, where the pool of tutors with real Diploma experience is small. For those, online matching is usually the only practical route, because restricting the search to tutors who can reach a specific address removes most of the candidates. Availability is subject to tutor schedules, and requests made close to an examination session have fewer options than earlier ones.

mainEntity.name: The school says my child does not need a tutor. Should we still arrange one?

acceptedAnswer.text: Take the school's view seriously and then look at the evidence yourself. Teachers see a full cohort and may be judging against the class average rather than your child's own trajectory. If recent papers show a steady position and the student is not distressed, extra hours may add pressure without adding marks. If the marks are drifting, or one specific assessment keeps returning with the same comment, that is worth addressing regardless of reassurance. The disagreement usually resolves once you both look at the same returned work.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tuition centre and a matched private tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: A centre offers a fixed timetable, a shared group and a set curriculum, which suits content revision and costs less per hour. A matched private tutor works to one student's diagnosis, which suits internal assessment supervision, extended essay mentoring and any problem specific to how that student writes or paces themselves. Searching for an IB tuition centre near Sector 15 and searching for a private tutor are really two different requests. Some families use both, keeping group sessions for content and individual time for assessment work.

mainEntity.name: If my child is retaking a subject in a November session, how does the plan change?

acceptedAnswer.text: A retake plan is narrower and more evidence-driven than first-time preparation. The starting point is the previous performance and, where available, the subject breakdown, since retake candidates usually lose marks in a consistent place rather than everywhere. Work concentrates on that pattern, on full timed papers, and on any internal assessment component being carried forward or resubmitted. Fewer months are available, so the schedule tends to be tighter from the outset. Tutor availability around examination periods is limited, which makes early planning more important than usual.

finalCta: Send the year group, the subjects and levels, your realistically free hours, and one piece of recent marked work. An advisor will read it, review options for Sector 15 and older Gurugram, and tell you whether an in-person slot is realistic or whether an online specialist will suit the student better.

contentBlocks.heading: What the IB Calendar Looks Like from Sector 21 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Ask a parent in Sector 21 what is due this term and the answer is usually approximate. The IB calendar is unforgiving about approximations. Internal assessment drafts, extended essay interim deadlines and TOK exhibition work all sit inside windows the school fixes months ahead of the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions, and no school moves them because a family began looking for a tutor late.

So the first useful question is not which tutor. It is what is due, and when.

IB Gram is an independent matching platform for families looking for IB tutors in Sector 21 Gurugram, covering Grade 1 to Grade 12 across the Primary Years Programme, Middle Years Programme and Diploma Programme. You describe the grade, the subjects and the deadlines already on the school calendar. We match that against tutors who have taught the specific level and the specific assessment type, rather than only the subject name.

A Grade 11 student who picked Math AA HL in October needs something different from a Grade 12 student sitting mocks in January. The first needs foundation work and a weekly habit. The second needs triage, deciding which topics are worth the hours that remain and which are not.

Starting late still helps. It simply buys narrower gains, and anyone who says otherwise is selling.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Choices That Decide Where a Sector 21 Student Needs Help
contentBlocks.body:
Most tutoring requests from this part of Gurugram cluster around six subjects: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A. The reasons differ enough that treating them as one request wastes everyone's time.

Math AA HL punishes students who were comfortable in MYP without ever becoming fluent in algebraic manipulation. The proof and calculus work in Paper 1 does not forgive weak foundations, and the repair is slow. Math AI HL is a different animal, heavier on modelling, data and interpretation, and a student who chose it expecting an easier route often struggles with the writing demands rather than the arithmetic.

Physics and Chemistry requests usually arrive in two forms. One is conceptual, where the student cannot connect a formula to a situation. The other is procedural, where the practical work and the IA write-up are the real problem and the theory is fine.

Economics tutoring lives or dies on command terms. Evaluate, examine and discuss carry different marks and different expectations, and students routinely lose points for describing when they were asked to judge.

English A support tends to be about structure and close reading rather than grammar, particularly for the individual oral and the Paper 2 comparison.
items: Math AA HL: algebra fluency, Paper 1 proof work
Math AI HL: modelling, data handling, written interpretation
Physics and Chemistry: concept gaps versus IA method
Economics: command terms and diagram accuracy
English A: individual oral, Paper 2 comparison

contentBlocks.heading: How a Shortlist Is Built for a Family in Sector 21 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The process is deliberately short, because parents in the middle of a term do not have a week to spend on it.

Step one is a requirement call or form. We ask for grade, programme, subjects and levels, the school's deadline calendar, preferred days and times, and whether you want home sessions in Sector 21 or online. If a recent report or a marked IA draft exists, that helps more than any description of the problem.

Step two is an internal match. Tutors are filtered by the level they have actually taught, the assessment component you need, and whether their schedule fits your slot. A tutor free at 4pm is no use to a student whose bus reaches home at 5.15pm.

Step three is a shortlist with an advisor call. You hear who is being suggested and why, including where the match is imperfect.

Step four is the first session, which is diagnostic rather than a sales pitch. The tutor works through recent school material to find where the understanding actually breaks.

Step five is a plan you can hold someone to: weekly focus, what is done in session, what is done alone.

Everything past step one depends on tutor availability for your subject and slot, and we would rather say so than promise a match that does not exist.

Recent report or marked draft, if available
Filtered match by level, component and schedule
Diagnostic first session
Weekly plan with a named focus

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Timelines Running Side by Side in Sector 21 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Families with two children often need two completely different kinds of help in the same house.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages roughly three to twelve, the useful work is reading stamina, number sense and the confidence to ask a question inside a unit of inquiry. Turning this into worksheet drilling is the common mistake, and it produces a child who is quicker at exercises and no better at thinking.

The Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, is where most parents first feel lost. Marks arrive against criteria A to D rather than as percentages, and a child can be strong on knowledge while losing marks on communication or on the reflection sections. Tutoring here is largely translation work: what does this criterion actually reward, and what separates an 8 from a 5.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, is a two-year machine with fixed parts. Six subjects, three at higher level, plus the extended essay, TOK and CAS. Tutoring usually starts with one subject and widens once the family sees how the hours behave.

Older DP cohorts near the May 2026 sitting need different planning from a Grade 11 group whose exams are still a year and a half away.
items: PYP: reading stamina, number sense, inquiry questions
MYP: criteria A to D, reflection and communication marks
DP: six subjects, three HL, plus EE, TOK and CAS

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Reaches Your Door
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is the part of a tutoring platform that is easiest to claim and hardest to see, so here is what it involves in practice.

Identity and background come first. Government photo identification, current address and contact details are collected and held on record. For any tutor travelling to a home, that record matters more than a polished profile page.

Qualifications are checked against the subject and level requested. A degree in mathematics is not automatically evidence of Math AA HL teaching. We look for where the person has taught IB specifically, which components they have handled, and whether they have marked work against IB criteria.

Subject knowledge is tested through a structured conversation rather than a certificate scan. A tutor is asked how they would open a topic with a struggling student, how they would approach an IA at draft stage, and what they would refuse to do for a student. Tutors who edit an IA rather than question it create an academic honesty problem for the family, and that answer tells you a great deal.

Professional conduct is monitored after matching. Punctuality, session notes and responsiveness are tracked, and repeated complaints end a listing.
items: Photo ID and address held on record
IB-specific teaching history, not general degrees
Component-level questioning at interview
Academic honesty expectations set upfront
Ongoing conduct monitoring after matching

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Home, Online or a Mix Through the Sector 21 Term
contentBlocks.body:
Mode is not a permanent decision. The sensible pattern changes as the term does.

Home tutoring earns its cost early in a course, with younger students, and with any child who quietly disengages the moment a screen is involved. A tutor at the table sees the notebook, the half-finished problem set and the body language. Home tutoring in Gurugram is most practical when location and timing are realistic, and Sector 21 is far enough from the main tutoring corridor that a 7pm start is easier to staff than a 5pm one.

Online tutoring is stronger than its reputation for exactly the cases parents worry about most. Past-paper work, worked solutions on a shared board, IA structure discussions and late-evening revision all transfer well. For rare subjects, higher level specialists or urgent DP revision, online usually produces a better match than insisting on someone who can drive to your sector.

A hybrid pattern suits many DP families: one home session a week for accountability, one online session for exam drilling, and a short online check-in during the fortnight before a deadline.

The honest trade-off is supervision. Online demands more from the student, and a Grade 8 child who needs someone watching will not thrive on it.
items: Home: younger students, early course, low self-supervision
Online: rare subjects, HL specialists, later slots
Hybrid: accountability plus exam drilling

Screen sessions need a quiet room, not a corridor

contentBlocks.heading: What Four Weeks of Tutoring Should Actually Show
contentBlocks.body:
Parents are often asked to judge tutoring by feel, which is unreliable. A month is enough time to see specific, checkable things, and if none of them appear then something is wrong with the match rather than with the child.

By the end of four weeks the student should be able to say what they are weak at in a sentence, without hedging. Vague answers usually mean the diagnosis never happened.

Homework behaviour should shift. Not necessarily more hours, but less avoidance and fewer blank starts on questions that used to stall them. School work should be arriving on time more often, because deadline management is part of the job.

There should be marked work in front of you. A past-paper question with the marks explained, an IA section with comments on structure rather than sentence polish, a set of practice problems with the errors sorted into types.

And there should be a plan you can read, not a promise you have to trust.

Grades often lag all of this by a full assessment cycle, so a month rarely moves a predicted grade. Anyone offering a guaranteed score is describing something the system does not permit.
items: Student can name their own weak areas
Less avoidance on question types that used to stall
Marked work with comments, not just ticks
A written weekly focus you can check
Grades usually lag by one assessment cycle

contentBlocks.heading: Starting the Conversation from Sector 21
contentBlocks.body:
The useful first message is short and specific: grade, subjects and levels, the next deadline on the school calendar, and whether you want a tutor at home in Sector 21 or online.

An advisor then calls to fill in the gaps, and a shortlist follows once tutors matching your subject, level and slot are identified. If nobody suitable is free for a home slot in your sector, we will say that and suggest online rather than send someone who cannot sustain the travel week after week.

Bring three things to that call if you can. The school's assessment calendar for the term, so the plan is built around real dates. The most recent marked work, even if it is only a class test, because a tutor learns more from five wrong answers than from a paragraph of description. And a realistic view of the family's evenings, including the days that are already taken by activities or a long commute home.

Parents often ask which subject to start with when two are struggling. The usual answer is the one with the nearest deadline, not the one with the lowest mark, because a deadline forces the work to become concrete quickly.

The first session is diagnostic. You should expect to hear, afterwards, exactly where the gap sits and what the next four weeks will do about it.

faqs.question: How late in the Diploma Programme can we start IB tuition and still see a difference?
faqs.answer: Later than most parents fear, but with narrower results. Starting in Grade 11 leaves room to fix foundations and shape the extended essay properly. Starting after mocks in Grade 12 is triage: a tutor picks the topics with the best mark return for the hours left, drills past papers, and tightens exam technique. That can move performance on specific papers. It rarely rebuilds two years of shaky groundwork before a May session, and a tutor who promises that is not being straight with you.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Year 4 and we live in Sector 21. Is that too early for subject tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is often the best moment. MYP Year 4 and 5 marks are given against criteria rather than percentages, and this is where students quietly develop habits that cost them later in the Diploma Programme, especially in mathematics and the sciences. Support at this stage is less about content and more about learning what each criterion rewards. It also means subject choices at the end of MYP get made from evidence rather than guesswork. Sessions here can be shorter and less frequent than DP tutoring.

faqs.question: Do you charge per session or per month, and what changes the fee?
faqs.answer: Fees are agreed with the tutor before sessions begin, and they vary rather than sitting at one published rate. The main factors are level, subject scarcity, mode and travel. Higher level Diploma subjects cost more than MYP support. A tutor travelling into Sector 21 from the Golf Course Road side prices that commute into the slot, which is one reason online sessions are usually lower. Frequency matters too, since a twice-weekly schedule is quoted differently from occasional doubt-solving.

faqs.question: Can a tutor actually travel to Sector 21 in the evening?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends heavily on the slot. Sector 21 sits away from the corridor where much of the senior IB tutoring experience is concentrated, so the evening run is real. Tutors who take it usually want a fixed weekly time rather than a slot that moves each week, and later starts are easier to staff than early ones. If nothing suitable is free for your subject and level, we will say so and suggest online rather than arranging travel that quietly collapses after three weeks.

faqs.question: What happens in the very first session?
faqs.answer: It is a diagnostic, not a lesson from page one of the syllabus. The tutor works through recent school material, a marked assignment or a past-paper question and watches where the student stalls. Expect questions about how the student revises, what they do when stuck, and how the school structures its deadlines. Afterwards you should get a plain summary: where the gap is, what the first four weeks will cover, and how much work sits outside the session. If that summary does not arrive, ask for it.

faqs.question: We want Math AA HL help before the May 2026 session. How many sessions a week is sensible?
faqs.answer: Two a week is the common pattern for a higher level mathematics student in the run-up to a May sitting, with one session on weak content and one on timed paper practice. Three can be justified during a short crisis period around mocks, though beyond that the limiting factor becomes independent practice rather than contact hours. One session a week works if the student is genuinely doing the set work between meetings. Availability at your preferred times will depend on tutor schedules.

faqs.question: If the tutor is not working out, how does a change happen?
faqs.answer: Tell the advisor, ideally with a specific reason rather than a general feeling. Pace, communication style, punctuality and depth of subject knowledge are all fixable by changing the match. A replacement is arranged where a suitable tutor is free for your subject, level and slot, and the incoming tutor gets the diagnostic notes so the student does not repeat the first fortnight. Some mismatches are solved without a change, by adjusting the session plan. Raise it in week two rather than week eight.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for Physics practicals and IA write-ups?
faqs.answer: For the write-up, yes, and often better than home sessions. IA work turns on method, uncertainty, data treatment and evaluation, all of which are discussed well over a shared screen with the draft open. The practical itself belongs to the school laboratory, and no tutor should be running your child's experiment. Online is weaker for early conceptual work with a younger student who drifts without someone physically present. That is a supervision problem rather than a subject problem, and it is worth being honest about.

faqs.question: What if there is no visible progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Raise it directly and ask for evidence rather than reassurance. A tutor should be able to show marked work, a list of topics covered and what changed in the student's approach. Marks themselves usually lag by a full assessment cycle, so a flat grade after four weeks is not proof of failure. Persistent vagueness is. If the notes are thin and the student still cannot name their weak areas, the match is wrong, and changing it early costs less than waiting for the next report.

The role is deliberately different from a school teacher's. contentBlocks.heading: What a Tutor Does That a Sector 22 Gurugram Classroom Cannot
contentBlocks.body:
A good IB subject teacher is doing something genuinely hard. Twenty or more students, a syllabus with fixed teaching hours, internal assessment supervision, reports, and a marking pile that has to come back to everyone at once. Inside that job there is very little room to stop for one student who did not follow the third step of a derivation in September.

That gap is the tutor's job. Not a second syllabus, and not a rival opinion on how to teach.

Parents in Sector 22 often arrive with a version of the same sentence: the school says he is capable, but the marks are not moving. Usually the teacher is right and the marks are right at the same time. The student understands the ideas in conversation and loses marks on execution, on structure, or on the specific thing the criterion asks for.

IB Gram matches families to tutors who have taught the exact level in question, then leaves the school's material at the centre of the sessions. Your child's worksheets, feedback sheets and drafts are the syllabus.

But a tutor cannot replace attendance or attention in class. When a student has stopped listening at school, tutoring becomes expensive damage control, and it is fairer to say so early.

Tutor: one student, one gap, flexible pace
School worksheets and feedback drive the sessions

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online and Hybrid Options for Sector 22 Gurugram Families
contentBlocks.body:
Three formats are possible, and each suits a different kind of student rather than a different kind of family.

At-home sessions put an adult beside the desk. For a Grade 6 or Grade 8 student, or a teenager who has learned to look busy, that physical presence does most of the work. Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules, and Sector 22 requests are handled the same way, slot by slot.

Online sessions suit the opposite profile: a motivated DP student who needs a specialist rather than a supervisor. Screen sharing is well suited to worked solutions, annotated past papers and reviewing an IA draft line by line with the marking criteria open alongside. Online tutoring remains available across Gurugram for all supported IB subjects, which widens the pool considerably for higher level sciences and mathematics.

Hybrid is the quiet favourite among Grade 11 and 12 families. One session in person each week to keep the relationship real, the rest online when a deadline bites.

Home tutoring here is most practical when location and timing are realistic. Ask about the tutor's travel time before agreeing a 5pm start, not after.

Online: specialist HL subjects, annotated past papers
Hybrid: one in-person anchor session per week
Travel time decides which evening slots are workable
Session length usually 60 to 90 minutes

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB Subject Marks Slip for Sector 22 Students
contentBlocks.body:
The subjects requested most often from this part of the city are Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A. The failure points are specific, and naming them saves a fortnight of guessing.

In Math AA HL, marks are usually lost in the middle of long questions rather than at the start. The student can begin, then loses the thread across a multi-part problem because the algebra is effortful instead of automatic. Math AI HL trips students on the modelling and the written justification, where a correct number without an interpretation earns very little.

Physics marks tend to disappear in the explain and deduce questions, where a formula is produced instead of an argument. Chemistry punishes students who memorise mechanisms without understanding energetics, and the IA suffers when the research question is too broad to control variables properly.

Economics answers fail on evaluation. A student who describes both sides and never reaches a supported judgement has written a good B and a poor A.

English A candidates often read well and write structurally weak essays, especially in the individual oral, where the extract must be tied to a global issue rather than summarised.

Math AI HL: interpretation of the model, not the number
Physics: explain and deduce command terms
Chemistry: IA research questions that are too broad
Economics: evaluation and supported judgement
English A: global issue framing in the individual oral

contentBlocks.heading: PYP to DP: Matching Support to the Stage Your Child Is In
contentBlocks.body:
The three programmes ask for different things from a tutor, and hiring the wrong kind of help is a common and expensive error.

A Primary Years Programme child, aged roughly three to twelve, needs someone patient enough to work through an inquiry without flattening it into an answer sheet. Reading fluency, number confidence and the willingness to say I do not understand are the real targets. A DP subject specialist is usually the wrong person for this.

Middle Years Programme students, aged eleven to sixteen, are marked against criteria A to D. The frequent complaint is that a strong answer received a 5, and the frequent cause is that the reflection or the communication strand was thin while the knowledge was fine. A tutor here spends real time on what the criterion wording actually demands.

Diploma Programme students, aged sixteen to nineteen, need subject depth first and organisation second. Six subjects with three at higher level, the extended essay, TOK and CAS, all running at once, and the failure mode is rarely a single hard topic. It is the collision of four deadlines in one fortnight during the run to the May 2026 or November 2026 sessions.
items: PYP: fluency, number confidence, inquiry habits
MYP: criterion wording, reflection and communication strands
DP: subject depth plus deadline collision management
Grade 1 to Grade 12 supported

contentBlocks.heading: From Enquiry to First Session for a Sector 22 Gurugram Family
contentBlocks.body:
Matching is a filtering exercise, and the quality of the filter depends almost entirely on what you tell us at the start.

The enquiry captures grade, programme, subject and level, the school, the days and times that are genuinely free, and whether you want someone at home in Sector 22 or online. Two extra details help more than parents expect: what the last teacher comment said, and what the student themselves thinks the problem is. Those two often disagree, and the disagreement is informative.

We then shortlist against teaching history at that level and component, not against a general subject label. Someone who has taught Chemistry SL for years is not automatically the right match for an HL student stuck on entropy.

An advisor talks you through the shortlist, including the compromises. Perhaps the strongest match is only free on Saturdays. Perhaps the tutor who fits your slot is stronger on Paper 2 than on the IA.

The opening session is spent finding the break point rather than teaching a set topic, and a short written summary follows it.

contentBlocks.heading: Judging a Tutor Without Waiting for the Report Card
contentBlocks.body:
School reports arrive too slowly to be a useful feedback loop for tutoring. By the time a grade shifts, a term has gone. So judge the process instead, using things you can observe from the next room.

Listen for question direction. In a productive session the student is asking as much as answering, and the tutor is often silent while the student works. A session that sounds like a lecture is usually one where the tutor is covering content rather than diagnosing.

Look at what the student writes during the hour. Worked attempts, corrections in a different colour, a short list of question types to redo. If the notebook after a session looks like a clean set of copied notes, very little has been tested.

Ask the student one question a week: what did you get wrong today, and why. A student who can answer that precisely is being taught well.

And check whether the tutor knows the school's next deadline without being reminded.

Nothing here predicts a final grade. No platform can promise a score, and the honest version of this page has to say that plainly.

The names that recur in enquiries include Pathways World School in the wider Gurugram region, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and GD Goenka World School towards the Sohna Road region.

What differs between them, from a tutoring point of view, is less the syllabus and more the internal machinery: how early the extended essay process begins, how much criterion detail comes back on a draft, how mocks are weighted, and whether the department runs its own revision sessions after school.

That last point changes the tutoring plan. A student already attending two school revision clinics a week does not need a third external session on the same content, and a tutor who suggests otherwise is padding.

contentBlocks.heading: The Checks Behind a Recommended Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Vetting has two purposes. One is safety, which matters most for home sessions. The other is competence at a specific level, which is where most tutoring disappointments actually originate.

On safety, government photo identification, a verified current address and working contact details are recorded before any home visit is arranged. Parents are entitled to ask what is on file, and the answer should not be evasive.

On competence, claimed qualifications are checked against the level being requested. Teaching experience is examined component by component. Someone may be excellent on Diploma Programme content and have never supervised an internal assessment, which is a fair thing for a family to know in advance rather than discover in November.

The interview is a subject conversation. Tutors are asked to explain a difficult idea aloud, to describe how they would respond to a student who has written a weak IA introduction, and to state where their own subject knowledge stops. Confident admission of a limit is a better signal than a claim to cover everything from PYP to HL.

After matching, punctuality, notes and parent feedback are monitored, and persistent problems remove a tutor from recommendation.
items: Photo ID and verified address before home visits
Level-by-level and component-by-component experience check
Live subject explanation at interview
Willingness to state the edge of their knowledge
Feedback monitored after the match is made

contentBlocks.heading: Booking an IB Tutor for Sector 22
contentBlocks.body:
Send four things and the first call becomes useful rather than exploratory: the grade and programme, the subjects with their levels, the school, and the times that are actually free once school buses and activities are accounted for.

Say plainly whether you want home sessions in Sector 22, online sessions, or a mix. If you are unsure, describe how your child studies alone, because that answer usually decides the format better than any preference.

An advisor will call, ask a few sharper questions, and come back with a shortlist where tutors matching that subject, level and slot are free. Where the match is thin, you will hear the trade-off rather than a reassurance. Some subjects at higher level are simply harder to staff on a weekday evening, and pretending otherwise wastes a month.

The opening session is used for diagnosis, and a written note follows it so you can see what the tutor found before committing to a longer schedule. From there the plan is reviewed roughly every four weeks against the school's own deadlines, and the frequency of sessions is adjusted rather than left running out of habit.

faqs.question: The school already offers extra help after class. Why would we add a tutor on top?
faqs.answer: Often you should not. If the department runs revision clinics and your child attends them, a third session on the same content adds hours without adding learning. Tutoring earns its place when the issue is individual: a gap from an earlier year, a writing problem the class pace cannot accommodate, or an internal assessment that needs sustained one-to-one attention. Compare what the school already provides against the specific difficulty before booking anything, and ask any tutor to explain what they will do differently.

faqs.question: Will a tutor's method clash with the way the school teaches the topic?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is worth heading off in the first session. A student who is shown two different notations for the same idea in the same week loses confidence rather than gaining insight. Tutors on the platform are asked to work from the school's material, follow the notation the teacher uses, and raise disagreements with the parent instead of the student. Bring the class notes to the opening session. Where a genuinely better method exists, it should be introduced only once the required one is secure.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's work against the IB criteria the way the school does?
faqs.answer: A tutor can apply the published criteria to practice work and explain the difference between mark bands, which is usually the most valuable hour of the week. What they cannot do is award anything official, moderate, or predict a final grade with authority. Only the school and the IB assessment process do that. There is also a boundary on internal assessment work: a tutor may question structure, method and clarity, but writing or rewriting sections of an IA would create an academic honesty problem for your child.

faqs.question: How do you match an English A tutor to a student who reads well but writes slowly?
faqs.answer: By treating it as a writing brief rather than a literature brief. The match looks for someone who teaches essay architecture, paragraph function and timed planning, not simply a strong reader of the set texts. In the opening session the tutor will usually ask the student to plan a Paper 2 response in ten minutes rather than write one, because planning speed is where the slowness normally starts. Progress here is measurable in structure and timing well before any mark changes.

faqs.question: Is group tuition available for Sector 22 families, or is it one-to-one only?
faqs.answer: Small groups are sometimes possible where two or three students are at the same level, in the same subject, and free at the same time. The saving on fees is real, but so is the cost: a group moves at the pace of its slowest member, and internal assessment work is difficult to run this way because each student's project is different. For content revision, a pair can work well. For an IA or an extended essay, one-to-one is the sensible arrangement.

faqs.question: How much extra homework will a tutor add on top of school work?
faqs.answer: Less than parents fear if the tutor is doing the job properly. The aim is to change how the existing school work is done rather than to pile on a parallel workload. A typical week might add one timed question set or a short redo of previously wrong problems, taking perhaps forty minutes. During a mock run or before an internal assessment deadline the load rises briefly. If a tutor is consistently adding hours without cutting anything, ask what they expect the student to stop doing.

faqs.question: Can the tutor's feedback be shared with my child's subject teacher?
faqs.answer: You can share it, and many families do, though it is your decision rather than the tutor's. Session notes describing which topics were weak and what has improved are usually welcomed by a teacher, particularly before a parent meeting. Keep it factual and avoid framing it as a correction of the school. Tutors on the platform do not contact schools directly and hold no relationship with them, since IB Gram is independent and not affiliated with any school unless specifically stated.

faqs.question: What sort of background do the IB tutors on this platform have?
faqs.answer: They come from a mix of routes: current and former IB subject teachers, examiners and moderators in some subjects, and specialists from university backgrounds who have taught the Diploma Programme for several years. What is checked is the same in each case, namely which levels and components they have actually taught, verified identity, and how they explain a difficult idea under questioning. Backgrounds vary enough that the useful question at shortlist stage is what a specific tutor has taught, not what the pool looks like overall.

faqs.question: My child is in a CBSE school in Sector 22 and moves to IB next year. Can tutoring bridge the gap?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the earlier it starts the less painful it is. The change is not mainly about content. It is about being marked on process, being expected to justify rather than recall, and having to write extended responses in subjects where a CBSE student is used to short answers. Bridging work usually covers criterion language, note-taking for concept-based lessons, and one subject in depth, most often mathematics. A few months before the switch is far better than the first reporting cycle after it.

contentBlocks.heading: The Travel Maths Behind IB Tutoring in Sector 23 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Work backwards from the clock and most tutoring decisions in this sector make themselves.

A school bus serving the international schools on the far side of the city often leaves before seven in the morning and drops back somewhere between half past four and half past five. Add a snack, a change of clothes and the slump that follows a nine-hour day, and the earliest honest start for a session is closer to six than to five. Now add the tutor's own journey across peak-hour Gurugram traffic. Those two numbers, not the syllabus, decide who can teach your child on a Tuesday.

Sector 23 sits among the established HUDA sectors on the Palam Vihar side, with the newer developments around Sobha City and Puri Diplomatic Greens on the Dwarka Expressway edge. The IB schools and much of the experienced tutoring supply sit south and east of that.

IB Gram takes the enquiry, tests it against real availability, and tells you which format actually holds. Sometimes a home tutor in Sector 23 is the right answer. Often, for a higher level subject on a weekday, an online specialist is the arrangement that survives past week three.

contentBlocks.heading: IB Subjects Sector 23 Families Ask About Most
contentBlocks.body:
Six subjects account for the bulk of enquiries: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A. Each carries a different kind of difficulty, and the useful conversation starts with which one you are actually facing.

With Math AA HL the problem is often speed under pressure. A student who can solve a problem in twenty unhurried minutes at home falls apart in a timed paper, and the remedy is sustained practice against the clock rather than more explanation.

Math AI HL asks students to build and defend a model. Those who came from a computational background find the writing uncomfortable, and the marks lost are in justification, not calculation.

Physics rewards students who can talk through a situation before touching a formula. Chemistry rewards precision in language, particularly around equilibrium and rates, where a slightly loose sentence loses the mark.

Economics needs current examples and diagram accuracy in equal measure. English A demands a defensible reading of a text rather than a summary of it, and the individual oral is where most students discover the difference.

Specialist availability varies by subject, and rarer higher level combinations are usually easier to staff online.

Math AI HL: defending the model in writing

Chemistry: precise language on equilibrium and rates
Economics: real examples plus accurate diagrams
English A: a defensible reading, not a summary

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Support by Programme, from PYP Reading to DP Papers
contentBlocks.body:
What a tutor should be doing changes completely across the three programmes, and hours spent on the wrong kind of help are hard to get back.

With Primary Years Programme children, aged around three to twelve, the target is confidence and fluency. Reading aloud, mental arithmetic that does not feel like a test, and the habit of asking why during a unit of inquiry. Sessions are short. Two thirty-minute sittings usually beat one long one at this age.

Middle Years Programme students, roughly eleven to sixteen, are being assessed against criteria A to D. Parents used to percentages find this opaque, and so do students. The tutoring work is to make the criterion wording concrete: what counts as analysis rather than description, and what an examiner expects in a reflection.

Diploma Programme students, sixteen to nineteen, carry six subjects with three at higher level, plus the extended essay, TOK and CAS. Support here is planned against dated commitments, with heavier work before the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions and lighter maintenance in between.

Younger DP cohorts benefit from starting earlier, when there is still room to change study habits rather than only content.

MYP: making criterion wording concrete
DP: work planned against dated commitments

Earlier start gives room to change habits

contentBlocks.heading: Weighing an Hour of Travel Against an Hour on Screen
contentBlocks.body:
Put the two formats side by side and the choice usually resolves itself within a minute.

A home session costs the tutor travel time in both directions, and that cost appears in the fee and in the fragility of the booking. What you get for it is presence. Nobody is checking a phone under the table, the tutor sees the handwriting and the crossed-out work, and a distracted younger child is kept on task without a parent hovering.

An online session costs nothing in travel and can start twenty minutes after the bus arrives. Past papers, annotated solutions, IA structure and revision planning all work well this way. For late slots, unusual subject combinations or a specialist at higher level, online is frequently the only route to a genuinely strong match from Sector 23.

Hybrid arrangements split the difference and tend to hold up best over a full term.

The real limitation of online is not the technology. It is a student who needs supervision to begin work, and no software fixes that. If your child abandons a difficult question the moment nobody is watching, book at home and accept the cost.

contentBlocks.heading: Who Is Standing at the Door: Tutor Checks Explained
contentBlocks.body:
A home booking means letting someone into your flat every week, so the checking process deserves a plain description rather than a badge on a profile.

Documented identity comes before anything else. Government photo identification, a current address that has been confirmed, and contact details on record. For home sessions in Sector 23 this record is the point of the whole exercise, and parents can ask what is held.

Teaching claims are then tested against the level requested. Having studied a subject at university is not evidence of having taught it at higher level, and having taught the Diploma Programme is not evidence of having guided an internal assessment through to submission. Those are separate skills and they are checked separately.

The interview is a working conversation rather than a formality. A tutor explains a topic aloud, describes how they would handle a student who has misunderstood something fundamental in Grade 9, and answers questions about academic honesty boundaries on coursework.

After a match begins, timekeeping and communication are tracked. A tutor who cancels repeatedly, whatever the reason, stops being recommended for that slot.

contentBlocks.heading: Honest Limits of What Tutoring Can Fix
contentBlocks.body:
Tutoring is a useful intervention with a defined reach, and a page that pretends otherwise is not worth reading.

What it does reliably: close identified gaps in content, teach exam technique, impose a weekly working rhythm, and give a student a place to be wrong without an audience. Those effects are visible within a month if the match is right.

What it does not do: replace classroom teaching, manufacture motivation in a student who does not want to be there, or compress two years of Diploma Programme content into six weeks. No tutor can promise a grade, and no platform should. The final mark is decided by the IB assessment process, not by the number of sessions bought.

There is also a limit around wellbeing. Some students underperforming in Grade 11 are not short of tuition, they are short of sleep, or carrying anxiety that the extra hours make worse. A tutor who notices this and says so is doing the job properly, even though it costs them the booking.

Fees, schedules and format can all be reviewed as the term changes.

faqs.question: Realistically, how long does a tutor take to reach Sector 23 in the evening?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on where they start. A tutor already in the older sectors or Palam Vihar side may be fifteen minutes away. Someone coming from the Golf Course Road or Sohna Road side during peak hours should be planning for a considerably longer run, which is why they will usually ask for a later start and a fixed weekly day. Before you agree a time, ask the tutor where they travel from. A booking that ignores this tends to unravel by the second month.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring cheaper than having a tutor come home in Sector 23?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, though the gap varies by subject and level. A home session prices in travel time that the tutor cannot spend teaching anyone else, and the further your sector sits from where they live, the more that shows up in the rate. Online removes that entirely, which also means more tutors are willing to take an awkward evening slot. Fees are agreed directly with the tutor before sessions start and depend on level, subject scarcity and how often you meet.

faqs.question: Can sessions be scheduled around a long school bus ride?
faqs.answer: That is the normal case here rather than an exception. Tell us the actual drop time and we treat everything before it as unavailable. Most students who travel a long way do better with a later weekday start and a longer weekend session than with an early evening slot they attend exhausted. Some families keep weekdays for short online reviews and put the substantial work on Saturday morning. Slot options depend on tutor availability, so the earlier you describe the timetable the better.

faqs.question: What happens to a home session if the tutor gets stuck in traffic?
faqs.answer: The expectation set with tutors is simple: message early, and offer either a shortened session, a switch to online for that day, or a rescheduled slot. Occasional delays happen in this city and are not a reason to change tutors. A pattern is different. If lateness repeats without warning, tell the advisor, because timekeeping is one of the things monitored after a match is made and it affects whether a tutor continues to be recommended for that area.

faqs.question: Do you cover Chemistry and Economics at higher level for students in this part of Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Both are among the subjects requested most often, alongside Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics and English A, and matches can be reviewed for higher level in each. What varies is the format. A higher level Chemistry specialist free at seven on a weekday evening is more likely to be available online than in person in Sector 23. If you need someone at home for these subjects, weekend slots widen the options considerably. Availability is confirmed on the advisor call rather than promised upfront.

faqs.question: Can we book weekend slots instead of weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Weekend mornings are often the strongest option for families in the older sectors. The student is rested, the traffic is lighter, and a ninety-minute session gets more done than two rushed weekday hours. The trade-off is spacing. One weekend session a week leaves a seven-day gap in which set work can quietly not happen, so it usually pairs well with a short midweek online check-in. Saturday demand is high, particularly before mocks, so it is worth asking early in the term.

faqs.question: How many students can share one home session?
faqs.answer: Two is workable when both are in the same subject and level and are genuinely close in ability. Three starts to become a class, and the pace settles on whoever is struggling most, which is unfair to the others. Sharing does reduce the cost per family and can make a longer trip viable for the tutor, so neighbours in the same sector sometimes arrange it together. Coursework is the exception. Internal assessment and extended essay work should be one-to-one, since each project is different.

faqs.question: What setup do we need at home for online IB tutoring to work properly?
faqs.answer: Less than people assume, but the basics matter. A stable connection, a laptop rather than a phone, a quiet room with a door, and a notebook the student writes in during the session rather than only watching. A graphics tablet helps in mathematics but is not essential, since photographing handwritten work and sharing it usually suffices. The setting matters more than the equipment. A student working at the dining table with the television audible will not concentrate, whatever the software is doing.

faqs.question: We may move from Sector 23 to another part of Gurugram mid-year. What happens to the tutoring?
faqs.answer: Tell the advisor as soon as the move is likely. If the sessions are online, nothing changes at all beyond the address on file. If a tutor is coming home, the new location may make their trip easier or impossible, and it is better to plan a handover during a quiet week than in the middle of a mock cycle. Where a change of tutor becomes necessary, the diagnostic notes and session records move across so the new match does not restart from the beginning.

introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 27 Gurugram are usually booked for one of four reasons: a Diploma subject that has slipped, an internal assessment with a school deadline, a Middle Years student who cannot decode criterion wording, or a primary child who needs steady reading and number work. Sector 27 sits close to Heritage City, DLF Richmond Park and the MG Road corridor, so both home visits and online sessions are workable. Before you book, know the grade, the subject level, and the deadline you are working against.

contentBlocks.heading: What to Establish Before You Book IB Tutors in Sector 27 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Start with a diagnostic question rather than a search: what exactly has gone wrong, and when did it start? A parent who can answer that gets a useful tutor in one round. A parent who cannot usually cycles through two or three before something sticks.

Most requests for IB tutors in Sector 27 Gurugram fall into a small number of shapes. A Grade 11 student took Math AA HL because the school counsellor suggested it and is now three topics behind. A Grade 9 student is writing well but scoring in the middle band because the criterion descriptors are being ignored. A Grade 4 child reads fluently and still stalls on word problems.

Each of those needs a different tutor. The Math AA HL case needs someone who has taught the current syllabus and can rebuild algebraic fluency without patronising a bright student. The Grade 9 case needs a tutor who marks against the criteria before praising the writing. The Grade 4 case needs patience and a slow build with real objects.

So before booking, write down three things: the grade, the subject and its level, and the nearest hard deadline. School report, IA draft date, mock week. That single line changes what a sensible shortlist should look like, and it saves an advisor twenty minutes of guessing.

Nearest hard deadline: IA draft, mock, report

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Requests We See From Sector 27 Families in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 27 requests cluster around six subjects, and each one fails differently.

Math AA HL is the most requested and the most misdiagnosed. Students rarely lose marks on the new higher level content. They lose them on Grade 9 and Grade 10 algebra that was never fully secured, which then resurfaces under time pressure in Paper 1. A tutor who starts by re-teaching calculus is treating the wrong thing.

Math AI HL is a different animal. It rewards modelling, interpretation and the ability to explain what a statistic means in context. Students who were strong in mechanical maths often struggle here because the questions are long and wordy.

Physics and Chemistry break at the practical end. The theory papers are manageable with steady work. The internal assessment is where students drift, because designing a defensible research question is a skill nobody explicitly taught them.

Economics is a marks-per-command-term subject. Evaluate, examine, discuss, distinguish. Students who write everything they know in an essay marked for evaluation come out mid-band and cannot understand why.

English A is the slowest to move. Reading response takes months, not weeks, and any tutor promising a quick jump on Paper 1 is selling something.

An IB maths tutor Sector 27 request and an IB science tutor Sector 27 request tend to arrive together, usually from the same Diploma cohort.
items: Math AA HL: algebra gaps surfacing under Paper 1 timing
Math AI HL: modelling and interpretation, not mechanics
Physics and Chemistry: IA research question design
Economics: command terms decide the band
English A: slow gains, no shortcuts

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: Which Stage Your Child Is Actually In
contentBlocks.body:
The three programmes need different things from a tutor, and parents often book help sized for the wrong one.

Primary Years work should look like conversation, manipulatives and reading aloud. Ages three to twelve. If a PYP session turns into a stack of worksheets, the tutor has misunderstood the programme and the child will resist within a fortnight.

Middle Years covers roughly ages eleven to sixteen and is where most confusion lives. Parents look at a report of 5s and 6s and cannot tell whether that is fine. The honest answer is that MYP grades describe performance against four criteria per subject, and a 5 in Criterion C can sit beside a 7 in Criterion A. A tutor worth booking will ask for the task sheet and the criterion descriptors before the first session.

The Diploma, ages sixteen to nineteen, is the pressure point. Six subjects, three at higher level, plus the extended essay, theory of knowledge and creativity, activity, service. For May 2026 candidates the useful window is already narrowing. November 2026 candidates still have room to plan properly.

Grade 1 to Grade 12 is covered, but the shape of help changes completely across that range. A parent booking for a Grade 3 child and a parent booking for a Grade 12 candidate are buying two unrelated services.
items: PYP: inquiry and reading, not worksheet stacks
MYP: four criteria per subject, read the descriptors
DP: six subjects, EE, TOK and CAS running at once
May 2026 candidates: planning window already tight
November 2026 candidates: room to build properly

contentBlocks.heading: Home Visits Around Heritage City Versus Online Sessions in Sector 27
contentBlocks.body:
The position of Sector 27 helps here. Heritage City, DLF Richmond Park and Unitech Heritage City sit within a short drive of MG Road and South City, so a tutor living anywhere along that central belt can reach a Sector 27 address without an hour in traffic. Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and Sohna Road as well, depending on tutor schedules.

The honest limitation: home visits get expensive in time. A tutor who crosses the city twice for a ninety-minute session will either charge for that or quietly stop being available. Local matches hold. Distant ones fray.

Online is stronger than most parents expect for Diploma subjects. Screen-shared past papers, annotated worked solutions and a shared document for IA drafts work better than a notebook passed back and forth. For Math AI HL and Economics in particular, an online match opens a wider specialist pool than what can physically arrive in Sector 27 on a Wednesday at seven.

Hybrid suits many families: one home session at the weekend for the harder teaching, one shorter online slot midweek for doubt-solving before a school submission.

Younger children usually do better in person. Under about Grade 6, attention on a screen is a real constraint, not a preference.

Online: wider specialist pool for HL and IA work
Hybrid: weekend teaching plus midweek doubt-solving
Under Grade 6: in person usually wins
Late evening slots: online is more reliable

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 27 Gurugram Tutor Request Turns Into a Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the sequence, in order.

One: you describe the need. Grade, subject, level, deadline, preferred mode, and the slot that actually works after school timings and activities. Two: an advisor reads it and asks the follow-up questions the form did not cover, usually about the school's internal deadlines and whether the subject is being taken at higher or standard level. Three: a shortlist is drawn from tutors whose IB experience matches that specific need, not just the subject name. Four: you speak to the tutor before committing. Five: a first session is scheduled, subject to tutor availability.

The first session is diagnostic, not a lesson. A good tutor spends it reading recent marked work, asking the student to talk through one problem out loud, and finding where the reasoning breaks. Parents sometimes feel this session was light. It is the session that determines whether the next twelve are aimed correctly.

Four weeks in, ask for something specific: which topics have been closed, what the student can now do unaided, and what remains open. If nobody can answer that, the match is wrong and should be changed. Changing a tutor early costs a fortnight. Staying with a poor fit for a term costs a grade band.

Requests for IB tuition near Sector 27 Gurugram usually move through this in a few days.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 27 Sits: South City, MG Road and the Sectors Next Door
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 27 sits in the older, central part of Gurugram, around Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park, with MG Road on one side and South City on the other. That matters practically. Families here are not on the newer Golf Course Extension corridor, so tutors coming from Sector 65 or Sohna Road face a longer and less predictable run in the evening peak.

Closer in, the useful neighbours are South City 1, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4. Nirvana Country, Sector 50 and Sector 65 are reachable but sit further out along the southern corridor. contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Sent to a Sector 27 Address

Screening is a filter, not a guarantee, and it is worth being precise about what it covers.

Identity is confirmed against government photo identification. Claimed qualifications are checked against documents rather than taken from a profile. IB teaching experience is probed specifically: which programme, which subjects, at which level, and over how many students. A tutor who has taught A Level Physics for a decade and one Diploma student is not the same as an experienced Diploma Physics tutor, and the profile should say which one you are getting.

Subject knowledge is tested with real tasks. For Math AA HL that means working through a Paper 1 question and explaining the method. For Economics it means marking a sample answer against the command term. For English A it means responding to an unseen passage.

What screening cannot tell you is whether this particular adult will get on with your particular teenager. That comes out in the first two sessions and nowhere earlier. So the practical safeguard is a short commitment at the start and a real conversation at the four-week mark.

Feedback from families is monitored, and tutors who are repeatedly unpunctual or who prepare thinly stop being recommended. No rating figures are published here, because a small number of comments dressed up as a score would mislead more than it informs.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IB tutor start in Sector 27 Gurugram?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the slot. Common Diploma subjects at standard evening times can usually be matched within a few days once the brief is clear. Higher level combinations, or a request for one specific weekday hour, take longer because the pool is smaller. Online matches move faster than home visits almost every time, since travel is removed from the equation.
