faqs.question: Is home tuition in Sector 27 more effective than online sessions?
faqs.answer: Neither is better in general; it depends on the age and the task. Children below roughly Grade 6 concentrate better with an adult in the room, so home sessions usually win there. Diploma students working through past papers and internal assessment drafts often do better online, because annotated documents and screen-shared solutions are easier to revisit than a notebook. Home visits also depend on someone being able to reach your address at the time you want. Many Sector 27 families settle on one home session at the weekend and a shorter online slot midweek.

faqs.question: What do IB tutors in Sector 27 charge?
faqs.answer: Fees vary with programme, level and mode, so no single figure would be truthful. Higher level Diploma subjects cost more per hour than Middle Years support, and home visits carry a travel component that online sessions do not. What you should ask before agreeing is the session length, how many sessions a week are being proposed, whether marked feedback between sessions is included, and the notice period for cancelling. Get those four answers in writing. A cheaper tutor who needs twice as many hours is not the cheaper option.

faqs.question: Our school in Gurugram already runs extra classes. Do we still need a tutor?
faqs.answer: School support and private tutoring do different jobs. A remedial class covers the gap the whole class shares, which is useful but not aimed at your child's specific break point. A tutor should start from your child's marked work and fix what is actually wrong there. If the school sessions are already producing visible improvement, wait. If a student has attended six weeks of extra classes and the same mistakes keep appearing in tests, that is the signal. Ask the subject teacher what they think the underlying gap is before you book anything.

faqs.question: Can we change the tutor if the first few sessions do not work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better to do it early than to wait politely. Say what is not working: pace, explanation style, punctuality, or simply that the student has not warmed up. An advisor can reissue a shortlist. Two sessions is usually enough to tell whether the teaching lands, and four weeks is enough to tell whether progress is real. Changing after a fortnight costs very little. Staying with a poor fit for a full term is the expensive mistake, particularly in a Diploma year where the calendar does not give the time back.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to arrange at short notice?
faqs.answer: The awkward ones are the smaller higher level options and second languages. Math AI HL, Economics HL and some language B combinations have fewer experienced Diploma teachers available in any one locality, so a home visit at a fixed weekday hour can be hard to arrange. Extended essay mentoring in a niche subject is similar. In those cases online matching is not a compromise, it is usually the only way to get someone who has actually taught the syllabus. Ask early rather than in the month before a submission deadline.

faqs.question: We live near Heritage City. Which nearby areas do tutors usually travel from?
faqs.answer: Tutors visiting the Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park side of Sector 27 usually come from the central belt: South City 1, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4 and the MG Road area. Golf Course Road and Sushant Lok are workable. Sector 65, Sohna Road and Nirvana Country are further out and become unreliable in evening traffic, so a tutor from there may prefer a weekend slot or an online arrangement. Say your exact block when you brief the advisor, because it changes which tutors can realistically commit.

faqs.question: What should we expect to see after four weeks?
faqs.answer: Ask for three specifics rather than a general impression. Which topics have been closed and can now be attempted unaided. What the student is still getting wrong and why the tutor thinks that is. What the plan for the next four weeks is. A tutor who can answer those clearly is doing the work even if marks have not moved yet, because marks lag understanding by several weeks. A tutor who answers with encouragement and nothing concrete is a problem regardless of how pleasant the sessions have been.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if my child sits the May 2026 exams?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the shape of help changes. With a few months to the May 2026 session, the useful work is past-paper technique, command-term discipline and closing the two or three topics that cost the most marks, not a full re-teach of the syllabus. Internal assessments should already be submitted or close to it. Be realistic about how many subjects can be rescued at once, because two is manageable and four is not. If the gap is very wide, a conversation with the school coordinator should come before booking hours.

contentBlocks.heading: The Assumption That Costs Sector 28 Gurugram Parents a Term
contentBlocks.body:
The assumption is this: that the IB is broadly like the board syllabus with more projects, so a good subject teacher will do. It is the single most expensive misunderstanding a parent can carry into a tutor search.

The IB assesses against criteria and command terms. A student can know the content and still land two bands lower because the answer did not do what the command term asked. Evaluate is not describe. Analyse is not explain. In the Middle Years Programme, four separate criteria are marked per subject, and a strong Criterion A does not compensate for a weak Criterion D.

A tutor who has never marked against those descriptors will teach the content, the student will feel more confident, and the report will not move. Parents then conclude that tuition does not work. What did not work was the match.

A second assumption is almost as common: that the problem is the current topic. Usually it sits two years upstream. Grade 11 Physics collapses because vector work from Grade 9 was never solid.

So when you look for IB tutors in Sector 28 Gurugram, ask what a tutor has marked, not only what they have taught. That one question filters a shortlist faster than any other.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Are Not Three Sizes of the Same Thing
contentBlocks.body:
Ages three to twelve, eleven to sixteen, sixteen to nineteen. The three programmes overlap in age and share almost nothing in method.

Primary Years teaching is inquiry-led. A tutor who arrives with a printed worksheet pack for a Grade 3 child is working against the school, and the child will notice before the parent does. Useful primary tutoring looks like reading together, talking about what was read, and building number sense through objects and conversation.

Middle Years is where the report card becomes confusing. Grades run one to seven, built from four criteria per subject, and a 5 can hide very different profiles. One student is strong on knowledge and weak on communication. Another is the reverse. The remedy differs entirely. Any Middle Years tutor should ask to see the actual task sheet and the criterion wording before planning anything.

Diploma students carry six subjects, three at higher level, an extended essay of four thousand words, theory of knowledge, and the creativity, activity, service requirement. Time, not ability, is the usual constraint. A Grade 11 student who is coping in October can be underwater by February simply because three internal assessment deadlines landed in the same month.

Support across Grade 1 to Grade 12 is possible, but be clear which of these three animals you are dealing with before you ask for hours.

contentBlocks.heading: Six IB Subjects Sector 28 Families Ask About Most
contentBlocks.body:
The six most requested here are Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A. Worth saying what each actually demands.

Math AA HL is proof-heavy and algebra-dependent. Students who arrive from a board background often have strong computation and weak justification, and Paper 1 punishes that without a calculator to hide behind.

Math AI HL asks for modelling and statistical interpretation in context. The mathematics is not simpler, it is differently shaped, and students who chose it expecting an easier route are the ones needing help by Grade 12.

Physics splits into theory and the internal assessment. Most students manage the theory with steady practice. The investigation, with its own research question and uncertainty analysis, is where good students lose marks they never expected to lose.

Chemistry has a similar shape, with the added problem that organic mechanisms reward pattern recognition that only comes from volume.

Economics lives or dies on diagrams and command terms. A correctly labelled diagram with a two-line explanation frequently outscores a page of undiagrammed prose.

English A moves slowly. Guided textual analysis improves over months of marked practice, which is why a parent booking six weeks before an exam should expect technique gains rather than a transformation. That is an honest limit, not a hedge.

Math AI HL: modelling in context, often chosen for the wrong reason
Physics and Chemistry IAs: uncertainty and research question
Economics: labelled diagrams outscore prose
English A: months, not weeks

contentBlocks.heading: From Enquiry to First Session for IB Tutors in Sector 28 Gurugram

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between a Home Tutor and an Online Tutor in Sector 28
contentBlocks.body:
The choice is usually decided by age and by what the session is for.

Home tutoring in Gurugram is most practical when location and timing are realistic. For a Sector 28 address that covers a fair number of tutors, since the central sectors are well placed. It stops being practical when a tutor is crossing the city at peak hour twice a week. Those arrangements quietly collapse after a month, usually through cancellations rather than a conversation.

Online has a genuine advantage for Diploma work. Past papers can be annotated live, a shared document lets a tutor comment on an internal assessment draft between sessions, and recordings mean a missed explanation is recoverable. For late evening slots, rare subjects or urgent revision before a mock, online is frequently the stronger match rather than the fallback.

Younger students are the reverse case. Below Grade 6, attention on a screen is a hard constraint. Sessions need to be shorter and a parent needs to be within earshot.

Many families run both: a longer home session at the weekend where new teaching happens, and a half-hour online check midweek for doubt-solving. IB home tuition Sector 28 Gurugram and online support are not competing choices, and treating them as one decision usually produces a worse timetable.

IB-specific experience, described precisely. Which programme, which subjects, which level, how long, and whether the work included marking against criteria or only teaching content. A tutor with strong subject knowledge and no criterion experience is still useful for a Middle Years content gap and is the wrong choice for a Diploma internal assessment.

Subject capability, tested live. A Diploma Chemistry candidate works through a past-paper question and explains the reasoning. An English A candidate responds to an unseen extract. Profiles are easy to write, and a marked task is harder to fake.

What none of this predicts is rapport. Screening produces a competent stranger, and whether that stranger works with your child shows up in session two. Keep the initial commitment short for exactly that reason, and say early if it is not landing.

faqs.question: Do IB tutors in Sector 28 Gurugram teach the same way as CBSE or ICSE tutors?
faqs.answer: Not usually, and that difference matters. Board teaching rewards accurate recall and well-practised question types. IB assessment rewards doing precisely what a command term asks, showing reasoning, and meeting criterion descriptors that are published in advance. A tutor who has only taught boards will often deliver excellent content and leave a student scoring in the same band as before. Ask any prospective tutor which IB programme they have taught, at what level, and whether they have marked work against the criteria. Their answer tells you more than a list of qualifications.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: Two hours a week per subject is a common starting point for a higher level Diploma subject, sometimes split into two shorter sessions rather than one long one. Standard level and Middle Years support often runs at one session a week. More is not automatically better. A student in tuition four evenings a week has no time left to attempt problems alone, and unsupported practice is where consolidation actually happens. Start lower than you think you need, review after a month, and add hours only where a specific gap justifies it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the extended essay and theory of knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a limit worth stating. Extended essay mentoring works best as structured supervision: narrowing the research question, checking the argument holds, reviewing referencing and helping with the reflection sessions. Theory of knowledge support usually means unpicking knowledge questions and building the exhibition or essay structure. What a tutor must not do is write or substantially rewrite any of it, because the work has to be the student's own and schools check. Availability for extended essay support in less common subjects is narrower, so ask early rather than close to a school deadline.

faqs.question: Our child is in MYP and the grades look fine. Is a tutor premature?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily premature, but check what the grades are made of first. A Middle Years 5 can come from strong knowledge and weak communication, or the reverse, and the two need entirely different help. Ask the subject teacher which criterion is dragging and look at the last two marked tasks against the descriptors. If one criterion is consistently low across subjects, that is a skill worth working on now, before the Diploma amplifies it. If the profile is even, the honest answer is that a tutor may not add much yet.

faqs.question: How is a fee decided, and what should be agreed before starting?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on programme, subject level, session length and whether the tutor travels. Higher level Diploma work sits at the top of the range and home visits carry a travel component. Before starting, agree four things in writing: the session length, the weekly frequency, whether marking and feedback between sessions is included, and the cancellation notice both sides will honour. Also agree how a change of tutor would be handled. Families who settle this at the outset rarely have an awkward conversation later, and the ones who skip it usually do.

faqs.question: Does a tutor from Delhi or Noida work for a Sector 28 address?
faqs.answer: For online sessions, distance is irrelevant and a Delhi or Noida tutor may be exactly the right specialist, particularly for a higher level subject with a small local pool. For home visits, be realistic. Weekend arrangements from Delhi are workable for some tutors. Regular weekday evening travel across the border is where commitments break down, and the failure mode is cancellations rather than a clear conversation. If home tutoring is essential, prioritise tutors already working in central Gurugram and the DLF phases, and treat anything further out as a bonus.

faqs.question: What happens in the very first session?
faqs.answer: It is a diagnostic rather than a lesson, and parents should expect it to feel unhurried. The tutor reads recent marked work, asks the student to talk aloud through one problem, and looks for where the reasoning breaks rather than where the answer went wrong. Some of it will look like conversation. By the end there should be a short plan: two or three things to fix first and roughly how long that will take. If the first session was pure syllabus coverage with no diagnosis, ask why.

faqs.question: Can we pause sessions during school exams or holidays?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, though it depends on the individual arrangement, so confirm it before the first session rather than after. Many families pause during school examination weeks and long holidays, and others increase frequency in the run-up to mocks. Give as much notice as you can, because a tutor holding a weekday evening slot may lose it to another family if it stays empty for a month. If the pause runs longer than a few weeks, expect a short re-diagnosis when sessions resume, since retention over a break varies more than parents anticipate.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is good but the marks still have not moved?
faqs.answer: Check the timeline first. Marks lag understanding, often by six to eight weeks, and school assessments may not yet have tested the topics that were repaired. Next, look at what is actually being submitted, because a student who understands the content but writes answers that ignore the command term will keep scoring the same. Then ask about work between sessions, since a tutor cannot substitute for independent practice. If all three check out and marks are still flat after two months, change the tutor rather than adding hours.

introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 29 Gurugram are most often booked after a mock result lands below the school's predicted grade. That gap has three usual causes: predictions built on coursework rather than timed papers, internal assessment marks that moderation later pulls down, and answers that ignore what the command term asked for. All three are diagnosable from a marked script. Sector 29 sits beside IFFCO Chowk and Leisure Valley in central Gurugram, so home visits and online sessions are both practical.

contentBlocks.heading: Predicted Grades and Final Grades: Where Sector 29 Gurugram Students Lose Points
contentBlocks.body:
Predicted grades are the school's estimate of where a student will finish. Final grades are what the examiners award. The gap between them is where most Diploma disappointment happens, and it is rarely caused by a lack of ability.

Three things usually create it. A predicted grade drawn from coursework and class tests, which measure a different skill from a timed Paper 2. Internal assessment marks that a school awards generously and moderation later pulls down. And a student who has been rewarded all year for effort, and has never had an answer marked strictly against a command term.

That gap is measurable and it is workable. Past papers marked by someone who knows the markscheme conventions will show it within two sessions. A student predicted a 6 who is writing responses at a 4 under timed conditions is not a mystery. That is a diagnosable problem with a normal remedy.

Families looking for IB tutors in Sector 29 Gurugram often arrive after a mock result has undercut the prediction. That is the right moment to act, not a reason to panic, provided the work that follows is about technique and marking as much as content.
items: Predicted grades measure coursework, papers measure timed reasoning
IA moderation can pull school marks down
Effort-rewarded feedback hides technique gaps
Timed marked papers expose the gap in two sessions
Mock results are the usual trigger for a search

contentBlocks.heading: Reaching a Sector 29 Address in Gurugram: IFFCO Chowk and Leisure Valley
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 29 sits on the IFFCO Chowk side of central Gurugram, next to Leisure Valley and a short distance from MG Road, with Sector 27 and Sector 28 as immediate neighbours. Access is good, which is genuinely useful for home tutoring, because the roads here are wide and a tutor on the metro corridor can arrive without depending on a car.

That last point is underrated. Tutors who travel by metro are far more punctual in October than tutors who drive from the far end of Golf Course Extension Road, and punctuality across a full term is worth more than a marginally better profile.

Nearby residential pockets that tutors commonly cover include South City 1, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4. Sushant Lok and Golf Course Road are close enough for regular weekday work. Sector 50, Sector 65 and Nirvana Country sit further along the southern corridor and suit weekend slots better.

Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and Sohna Road depending on tutor schedules. Online tutoring remains available across Gurugram for all supported IB subjects.

Tutors based in Delhi, Noida or Faridabad are practical online. Treat weekday home visits from those cities as unlikely rather than merely difficult.

Metro-corridor tutors stay more reliable across a term
South City 1 and the DLF phases within easy reach

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions in Sector 29 or Online: What Each One Is Good At
contentBlocks.body:
Each mode is good at something specific, and the useful question is what this particular student needs next.

Home sessions are good at attention. A tutor sitting at the table can see a student guessing, can stop them mid-line, and can insist that a problem is attempted before the method is shown. For a student who drifts, this is worth a great deal. Home tutoring in Gurugram is most practical when location and timing are realistic, and a Sector 29 address is one of the easier ones to serve.

Online is good at documents and repetition. Marking an internal assessment draft with comments in a shared file, working through a past paper with both people annotating the same page, replaying an explanation that did not land the first time. For students closing a predicted-versus-final gap, that document trail is the whole point.

Online is also the honest answer for late evening slots, urgent revision before a mock, and higher level subjects where the specialist pool in any one locality is thin.

The awkward case is the younger child. Below roughly Grade 6, screen sessions need to be shorter and supervised, and most families find in-person work better value.

A weekend home session with a midweek online review handles most Diploma cases without wrecking the week.

Online: shared annotation and a document trail
Online wins for late slots and thin specialist pools
Below Grade 6: shorter, supervised, in person

contentBlocks.heading: The Subjects Where Predictions and Results Diverge Most
contentBlocks.body:
Some subjects produce wider prediction gaps than others, and it is worth knowing which before choosing where to spend hours.

Math AA HL produces the widest. Class tests are topic-bounded and Paper 1 is not, so a student who can do every question when told which chapter it comes from will freeze when the same content arrives unlabelled. Mixed-topic timed practice is the specific remedy.

Math AI HL gaps come from writing. The mathematics is often correct and the interpretation sentence, which carries the marks, is missing or vague.

Physics and Chemistry gaps usually trace to the internal assessment and to extended response questions where reasoning must be shown step by step. Predicted grades built partly on generously marked school investigations can shift after moderation.

Economics has the most fixable gap of the six. Diagram accuracy and command-term discipline are teachable within weeks, and evaluation paragraphs follow a structure that can be practised.

English A has the narrowest room for a quick change. Predictions here are usually reliable, and a student a full band below their prediction is often making one repeatable structural error rather than lacking insight.

An IB maths tutor Sector 29 request and an IB science tutor Sector 29 request need different diagnostic work in the first session.

Math AI HL: the interpretation sentence carries the marks
Physics and Chemistry: moderation moves IA marks
Economics: diagram and command-term work pays quickly
English A: usually one repeatable structural error

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Shortlists IB Tutors in Sector 29 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Five steps, and the first is the one parents most often rush.

Write the brief properly. Grade, subject, level, current predicted grade if there is one, the most recent actual mark, and the next deadline. That last pair, prediction against reality, tells an advisor more than a paragraph of description.

An advisor then calls to establish what the numbers do not show: whether the student is struggling with content, timing or technique, and whether anything has already been tried.

A shortlist follows. Tutors are matched on demonstrated IB experience for that programme and level, and where the need is exam technique the match is weighted towards tutors with marking experience rather than teaching hours alone.

You speak to the shortlisted tutor before agreeing to anything. Nothing is booked over your head.

Sessions start subject to tutor availability, with a diagnostic first session where recent marked work is read and one problem is worked through aloud.

Then hold a four-week review. Ask what has closed, what is still open, and what would need to change for the distance between the prediction and the timed performance to narrow. If those answers are thin, replace the tutor. Waiting rarely improves a poor match.

Advisor call separates content, timing and technique problems
Marking experience weighted for exam-technique cases
Parent speaks to the tutor before any commitment
Four-week review measured against the original gap

contentBlocks.heading: From Primary Years Inquiry to a Diploma Timetable
contentBlocks.body:
Support runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, and the shape changes completely across that span.

Primary Years, ages three to twelve, should stay inquiry-led. Reading together, talking about the reading, building number sense through real objects. There is no predicted grade to chase here and no reason to invent pressure. A tutor who imports Diploma-style drilling into a Grade 2 session is doing damage that takes a year to undo.

Middle Years, ages eleven to sixteen, is where the habits that later cause prediction gaps are formed. Four criteria are marked per subject, and students who never read the descriptors learn to write what feels thorough rather than what is being assessed. Fixing that at Grade 8 is straightforward. Fixing it at Grade 12 is not.

The Diploma, ages sixteen to nineteen, runs six subjects with three at higher level, alongside the extended essay, theory of knowledge and creativity, activity, service. Support covers internal assessment structure, extended essay mentoring, theory of knowledge, past-paper revision, school assignment review and exam planning.

May 2026 candidates are inside the working window now. November 2026 candidates can still build in the right order, which is a real advantage and one that families rarely use fully.
items: PYP: inquiry, reading, number sense, no manufactured pressure
MYP: criterion habits formed here decide DP outcomes
DP: IA, EE, TOK, past papers and exam planning
May 2026: a working window, not a planning window
November 2026: room to build in the right order

contentBlocks.heading: The Limits of What Tutoring Can Do
contentBlocks.body:
A page about closing the distance between a prediction and a result should be clear about what cannot be promised.

No grade is guaranteed. Not a 7, not a total, not a percentage lift. A tutor controls the quality of teaching and the accuracy of feedback. The student controls the hours of independent practice, and the examiner controls the paper. Anyone offering a guaranteed outcome is ignoring two of those three.

No tutor numbers are quoted, and no ratings or testimonials are published.

No affiliation with any school is claimed.

Availability is described conditionally because it is conditional. A specific higher level subject at a specific hour can be reviewed, and often arranged, but stating it as fact before checking would be a sales line.

Two honest limitations follow. Starting late constrains what is possible: six weeks before a session, the realistic aim is protecting the marks a student can already earn, not adding a band. And in a small number of cases the right recommendation is fewer subjects rather than more tutoring, which is a conversation for the school coordinator.

An advisor who says any of this to you is being useful. One who agrees to everything is selling hours.

faqs.question: Why is my child's predicted grade higher than their mock result?
faqs.answer: Usually because the two measure different things. A prediction leans on coursework, class tests and internal assessment marks, all completed with time, notes and often a second attempt. A mock is a timed, mixed-topic paper marked to examiner conventions. A student who understands the content but works slowly, or who answers a describe question when the paper asked them to evaluate, will score lower under those conditions. The gap is diagnosable from the script itself, and in most cases it points at technique and timing rather than knowledge.

faqs.question: Can an IB tutor in Sector 29 Gurugram help before the May 2026 session?
faqs.answer: Yes, though the plan should look different from one built a year out. With months rather than terms remaining, the work is timed past-paper practice, command-term discipline, and closing the two or three topics that cost the most marks across Paper 1 and Paper 2. A full re-teach is not realistic and should not be attempted. Internal assessments ought to be finished or nearly so by this point. Be selective about subjects, because concentrated work on two is far more likely to move results than thin attention spread across four.

faqs.question: How long before we see a change in marks?
faqs.answer: Understanding usually shifts within three or four sessions. Marks follow later, often six to eight weeks later, because school assessments have to come round to the repaired topics before anything shows on paper. This lag catches parents out and causes tutors to be changed just as the work starts landing. The better early indicator is whether the student can now attempt a question type unaided that they could not attempt a month ago. Ask for that specifically at the four-week review rather than waiting for the next report card.

faqs.question: Do you help with internal assessment moderation issues?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help a student write an internal assessment that holds up under moderation, which mostly means a defensible research question, honest data handling, clear analysis and proper evaluation of limitations. What a tutor cannot do is contest a moderation outcome or rewrite the work, since the school owns the submission process and the work must be the student's own. mainEntity.name: Why is my child's predicted grade higher than their mock result?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually because the two measure different things. A prediction leans on coursework, class tests and internal assessment marks, all completed with time, notes and often a second attempt. A mock is a timed, mixed-topic paper marked to examiner conventions. A student who understands the content but works slowly, or who answers a describe question when the paper asked them to evaluate, will score lower under those conditions. The gap is diagnosable from the script itself, and in most cases it points at technique and timing rather than knowledge.

mainEntity.name: Can an IB tutor in Sector 29 Gurugram help before the May 2026 session?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, though the plan should look different from one built a year out. With months rather than terms remaining, the work is timed past-paper practice, command-term discipline, and closing the two or three topics that cost the most marks across Paper 1 and Paper 2. A full re-teach is not realistic and should not be attempted. Internal assessments ought to be finished or nearly so by this point. Be selective about subjects, because concentrated work on two is far more likely to move results than thin attention spread across four.

The better early indicator is whether the student can now attempt a question type unaided that they could not attempt a month ago. Ask for that specifically at the four-week review rather than waiting for the next report card.

h1: IB Tutors in Sector 30 Gurugram for PYP, MYP and DP Students
heroSubtitle: Sector 30 sits in the central belt near MG Road, South City and Heritage City, which keeps travel times sane for home sessions. IB Gram helps you compare a short list of tutors on assessment knowledge, availability and teaching style before you commit to a full term.
introSummary: Most parents looking for IB tutors in Sector 30 Gurugram end up holding two or three names with no reliable way to tell them apart. This page gives you the comparison method: what to ask on the first call, what a trial session should show, and what an IB specialist does differently from a strong general tutor. Sector 30 sits close to MG Road, South City and the Heritage City pocket, so home visits and online sessions are both realistic here. The choice between them matters more than most families expect.

contentBlocks.heading: Shortlisting IB tutors in Sector 30 Gurugram without guesswork
contentBlocks.body:
Two tutors can both teach Physics HL and be nothing alike in practice. One has taught the current syllabus through several May sessions and can tell you inside ten minutes which paper your child is losing marks on. The other is a capable graduate who explains clearly but has never marked a script against IB criteria. Both sound convincing on a first call.

So the useful question is not who is free on Tuesday evenings. It is what you compare them on. Ask each tutor to look at one recent piece of marked school work and say what they would do first. The answers separate fast. A tutor who talks about command terms, criterion descriptors and where the marks actually sit is reading the assessment. A tutor who talks only about more practice and more revision is working from instinct, which is not the same thing.

Sector 30 makes the comparison easier than some parts of the city. The address sits in the central belt near MG Road and South City, close to Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park, so a tutor travelling in from DLF Phase 1 or South City 1 is not signing up for a forty minute crawl in each direction. That widens the pool you can realistically draw from.

A wider pool only helps if you know how to cut it down. Give yourself two sessions to do it.
items: Ask for a read of one marked script, not a generic study plan
Listen for criteria and command terms, not just topic names
Travel time from DLF Phase 1, South City 1 and Sector 50
Two trial sessions before any monthly commitment

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 30 Gurugram shortlist gets cut down to two names
contentBlocks.body:
The intake conversation is where most of the filtering happens, and it is short. An advisor asks which programme the student is in, which subjects and levels are causing trouble, what the school has already flagged, and what the calendar looks like between now and the next reporting cycle. Grade 1 through Grade 12 is covered, so the questions change a great deal depending on whether the answer is early reading or a Physics HL internal assessment due in six weeks.

Then the practical constraints. Which evenings are genuinely free after school timings, sport and travel. Whether a tutor coming to the flat is preferred, or whether a screen is acceptable. What the family is comfortable spending per session, since that decides how many sessions a month is sustainable rather than how good the tutor is.

Only after that do profiles get sent. Usually two, sometimes three, with a note on what each one is stronger at. One may be better at rebuilding shaky Grade 9 foundations. Another may be sharper on paper technique for a student who understands the content but keeps dropping marks in the last twenty minutes of Paper 2.

Matching depends on tutor availability and is not instant. A rare subject at higher level during a busy stretch of the year can take longer than a common one.
items: Programme, subject, level and the nearest real deadline
Honest free evenings after school and activities
Session budget set before profiles are shared
Two or three profiles with stated strengths, not a long list

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP ask for three genuinely different tutors
contentBlocks.body:
Parents often assume a good IB tutor is a good IB tutor. The three programmes reward different things, and a mismatch here wastes a term.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, the work is inquiry driven and the tutoring should protect that. A child who is behind on reading fluency or number sense needs patient, short, frequent sessions and a tutor who resists turning the hour into a worksheet factory. Progress shows up in willingness to attempt things, not in scores.

The Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, is where criterion language starts to bite. Students who write well in general English can still lose marks in Criterion C because they never learned what the descriptor is asking for. The right tutor here spends time on the rubric itself and on planning before writing, which feels slow to parents and pays off in the next assessment cycle.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, is specialist territory. Internal assessment direction, extended essay mentoring, theory of knowledge structure and past paper drilling under real timing all sit here, aimed at the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions. A DP tutor who has not marked against the current criteria will teach the content well and still leave marks on the table.
items: PYP: reading fluency, number sense, short sessions
MYP: criterion descriptors and planning before drafting
DP: IA direction, EE mentoring, TOK structure, timed papers
Earlier planning for younger DP cohorts, not only exam year support

contentBlocks.heading: Home sessions near Heritage City or online across Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring in Sector 30 is usually workable because of where the sector sits. Tutors already working in South City, DLF Phase 1 or around MG Road can add a slot without rebuilding their week. Home tuition in Sector 30 Gurugram suits younger students who need someone physically alongside them, and it suits families who want the session visible rather than behind a bedroom door.

It has real limits. Evening traffic on the central corridor is unpredictable, and a tutor who is late twice a month is not delivering the hour you agreed. Home visits also narrow the field to whoever can reach you, which for a subject like Math AI HL or a specific language A pairing can mean the strongest available person is simply out of reach.

Online changes that arithmetic. An online tutor in Sector 30 Gurugram can be a subject specialist based anywhere, which matters most for late evening slots, uncommon subject combinations and urgent DP revision close to a session. Screen sharing a past paper and annotating it live works better than most parents expect for older students.

Hybrid is common and sensible: one home session for accountability, one online session for depth. Availability for either mode depends on tutor schedules and the time slot you need.
items: Home visits feasible from South City, DLF Phase 1 and the MG Road side
Online widens subject choice for HL and rare pairings
Late evening slots are easier to fill online
Hybrid split: one in person, one on screen

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing subject specialists: Math AA HL, Physics, Economics
contentBlocks.body:
Subject fit is where a shortlist is usually won or lost. Math AA HL and Math AI HL both say maths on a school report and need different teachers. AA HL rewards algebraic fluency, proof and calculus depth. AI HL rewards modelling, interpretation and confident use of technology on a real data set. A tutor strong in one can be merely adequate in the other, and it is fair to ask directly which one they teach more often.

Physics and Chemistry at higher level need someone who works through the data booklet and the mark scheme rather than a textbook chapter order. In Chemistry the marks frequently sit in the working shown for a calculation, not the final number. In Physics the gap is usually definitions and the ability to justify a step in words.

Economics rewards diagram accuracy and the discipline of answering the command term that was actually used, since evaluate and explain earn very different responses. English A support tends to focus on close analysis, comparative structure and building an argument that survives a second reading.

An IB maths tutor in Sector 30 or a science specialist can also help with school assignment review between assessments, which keeps the tutoring anchored to what the class teacher is grading.
items: Math AA HL: proof, calculus, algebraic fluency
Math AI HL: modelling, data interpretation, technology use
Chemistry: marks in the working, not the final answer
Economics: diagram accuracy plus the right command term
English A: close analysis and comparative structure

contentBlocks.heading: School context that changes what a Sector 30 Gurugram tutor prepares
contentBlocks.body:
Families in and around Sector 30 send children to a range of international schools across the wider city, and the school a student attends changes what a tutor should walk in ready to do. Pathways World School in the Gurugram region, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and GD Goenka World School towards Sohna Road all run their own internal calendars, assessment rhythms and subject option blocks.

That matters practically. Two students in the same DP subject can be six weeks apart in sequence because their schools ordered the units differently. A tutor who asks for the school scheme of work in the first session, rather than assuming a standard order, avoids teaching something the class covered in September.

It matters for deadlines too. Internal assessment drafts, mock windows and report cycles do not line up across schools, so the useful tutoring plan is built around the student's actual school calendar and not a generic exam countdown.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Naming them here is about context for parents comparing options, nothing more. Tutors are matched to the student's syllabus and level, not to a school brand.
items: Ask the tutor to read the school scheme of work first
Unit order differs between schools in the same subject
Draft and mock windows vary by school calendar
Independent platform, no school affiliation claimed

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 30 Gurugram and the pockets that sit right next to it
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 30 is bounded by the central Gurugram grid rather than by the newer expressway corridors, which shapes who can teach here. Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park are the anchors most tutors recognise when they are given an address, and directions rarely need explaining twice.

The neighbours matter for scheduling. South City 1 and DLF Phase 1 are close enough that a tutor finishing a session there can reach Sector 30 without a long gap. Nirvana Country and Sector 50 sit further out towards Sohna Road, which is fine at four in the afternoon and much less fine at seven. DLF Phase 4 and Sector 65 pull in tutors who work the Golf Course Extension side of the city.

Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities, subject to tutor schedules. Online tutoring remains available across Gurugram for all supported IB subjects, and for families who travel to Delhi, Noida or Faridabad during term time it keeps the routine intact.

If your preferred slot is after seven in the evening, expect the online option to produce a better match than the in person one.
items: Anchors: Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City, DLF Richmond Park
Quick reach: South City 1, DLF Phase 1
Longer at peak hour: Nirvana Country, Sector 50, Sector 65
Online keeps sessions running during travel to Delhi or Noida

contentBlocks.heading: What a fair comparison looks like four weeks in
contentBlocks.body:
Judging a tutor after one session is unfair to both sides. Judging after a full term is expensive. Four weeks is roughly the right window, and there are specific things to look for rather than a general feeling that it is going well.

The student should be able to say what they are being marked on. Not the topic, the criteria. A Grade 10 student who can explain why a paragraph scored where it did has learned something a score alone never teaches. The tutor should be able to name two things that improved and one that has not moved, without being prompted and without softening it.

School feedback is the outside check. If the class teacher has noticed a change in written work or in classroom questions, that is worth more than a comfortable session.

Be honest about the negative case too. Some students do not respond to a particular teaching style, and no amount of patience fixes that. Changing tutors early costs less than staying in a poor match out of politeness. Progress also depends on the work done between sessions, and a tutor cannot supply that part of it.
items: Student can name the criteria, not only the topic
Tutor volunteers what has not improved yet
A visible change in school written work
Switch early if the style does not fit, rather than waiting

contentBlocks.heading: The checks a tutor passes before the name reaches you
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is meant to remove the obvious mismatches before a parent spends an evening on a trial session. It is a filter, not a promise about outcomes.

The first check is identity and academic background, confirmed against documents rather than a claim on a profile. The second is teaching history in the actual programme: how many years with IB students, at which levels, and in which specific subjects. Someone who has taught A Levels for a decade and IB for one term is described that way rather than listed as an IB specialist.

Assessment familiarity is checked separately from subject knowledge, because they come apart often. A tutor should be able to talk through how an internal assessment is graded, what an extended essay supervisor actually does, and how command terms shape a written answer. For DP subjects, familiarity with the criteria in current use matters more than years of general experience.

After that, references where available, plus a review of how the tutor handles a first session. Feedback from families is read and acted on, and repeated concerns end a listing.

No screening process can predict chemistry between a tutor and a fifteen year old. That is what a trial session is for.
items: Identity and qualifications confirmed against documents
Programme specific experience, stated by level and subject
Assessment familiarity checked apart from subject depth
Ongoing family feedback reviewed after matching

contentBlocks.heading: Starting the search for IB tutors in Sector 30 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Begin with the enquiry form or a call. Have three things ready: the programme and year, the subjects and levels you want covered, and the two or three evening slots that are genuinely free once school timings and activities are accounted for. If you have a recent report or a marked assignment, mention it. That single document tells an advisor more than a long description of how the year has gone.

You will be asked about mode. Home tuition near Sector 30 is often practical given the location, and online sessions widen the specialist pool for higher level subjects or later slots. Many families end up with one of each.

What follows is a short shortlist rather than a directory, with a note on what each tutor is stronger at. Book a trial with two of them if you can. Comparing the same student in front of two teachers is far more informative than comparing two profiles on a screen.

Fees depend on level, subject and session frequency, and availability is subject to tutor schedules. Ask about both before you plan a full term, and ask what a typical first month looks like for a student at your child's stage.
items: Have programme, subjects, levels and free slots ready
Share a recent report or a marked piece of work
Trial two tutors rather than one where possible
Confirm fees and availability before planning a term

faqs.question: How do I compare two IB tutors in Sector 30 without wasting a month?
faqs.answer: Give both the same task. Send each one the same recent marked assignment and ask what they would work on first and why. One will talk about criteria, command terms and where marks were lost. The other will talk about doing more questions. Then book a single trial session with each, ideally in the same week, and ask your child afterwards which session they understood more of. Two evenings gives you a far better read than two weeks of profile comparison, and it costs you very little.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor realistic in Sector 30, or should we plan for online?
faqs.answer: Both work here. Sector 30 sits in the central belt near MG Road and South City, so tutors from South City 1, DLF Phase 1 and the surrounding sectors can usually reach you without an unreasonable journey. Home tutoring suits younger students and anyone who needs the session physically supervised. Online becomes the better option for slots after seven in the evening, for higher level subjects with a smaller pool of specialists, and during heavy revision stretches when a family wants to avoid travel entirely. Availability in either mode depends on tutor schedules.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP and the school says the issue is Criterion C. What kind of tutor helps?
faqs.answer: Someone who teaches the rubric directly. Criterion problems are rarely knowledge problems. A student can understand the content and still lose marks because the response does not do what the descriptor asks for, particularly around organisation and communication. A useful tutor will spend early sessions taking apart the criterion wording, then work on planning before writing rather than editing after. Expect the first few sessions to feel unusually slow. The payoff shows in the next assessment cycle rather than the next homework, so give it a full reporting period.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Math AA HL and Math AI HL for tutoring purposes?
faqs.answer: They need different teachers. Analysis and Approaches at higher level leans on algebraic fluency, proof and substantial calculus, so the tutoring is heavy on technique and precision in working. Applications and Interpretation at higher level leans on modelling, statistics, interpreting real data and using technology confidently, so the tutoring is heavier on judgement and explanation. Ask any prospective maths tutor which of the two they teach most often and how many cohorts they have taken through it. A tutor strong in one can be only adequate in the other.

faqs.question: How soon can sessions start once we enquire?
faqs.answer: For common subjects at standard level, a shortlist can usually be shared quickly and a trial arranged within a few days. Higher level sciences, Math AA HL and less common language pairings take longer, especially close to a busy stretch of the school year when experienced tutors are already committed. Everything is subject to tutor availability and to the specific slot you need. If your evenings are tight, say so at the enquiry stage rather than after profiles are sent, because the time slot narrows the pool more than the subject usually does.

faqs.question: We are starting in Grade 12 with the May session close. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: It is late, and it is fair to say so plainly. What a tutor can do in a short window is real but bounded: paper technique, timing under exam conditions, targeting the two or three topics where the most marks are recoverable, and cleaning up how answers are written. What cannot be rebuilt in a few weeks is two years of missing foundations across a full subject. Expect a tutor to be direct about which category your child is in during the first session rather than promising a broad recovery.

faqs.question: Do you work with students from Pathways, Lancers, Scottish High or GD Goenka?
faqs.answer: Students from many international schools across Gurugram book sessions, including those schools. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any of them unless specifically stated. What the school name changes in practice is sequencing: different schools cover units in a different order and run internal assessment drafts and mocks on different dates. A tutor should ask for the school scheme of work and the deadline calendar in the first session so the plan follows the class rather than a generic syllabus order.

faqs.question: What should we do if there is no visible improvement after a month?
faqs.answer: Raise it directly and early. Ask the tutor for a specific account of what has improved, what has not, and what they intend to change. A serious answer names something that is still weak. If the response is vague, or if your child cannot explain what they are being marked on, that is a reason to switch rather than to add more sessions. Changing tutors after four weeks costs far less than finishing a term in a mismatch. Progress also depends on work done between sessions, which no tutor can supply.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both the internal assessment and regular subject teaching?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is usually the more efficient arrangement, because the same person sees where the subject understanding is thin and where the write up is losing marks. It works less well when the internal assessment is in a subject the tutor does not teach at that level, since IA guidance depends on knowing exactly how that subject is assessed. For extended essay support, many families prefer a separate mentor whose job is structure, research discipline and drafting rather than content teaching. Both arrangements are subject to tutor availability.

mainEntity.name: How do I compare two IB tutors in Sector 30 without wasting a month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Give both the same task. Send each one the same recent marked assignment and ask what they would work on first and why. One will talk about criteria, command terms and where marks were lost. The other will talk about doing more questions. Then book a single trial session with each, ideally in the same week, and ask your child afterwards which session they understood more of. Two evenings gives you a far better read than two weeks of profile comparison, and it costs you very little.

mainEntity.name: Is a home tutor realistic in Sector 30, or should we plan for online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both work here. Sector 30 sits in the central belt near MG Road and South City, so tutors from South City 1, DLF Phase 1 and the surrounding sectors can usually reach you without an unreasonable journey. Home tutoring suits younger students and anyone who needs the session physically supervised. Online becomes the better option for slots after seven in the evening, for higher level subjects with a smaller pool of specialists, and during heavy revision stretches when a family wants to avoid travel entirely. Availability in either mode depends on tutor schedules.

mainEntity.name: My child is in MYP and the school says the issue is Criterion C. What kind of tutor helps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Someone who teaches the rubric directly. Criterion problems are rarely knowledge problems. A student can understand the content and still lose marks because the response does not do what the descriptor asks for, particularly around organisation and communication. A useful tutor will spend early sessions taking apart the criterion wording, then work on planning before writing rather than editing after. Expect the first few sessions to feel unusually slow. The payoff shows in the next assessment cycle rather than the next homework, so give it a full reporting period.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Math AA HL and Math AI HL for tutoring purposes?

acceptedAnswer.text: They need different teachers. Analysis and Approaches at higher level leans on algebraic fluency, proof and substantial calculus, so the tutoring is heavy on technique and precision in working. Applications and Interpretation at higher level leans on modelling, statistics, interpreting real data and using technology confidently, so the tutoring is heavier on judgement and explanation. Ask any prospective maths tutor which of the two they teach most often and how many cohorts they have taken through it. A tutor strong in one can be only adequate in the other.

mainEntity.name: How soon can sessions start once we enquire?

acceptedAnswer.text: For common subjects at standard level, a shortlist can usually be shared quickly and a trial arranged within a few days. Higher level sciences, Math AA HL and less common language pairings take longer, especially close to a busy stretch of the school year when experienced tutors are already committed. Everything is subject to tutor availability and to the specific slot you need. If your evenings are tight, say so at the enquiry stage rather than after profiles are sent, because the time slot narrows the pool more than the subject usually does.

mainEntity.name: We are starting in Grade 12 with the May session close. Is it too late?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is late, and it is fair to say so plainly. What a tutor can do in a short window is real but bounded: paper technique, timing under exam conditions, targeting the two or three topics where the most marks are recoverable, and cleaning up how answers are written. What cannot be rebuilt in a few weeks is two years of missing foundations across a full subject. Expect a tutor to be direct about which category your child is in during the first session rather than promising a broad recovery.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with students from Pathways, Lancers, Scottish High or GD Goenka?

acceptedAnswer.text: Students from many international schools across Gurugram book sessions, including those schools. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any of them unless specifically stated. What the school name changes in practice is sequencing: different schools cover units in a different order and run internal assessment drafts and mocks on different dates. A tutor should ask for the school scheme of work and the deadline calendar in the first session so the plan follows the class rather than a generic syllabus order.

mainEntity.name: What should we do if there is no visible improvement after a month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Raise it directly and early. Ask the tutor for a specific account of what has improved, what has not, and what they intend to change. A serious answer names something that is still weak. If the response is vague, or if your child cannot explain what they are being marked on, that is a reason to switch rather than to add more sessions. Changing tutors after four weeks costs far less than finishing a term in a mismatch. Progress also depends on work done between sessions, which no tutor can supply.

mainEntity.name: Can one tutor cover both the internal assessment and regular subject teaching?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes, and it is usually the more efficient arrangement, because the same person sees where the subject understanding is thin and where the write up is losing marks. It works less well when the internal assessment is in a subject the tutor does not teach at that level, since IA guidance depends on knowing exactly how that subject is assessed. For extended essay support, many families prefer a separate mentor whose job is structure, research discipline and drafting rather than content teaching. Both arrangements are subject to tutor availability.

h1: IB Tutors in Sector 31 Gurugram Across the Full School Year
heroSubtitle: Sector 31 sits in the older central grid off MG Road, alongside South City and the Heritage City pocket. Tutoring here is arranged around the school calendar: unit tests in autumn, mocks in the new year, internal assessment drafts, then the run-in to a May or November session.
introSummary: Families searching for IB tutors in Sector 31 Gurugram usually start in a panic month, which is why the help arrives in the wrong shape. A September problem is a foundations problem. A February problem is a technique and deadline problem. They need different tutors and different session lengths. This page walks through how an IB year actually unfolds for students living around Sector 31, near MG Road, South City and Heritage City, and what to arrange at each stage rather than all at once.

contentBlocks.heading: How an IB year changes for a student in Sector 31 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
In August the student is confident and the parent is calm. By February one of those two things has usually changed.

The first term is quiet on paper. Units are being introduced, marks are provisional, and nothing feels urgent enough to book a tutor for. This is also the cheapest point at which a gap can be fixed, because a Grade 11 student who never really understood logarithms in September will meet that same weakness again in April with far less time to spare.

The middle stretch is where families notice. Report cards land, internal assessment proposals are due, and the first real timed papers come back marked against criteria rather than out of a friendly total. Students who coped by working hard suddenly find that effort alone does not answer the command term in front of them.

The final stretch is triage. Past papers under proper timing, targeted topic repair, and steadying nerves before the May 2026 session. Younger DP cohorts and November candidates run the same arc on a shifted calendar.

So the sensible question for a parent in Sector 31 is not simply who is good. It is what stage the student is at, and what kind of teaching that stage rewards.
items: Autumn: foundations, unit tests, habits that hold up later
New year: mocks, criterion feedback, first honest picture
Spring: IA drafts, EE progress, TOK deadlines
Run-in: timed papers, topic repair, exam routine

contentBlocks.heading: Where the pressure lands: Chemistry, Math AA HL and English A
contentBlocks.body:
Different subjects break at different points in the year, and knowing that saves a term of guessing.

Chemistry usually causes trouble around the second term, when the calculation-heavy topics stack up and the internal assessment demands a research question the student can actually control. Marks are lost in uncertainty handling and in the working, not the arithmetic. A good Chemistry tutor will slow down the write-up and speed up the practice.

Math AA HL bites earlier. Calculus and proof punish anyone whose algebra was shaky at the start, and the deficit compounds quietly for months. Math AI HL runs a different rhythm: the pressure arrives with modelling tasks and statistical interpretation, where students who can compute still struggle to say what a result means.

Physics tends to produce a mid-year wobble around definitions and justification in words. Economics builds steadily and then collapses at evaluation, because a well drawn diagram scores nothing if the command term asked for a judgement.

English A is the slow burner. Nobody fails it in October. But comparative essays and oral components need drafting time that cannot be compressed, and an English A tutor booked in March is often three months late.
items: Chemistry: uncertainty, working shown, IA research question control
Math AA HL: algebra debt surfacing in calculus
Math AI HL: interpreting a model, not just computing it
Economics: evaluation, not diagram accuracy alone
English A: drafting time that cannot be compressed

contentBlocks.heading: Matching a tutor to the month you are actually in
contentBlocks.body:
An advisor call starts with the calendar rather than the subject. What year is the student in, which session are they sitting, and what is the next dated thing on the school planner. That last answer reshapes everything after it.

Early in the year the brief is usually foundational, so a patient teacher who rebuilds slowly is a better fit than a fast exam coach. Sessions can be shorter and less frequent. Closer to mocks the brief flips: the student needs someone who marks strictly, times them, and refuses to accept vague answers. Those are rarely the same person, and it is normal for a family to change tutors between stages rather than treating a switch as a failure.

Subject, level and grade come next, anywhere from Grade 1 through Grade 12, then the honest weekly picture. School timings, sport, travel, and the evenings a teenager will actually cooperate.

Profiles follow, with a short note on why each was picked for this stage. Two is typical. Everything depends on tutor availability, and a request made three weeks before mocks meets a thinner pool than the same request made in October.
items: Next dated deadline drives the brief, not the subject alone
Foundations tutor and exam coach are different people
Shorter early sessions, longer timed ones near mocks
Requests made in peak weeks meet a thinner pool

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 31 Gurugram and the roads that decide your session time
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 31 sits inside the older central grid, with Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park as the landmarks tutors use to find an address. MG Road and the South City stretch frame the area, which is why afternoon travel here behaves differently from the expressway corridors.

Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules. Pick the slot first. Then ask who can serve it.

Reliable afternoon runs from South City 1 and DLF Phase 1

contentBlocks.heading: PYP reading, MYP criteria, DP deadlines: three different years
contentBlocks.body:
The shape of a school year differs sharply by programme, and the tutoring should follow that shape.

A Primary Years Programme child, ages three to twelve, has no exam calendar to work backwards from. The year is about accumulating fluency, so support works best in short regular sessions spread evenly rather than concentrated before any particular week. If a Grade 3 student is behind on reading, the useful measure in March is whether books are being finished, not whether a test score moved.

Middle Years Programme students, ages eleven to sixteen, live in assessment cycles. Each unit ends with criterion-marked work, which means there is a natural checkpoint every few weeks. Tutoring plugged into that rhythm is far more effective than a general weekly hour, because the student can see the criterion feedback change from one unit to the next.

Diploma Programme students, ages sixteen to nineteen, run to dates: IA proposals, EE first drafts, TOK exhibition and essay, mocks, then the session itself. A DP tutor should be able to sketch the term ahead in the first meeting. Younger DP cohorts benefit from starting this planning a year earlier than most families do.
items: PYP: even spread, fluency measured by behaviour not scores
MYP: work to the unit cycle and its criterion feedback
DP: IA, EE, TOK and mock dates mapped in session one
May 2026 and November 2026 candidates run offset calendars

contentBlocks.heading: What is checked before a Sector 31 Gurugram tutor is suggested
contentBlocks.body:
Screening happens before any name is shared, and it is deliberately narrow in what it claims. It removes clear mismatches. It does not predict how a term will go.

Documents come first: identity, degrees and any teaching qualifications, verified rather than accepted on trust. Then the teaching record, described precisely. Two years with MYP students is written as two years with MYP students, not as long IB experience, because those two descriptions send parents in very different directions.

Assessment literacy is treated as its own test. A tutor is asked how internal assessment criteria work in their subject, what supervision of an extended essay involves, and how a command term changes the shape of a required answer. Strong subject knowledge and weak assessment literacy is a common combination, and it is exactly the combination that costs marks late in the year.

Where references exist they are followed up. After matching, family feedback is reviewed, and a pattern of concerns ends a listing rather than earning a warning.

The honest limit: no check tells you whether a particular teenager will work well with a particular adult. Only a session does.
items: Documents verified, not taken on trust
Experience described by programme, level and years
Assessment literacy tested separately from subject depth
Repeated family concerns end a listing

contentBlocks.heading: Home tuition in term time, online during the exam run-in
contentBlocks.body:
Most Sector 31 families end up using both modes, at different points in the year, and that is usually the right answer rather than a compromise.

Home tuition in Sector 31 Gurugram works well through the settled middle of a term. A tutor in the room can see a Grade 8 student drifting in a way a camera hides, and younger children simply concentrate better with an adult beside them. The location helps here, since the central grid keeps journeys from South City and the DLF phases manageable.

The case weakens under time pressure. During the exam run-in the student needs more contact hours, and every home visit spends twenty minutes each way on the road, which the tutor is reasonably counting as part of their evening. Online sessions in Sector 31 Gurugram remove that cost, allow a quick thirty minute doubt-solving slot the night before a test, and open the pool to specialists who do not travel at all.

Online is worse for students who need supervision to stay on task. Be honest about which kind of child you have before deciding, and expect availability in either mode to depend on tutor schedules.
items: In person suits younger students and settled term weeks
Online suits high-frequency revision and short doubt slots
Travel time is real time and shapes what a tutor can offer
Supervision-dependent students do worse on screen

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars around Sector 31 Gurugram that shape tutoring
contentBlocks.body:
Children from the Sector 31 area attend international schools spread across the city, and each school runs its own dates. Pathways World School in the Gurugram region, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and GD Goenka World School towards Sohna Road set their own mock windows, draft deadlines and reporting cycles.

This is not a detail. If one school runs mocks in the first week of January and another in early February, the same tutoring plan will be four weeks out of phase for one of the two students. A tutor who begins by asking for the term calendar and the assessment schedule can build backwards from real dates. A tutor who works from a generic syllabus order ends up teaching in the wrong sequence.

Subject option blocks differ too, which affects who a student can be grouped with and which combinations of higher level subjects are common at that school.

Ask the tutor to plan backwards from real term dates
