Independent platform, no affiliation with any school claimed

contentBlocks.heading: Signs the year is going right, and signs it is not
contentBlocks.body:
Progress across an IB year is uneven, so a single set of marks is a poor instrument. Watch behaviour instead.

Good signs are specific. The student starts a piece of written work by looking at the criteria rather than the topic. Homework arguments get shorter. A doubt gets asked on the day it appears instead of a week later. In a subject like Economics, the student begins distinguishing between what an explain question and an evaluate question want without being told each time.

Warning signs are equally specific. Sessions become a place where homework is completed rather than taught. The tutor cannot say what will be different next month. Marks move but the student cannot explain why. And if a Grade 11 student is still relying on the tutor to start every problem in February, the dependence is now part of the problem.

A plain limitation: tutoring cannot replace class attention or offset a subject choice that never suited the student. It can make a hard year manageable. Anyone promising more than that is guessing, and results depend on the work done between sessions.
items: Student opens a task by reading the criteria
Doubts raised same day, not saved up for weeks
Tutor can state what will change next month
Dependence on the tutor to start every question is a red flag

contentBlocks.heading: Booking IB tutors in Sector 31 Gurugram before the next deadline
contentBlocks.body:
Start by writing down the next three dated items on the school calendar. A unit test, an internal assessment draft, a mock. Those dates decide what kind of tutor is useful right now, and they make the first advisor call much shorter.

Then add the practical facts: programme and grade, subjects and levels, the mode you would prefer, and the evenings that are genuinely free. If your child sat a recent assessment, keep the marked copy handy. It is the fastest way for anyone to see whether the issue is content, technique or timing.

A short list follows, usually two names, with a note on why each suits this stage of the year. Trial sessions can be arranged at home where a tutor covers the Sector 31 area, or online for wider subject choice. Sit in on the first ten minutes if your child will tolerate it, because you learn more from watching one exchange than from any profile.

Fees vary by level, subject and how often you meet. Availability is subject to tutor schedules, and the weeks around mocks and the May session are the tightest of the year, so earlier requests get more choice. If the stage you are at calls for a short intensive block rather than a weekly slot, say that at the start.
items: List the next three dated school deadlines first
Keep a recent marked assessment ready to share
Choose your mode by the stage of the year
Book earlier for mock season and the May run-in

faqs.question: When in the school year should we actually start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do. The strongest results come from starting in the first term, when a gap is still small and there is room to rebuild without touching revision time. Starting after the first report card is common and still workable. Starting after mocks limits what is possible to technique, timing and targeted topic repair. If you are reading this in the second half of the year, book anyway, but ask the tutor to be blunt in the first session about which weaknesses can realistically be fixed in the time left.

faqs.question: Should we change tutors between the foundations stage and exam season?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is not a failure. The teacher who patiently rebuilds algebra over three months and the coach who marks strictly under timed conditions are often different people with different temperaments. If your current tutor is candid about it, they will say so themselves. A reasonable approach is to review the fit at each major checkpoint in the calendar, such as after the first report or after mocks, rather than assuming one name should carry the whole year. Any change depends on tutor availability at the time.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week make sense at different points in the year?
faqs.answer: One session a week is usually enough during the settled part of a term, provided the student does something with it between meetings. Two becomes sensible when an internal assessment is being drafted alongside normal class work, since the two competing demands each need attention. Closer to mocks or the May session, families often add short focused slots rather than more full hours, because a thirty minute doubt-solving session the evening before a paper does more than an extra ninety minutes a week earlier. Frequency also depends on what is affordable to sustain.

faqs.question: Our child is in MYP and marks swing wildly between units. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is common, and it usually points at criteria rather than knowledge. Different units emphasise different criteria, so a student who is strong on knowledge and understanding but weak on communication will look inconsistent across a year even though the underlying picture is stable. A tutor who tracks results by criterion rather than by percentage will spot this within a few weeks. The fix is targeted work on the weaker criterion, which is slower and less satisfying than covering more content, but it stops the swing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the extended essay, or only with subjects?
faqs.answer: Extended essay support is available, though it works differently from subject teaching. The school supervisor stays responsible for the formal process. A tutor or mentor helps with narrowing a research question that is genuinely answerable, planning a realistic drafting schedule, keeping the argument coherent, and holding the student to interim deadlines that the school may only check occasionally. The work is mostly structure and discipline rather than content delivery. Matching for extended essay mentoring in a specific subject area is subject to tutor availability.

faqs.question: Does home tuition in Sector 31 get harder during monsoon months?
faqs.answer: It can. The central roads around MG Road and South City handle rain poorly, and a tutor travelling in from Sector 65, DLF Phase 4 or out towards Sohna Road may lose a good part of an evening to it. Families who rely on a fixed weekday slot often keep one online session as a fallback for exactly these weeks, so the routine holds even when travel does not. Discuss this at the booking stage rather than improvising when the first wet evening arrives.

faqs.question: What does a first session usually cover?
faqs.answer: A good first session is mostly diagnosis. The tutor looks at recent marked work, asks the student to attempt something unaided, and watches where the process breaks down rather than only whether the answer is right. Expect questions about the school calendar, the next assessment and how the student prepares now. By the end you should hear a short plan for the coming weeks with one or two specific targets. If the first session was mainly the tutor talking through a syllabus, ask for something more diagnostic next time.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely as effective for IB as sitting in the room?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma Programme students, yes, and occasionally better, because the specialist pool is wider and past papers can be annotated live on a shared screen. For younger students it is generally weaker. A Grade 5 or Grade 6 child who needs an adult present to stay on task will drift once the novelty passes, whatever the platform. Age and temperament matter more than the technology here. Many families in the Sector 31 area settle on one visit at home plus one online session each week.

faqs.question: How do fees work and what changes them?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the level, the subject and how often sessions run. Higher level sciences and Math AA HL usually sit above standard level support because the pool of tutors who teach them confidently is smaller. Longer commitments and regular weekly slots are treated differently from occasional intensive blocks before mocks. Travel is a factor for home sessions, which is part of why online rates can differ. Ask for the specific figure for your subject and level during the enquiry call rather than working from a general range.

heroSubtitle: Sector 32 sits in the central Gurugram grid near MG Road and South City, with Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park as the nearby anchors. IB Gram matches PYP, MYP and DP students to tutors and is direct about what a session should contain before you pay for a term of them.
introSummary: Parents comparing IB tutors in Sector 32 Gurugram tend to compare hourly rates, which is the least useful number available. A session is worth what the tutor did before it and what they do with the marked work afterwards. Preparation against your child's actual syllabus, feedback written against criteria, and travel across the central Gurugram roads all sit inside the fee. This page explains what a fair hour contains at PYP, MYP and DP level, and what to check before committing beyond a first month.

contentBlocks.heading: What an hour of IB tutoring in Sector 32 Gurugram should buy
contentBlocks.body:
The hourly rate is the wrong thing to look at first. Two tutors can quote the same figure and deliver entirely different amounts of work.

A properly prepared session starts before the tutor arrives. Someone has read the school's unit plan, looked at the last marked assignment, and decided what the hour is for. During the hour the student should be doing most of the thinking, with the tutor interrupting rather than lecturing. Afterwards there should be something written down: what was covered, what to practise, and where the marks were being lost. That third part is the piece families most often never receive, and it is where a large share of the value sits.

Then there is travel. A tutor crossing from South City 1 or the DLF phases to reach an address in Sector 32 gives up close to an extra hour of their evening, and any rational rate reflects that. Which is precisely why online sessions can be cheaper for the same teacher.

Cheap sessions that consist of watching your child finish homework are not a saving. They are a slow way of paying for supervision. Ask what happens before and after the hour, and the fee starts making sense.
items: Preparation against the school's own unit plan
Student working, tutor interrupting, not lecturing
Written notes after the session on marks lost
Travel time built into any home visit rate

contentBlocks.heading: Travel time is billed time: home, online and hybrid sessions
contentBlocks.body:
The mode you pick changes the economics more than most parents realise.

Home tutoring buys presence. For a Grade 4 or Grade 7 student who wanders off task the moment nobody is beside them, that presence is the product, and it is worth paying for. Sector 32 helps here, since the central grid near MG Road and South City is reachable for tutors already teaching in South City 1, DLF Phase 1 or the surrounding sectors. Home tuition in Sector 32 Gurugram is generally practical for afternoon and early evening slots.

It is also the most expensive way to buy an hour, because you are funding a journey. And the pool shrinks to whoever can make the trip, which for Math AA HL or a less common language pairing can mean settling for availability over fit.

Online removes the journey from the bill and puts a specialist within reach regardless of where they live. An online tutor in Sector 32 Gurugram can also offer a short thirty minute doubt-solving slot, which no one will drive across the city to deliver.

Hybrid splits the difference sensibly: presence where it is needed, screen time where depth or frequency matters more. Availability in every mode depends on tutor schedules.
items: Home visits: presence for younger or easily distracted students
Online: no journey funded, wider specialist pool
Short doubt slots only realistically exist online
Hybrid pairs one in-person hour with one screen session

contentBlocks.heading: Subjects where an hour goes further, and where it does not
contentBlocks.body:
Not every subject converts tutoring time into marks at the same rate, and it is worth knowing which one you are buying.

Mathematics is the most efficient. Math AA HL and Math AI HL both respond quickly to focused work because the weakness can usually be located precisely, then drilled. A student stuck on integration by substitution can be visibly better in three sessions. The same is broadly true of Physics, where problem-solving method is teachable and repeatable.

Chemistry sits in the middle. Calculation topics move fast, but internal assessment work is slower because a research question has to be narrowed, tested and then written up, and none of that compresses well.

English A is the slowest converter and the one parents most often abandon too early. Analytical writing improves over months, in small increments, and a tutor who claims otherwise is overselling. Economics is unusual: content is quick, but evaluation as a skill takes patience, and marks stay flat until it clicks.

Higher level subjects usually cost more per session than standard level, simply because fewer tutors teach them confidently. Rate differences across subjects are about scarcity, not about how hard the tutor is working.
items: Fast: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics problem method
Medium: Chemistry calculations, slower on IA write-up
Slow: English A analysis, Economics evaluation
Higher level rates reflect scarcity of specialists

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 32 Gurugram addresses a tutor can realistically reach
contentBlocks.body:
Where you live decides which tutors will quote you a workable rate for home visits. Sector 32 sits within the older central layout, with Heritage City, Unitech Heritage City and DLF Richmond Park as the reference points on most tutors' mental maps of this part of the city.

South City 1 and DLF Phase 1 are the shortest hops, so tutors working there can add a Sector 32 slot without pricing in a long journey. Sector 50 and Nirvana Country lean towards Sohna Road, which is manageable in the afternoon and slow later. DLF Phase 4 and Sector 65 sit across on the Golf Course Extension side, and a tutor coming from there is realistically giving up a large part of an evening for one session.

Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules. Online tutoring remains available across Gurugram for all supported IB subjects, and it holds up when families travel to Delhi, Noida or Faridabad during term.

If you want the lowest sensible fee for in-person work, ask for tutors already teaching within a few kilometres rather than the single most qualified name on offer.
items: Short hops: South City 1, DLF Phase 1
Slower after five: Sector 50, Nirvana Country towards Sohna Road
Long runs: DLF Phase 4 and Sector 65 on the Extension side
Nearby tutors usually quote better in-person rates

contentBlocks.heading: Cost by programme: PYP habits, MYP criteria, DP specialists
contentBlocks.body:
Spending is very different across the three programmes, and understanding why prevents both overspending early and underspending late.

Primary Years Programme families, covering ages three to twelve, usually need the least expensive arrangement and the most consistent one. Short sessions two or three times a week beat one long weekly hour, since fluency in reading or number work is built by repetition. The tutor's job here is largely habit formation, and paying for a highly specialised teacher is rarely the best use of money at this stage.

Middle Years Programme students, ages eleven to sixteen, need someone who understands criterion marking. That is a specific skill and it costs more than general subject help, but it is the point at which spending starts paying back, because criterion habits carry into the Diploma years.

Diploma Programme students, ages sixteen to nineteen, are the expensive stage. Higher level subject specialists, internal assessment direction, extended essay mentoring, theory of knowledge support and past-paper work aimed at the May 2026 or November 2026 session all sit here. Families who invested a little in the MYP years usually spend less in DP, because there is less to repair. Grade 1 through Grade 12 support is available across all three.
items: PYP: frequency over specialisation, shorter sessions
MYP: pay for criterion literacy, it compounds later
DP: HL specialists, IA and EE mentoring, timed papers
Earlier planning for younger DP cohorts lowers later spend

contentBlocks.heading: From enquiry to a Sector 32 Gurugram tutor: the steps in between
contentBlocks.body:
The first call is short and mostly practical. Which programme and grade, which subjects and at what level, what the school has flagged, and what the family can sustain each month. That last figure is asked early on purpose, because there is no point recommending a specialist for three sessions a week if the budget supports one.

Then the timetable. School timings, activities, travel, and the evenings that are genuinely open. A slot request narrows the pool faster than almost anything else, and late evening requests narrow it further.

After that, two or three profiles arrive with rates attached and a line on what each tutor is strongest at. The comparison should be made on fit and on what the session includes, not on the number alone. A slightly higher rate that comes with written feedback after every session is usually the better purchase.

A trial follows. Treat it as a purchase decision rather than a formality, and ask afterwards what the tutor thinks the first month will cost in sessions and in the student's own working time.

Matching depends on tutor availability, and rare higher level combinations take longer to fill than common ones.
items: Monthly budget discussed before profiles are sent
Slot requests narrow the pool more than subjects do
Rates shared alongside strengths, not after the trial
Ask what the first month costs in sessions and student hours

contentBlocks.heading: Value you can audit after four weeks of sessions
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks in, a family should be able to answer three questions without hedging. What did the tutor change. What can the student now do unaided that they could not before. What is still broken.

If the answers are vague, the money is being spent on company rather than teaching. Specific answers look like this: the student now plans an Economics essay before writing it, or shows working in Chemistry calculations that previously jumped to an answer, or finishes Paper 1 questions inside the time allowed instead of running over by ten minutes.

The cheapest audit available is asking your child to explain a recent correction to you. If they can say why the mark was lost and what the criterion wanted, the sessions are landing. If they can only repeat the corrected answer, they are not.

An honest caveat. Some months produce no visible movement even when the teaching is sound, particularly in written subjects where progress arrives in steps rather than smoothly. And no amount of paid tutoring compensates for work not done between sessions, which remains the student's part of the arrangement.
items: Name one thing the student can now do unaided
Ask the child to explain a correction, not repeat it
Written subjects improve in steps, not smoothly
Unfinished work between sessions cancels out the spend

contentBlocks.heading: School fees are fixed, tutoring is not: the Sector 32 Gurugram context
contentBlocks.body:
Children from the Sector 32 area attend international schools spread across the city. Pathways World School in the Gurugram region, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and GD Goenka World School out towards Sohna Road each run their own timetables, option blocks and assessment calendars.

The school matters to the tutoring budget in a way that is rarely discussed. Where a school already provides strong internal assessment supervision and regular written feedback, a family needs less paid support and can spend it narrowly on one weak subject. Where feedback is thinner, or where a subject is taught in a large group, the tutoring has to carry more and costs more.

So the useful first step is not booking a tutor for every difficult subject. It is working out what the school is already doing well, then paying only for the gap.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. They are listed to help you place yourself locally. Tutors are matched to a student's syllabus, level and deadlines rather than to any school's name.
items: Identify what the school already covers well
Pay for the gap, not for every difficult subject
Group-taught subjects usually need more outside support
Independent platform, no school affiliation claimed

contentBlocks.heading: What screening removes before you pay for a session
contentBlocks.body:
Vetting exists so that a family's first paid hour is not spent discovering something a document check would have caught.

Identity and qualifications are confirmed against records rather than taken from a profile description. Teaching history is recorded specifically: which programme, which levels, which subjects, and for how long. A tutor with strong university mathematics but no experience of Math AI HL is listed that way, because sending them to an AI HL student wastes the family's money and the tutor's evening.

Assessment familiarity is checked on its own. Can the tutor explain how an internal assessment is marked in their subject, what an extended essay supervisor does, and how a command term changes what an answer must contain. This is the check that most protects a Diploma Programme budget, since content knowledge without criterion knowledge produces well taught students who still lose marks.

References are followed where they exist, and family feedback after matching is reviewed. Repeated concerns end a listing.

What vetting cannot do is guarantee a personality fit or an outcome. That is why the first session matters and why nobody should commit to a long block before it happens.
items: Records checked before any profile is shared
Experience recorded by programme, level and subject
Criterion knowledge tested separately from content depth
No long commitment before the first session

contentBlocks.heading: Asking about IB tutors in Sector 32 Gurugram and fees
contentBlocks.body:
When you enquire, give four things: the programme and grade, the subjects and levels, the mode you would prefer, and the monthly amount you are comfortable committing. The last one is not intrusive. It decides whether the sensible recommendation is a weekly session with a specialist or twice-weekly support with a strong generalist, and getting it wrong wastes a month.

Ask directly what each quoted session includes. Preparation, written feedback, availability for a question between sessions, and whether a missed slot can be rescheduled. Those inclusions vary far more between tutors than the headline rate does.

A short list follows with rates and strengths noted. Book a trial before agreeing to anything longer, and treat the first month as an evaluation period with a specific target you have agreed in advance. Write that target down somewhere you will see it again, because a month later most families remember the feeling of the sessions and not the thing they originally wanted fixed.

Fees depend on level, subject and frequency, higher level sciences and Math AA HL sitting above standard level work. Availability is subject to tutor schedules, and the busiest weeks of the school year leave the least choice, so ask early if your timing is fixed.
items: State a monthly figure at the enquiry stage
Ask what preparation and feedback are included
Check rescheduling and between-session question policy
Agree one specific target for the first month

faqs.question: Why do IB tutor fees in Sector 32 vary so much for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Three things drive the difference. Level comes first, since higher level sciences and Math AA HL have a smaller pool of confident teachers. Mode comes second, because a home visit funds a journey across the central Gurugram roads that an online session does not. Experience with assessment comes third, and it is the one parents underweight. A tutor who has marked internal assessments and knows the criteria well charges more and usually saves you sessions. Compare what is included per hour before comparing the hourly figures themselves.

faqs.question: Is a group class cheaper in a useful way, or a false economy?
faqs.answer: It depends on the reason for the difficulty. If the student understands most of the subject and needs structured revision with worked examples, a small group is a reasonable use of money and the peer questions help. If the gap is specific, such as one topic never understood properly or a persistent problem with how answers are written, a group will not find it. Paying less per hour to have a weakness go unaddressed is more expensive over a term. Group availability is subject to tutor schedules and current demand.

faqs.question: Should we pay for a package upfront or session by session?
faqs.answer: Start session by session, or with a short block, until the trial period is over. A first month is an evaluation, and locking into a long commitment removes your ability to change a tutor who is not the right fit. Once the arrangement is clearly working, a longer block booked in advance often secures a preferred slot, which matters most in mock season and the run-in to the May session. Ask about cancellation and rescheduling terms before committing to anything longer than a month.

faqs.question: How many hours a week are actually needed for a DP student?
faqs.answer: For one subject that is causing trouble, a single well-prepared weekly session plus the student's own follow-up work is usually enough during normal term weeks. Two subjects in difficulty means two sessions, not one longer combined hour, because switching subjects mid-session tends to waste the second half. During internal assessment drafting or the weeks before mocks, families often add short focused slots. Adding hours without changing what happens inside them rarely helps, so ask the tutor what the extra time would be spent on.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor coming to Sector 32 cost more than an online tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is straightforward. A tutor travelling in from South City 1, the DLF phases or further out along Sohna Road spends a substantial part of the evening on the road, and that time cannot be sold to anyone else. Online removes that cost entirely and also removes the geographic limit on who you can hire. For younger children the in-person premium is generally worth paying. For a Diploma Programme student working on past papers, it often is not.

faqs.question: What should be included in the fee besides the teaching hour itself?
faqs.answer: At a minimum, preparation aligned to the student's actual school unit plan, and a short written note after each session covering what was done and what to practise. Many tutors also mark a piece of work between sessions and allow a brief question by message. None of this is universal, so ask specifically. A rate that looks higher but includes marked feedback is usually better value than a lower rate that covers only the hour spent talking, because the marking is where criterion errors get caught.

faqs.question: We are on a tight budget. What is the single best thing to spend on?
faqs.answer: Buy assessment expertise for the one subject that is doing the most damage to the overall picture, rather than spreading thin support across three subjects. A student losing marks across several subjects for the same reason, usually how answers are written against command terms, will often improve everywhere from work done in one subject. Ask an advisor to help identify that subject during the enquiry call. Frequency can be reduced later once the habit is established, which keeps the arrangement sustainable across a full year.

faqs.question: If we stop sessions for the holidays, will the slot still be there?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Regular slots in the late afternoon and early evening are the ones most in demand across Gurugram, and a tutor with a gap will usually fill it. Families who plan a break often keep one shorter session a fortnight through the holiday to hold the arrangement and keep the routine from collapsing entirely. Discuss it with the tutor before the break rather than after. Resuming at the same time depends on tutor availability when you return.

faqs.question: How do we know we are not paying for supervised homework?
faqs.answer: Look at what the student is doing during the hour. If the session is mostly the child working quietly with occasional corrections, that is supervision, and it costs the same as teaching while achieving much less. Real teaching looks like the tutor stopping the student mid-problem to ask why they chose that step, or refusing to give an answer until the student has attempted it. Ask your child what they were asked during the session. The answer tells you quickly which one you bought.

contentBlocks.heading: When a Tutor Leaves Halfway Through DP1
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor stops in October. The student is midway through a Chemistry internal assessment, has two marked mock papers behind them, and the replacement opens by asking questions the previous tutor answered in week three. That is the ordinary failure mode for IB families, and it explains why many parents searching for IB tutors in Sector 38 Gurugram arrive already tired of the process.

Sector 38 sits in the central band of the city, close to the Golf Course Road corridor on one side and the older South City stretch on the other. Families here live around The Aralias, The Magnolias, Suncity and Mayfield Garden, and most students are travelling out of the sector for school in any case. So the tutoring question is rarely about distance alone. It is about whether the next tutor can pick up unfinished coursework without quietly starting it again.

IB Gram treats that as a matching problem rather than a scheduling one. Before any tutor is suggested, an advisor asks what stage the student has reached: which criteria the school has already marked, what the last written feedback actually said, whether the IA topic is locked or still moving. A tutor who can read that history and carry it forward is worth more than a tutor with a longer subject list.

Continuity is the thing being bought. The rest is logistics.

Last school feedback read, not re-derived from scratch
IA stage confirmed: topic, data, first draft or edit
Same weekly slot preserved wherever travel allows

contentBlocks.heading: From First Call to Shortlist for a Sector 38 Family
contentBlocks.body:
The opening conversation is short and mostly diagnostic. An advisor asks for the year group, the programme the school runs, the subject list with levels attached, and the reason the search began this month. The reason matters more than parents expect. A DP1 student drifting in Math AA HL needs a different profile from a DP2 student who has collected data but written no analysis.

After that, IB Gram looks for tutors whose recent teaching sits close to the request, not tutors who merely list the subject somewhere on a profile. For an IB home tutor in Sector 38 request, availability is tested against the slot a family can genuinely hold every week rather than an aspirational one. A Tuesday seven o'clock session that survives football practice beats an ambitious five o'clock session that collapses by November.

You then receive a short shortlist, usually two or three profiles, describing what each tutor has taught, at which level, and how they prefer to run a first month. An introductory session can be arranged, subject to tutor availability and the level requested.

If nothing on that list fits, say so plainly. A second pass costs a few days. A poor match that runs unchallenged for six weeks costs considerably more.

Reason for switching recorded in the tutor brief
Two or three profiles, not an open directory
Slot tested against real evening travel from nearby sectors

contentBlocks.heading: Subjects Where a Handover Costs the Most Time
contentBlocks.body:
Not every subject loses the same amount when a tutor changes. Math AA HL loses least, because the syllabus order is public and a competent teacher can locate the gap inside one session of problem solving. Physics and Chemistry lose more, since the internal assessment belongs to the student and a new tutor has to rebuild the reasoning behind a method choice before improving anything.

Economics sits between those two. The commentary rests on the article chosen and the diagram the student already committed to, so a replacement needs the drafts themselves and not a summary of them. English A loses the most. The individual oral and the written work depend on texts the student has annotated in one particular direction, and rebuilding that reading takes weeks nobody has spare in DP2.

Math AI HL deserves separate mention. Families sometimes move a student across from AA and assume tutoring will absorb the change quietly. It usually cannot. The modelling and statistics content differs enough to need its own plan and its own timeline.

An IB maths tutor Sector 38 enquiry and an IB science tutor Sector 38 enquiry are therefore handled differently at the diagnostic stage, even when the student behind both is the same child.

Math AI HL: modelling and statistics need a fresh plan, not a patch
Physics and Chemistry: method justification rebuilt before marks move

English A: annotated texts are the slowest thing to hand over

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Handovers Look Nothing Alike
contentBlocks.body:
Primary Years Programme families rarely have a paper trail to pass on. What transfers instead is routine: how long the child can sit, which inquiry topics held attention, what reading level the school last reported. A tutor starting with a Grade 3 or Grade 4 student should spend the first two sessions watching before changing anything at all.

Middle Years Programme handovers turn on criteria. A student in MYP 4 has been marked against strands A to D in each subject, and school feedback usually names the weakest one. That is the document worth transferring. Without it a replacement tutor teaches content the student already holds and misses the investigation or communication strand that is quietly costing marks.

Diploma Programme handovers are hardest, because they are timed. The internal assessment, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay all sit on school deadlines that do not shift for a tutor change. IB Gram supports students from Grade 1 to Grade 12, and for candidates aiming at the May 2026 or November 2026 sessions the honest advice is to hand over early in a term rather than after the first mock result arrives.

Younger DP cohorts have the luxury of planning. A DP2 student in February does not.
items: PYP: routine and attention span transfer, paperwork rarely does
MYP: the marked criterion strand is the handover document
DP: IA, EE and TOK deadlines override tutor convenience
Grade 1 to Grade 12 supported across the three programmes

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 38 and the Roads That Decide Your Timing
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 38 is defined by the movement around it. The Golf Course Road corridor pulls traffic north east, Sohna Road pulls it south, and the older South City 1 grid feeds in from the west. A tutor travelling from DLF Phase 5 or Sector 57 reaches the sector comfortably at four in the afternoon and painfully at seven. That single fact shapes more arrangements here than subject preference does.

Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and neighbouring communities, depending on tutor schedules. Nirvana Country, South City 1, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, Sector 50 and Sector 65 all sit inside a plausible travel band for tutors who already work the central sectors.

Plausible is doing real work in that sentence. A tutor living in Sector 65 and teaching in Sector 38 at eight in the evening has committed to a return journey that will eventually be renegotiated, usually in the middle of exam term. Parents comparing options for IB tuition near Sector 38 tend to do better by fixing the hour first and the mode second.

Online tutoring remains available across Gurugram for all supported IB subjects, and that is precisely what keeps the late slots survivable for everyone involved.
items: Golf Course Road and Sohna Road frame the sector's traffic
South City 1 and Nirvana Country are short hops west
Sector 50 and Sector 65 reachable, though not at peak hours
Fix the weekly hour before choosing home or online

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Both for Sector 38 Students
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring earns its cost in two situations. The first is a younger student who needs an adult physically present to keep the session moving. The second is a DP candidate in the final stretch before an exam session who benefits from a fixed appointment that cannot be quietly skipped. Presence creates accountability a screen does not manufacture on its own.

Online tutoring wins on match quality. If a student needs Math AI HL rather than AA, or Physics taught by someone who has recently supervised internal assessments, the number of such people who can also drive into the central sectors on a Wednesday evening is small. An IB online tutor Sector 38 Gurugram arrangement removes the travel constraint and widens the pool considerably.

Most families here settle on a mix. Weekly online teaching, then one longer home session a fortnight for supervised revision. During IA season the ratio often reverses.

The honest limitation is worth stating. Online works badly for a student who will not keep a camera on, will not write during the session, and has no adult within earshot. If that describes a fourteen year old in your house, IB home tuition in Sector 38 Gurugram is the safer purchase even at a higher fee and a narrower subject match.
items: Home: younger students, supervised revision, unmissable appointments
Online: rare subject levels, late slots, wider specialist pool
Hybrid: weekly online teaching plus fortnightly home revision
Online fails without a camera on and a pen moving

contentBlocks.heading: What IB Gram Checks Before a Name Reaches You
contentBlocks.body:
Verification here means a defined set of checks rather than a badge on a profile. Identity is confirmed. Qualifications are requested and examined. Teaching history is discussed in enough detail that a tutor claiming several years of DP Chemistry can describe how an internal assessment is moderated and what a supervisor may and may not do to a draft. Subject level claims are separated from subject claims, because comfort with Math AI SL does not imply readiness for AA HL.

References are asked for where a tutor has prior school or tutoring experience. Where they cannot be produced, that gap is noted rather than smoothed over.

What the process cannot do is predict chemistry between one tutor and one particular fifteen year old, or measure patience under deadline pressure. Those appear in the first month or not at all. So the more useful safeguard is the review point. After roughly four weeks you should be able to name something specific that changed: a criterion the school now marks higher, a paper section the student finishes in time, a topic that no longer needs explaining twice.

If you cannot name it, ask for a different tutor. That request is routine and should not require an argument.
items: Identity and qualification documents checked before shortlisting
Subject level claims verified separately from subject claims
References requested; missing ones recorded, not hidden
Four week review built around one named, specific change

contentBlocks.heading: Where Tutoring Cannot Help, and Saying So Early
contentBlocks.body:
Some situations make a tutor the wrong purchase. A student missing school regularly needs that addressed before anything else. A DP2 candidate who has not begun an Extended Essay in February faces a deadline problem rather than a teaching problem, and the sensible first move is a conversation with the school coordinator. A child who freezes in assessments to the point of distress may need support of a kind that tutoring does not provide, and adding two more evening hours can make that worse.

No one can guarantee a grade in the Diploma Programme, and a tutor who offers a specific score is telling you something about their judgement rather than their ability. IB Gram does not publish success percentages because the platform cannot verify them, and an unverifiable number is worth nothing to a parent making a decision.

What can be described honestly is process. How a shortlist is assembled. What a first session covers. What a monthly review contains. Whether a tutor is genuinely free at the hour you need.

Fees depend on level, subject and mode, and are discussed openly before anything is booked. Anyone hunting for the best IB tutor Sector 38 parents can find should expect all of that in writing.
items: Attendance and wellbeing problems come before subject tutoring
No guaranteed scores and no published success percentages
Fees vary by level, subject and mode, quoted before booking
Process described in writing, outcomes never promised

contentBlocks.heading: Starting a Sector 38 Gurugram Tutor Search This Week
contentBlocks.body:
Begin with the smallest useful message. Year group, the programme the school runs, subjects with levels, the two time windows that genuinely work each week, and one line about what went wrong previously if a tutor has already been tried and dropped.

An advisor reads that, asks two or three follow up questions, and returns a shortlist rather than a catalogue. Home options across the central sectors can be reviewed against tutor schedules, and online options are placed beside them so you compare rather than guess. Nobody benefits from a family discovering in week five that the commute was never realistic.

A first session is then arranged, subject to tutor availability. It should finish with a plan you can read in under a minute: what gets covered over four weeks, which assessment that maps to, and what evidence you should expect to see by the end of it.

If the fit is wrong, say so quickly. Changing in week two costs a fortnight. Changing in week ten costs a term, and in DP that is the difference between fixing an internal assessment and submitting whatever exists on the day.
items: Send year group, subjects, levels and two workable time windows
Mention the previous tutor and why the arrangement ended
Compare home and online quotes side by side
Expect a readable four week plan after session one

faqs.question: Our previous tutor stopped mid-term. What should we ask a new one to do first?
faqs.answer: Ask them to read before they teach. The first session should cover the school's most recent written feedback, the current state of any internal assessment, and the marks already recorded for the term. A tutor who opens with a fresh diagnostic test and ignores the existing paper trail is repeating work your child has already done once. Expect the tutor to tell you within two sessions which specific criterion or paper section they intend to attack first, and roughly how long they think that will take to show up in school marks.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IB home tutor start in Sector 38?
faqs.answer: It depends on subject, level and the hour you need. Common requests such as MYP mathematics or DP Economics at a mid-evening slot usually move faster than a request for a specific HL science at eight in the evening. Home availability across the central sectors can be reviewed against current tutor schedules, and an introductory session is arranged subject to that availability. Where the home slot proves difficult, an online start the same week is often possible while a suitable home tutor is confirmed for later in the term.

faqs.question: Is Sector 38 easy for tutors to reach in the evening?
faqs.answer: Reachable, though not at every hour. Tutors coming from Sushant Lok, South City 1 or Nirvana Country manage the trip comfortably. Journeys from Sector 65 or the far end of Sohna Road get slow after about half past six, and a slot that ignores this tends to unravel by the second month. The practical approach is to name your two workable windows early, so an advisor can filter for tutors who already travel that route rather than tutors who are willing to try it once and then rethink.

faqs.question: How are fees for IB tuition near Sector 38 worked out?
faqs.answer: Fees vary with programme level, subject, teaching mode and how much preparation the tutor does outside sessions. HL sciences and Math AA HL usually sit higher than MYP subjects. Home sessions generally cost more than online ones because travel time is being paid for. Extended Essay or internal assessment mentoring may be quoted differently from weekly teaching, since the workload is uneven across a term. All of it is discussed before a session is booked, never afterwards on an invoice.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 4 and the school keeps mentioning criteria. Can a tutor work on that directly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually the fastest route to a better mark. MYP subjects are assessed against strands, and a student can know the content well while losing marks in investigation or communication. A tutor who reads the school's criterion feedback targets the weak strand instead of reteaching material the student already holds. Bring the last two marked assignments to the first session. They tell a tutor more in ten minutes than a general conversation about the subject will in an hour.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have any connection with Lancers International School or Scottish High International School?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform with no formal relationship to Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, Pathways World School, GD Goenka World School, or any other campus named on this page. Schools are mentioned only to describe the commuting and timetable patterns that shape tutoring around the central sectors. If a tutor suggests they hold inside knowledge of a school's marking or admissions, treat that as a warning rather than a selling point.

faqs.question: We are thinking of moving from Math AA HL to Math AI HL. Will tutoring make that switch painless?
faqs.answer: Painless, no. Manageable, often yes, if the decision is taken early in DP1. The two courses share less than parents expect: AI leans on modelling, statistics and technology use, and the assessment style differs accordingly. A tutor can map what carries across, identify the AI content that has not been covered, and build a catch-up sequence around the school's own order of teaching. Made late in DP2, the same switch becomes a serious risk and the school coordinator belongs in that conversation.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor supervise an Extended Essay and teach the subject?
faqs.answer: A tutor can support an Extended Essay, but the supervisor role belongs to the school and cannot be outsourced. What an external tutor does is help the student narrow a research question, plan a realistic reading list, structure the argument and hold to internal checkpoints. The writing stays the student's own, and any tutor offering to draft sections is putting an academic honesty case at risk. Combining subject teaching with essay mentoring in one tutor works well, provided the weekly time is split deliberately.

faqs.question: What if there is no visible progress after two months?
faqs.answer: Then something should change, and the conversation should be direct. Ask the tutor to show what has been covered against what was planned, and set that beside the school's marks for the same period. Sometimes the plan was right and the student is not doing the between-session work, which is a different problem with a different fix. Sometimes the match is simply wrong. Requesting a different tutor is a normal step and does not require a long justification or the end of a term.

h1: IB Tutors in Sector 39, Gurugram: Working Backwards From the Deadline
heroSubtitle: The IB year is a sequence of fixed dates: interim IA drafts, the TOK essay, mock weeks, then the session itself. Tutoring in Sector 39 works when it is scheduled against those dates rather than against a convenient evening, and reviewed each month.
introSummary: Families comparing IB tutors in Sector 39 Gurugram are usually reacting to a date rather than a subject. An interim internal assessment draft is due, mocks are six weeks away, or the May 2026 session has stopped feeling distant. IB Gram starts from that calendar: which assessment lands first, how many teaching weeks remain before it, and what a tutor can realistically finish inside them. Home sessions across the central sectors depend on tutor schedules. Online teaching runs across Gurugram for every supported subject and level.

contentBlocks.heading: Reading the Year Backwards From the Exam Session
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma Programme is not taught to a syllabus so much as to a sequence of submission dates. An interim internal assessment draft in one term. A TOK exhibition earlier than most parents expect. The Extended Essay checkpoints that schools set months ahead of the official deadline. Mock papers. And only then, at the end, the May or November session that everyone was actually thinking about.

So the useful first question for anyone comparing IB tutors in Sector 39 Gurugram is not who is available on Thursday. It is which of those dates arrives next, and how many teaching weeks stand between now and it.

Sector 39 sits in the central residential band of the city, with the Golf Course Road corridor to one side and the older South City area on the other. Households around The Aralias, The Magnolias, Suncity and Mayfield Garden share a common pattern: long school days, a bus that returns later than the timetable suggests, and evening activities that already claim two or three slots a week.

IB Gram builds the tutoring plan against the assessment calendar first and fits it into that evening pattern second. Doing it the other way round produces a comfortable schedule that misses the thing it was bought for.
items: Next submission date established before any tutor is suggested
Teaching weeks counted, not assumed
Mock weeks treated as a hard boundary in the plan
May 2026 and November 2026 sessions planned in reverse

contentBlocks.heading: What Each Subject Actually Asks of a Sector 39 Student
contentBlocks.body:
Marks are lost in specific places, and they differ by subject. In Math AA HL the common failure is not topic ignorance but method selection under time pressure: the student recognises the calculus but reaches for the longer route and runs out of paper time. Tutoring for that looks like timed sets and a deliberate rehearsal of which technique to reach for, not another explanation of the theory.

Math AI HL punishes something different. The modelling questions reward a student who can justify why a function family suits a data set, and technology use has to be shown rather than assumed.

Physics and Chemistry papers separate students on command terms. Explain, describe, deduce and justify each carry a different mark expectation, and a strong answer to the wrong verb still scores badly. Any IB science tutor Sector 39 families engage should be drilling that vocabulary alongside the content.

Economics lives on diagram accuracy and evaluation depth. English A rests on close reading that survives being questioned. An IB maths tutor Sector 39 request and an English A request therefore need different tutor profiles even at the same grade level.
items: Math AA HL: timed method selection, not extra theory
Math AI HL: justified modelling choices and visible technology use
Sciences: command term vocabulary drilled with content
Economics: diagram precision plus genuine evaluation
English A: close reading that holds up under questioning

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Timelines for Sector 39 Families
contentBlocks.body:
Each programme has its own rhythm, and the tutoring that suits one can be actively unhelpful in another.

In the Primary Years Programme the calendar is loose. There is no external deadline, and the risk is the opposite: turning inquiry-based learning into worksheet drilling because that is easier to measure at home. Support for a Grade 2 or Grade 5 student should follow reading fluency, number sense and confidence in explaining thinking aloud.

The Middle Years Programme introduces fixed internal dates. Interdisciplinary units, the Personal Project in MYP 5, and criterion-marked assessments that repeat across the year. A tutor here earns their fee by teaching a student to read the criteria before writing, which most fourteen year olds will not do unprompted.

The Diploma Programme is where dates dominate. Two years, six subjects, an Extended Essay, TOK and CAS running underneath. IB Gram supports Grade 1 through Grade 12, and the practical advice for DP families is to book against the school's internal deadline rather than the official one, because the school deadline is the one that actually binds. Parents often discover the difference only after a term has gone.
items: PYP: fluency and confidence, no external deadline pressure
MYP: criteria read before writing, Personal Project in MYP 5
DP: school internal deadlines bind earlier than official ones
Grade 1 to Grade 12 supported across all three programmes

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between Home and Online in Sector 39 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Mode should follow the task, not habit. Work that needs a student writing under supervision, marking their own paper against a scheme, and being stopped mid-error, tends to go better in person. That is a strong argument for IB home tuition Sector 39 Gurugram families arrange during mock preparation, when the point of the session is discipline as much as content.

Work that needs a specialist goes better online. There are only so many people teaching Math AI HL or a specific HL science who are also willing to reach the central sectors by seven in the evening. An IB online tutor in Sector 39 Gurugram arrangement removes travel from the equation and widens the choice, which matters most for subjects with a thin local pool.

A blunt caveat about the hybrid model, which suits many families: two tutors for one subject rarely works. Two tutors for two subjects is fine. Splitting a single subject between a home tutor and an online specialist tends to produce contradictory advice on an internal assessment, and the student ends up mediating between adults instead of writing.

Pick one owner per subject. Add a second mode only for revision supervision.
items: In person for supervised writing and timed practice
Online for thin-pool subjects and late evening slots
One owner per subject, never two voices on one IA
Second mode used for supervision, not for teaching

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 39 Enquiry Becomes a Weekly Timetable
contentBlocks.body:
The intake conversation is deliberately narrow. Year group, programme, subjects with levels, the next assessment date, and the evening windows that survive a normal week. Parents often want to describe the whole history; an advisor will listen, but the four items above are what determine the shortlist.

From there, IB Gram filters for tutors whose recent teaching matches the level requested and whose free hours line up with yours. A tutor free at four in the afternoon is no use to a family whose child reaches home at twenty past five. That sounds obvious and is the single most common reason arrangements collapse in the first month.

You receive a small number of profiles, each with subject levels taught, assessment experience, and preferred session length. A first session can be arranged, subject to tutor availability.

The output of that session should be a timetable, not an impression. Which topics get covered in which weeks, which of them are needed for the next submission, and what gets deliberately left until after it. Anything a tutor cannot fit before the deadline should be named as such rather than promised quietly.
items: Four intake items: year, levels, next deadline, real windows
Tutor free hours matched against school return times
Profiles list assessment experience, not just subjects
Week-by-week timetable produced after session one
Work that will not fit before the deadline is named openly

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 39 on the Gurugram Map, and What Travel Costs You
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 39 has neighbours on every side that matter for scheduling. South City 1 and Nirvana Country lie close enough that a tutor working in either can reach the sector without rearranging their evening. DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 sit a short run north. Sector 50 and Sector 65 are further out along the Golf Course Extension and Sohna Road side, and the difference between a six o'clock and a seven o'clock start on those routes can be twenty five minutes.

Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities, depending on tutor schedules. Online tutoring remains available across Gurugram for all supported IB subjects.

For families weighing IB tuition near Sector 39, the honest framing is that travel is a fee you pay in either money or reliability. A tutor absorbing forty minutes each way will price it in, or will start cancelling in exam term when their own load rises.

Delhi, Noida and Faridabad tutors do teach Gurugram students, though almost always online. Treat any promise of a regular cross-city home visit with scepticism.
items: South City 1 and Nirvana Country: shortest realistic travel
DLF Phase 1 and Phase 4: manageable before evening peak
Sector 50 and Sector 65: viable earlier in the evening only
Delhi, Noida and Faridabad tutors: online in practice

contentBlocks.heading: The Checks Behind a Recommended Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
A recommendation is only worth what sits behind it, so the checks are specific. Identity documents are confirmed. Degree and teaching qualifications are requested and reviewed. Teaching history is probed in conversation rather than accepted from a form, and the questions are practical ones: how an internal assessment is moderated, what a supervisor is permitted to do with a draft, how a command term changes the shape of an answer.

Level claims are separated from subject claims. Someone who has taught MYP mathematics for years is not automatically ready for Math AA HL, and saying so early saves a family two wasted months.

References are requested where prior experience is claimed. Gaps get recorded rather than quietly dropped.

There is a limit to what any screening reveals. It cannot tell you whether a particular tutor will hold a distracted seventeen year old's attention at eight in the evening, or whether they stay calm three days before a submission. contentBlocks.heading: What Cannot Be Promised, and Why That Matters to You
contentBlocks.body:
A tutoring platform can honestly describe its process. It cannot honestly describe your child's result before the fact. So no score is promised here, no grade improvement is quoted, and no success percentage is published, because none of that can be verified and an unverifiable figure only makes a decision worse.

There are also cases where the answer is to spend less, not more. A DP2 student six weeks from mocks with five subjects in difficulty is over-committed, and adding tutoring in all five will reduce sleep before it raises marks. Choosing two is harder advice to hear and usually the correct one. A student who is not completing school work is signalling something that a Sunday evening session does not fix.

Fees vary by level, subject and mode and are quoted before anything begins.

What you can hold a tutor to is narrower and more useful: an agreed plan, visible session records, and a monthly conversation about whether the plan is being followed. Anyone searching for the best IB tutor in Sector 39 should judge on that, not on promises.

faqs.question: How far ahead of an internal assessment deadline should we bring in a tutor?
faqs.answer: A term ahead is comfortable, six weeks is workable, two weeks is damage control. With a full term available a tutor can work on the research question, the method and the analysis in sequence, which is where the marks actually sit. At six weeks the focus narrows to structure and evaluation of whatever data already exists. At two weeks a tutor can help a student finish and proofread honestly, and little more. Schools also set their own interim dates, so check those before deciding how urgent the situation really is.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the TOK essay and exhibition, or is that only the school's job?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help, within limits. TOK rewards clear knowledge questions, real examples and an argument that acknowledges its own weak points, and those are teachable skills. What an external tutor must not do is supply the argument or write the commentary. The prescribed titles come from the school and the assessment is the student's own work. Useful support looks like discussing candidate titles, stress-testing examples, and reading a draft for whether the knowledge question is genuinely being answered.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring practical in Sector 39, or should we assume online?
faqs.answer: Both are practical, with different constraints. Home sessions work well when the slot sits before evening traffic thickens and the tutor is already based nearby, in South City 1, Nirvana Country or the DLF phases. Later slots and specialist subject levels tend to be easier to fill online. Home availability across the central sectors depends on current tutor schedules and can be reviewed when you enquire. Many families here end up with online teaching through the week and an occasional in-person revision session.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and doing fine in school tests but badly in mocks. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because school tests cover a unit and mocks cover a year. The gap is rarely knowledge, it is retrieval and pacing across unrelated topics under a clock. Tutoring that helps here looks unglamorous: mixed past-paper sets, strict timing, and a habit of marking against the official scheme so the student sees where method marks were lost. Ask a prospective tutor how they run timed practice. If the answer is that they teach topics and set homework, they are not addressing the problem you described.

faqs.question: How is the fee for IB tuition near Sector 39 decided?
faqs.answer: Level, subject, mode and workload. Higher level sciences and Math AA HL generally sit above MYP subjects. In-person sessions carry the tutor's travel time. Extended Essay or internal assessment mentoring is often quoted separately from weekly teaching because it clusters around deadlines rather than spreading evenly across the term. Session length matters too: some subjects work better as one long weekly session than two short ones. Everything is discussed and agreed before the first paid session takes place.

faqs.question: Do you work with Pathways World School or GD Goenka World School directly?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and holds no partnership, endorsement or working relationship with Pathways World School, GD Goenka World School, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School or any other campus mentioned here. They are named only because commute times and internal deadline habits differ between them, and both affect how tutoring is scheduled. Tutors are matched on subject level and assessment experience, never on a claimed connection to a school.

faqs.question: We may switch a subject from HL to SL. Should tutoring wait until that is decided?
faqs.answer: No, though the plan should stay provisional. A tutor can work on the shared content while the decision is pending, since HL and SL overlap substantially in most subjects and the extra HL material is usually identifiable. What should wait is anything level-specific, such as HL-only extension topics or an internal assessment scope that assumes the higher level. Talk to the school coordinator quickly, because these changes have registration deadlines that sit well before the exam session.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two subjects, or is that a bad idea?
faqs.answer: It can work, particularly for related subjects such as Physics and Math AA, and it reduces the number of evenings a family has to protect. The problem appears when both subjects reach an assessment crunch in the same fortnight and one quietly gets less attention. If you do combine, agree in advance how the weekly time is split and review it monthly. For unrelated pairings, such as Chemistry and English A, separate tutors almost always give better depth.

faqs.question: What does a monthly review actually cover?
faqs.answer: It should be short and evidence-based. What was planned for those four weeks, what was actually covered, and what the school's own marks or feedback say for the same period. A tutor should be able to name one concrete change: a paper section now finished in time, a criterion marked higher, a topic no longer needing re-explanation. If the review turns into a general conversation about effort and attitude with nothing specific attached, that is a signal worth acting on rather than waiting out.

h1: IB Tutors in Sector 40, Gurugram: Judge the Match by Session One
heroSubtitle: Most parents cannot judge subject expertise from a profile. What they can judge is a first session: whether the tutor diagnosed something specific, wrote it down, and proposed a plan for the next four weeks that maps to the school's own marking.
introSummary: Parents comparing IB tutors in Sector 40 Gurugram often ask how to tell a good match from a confident one. The clearest test is the first session. A useful one ends with a written diagnosis, a named weakness tied to a criterion or paper section, and a plan for the following four weeks. IB Gram arranges that session after matching on subject level, programme stage and the evening slot your family can hold. Home options across the central sectors depend on tutor schedules; online teaching covers all supported subjects.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Good First Session Leaves Behind
contentBlocks.body:
Ninety minutes with a new tutor should produce something you can hold. Not a warm feeling about rapport, though that helps. A note naming what the student can already do, what they cannot, and which specific piece of assessment the weakness shows up in.

Weak first sessions look the same everywhere. The tutor talks for most of the hour, asks the student whether they understand, receives a yes, and books the next slot. Nothing has been measured. Four weeks later the parent is still guessing.

A stronger one is quieter. The tutor asks the student to attempt something, watches how they attempt it, interrupts at the point of error rather than at the end, and then asks to see the last two marked pieces of school work. By the close there is a sentence like this: he understands equilibrium but loses marks because he never justifies the direction of shift, and that costs him on the six mark questions.

That is what parents searching for IB tutors in Sector 40 Gurugram should be buying. Sector 40 sits in the central residential band with the Golf Course Road corridor on one side and the older South City area on the other, so most families have several options and no easy way to rank them. Session one is the ranking tool.
items: A written diagnosis, not a verbal impression
Student attempting work while the tutor watches
Last two marked school pieces reviewed
One named weakness tied to a mark scheme

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 40 Diagnostic Changes From PYP to DP
contentBlocks.body:
The same first session looks different depending on the programme, because the evidence available differs.

With a Primary Years Programme child, there is almost nothing written to examine. So the diagnostic is observational: how long they stay with a task, whether they read aloud fluently or decode word by word, whether they can explain a method rather than only produce an answer. A tutor working with a Grade 2 or Grade 4 student who arrives with a worksheet pack has misread the programme.

With a Middle Years Programme student there is real evidence, and it is criterion-shaped. A first session should involve reading the school's marked task alongside the rubric, then asking the student to explain why a strand scored what it did. Most cannot, and that gap is often the entire problem.

With a Diploma Programme student the evidence is heaviest: mock scripts, internal assessment drafts, predicted grade discussions, an Extended Essay in some state of progress. A DP diagnostic is closer to an audit. IB Gram works with students from Grade 1 to Grade 12, and the depth of that first hour rises steeply with the year group.
items: PYP: observation of fluency, attention and explanation
MYP: marked task read next to the criteria with the student
DP: mock scripts, IA drafts and EE progress audited
Grade 1 to Grade 12, with diagnostics scaled to the year

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 40 Gurugram and Its Immediate Neighbours
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 40 is surrounded by areas that supply most of its tutors. South City 1 and Nirvana Country are the closest in practical terms. DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 are a short run away, and the Golf Course Road corridor beyond them. Sector 50 and Sector 65 sit further along towards Sohna Road and the Golf Course Extension, reachable but slower once the evening thickens.

Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities, depending on tutor schedules. Online tutoring remains available across Gurugram for all supported IB subjects.

Households near The Aralias, The Magnolias, Suncity and Mayfield Garden tend to have gate and visitor procedures worth mentioning at booking. It sounds trivial. A tutor held at a gate for ten minutes every week loses close to an hour a term, and that time comes out of the session rather than out of their evening.

Tutors based in Delhi, Noida or Faridabad do teach students here, almost entirely online. A weekly cross-city home visit is a promise that tends not to survive the monsoon or exam season.

DLF Phase 1 and Phase 4: short run, easier before peak

contentBlocks.heading: The First Hour in Maths, Sciences, Economics and English A
contentBlocks.body:
Each subject has a diagnostic that works and several that waste time.

For Math AA HL, give the student three questions of rising difficulty and watch where the method stalls. A student who sets up correctly and errs in algebra has a different problem from one who cannot choose an approach at all, and the two need opposite kinds of teaching. Any IB maths tutor in Sector 40 who begins by lecturing on a topic before seeing the student work is guessing.

For Math AI HL, the first hour should include a small modelling task, because that is where the course actually differentiates students.

For Physics and Chemistry, take a marked six mark answer and rewrite it together against the command term. The gap is usually justification, not recall. An IB science tutor Sector 40 families keep tends to be the one who made that visible in week one.

Economics diagnoses through a diagram drawn from memory and then interrogated. English A diagnoses through a short passage read cold, where the tutor asks what the student notices before offering any reading of their own.

Math AI HL: a small modelling task in the first hour
Sciences: rewrite a marked six mark answer to the command term

English A: cold passage, student notices first

contentBlocks.heading: School Workload Patterns Around Sector 40

Students living here attend campuses spread across the city. Lancers International School on the Golf Course Road side and Scottish High International School in Sector 57 are the shorter journeys. Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School, further out towards the Sohna Road side, involve a longer bus route that ends the day later than the timetable implies.

That matters for the first session in a specific way. A student arriving home at half past five after ninety minutes on a bus is not going to give a useful diagnostic at six. Schedule the first session on a lighter day, or at a weekend, and accept a less convenient time in exchange for a more accurate picture.

Homework load also varies. Some campuses run continuous criterion-marked tasks through the term, others concentrate assessment into shorter windows, and a tutor should ask which pattern applies before proposing a weekly plan.

IB Gram is independent of every school named above. There is no partnership, no endorsement, and no privileged access to any school's marking or admissions. Tutors are matched on subject and assessment experience alone.

contentBlocks.heading: Turning a Sector 40 Enquiry Into Two or Three Names
contentBlocks.body:
Matching runs before the first session, and its job is to make that session worth booking. An advisor asks for the year group, the programme, the subjects with levels, what has already been tried, and the evening windows that genuinely exist. Families sometimes offer a wide window to seem easy to accommodate. That backfires. A precise window produces a better match than a generous one.

IB Gram then filters for tutors who have recently taught at that level, whose free hours overlap yours, and who are willing to run a diagnostic first session rather than start teaching immediately. Not every tutor works that way, and the ones who do are usually worth waiting a week for.

You receive a small shortlist with what each tutor has taught, at what level, and how they structure an opening session. A first session is arranged subject to tutor availability.

If the diagnosis that comes back is vague, ask for it again in writing. A tutor who cannot name the weakness specifically has not found it, and four more weeks will not change that on their own.

Filtered for recent teaching at the exact level
Tutors who run a diagnostic opening session preferred

First session arranged subject to tutor availability

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions, Online Sessions and the Sector 40 Commute
contentBlocks.body:
For a first session specifically, in person has an advantage. A tutor sitting beside a student sees hand movement, hesitation and the moment attention drops, and those are diagnostic signals a video call flattens. If an IB home tutor Sector 40 Gurugram slot is available for the opening session, it is usually worth taking even if the ongoing arrangement later moves online.

After that, the calculation shifts. Online widens the pool of specialists considerably, particularly for HL sciences, Math AI and anything needing recent assessment experience. It also survives traffic, rain and the tutor's own exam-term workload in a way home visits do not.

Costs differ as well. Home sessions price in travel; online generally does not.

One honest limitation, since it comes up often. Online is a poor fit for a student who will not write during the session or who needs an adult present to stay on task. Buying an excellent online specialist for a distracted thirteen year old with no supervision at home is a common and expensive mistake. Presence beats expertise at that age. Later, the balance reverses.
