Ongoing teaching often better online for HL specialists
Home sessions carry travel cost, online usually does not
Younger or distracted students need presence over expertise

contentBlocks.heading: Promises That Should Make You Slow Down
contentBlocks.body:
Some claims are worth treating as warnings. A promised score. A quoted percentage improvement. A tutor who says a grade is assured with enough sessions. None of that can be substantiated by anyone, and a person willing to say it once will say other convenient things later, usually when a deadline slips and an explanation is needed.

IB Gram publishes no success rates and no student statistics, for the same reason: they cannot be verified, and an unverifiable number is worse than no number because it feels like information.

Be careful too with the offer to help heavily on an internal assessment or Extended Essay. Support means questioning, structuring and reading drafts. It does not mean writing, and a tutor blurring that line is exposing the student to an academic honesty investigation that no mark is worth.

Fees depend on subject, level and mode, and should be settled before the first session rather than discussed afterwards. What a family looking for the best IB tutor Sector 40 can legitimately demand is a described process, a written plan, and a straightforward route to changing tutor if the match does not hold.
items: Promised scores and quoted improvements are warning signs
No published success rates or student statistics
IA and EE support means questioning, never writing
Fees agreed before session one, tutor changes available on request

contentBlocks.heading: Evidence a Parent Can Reasonably Ask For
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor is recommended, identity is confirmed and qualifications are requested and reviewed. Teaching history is discussed rather than accepted on paper, with practical questions about assessment: how internal assessment moderation works, what a supervisor may do with a draft, how command terms shape a mark scheme. Claims about level are checked separately from claims about subject, since teaching a subject at one level says little about readiness at another.

References are asked for where prior experience is claimed, and missing ones are recorded rather than glossed over.

You are entitled to ask directly as well. Which levels have you taught in the last two years. Have you worked with an internal assessment through to submission. What does your first session look like. A tutor comfortable with those questions is usually comfortable with the job.

Screening still cannot predict fit. So treat the first month as the real test, and use the four week review to check whether the diagnosis from session one has turned into something visible in school marks or teacher feedback. If it has not, changing tutor is a reasonable next step, not a failure.
items: Identity and qualification documents reviewed before recommendation
Assessment knowledge probed in conversation
Ask directly which levels were taught in the last two years
Four week review against school marks or teacher feedback

contentBlocks.heading: Arranging a First Session From Sector 40 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Send four things. The year group and programme, the subject list with levels, the two evening windows that reliably work, and one line about what prompted the search this month. If a previous tutor did not work out, say why in a sentence, because that is often the most useful line in the whole message.

An advisor comes back with a short shortlist rather than a directory, covering what each tutor has taught and how they open an arrangement. That list is short on purpose, because comparing eight profiles takes longer than trying one. Home availability across the central sectors is reviewed against current tutor schedules, and online options are quoted alongside so the comparison is honest.

Then book the first session and judge it on what it produces. A named weakness. A written four week plan. A clear statement of what will not be covered in that time, which is the part most tutors skip and the part that prevents an argument in March.

If the session produces none of those, ask for a different tutor before a routine forms. Two weeks in, that is a small correction. Two months in, it is a lost term.
items: Send year group, levels, two windows and the reason for searching
Expect a shortlist, not a directory of profiles
Judge session one on the diagnosis it produces
Change tutor early if the plan never arrives in writing

faqs.question: What should we actually receive after the first tutoring session?
faqs.answer: A short written summary. It should name what the student did during the session, one or two specific weaknesses tied to a criterion or paper section, and a plan for the next four weeks including what will deliberately be left out. Two sentences of encouragement is not a summary. If the tutor prefers to speak rather than write, ask for a message afterwards confirming the same points, because a plan you cannot re-read is a plan you cannot check against later.

faqs.question: Should we sit in on the first session?
faqs.answer: For a younger child, yes, at least partly, since you will learn how the tutor handles frustration and whether they let the child think. For a teenager, usually no. Most fifteen and sixteen year olds perform for a watching parent and hide what they do not know, which defeats the purpose of a diagnostic. A reasonable compromise is to be present for the first ten minutes and the last five, then leave the middle to them and read the written summary afterwards.

faqs.question: Is it normal to pay for a first session that is mostly diagnosis?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is generally money well spent. A proper diagnostic takes preparation and produces a written output, so tutors reasonably charge for it. Some offer a shorter introductory session at a reduced rate, subject to availability. What should concern you is the opposite: a tutor who skips diagnosis entirely to start teaching immediately, because that session feels productive and usually is not. Fees for the first session are agreed before it happens, alongside the ongoing rate.

faqs.question: How soon can an IB home tutor start in Sector 40?
faqs.answer: It depends on the level and the hour requested. Mid-evening slots for MYP subjects or DP Economics generally fill faster than a late slot for a specific higher level science. Home availability across the central sectors is reviewed against current tutor schedules when you enquire, and the first session is arranged subject to that availability. Where the home slot needs time to arrange, starting online in the same week is often possible, then moving in person once a suitable tutor is free.

faqs.question: My child says the tutor explains well but marks are unchanged. What now?
faqs.answer: Explaining well and teaching well are different things. A student can enjoy clear explanations and still lose marks because they never practise under exam conditions or never read the mark scheme. Ask the tutor what the student has produced, not what has been covered: completed past papers, marked drafts, timed sections. mainEntity.name: What should we actually receive after the first tutoring session?

acceptedAnswer.text: A short written summary. It should name what the student did during the session, one or two specific weaknesses tied to a criterion or paper section, and a plan for the next four weeks including what will deliberately be left out. Two sentences of encouragement is not a summary. If the tutor prefers to speak rather than write, ask for a message afterwards confirming the same points, because a plan you cannot re-read is a plan you cannot check against later.

mainEntity.name: Should we sit in on the first session?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a younger child, yes, at least partly, since you will learn how the tutor handles frustration and whether they let the child think. For a teenager, usually no. Most fifteen and sixteen year olds perform for a watching parent and hide what they do not know, which defeats the purpose of a diagnostic. A reasonable compromise is to be present for the first ten minutes and the last five, then leave the middle to them and read the written summary afterwards.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal to pay for a first session that is mostly diagnosis?

What should concern you is the opposite: a tutor who skips diagnosis entirely to start teaching immediately, because that session feels productive and usually is not. Fees for the first session are agreed before it happens, alongside the ongoing rate.

h1: IB Tutors in Sector 42 Gurugram
heroSubtitle: Sector 42 sits between Golf Course Road and South City, and that position shapes what tutoring is practical here. This page covers home sessions near The Aralias and Mayfield Garden, online options for rarer Diploma subjects, how tutors are screened, and what the first four weeks should look like.
introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 42 Gurugram support students from Grade 1 through Grade 12, across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes. Home tutoring may be possible near Golf Course Road, Sushant Lok and the surrounding sectors depending on tutor schedules, and online sessions run across the city for every supported subject. Requests from this pocket usually concern Math AA HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics or English A, plus internal assessment direction and revision planning for the May and November sessions.

contentBlocks.heading: What the school week looks like for Sector 42 students
contentBlocks.body:
A Sector 42 student's week is usually decided by two things: which school bus route they are on, and how many internal deadlines their teachers have stacked into the same fortnight. Families here sit close to Golf Course Road, so the schools in play are spread wide. Lancers International School is on Golf Course Road itself. Scottish High International School sits out at Sector 57. Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School pull students from across the Gurugram region, which means a long bus ride at both ends of the day.

That travel time is the real constraint on tutoring here. A Diploma Programme student getting home at half past four after an hour on the road has very little appetite for a session starting at five. Parents in The Aralias, The Magnolias, Suncity and Mayfield Garden usually end up asking for seven or half past seven, and that is the hour every other family in the neighbourhood wants too.

So the honest starting point for IB tutors in Sector 42 Gurugram is scheduling, not subject expertise. Expertise you can find. A specialist who is free at the exact hour your child can still concentrate is the harder half of the problem, and it is the half most parents discover only after three tutors have already declined the slot.
items: Grade 1 to Grade 12, PYP through DP
Bus journeys of 40 to 60 minutes for the further schools
Evening slots between 7pm and 8.30pm in heaviest demand
Scheduling decides matches more often than subject scarcity does

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 42, the Aralias belt and the roads in between
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 42 is one of the central sectors, close enough to Golf Course Road that a tutor coming from Sector 53 or Sector 54 can reach you in a quarter of an hour outside peak time and closer to forty minutes inside it. South City 1 is on one side. Nirvana Country and Sector 50 lie further along towards Sohna Road, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 to the north, and Sector 65 is a longer run down Golf Course Extension Road.

Those distances decide who will actually accept a home slot. A tutor living in DLF Phase 5 near The Crest will usually agree to Sector 42 on a weekday evening. The same tutor may turn down a six o'clock request in Sector 65 on the same day, because the return leg past Vatika Chowk is unpredictable enough to eat the following hour.

If you live in Suncity or Mayfield Garden you are in the easier part of this map. The Aralias and The Magnolias sit right on the Golf Course Road spine, which is well connected and slow at six.

Requests ask about nearby areas for a practical reason. A parent in South City 1 who will accept a tutor based near Sushant Lok gets a shortlist faster than one who insists on somebody living inside Sector 42 itself.
items: South City 1, Nirvana Country, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 within easy reach
Sector 50 and Sector 65 treated as separate trips by most tutors
Rapid Metro corridor near Sector 53 and Sector 54 helps non-driving tutors
Widening the accepted radius shortens the wait for a shortlist

contentBlocks.heading: Home visits on Golf Course Road, or an online slot nobody cancels
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring works well in Sector 42 when the subject is common and the slot is early. Mathematics up to MYP level, standard level Physics and Chemistry, English A, primary numeracy and reading: for these there are enough capable tutors living within a few kilometres that a weekly visit is realistic.

It stops being realistic in two situations. The first is a rare Diploma subject at higher level, where the pool of tutors across the whole of Gurugram is small and none of them may happen to live near Golf Course Road. The second is late-evening DP revision, where a half past eight start followed by a drive back through Sushant Lok is a poor trade for the tutor, and sessions start quietly getting rescheduled.

Online tutoring in those cases is not a consolation. A Math AA HL specialist working from Delhi or Noida can share a whiteboard, mark a past paper live while the student watches, and leave a recording behind for revision week. Rain on Golf Course Road cancels nothing.

Plenty of families here settle on a mix: a home visit once a fortnight for accountability, weekly online sessions for the teaching itself. That pattern tends to survive exam season better than a purely home arrangement does.
items: Home visits strongest for PYP and MYP subjects
Online preferred for scarce higher level Diploma specialists
Recorded sessions useful before mocks
Fortnightly home plus weekly online is a common compromise
Availability in any mode subject to tutor schedules

contentBlocks.heading: Which Sector 42 subject requests are hardest to fill
contentBlocks.body:
The requests arriving from this part of Gurugram cluster tightly. Math AA HL is the most common, usually from Grade 11 students who chose it with engineering or economics applications in mind and then met the proof and calculus content head on. Math AI HL comes next, and it is genuinely a different course: more modelling, more statistics, and a Paper 3 that rewards reading a long unfamiliar investigation carefully rather than recalling a technique quickly.

Physics and Chemistry requests divide between conceptual gaps and internal assessment trouble. A student can understand equilibrium perfectly and still design an IA with no controlled variable worth measuring. Those two problems need different session plans, and sometimes different tutors.

Economics tends to arrive in Grade 12, once the paper structure becomes real: definition, diagram, application to the stimulus, then evaluation that actually weighs one side against another. English A requests are about the individual oral and the comparative essay far more often than about reading the set texts.

Younger requests look nothing like any of this. A parent in Mayfield Garden with a Grade 3 child is usually asking for reading fluency and number sense, and the wrong answer is a worksheet routine that teaches an eight-year-old to dread sitting down with a book.
items: Math AA HL and Math AI HL are not interchangeable matches
Physics IA: uncertainties and variable control
Chemistry: equilibrium, energetics, organic mechanisms
Economics HL: evaluation and the quantitative paper
English A: individual oral and comparative essay
Primary requests centre on fluency, not syllabus

contentBlocks.heading: From your first message to a tutor sitting at your table
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is short, and it helps to know it before you send anything.

One. You give the grade, the programme, the subject and level, and the two or three evening slots that genuinely work. Slots matter far more than parents expect them to.

Two. An advisor reads the request and asks the questions that change the match. Is this a gap in understanding or a gap in producing the assessment? Is there a school deadline inside the next fortnight? Has a tutor already been tried, and what exactly went wrong?

Three. We check who is free for that subject, at that level, in that window. If nobody able to reach Sector 42 fits, we say so and offer an online specialist rather than sending a weaker local option to look responsive.

Four. A shortlist arrives, each name carrying subject background, IB teaching experience and the modes on offer. Availability stays subject to tutor schedules and can be reviewed if your timings change.

Five. The first session is diagnostic. The tutor should come back to you with what the student can already do, what is missing, and a plan for the coming month.

By week four you should see homework being started earlier and school feedback beginning to shift. If neither has moved, say so and the match gets changed.
items: Six details make a complete request
Advisor reads every request before any names go out
Shortlist shows subject background and IB experience
First session diagnoses before it teaches
Four-week checkpoint on habits, not marks

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP ask for three different kinds of help
contentBlocks.body:
Primary Years students in Sector 42 need someone who can work inside the inquiry rather than against it. In practice that means reading, writing stamina and number sense built through short sessions, using the class unit as material instead of running a parallel textbook at home. Ages three to twelve covers an enormous range of attention spans, and a thirty-minute session often achieves more than an hour.

Middle Years is where most families first go looking. Students move to assignments where the command term decides the mark, and a child who understands the science can still score poorly for describing when the criterion asked for analysis. MYP tutoring is largely translation work: turning what the student knows into the form the criterion rewards. Grade 9 and Grade 10 also carry the personal project, which tests planning discipline more than subject knowledge.

Diploma students need specialists. Higher level content runs deep, the internal assessment carries real weight, the extended essay stretches across a year, and Theory of Knowledge asks for writing no other subject on the timetable teaches.

The three programmes are separate enough that a tutor who is excellent with one may be poorly suited to another. Asking a DP Physics specialist to teach MYP Grade 7 science rarely ends well for either of them.
items: PYP: short sessions, inquiry-linked, no worksheet packs
MYP: criterion language and command terms
Grade 10 personal project: planning support
DP: HL depth, IA, EE, TOK, exam strategy
Matching runs on programme plus task, not subject name

contentBlocks.heading: The Gurugram schools this Sector 42 page is written around
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 42 families are spread across several IB schools rather than concentrated in one. Lancers International School on Golf Course Road is the nearest of the ones we see most often. Scottish High International School in Sector 57 draws students from the whole Golf Course Extension corridor. Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School sit further out across the Gurugram region and towards Sohna Road, so students there spend real time on the bus each way.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. They are named here because the school changes the tutoring, not to suggest any relationship.

It changes it in concrete ways. Schools differ on when the internal assessment draft falls due, how much drafting and feedback a teacher may give, and whether Theory of Knowledge is timetabled weekly or delivered in blocks. A tutor who has worked with students from your child's school already knows which of those applies, and will not build a four-week plan that runs straight into a school draft deadline.

When you send a request, name the school. After subject and level it is the single most useful line on the form.
items: Lancers International School, Golf Course Road
Scottish High International School, Sector 57
Pathways World School, Gurugram region
GD Goenka World School, Sohna Road side
Independent platform, no school affiliation claimed

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before we send you a name
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is deliberately unglamorous. The aim is to look at what somebody has actually taught rather than what they say they could teach.

The subject and level claim goes first. Teaching Math AA HL is not the same as holding a mathematics degree, and an applicant whose experience is board-syllabus mathematics is not put forward for a higher level Diploma request. Where the work involves an internal assessment or extended essay mentoring, we look for evidence the tutor has supervised that particular task before, because the criteria are the job rather than a formality attached to it.

Identity and qualification documents are collected. References from earlier families are contacted where those families are willing. A structured conversation covers how the tutor handles a student who is behind, how often they report back to parents, and what they do when a school deadline and their own plan disagree.

None of this is a promise about outcomes. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and one who offers to is describing something outside their control.

What screening buys you is a shorter list of people who have done this specific work before, so that the first hour can be spent diagnosing rather than discovering.
items: Subject and level experience checked against IB teaching, not qualification alone
IA, EE and TOK requests need prior supervision evidence
Identity and qualification documents collected
References contacted where available
No tutor counts, ratings or outcome claims published

contentBlocks.heading: Where tutoring in Sector 42 stops being the answer
contentBlocks.body:
There are situations in which hiring a tutor is not the right move, and hearing that now is cheaper than hearing it in March.

If a Grade 12 student begins in January before a May session with substantial gaps across three higher level subjects, tutoring can improve exam technique and rescue particular topics. It cannot rebuild two years in four months. The realistic conversation is about triage: which papers hold the most recoverable marks, which subject to protect, what to accept losing.

If attendance is the problem, or sleep is, or the student is carrying something heavier than a syllabus, a tutor is not the intervention. Say that early and you will hear the same back.

And if a student already works hard, understands the material and simply wants to be stretched, weekly tutoring may be less useful than fortnightly sessions built around past papers and marked feedback. Paying for four sessions a month where two would do is a quiet and common waste in this part of the city.

We would rather match fewer families well. A tutor who turns out to be the wrong fit can be changed, and a request can be paused when the term calms down.
items: Late DP starts get triage, not full coverage
Sleep, anxiety and attendance issues need other help first
Strong students often need fewer sessions, not more
Matches can be changed and requests paused

contentBlocks.heading: Starting a Sector 42 request this week
contentBlocks.body:
Send the grade, the programme, the subject and level, your child's school, and the two or three evening slots that realistically work once the bus has got home. Those few lines are enough for an advisor to tell you something useful straight away.

What comes back is an assessment rather than a brochure. If a tutor for that subject and level can reach Sector 42 inside your window, you get names along with their teaching background and the modes they offer. If not, you are told that plainly, together with an online specialist option and the reason the online route is likely to be steadier for that particular subject.

Home tutoring near The Aralias, Suncity, Mayfield Garden and the surrounding sectors depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed if your timings shift later in the term. Online sessions run across Gurugram for all supported subjects.

Nothing is committed before the first session. If the fit is wrong, say so and the match changes. If the term settles and you want to pause, pause. Beginning a conversation now about a May 2026 session costs nothing and usually prevents a scramble in February.
items: Grade, programme, subject, level, school, slots
Straight answer on home feasibility near Golf Course Road
Online options across Gurugram for all supported subjects
No commitment before the first session

faqs.question: What do IB tutors in Sector 42 Gurugram usually charge?
faqs.answer: There is no single figure. Fees depend on the programme, the subject, the level, and whether the tutor travels to you. A Diploma higher level specialist in Math AA or Physics costs more per hour than MYP science support, and a home visit near Golf Course Road carries the tutor's travel time inside it even when that is not itemised. Online sessions with the same person are usually lower. Ask for the range at shortlist stage rather than after the first session, and ask how many sessions a month the tutor genuinely thinks are needed.

faqs.question: My child is at Scottish High in Sector 57 but we live in Sector 42. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It changes more than the address does. Schools in Gurugram set internal assessment deadlines at different points and allow different amounts of drafting, so a tutor who has already worked with students from that school knows the rhythm your child is on. The Sector 57 commute matters too: if your child reaches home at five, a six o'clock start is optimistic and will be missed often. Give us the school and the usual arrival time. IB Gram is not affiliated with any school, but the school name is one of the most useful details in a request.

faqs.question: How late in the evening will a home tutor come to Sector 42?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect, though the trade-off is real. Tutors will often take a half past seven or eight o'clock slot here because Golf Course Road eases somewhat by then. Beyond about half past eight the return journey starts making the arrangement fragile, and fragile arrangements collapse during exactly the weeks you need them most. For late Diploma revision, a nine o'clock online session is more dependable than a home visit at a quarter to nine. Availability at any hour remains subject to tutor schedules and can be reviewed.

faqs.question: Is Math AI HL an easier option than Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: No, it is different rather than easier. Analysis and Approaches leans on algebraic fluency, proof and calculus, and rewards students who manipulate expressions quickly. Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling, statistics and reading real contexts, with a Paper 3 that asks you to work through an extended unfamiliar investigation under time pressure. Students who struggle with abstraction sometimes do better in AI, and students who dislike long written interpretation sometimes find AA cleaner. University entry requirements should drive the choice more than perceived difficulty. A tutor can help you compare the two before any switch.

faqs.question: We only want help with the internal assessment. Is that enough work for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common request in Grade 11 and Grade 12. Internal assessment mentoring is a defined piece of work: choosing a question that can actually be investigated, planning the method or the data collection, understanding what each criterion rewards, and drafting within the school's rules on feedback. It usually runs across four to eight sessions rather than a full year. The tutor supports the process and writes none of it. If the student later needs content teaching as well, that can be added, but the two do not have to be bundled together.

faqs.question: What if the tutor and my child simply do not get on?
faqs.answer: Tell us early. A poor fit shows up within the first two or three sessions, usually as a student who goes quiet or a tutor who talks through the whole hour. That is a matching problem rather than a judgement about either person, and it is far easier to fix in week two than in week eight. We will ask what specifically did not work, because the answer changes who we suggest next. A student who needs a patient rebuilder and a student who needs to be pushed hard rarely thrive with the same tutor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work with my Grade 4 child without turning it into worksheets?
faqs.answer: That is the right worry to have. Primary Years support should sit inside the inquiry your child is already doing at school rather than running a parallel worksheet programme alongside it. Good sessions at that age are short, mostly spoken, and built around reading together, talking about what was read, and number work that comes out of something real. Progress looks like a child picking up a book unprompted. If a tutor's opening plan is a printed pack for a Grade 4 student, ask what it is for, and tell us if the answer is thin.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect to see something change?
faqs.answer: Four weeks is a fair first checkpoint. By then you should see homework being started earlier, fewer panicked evenings before a deadline, and a student who can explain what a question is asking before attempting it. Marks usually move later than habits do, particularly in MYP where criterion language takes time to internalise. Nobody can promise a grade, and a tutor who does is not being straight with you. What you can reasonably expect is a tutor who tells you in plain terms what has improved and what has not yet.

faqs.question: We may move to DLF Phase 4 next year. Does the arrangement survive that?
faqs.answer: It usually does. DLF Phase 4 is close enough to Sector 42 that most tutors taking home visits in one will consider the other, although the evening slot may need to shift by half an hour. Moving further out, towards Sector 65 or the Sohna Road side, is a bigger change, and a tutor may prefer to continue online rather than lose an hour on the road each way. Tell us before the move rather than after it. Continuity with a tutor who already knows the student is worth protecting where it is possible.

A Diploma higher level specialist in Math AA or Physics costs more per hour than MYP science support, and a home visit near Golf Course Road carries the tutor's travel time inside it even when that is not itemised. Online sessions with the same person are usually lower. Ask for the range at shortlist stage rather than after the first session, and ask how many sessions a month the tutor genuinely thinks are needed.

mainEntity.name: My child is at Scottish High in Sector 57 but we live in Sector 42. Does that change anything?

acceptedAnswer.text: It changes more than the address does. Schools in Gurugram set internal assessment deadlines at different points and allow different amounts of drafting, so a tutor who has already worked with students from that school knows the rhythm your child is on. The Sector 57 commute matters too: if your child reaches home at five, a six o'clock start is optimistic and will be missed often. Give us the school and the usual arrival time. IB Gram is not affiliated with any school, but the school name is one of the most useful details in a request.

mainEntity.name: How late in the evening will a home tutor come to Sector 42?

acceptedAnswer.text: Later than most families expect, though the trade-off is real. Tutors will often take a half past seven or eight o'clock slot here because Golf Course Road eases somewhat by then. Beyond about half past eight the return journey starts making the arrangement fragile, and fragile arrangements collapse during exactly the weeks you need them most. For late Diploma revision, a nine o'clock online session is more dependable than a home visit at a quarter to nine. Availability at any hour remains subject to tutor schedules and can be reviewed.

mainEntity.name: Is Math AI HL an easier option than Math AA HL?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, it is different rather than easier. Analysis and Approaches leans on algebraic fluency, proof and calculus, and rewards students who manipulate expressions quickly. Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling, statistics and reading real contexts, with a Paper 3 that asks you to work through an extended unfamiliar investigation under time pressure. Students who struggle with abstraction sometimes do better in AI, and students who dislike long written interpretation sometimes find AA cleaner. University entry requirements should drive the choice more than perceived difficulty. A tutor can help you compare the two before any switch.

mainEntity.name: We only want help with the internal assessment. Is that enough work for a tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is a common request in Grade 11 and Grade 12. Internal assessment mentoring is a defined piece of work: choosing a question that can actually be investigated, planning the method or the data collection, understanding what each criterion rewards, and drafting within the school's rules on feedback. It usually runs across four to eight sessions rather than a full year. The tutor supports the process and writes none of it. If the student later needs content teaching as well, that can be added, but the two do not have to be bundled together.

mainEntity.name: What if the tutor and my child simply do not get on?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us early. A poor fit shows up within the first two or three sessions, usually as a student who goes quiet or a tutor who talks through the whole hour. That is a matching problem rather than a judgement about either person, and it is far easier to fix in week two than in week eight. We will ask what specifically did not work, because the answer changes who we suggest next. A student who needs a patient rebuilder and a student who needs to be pushed hard rarely thrive with the same tutor.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor work with my Grade 4 child without turning it into worksheets?

acceptedAnswer.text: That is the right worry to have. Primary Years support should sit inside the inquiry your child is already doing at school rather than running a parallel worksheet programme alongside it. Good sessions at that age are short, mostly spoken, and built around reading together, talking about what was read, and number work that comes out of something real. Progress looks like a child picking up a book unprompted. If a tutor's opening plan is a printed pack for a Grade 4 student, ask what it is for, and tell us if the answer is thin.

mainEntity.name: How quickly should we expect to see something change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four weeks is a fair first checkpoint. By then you should see homework being started earlier, fewer panicked evenings before a deadline, and a student who can explain what a question is asking before attempting it. Marks usually move later than habits do, particularly in MYP where criterion language takes time to internalise. Nobody can promise a grade, and a tutor who does is not being straight with you. What you can reasonably expect is a tutor who tells you in plain terms what has improved and what has not yet.

mainEntity.name: We may move to DLF Phase 4 next year. Does the arrangement survive that?

acceptedAnswer.text: It usually does. DLF Phase 4 is close enough to Sector 42 that most tutors taking home visits in one will consider the other, although the evening slot may need to shift by half an hour. Moving further out, towards Sector 65 or the Sohna Road side, is a bigger change, and a tutor may prefer to continue online rather than lose an hour on the road each way. Tell us before the move rather than after it. Continuity with a tutor who already knows the student is worth protecting where it is possible.

finalCta: Tell us the grade, the subject and level, the school, and the evenings that work. An advisor reads every request personally and replies with what is realistically available near Sector 42 and what is stronger online. First sessions are diagnostic, and the match can be changed if it turns out to be wrong.

h1: IB Tutors in Sector 43 Gurugram
heroSubtitle: Some families here plan a year ahead. Others call six weeks before a paper. Both are workable, but they need different tutors and different plans. This page sets out what each looks like in Sector 43, what a home visit costs you in travel, and when online is the steadier arrangement.
introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 43 Gurugram work with students from Grade 1 to Grade 12 in two fairly different ways: steady support across a school year, or concentrated preparation for a May or November session. Sector 43 lies among the central sectors near Golf Course Road and South City, so home tutoring may be possible depending on tutor schedules, while online sessions run across the city for every supported subject, including internal assessment guidance, extended essay mentoring and Theory of Knowledge.

contentBlocks.heading: Two ways families in Sector 43 arrive at this page
contentBlocks.body:
Requests from Sector 43 tend to take one of two shapes, and the difference matters more than the address does.

The first is the family that starts early. A Grade 11 student has picked higher level Chemistry and Math AA, term one has just finished, and the parent wants a weekly hour so the content does not stack up before the internal assessments arrive. Nothing is on fire. The work is pacing, past questions, and the slow habit of writing answers in the language examiners actually reward.

The second is the family calling in February with a May session ahead. Something has gone wrong in one subject, or in three. The plan there is triage rather than curriculum coverage.

Both are legitimate. They need different tutors, though. The first job suits someone patient who builds routine well. The second needs a specialist who knows which topics carry recoverable marks and is willing to be blunt about what will not be repaired in ten weeks.

Say which of the two you are in your first message. It saves a round of questions and it changes who we go looking for. Planning ahead of the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions is easier in September than in January, though a late start is still worth making.

Different tutor temperaments suit each
May 2026 and November 2026 sessions in scope

contentBlocks.heading: How a request from Sector 43 turns into a tutor
contentBlocks.body:
The process is short. What makes it work is the detail you put in at the start.

You send the grade, the programme, the subject and level, the school, and the times that are genuinely free. An advisor reads it. Where something is ambiguous, and it usually is, we ask: is the difficulty in understanding the content, or in producing the assessment? Has anything already been tried, and how did it end?

Availability is then checked against that exact combination. Subject, level, mode and hour together decide the answer. Plenty of capable tutors exist for Economics at higher level. Far fewer are free at eight on a Tuesday and willing to come into the central sectors.

A shortlist follows, each entry carrying teaching background and IB experience. Everything remains subject to tutor availability, and it can be reviewed if your schedule shifts mid-term.

The first session should be diagnostic. Expect the tutor to spend part of it finding out what the student can already do rather than teaching from the front. Afterwards you should receive a plain account of where the gaps are and what the next four weeks will cover.

If that account never arrives, chase it. It is the part that tells you whether the tutor is planning or improvising.
items: Content gap and assessment gap are diagnosed separately
Subject, level, mode and hour checked together
Shortlist carries teaching background, not marketing copy
Written summary expected after the first session

contentBlocks.heading: What changes between Grade 5, Grade 9 and Grade 12
contentBlocks.body:
A Grade 5 student in the Primary Years Programme is being taught to ask questions and follow them somewhere. Tutoring at that stage should protect that instinct. Reading aloud, talking about what was read, number work that comes out of a real situation. Sessions stay short because attention is short, and the age range runs from three to twelve, so what suits a nine-year-old will not suit a five-year-old.

By Grade 9 the Middle Years criteria have taken over. Marks now depend on whether the student analysed, evaluated or merely described, and the distance between knowing the science and scoring in the science becomes visible on every report. Much of the tutoring here is reading the command term properly and structuring an answer to it. The Grade 10 personal project adds a planning load that catches otherwise organised students off guard.

Grade 12 is another world entirely. Higher level content runs deep, the internal assessment is written or overdue, the extended essay is due, and Theory of Knowledge wants an essay unlike anything else on the timetable.

A tutor strong in one programme is not automatically useful in another. Matching runs against the programme and the specific assessment, not the subject name alone.
items: PYP ages three to twelve: fluency and curiosity
MYP criteria reward analysis over description
Grade 10 personal project is a planning test
DP ages sixteen to nineteen: HL depth plus IA, EE and TOK

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing between a tutor at your dining table and one on a screen
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring has one advantage that is hard to replicate. A student cannot quietly disengage with an adult sitting across the table. For younger children, and for teenagers who have learned to look attentive on a video call while doing very little, that alone can settle the question.

The cost is fragility. A home slot depends on one person's commute holding up on a weekday evening in Gurugram. Miss two in a month during a heavy term and the arrangement has stopped being weekly support.

Online removes the journey and widens the pool to the whole city and beyond, which matters most for uncommon higher level subjects. Screen-shared past papers, live marking and a recording the student can rewatch before a test are practical gains rather than compensations.

A hybrid pattern is worth considering if you cannot choose. One home visit a fortnight to keep the relationship real, weekly online sessions for content. Families near Suncity and Mayfield Garden use this often, because the evening slots they want are the same ones every neighbour wants.

Home tutoring in this part of Gurugram remains subject to tutor schedules, and it is worth asking about rather than assuming either way.
items: Presence beats convenience for younger and avoidant students
Home slots become fragile in heavy terms
Online widens the pool for uncommon HL subjects
Fortnightly home plus weekly online used widely near Suncity

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by subject, where the year usually goes wrong
contentBlocks.body:
Chemistry. Students keep pace until the mole concept and equilibrium arrive close together, and then the arithmetic starts hiding the concept. The internal assessment afterwards asks for a research question narrow enough to measure, and a broad one costs marks that no amount of laboratory skill recovers.

Physics. The mechanics is rarely the real problem. Uncertainties, graph analysis, and explaining a mechanism rather than describing an effect are where marks quietly disappear.

Math AA HL. The proof and calculus load in the second year is where students who coasted through Grade 10 algebra come unstuck. Math AI HL is not the softer choice either. Its Paper 3 investigation punishes anyone who has not practised reading long unfamiliar prompts calmly.

Economics. Diagrams get learned; evaluation does not. A Grade 12 student who can draw every diagram and still writes one-sided evaluation is the most common Economics request we receive.

English A. The individual oral and the comparative essay drive most requests, and the fix is usually about building an argument rather than reading more widely.

The younger end of Grade 1 to Grade 12 sits outside all of this. Those requests are about fluency, confidence and a child who has decided they are bad at something.
items: Chemistry: mole concept, equilibrium, narrow IA questions
Physics: uncertainties and graph analysis
Math AA HL proof and calculus in year two
Math AI HL Paper 3 investigation practice
Economics evaluation, not diagram recall
English A oral and comparative essay structure

contentBlocks.heading: School calendars around Gurugram and why they drive the timing
contentBlocks.body:
Students on this page attend a spread of IB schools rather than a single one. Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School sit out in the wider Gurugram region and towards Sohna Road. Lancers International School is on Golf Course Road. Scottish High International School is in Sector 57.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. They appear here because their calendars shape the tutoring, not to imply any relationship.

Each school sets its own internal deadlines inside the wider IB timetable: when the first internal assessment draft is expected, how many rounds of feedback a teacher may give, when mock exams land, whether Theory of Knowledge occupies a weekly period or a blocked week. A tutoring plan built without that information will collide with it.

So when a parent gives us the school, the first useful thing an advisor can do is avoid scheduling four weeks of content revision straight into a fortnight when the student already owes two drafts.

If your child's school is not one of those four, send the name anyway. The same reasoning applies, and a tutor who has taught students from that school will ask better questions in the first hour.
items: Draft deadlines and feedback rules vary by school
Mock exam weeks reshape any four-week plan
TOK timetabled weekly at some schools, blocked at others
School name requested for planning, not affiliation

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 43 sits, and how far a tutor will travel
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 43 belongs to the central group of sectors, with Golf Course Road on one side and South City on the other. The Aralias and The Magnolias are the landmarks most people use to place it, and Suncity and Mayfield Garden sit close by.

Around it, the practical radius for a home tutor covers South City 1, Nirvana Country, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4 and Sector 50. Sector 65 and the far end of Golf Course Extension Road are reachable, but tutors treat them as a separate trip and will price or schedule accordingly. Sushant Lok, Sector 53 and Sector 54 are close enough that tutors living there are usually willing without much persuasion.

Traffic decides the rest. A tutor coming from the Sohna Road side past Vatika Chowk at six faces a very different journey from the same trip at eight, which is why the slots that fill first are the ones nobody actually wants.

If you will accept a tutor from a neighbouring area rather than one living inside Sector 43, your shortlist gets longer and arrives sooner. Most families do not realise this is a choice they are quietly making.
items: Central sectors, Golf Course Road on one flank
South City 1, Nirvana Country, Sector 50 in easy radius
Sector 65 and Golf Course Extension treated as a separate run
Accepting neighbouring-area tutors speeds up matching

contentBlocks.heading: The limits of starting late
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor hired in March for a May session can do particular things well. Past-paper technique. Two or three high-yield topics. Cutting the marks lost to misread command terms. Calming a student enough that they sleep the night before Paper 1.

A tutor cannot cover two years of higher level content in eight weeks, and any promise that sounds like it might should make you suspicious. Nobody can guarantee a score, and a tutor who offers one is describing something they have no way of knowing.

Starting late narrows the field as well. February and March are when Diploma specialists are fullest, so the choice of tutor is smaller than it would have been in October, and the slots left are the awkward ones.

There is also a version of this that has nothing to do with timing. If a student is not sleeping, is anxious to the point of avoidance, or has stopped attending classes, tutoring is the wrong tool and adding hours makes it worse. We would rather say that than take the request.

The honest position is straightforward. Early support is cheaper, calmer and more effective. Late support is still worth doing. It is simply a narrower job with a narrower promise attached to it.
items: Late starts: technique, high-yield topics, triage
Specialist availability tightens in February and March
No score or grade promises from any tutor here
Anxiety and attendance problems need other support first

contentBlocks.heading: What we check, and what we refuse to claim
contentBlocks.body:
Checks happen before a name reaches you, and they are mostly about matching claims to evidence.

We confirm what the tutor has taught, at which level, and for how long. Somebody who has taught Economics to board students is not put forward for a higher level Diploma Economics request without evidence of IB teaching behind it. Where the request involves an internal assessment, an extended essay or Theory of Knowledge, we look for prior experience with that exact task, because those criteria are specialised and reading them once is not the same as having marked against them.

Identity documents are collected, and references are contacted where families are willing to give them. A structured conversation covers how the tutor handles a student who is behind, how often they report to parents, and what they do when the school's plan and their own disagree.

What we will not do is publish numbers this platform cannot support. No counts of tutors, no success rates, no invented ratings or reviews.

Screening reduces the risk of a wasted month. It does not remove your own job, which is to judge the first session honestly and say something if it was poor rather than waiting politely.
items: IB teaching experience treated separately from qualifications
IA, EE and TOK need task-specific track record
Documents collected, references contacted where offered
No published counts, rates or ratings

contentBlocks.heading: Booking ahead of the May and November sessions from Sector 43
contentBlocks.body:
A request takes a few minutes. Grade, programme, subject and level, school, and the evenings that are free. Add one line saying whether you want steady support or help before a specific session, because that single line changes the kind of tutor we look for.

An advisor replies with what is realistically available. If a home tutor for that subject can reach Sector 43 inside your window, you get names and backgrounds. If not, you are told plainly and offered online options covering the same subject at the same level across Gurugram.

Home tutoring near Suncity, Mayfield Garden, South City 1, DLF Phase 4 and the surrounding sectors depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed later in the term if your timings move.

Nothing is committed before the first session, and the match can be changed if it does not work. Families planning for the May 2026 session usually find September and October the easiest months in which to arrange things. Those working towards November 2026 have more room, and younger Diploma cohorts benefit from planning earlier still, particularly where a subject or level change is being considered.

Home feasibility answered plainly, online offered otherwise

Match changeable, request pausable

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring if the exam session is only a few months away?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the job changes. With ten to twelve weeks left, a tutor should be working from past papers and mark schemes rather than teaching a syllabus in order. Expect them to identify three or four topics where marks are genuinely recoverable and to spend real time on how answers are written, since command terms cost more marks than content gaps at that stage. Diploma specialists are also busiest in the months before a session, so the choice narrows. Send the request sooner rather than waiting for mock results to confirm what you already suspect.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma student actually need?
faqs.answer: Usually one or two per subject, and fewer than most parents assume. A student with three sessions a week across two subjects has very little time left to attempt problems alone, which is where the learning actually happens. A reasonable pattern for Grade 11 is one weekly session per difficult subject during term, rising temporarily around internal assessment deadlines and mocks. If a tutor recommends more than that from week one, ask what the extra hour is for. Frequency should follow the work in front of the student rather than fill a timetable.

faqs.question: Do higher level subjects cost more than standard level?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, because the pool of tutors who can teach a higher level Diploma subject well is smaller than the pool for MYP or standard level work. Math AA HL, Physics HL and Chemistry HL sit at the higher end. Travel affects it too, since a home visit into the central sectors includes the tutor's journey in practice even when nobody itemises it. Online sessions with the same tutor are usually lower. Ask for the range before the first session, and ask how many sessions the tutor believes are needed rather than only the hourly figure.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP and the school says effort is fine but the grades are not. What is going on?
faqs.answer: This is the most common MYP situation and it is rarely about effort. The criteria reward specific skills: analysing, evaluating, applying, communicating in a particular form. A student can revise thoroughly, understand the topic well, and still write a descriptive answer to a question that asked for evaluation. More content revision will not fix it. Practice at reading what the task demands and structuring a response to it will, using the school's own rubrics and the student's returned work. Four to six weeks of that usually shows in teacher feedback before it shows in grades.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor help with the Extended Essay and a subject at the same time?
faqs.answer: Often, but check the pairing carefully. If the extended essay sits in the same subject the tutor teaches, one person can handle both and the sessions reinforce each other. If it sits in a different subject, a separate mentor is usually better, because supervising an extended essay is about research questions, scope and argument structure rather than subject teaching. Either way the tutor supports the process and does not write it, and the school supervisor remains the authority on what is permitted. Availability for essay mentoring depends on the subject and on the time of year.

faqs.question: Are online IB tutors as good as someone who comes to Sector 43?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma subjects, yes, and occasionally better. Online widens the pool well beyond whoever happens to live near the central sectors, which matters when a subject is uncommon at higher level. Screen sharing, live annotation of a past paper and a recording to rewatch are real advantages. The weakness is attention. A younger child, or a student who avoids work, can drift on a call in a way they cannot with an adult at the table. For Grade 1 to roughly Grade 8 we usually suggest home tutoring first where a tutor is available.

faqs.question: What should I include when I first write to you?
faqs.answer: Six things. Grade and programme. Subject and level. The school. The two or three evening windows that are genuinely free. Whether you want ongoing support or help before a particular session. And a sentence about what has actually gone wrong, in your own words. That last item is the most useful part of any request we receive, because it separates a content gap from an assessment-writing gap, and those two need different tutors. Anything left out simply becomes a question we have to ask before the search can start.

faqs.question: We tried a tutor last year and it did not help. Why would this be different?
faqs.answer: It may not be, and asking is fair. Tell us what happened, in detail. A tutor who explained well but never set work is a different failure from one who was strict but did not know the syllabus, and each points towards a different next choice. Sometimes the problem was the format rather than the person, and a student who ignored a screen responds to someone in the room. Sometimes the timing was wrong and sessions were always the last thing in a very long day. We would rather change the variable that failed than repeat it.

faqs.question: Can you support a student in Sector 43 who is repeating a year or switching level?
faqs.answer: Yes, and both situations deserve a specific plan rather than ordinary weekly tutoring. A student moving from higher to standard level needs help identifying what is now out of scope and rebuilding confidence, which is often the larger problem of the two. A student repeating a year needs the opposite: enough new challenge that the second pass does not turn passive. In either case the school's guidance sets the boundaries and the tutor works inside them. Send the details of the change with the request so the first session starts from the right place.

Home tutoring depends on tutor schedules near Golf Course Road and the central sectors, while online covers every supported subject across the city. contentBlocks.heading: The short answer for Sector 44 parents
contentBlocks.body:
The plain version first. You can usually get an IB tutor at home in Sector 44 if the subject is reasonably common and your preferred hour is not the busiest one of the evening. If the subject is a higher level Diploma one and the slot is late, an online specialist will almost certainly be the better arrangement. Everything from Grade 1 to Grade 12 is in scope, internal assessment guidance and extended essay mentoring included, along with Theory of Knowledge.

That is the answer. The rest of this page is the reasoning behind it, because the reasoning is what lets you judge a shortlist instead of simply accepting one.

Sector 44 sits among the central sectors, with Golf Course Road on one side and South City on the other, and The Aralias, The Magnolias, Suncity and Mayfield Garden as the usual reference points. By Gurugram standards that location is unusually convenient for tutoring. It does not solve the two things that decide most matches, which are subject scarcity at higher level and the fact that every family in the neighbourhood wants the same two hours of the evening.

contentBlocks.heading: Six subjects that account for most Sector 44 requests
contentBlocks.body:
Math AA HL. Requests peak in the second half of Grade 11, when proof, calculus and heavier algebra arrive at once. Students who relied on pattern recognition through Grade 10 feel it first, and the repair work is fluency rather than new content.

Math AI HL. A different course, not a lighter one. Modelling and statistics dominate, and Paper 3 sets an extended investigation in an unfamiliar context, which rewards students who have practised reading long prompts without panicking.

Physics. Most marks are lost in uncertainties, graph work, and the gap between describing an effect and explaining a mechanism. The internal assessment needs a variable that can genuinely be controlled and measured with school equipment.

Chemistry. Equilibrium, energetics and organic mechanisms are the usual walls, and the IA needs a question narrow enough to produce a real data set.

Economics. Diagrams get learned; evaluation is what separates marks in Grade 12, and higher level students also carry a quantitative paper that punishes weak arithmetic under time pressure.

English A. The individual oral and the comparative essay drive most requests. Reading more rarely helps. Building an argument does.

Younger students want something else altogether: fluency, confidence, number sense.
items: Math AA HL: algebraic fluency and proof
Math AI HL: modelling, statistics, Paper 3 investigation
Physics: uncertainties and explanation over description
Chemistry: equilibrium, energetics, workable IA questions
Economics HL: evaluation plus the quantitative paper
English A: individual oral and comparative essay

contentBlocks.heading: What happens between your message and the first session
contentBlocks.body:
Five steps, in order.

You send the details: grade, programme, subject, level, school, and the hours that genuinely work. An advisor reads them and asks whatever is missing. The question that matters most is whether the student is struggling to understand the material or struggling to produce the assessment, because those two need different people.

We then look at who is free for that subject, at that level, in that window, in the format you want. This is where a request either fills quickly or does not. Common subjects with earlier slots fill fastest, and a late higher level request can take a fortnight.

You receive a shortlist, each tutor described by teaching background, IB experience and the modes they can offer. Availability is subject to tutor schedules throughout, and it can be reviewed if your term timings change.

The first session is diagnostic. A good one ends with the tutor telling you what the student can already do, what is missing, and what the next four sessions will cover. A weak one ends with an hour of teaching and no summary at all.

Four weeks later, look for changed habits before changed marks: work started earlier, questions read properly, fewer late-night panics.

Fill speed depends on level, hour and format together

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 44 on the map: neighbours, distances, traffic
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 44 sits inside the central sector grid and within easy reach of Golf Course Road, which is what makes home tutoring workable here at all. South City 1 is nearby, along with Nirvana Country, Sector 50, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4. Sector 65 lies further out along Golf Course Extension Road, and tutors count it as a separate trip rather than an extension of the same one.

The Rapid Metro corridor near Sector 53 and Sector 54 matters more than people expect, because a tutor who does not drive can still reach the central sectors on it. That widens your pool slightly, particularly for the evening slots that everyone competes over.

Tutors living in Sushant Lok will usually travel here without much negotiation. Those based on the Sohna Road side near Vatika Chowk or Sector 49 are more selective, and they will often ask for a later start so the journey is not made at the worst possible hour.

One note that saves time. If you are open to a tutor from any of the neighbouring areas rather than one living inside Sector 44, your shortlist becomes meaningfully longer and usually arrives a few days sooner.

South City 1, Nirvana Country, DLF Phase 1 and 4 nearby
Rapid Metro helps tutors who do not drive
Sohna Road side tutors prefer later starts

contentBlocks.heading: Three programmes, three different jobs
contentBlocks.body:
Primary Years, ages three to twelve. The job is fluency and confidence. Sessions should be short, mostly conversational, and tied to the inquiry the child is already doing at school. A tutor who turns up with a printed pack has misunderstood the assignment.

Middle Years, ages eleven to sixteen. The job is translation. Students know more than their marks suggest, because the criteria ask for analysis and evaluation while the student is producing description. Working from the school's own rubric, with the student's returned assignments in front of you, does more than any general revision programme. Grade 10 adds the personal project, where the failure mode is planning rather than content knowledge.

Diploma, ages sixteen to nineteen. The job is specialist depth plus assessment management. Higher level content, an internal assessment in every subject, an extended essay running across a year, Theory of Knowledge, and a set of command terms that quietly decide how each answer should be built.

A tutor who is excellent with a Grade 4 reader is not automatically the right person for a Grade 12 Physics IA, and the reverse holds just as firmly. Matching runs on the programme and the specific task, never on the subject label alone.
items: PYP: conversational sessions, inquiry-linked material
MYP: school rubric plus the student's own marked work
Grade 10 personal project: scheduling and scope
DP: IA in every subject, EE across the year, TOK essay

contentBlocks.heading: The checks a tutor passes before you hear their name
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor appears on any shortlist, a few unglamorous things happen.

Subject and level claims are checked against what the person has actually taught. IB teaching experience is treated separately from subject qualification, because a strong mathematician who has only ever taught board syllabus content will not necessarily handle a Math AA HL student well. For requests involving an internal assessment, an extended essay or Theory of Knowledge, we look for evidence the tutor has supervised that task before, since the criteria are the work rather than an afterthought.

Identity and qualification documents are collected. References from earlier families are contacted where those families can be reached. A structured conversation covers how the tutor works with a student who is behind, how they report to parents, and how they handle a clash between a school deadline and their own plan.

We do not publish tutor counts, success percentages or ratings, because they are not things this platform can substantiate. Nor can any tutor here promise a particular grade.

Screening lowers the odds of a wasted month. Your own judgement after the first session still matters, and saying it went badly is far more useful than continuing politely for six weeks.
items: IB teaching experience checked apart from qualifications
Prior IA, EE or TOK supervision evidence required for those requests
Identity and qualification documents on file
No counts, ratings or outcome promises published

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online, or a mix that fits Gurugram evenings
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is the default request from this part of the city, and for younger students it is usually the right one. Presence holds attention. Parents can see what happened without having to ask. Materials stay on the table between sessions instead of vanishing into a folder.

It has two weaknesses worth naming. Travel makes the slot fragile through a heavy term, and it limits you to tutors living within a sensible radius, which becomes a genuine constraint for higher level Diploma subjects.

Online tutoring inverts both. The pool covers Gurugram, Delhi, Noida and further, so an unusual subject and level combination becomes findable. Sessions can run late without a journey attached to either end. Past papers can be annotated live and kept for revision week.

Hybrid arrangements are common here and work well: one home visit a fortnight, weekly online sessions in between. It gives you presence without depending on a car reaching Sector 44 at six every single week during exam term.

Whatever the mode, availability depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed. Ask about it when you send the request rather than assuming one option has already been ruled out.

contentBlocks.body:

Internal deadlines vary between schools: when a first IA draft is expected, how much teacher feedback is permitted, when mocks fall, whether Theory of Knowledge is weekly or blocked. A tutoring plan built without that information tends to arrive at exactly the wrong time, adding pressure in the fortnight the student can least afford it.

Name the school in your request even if it is not one of the four above. It lets an advisor avoid the obvious collisions, and it lets a tutor ask sensible questions in the first session instead of spending that hour discovering the calendar.

contentBlocks.heading: Honest about what a tutor near Sector 44 cannot do
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor can close specific gaps, teach exam technique, build a weekly routine, and give a student someone to think out loud with. That is a great deal. It is not everything.

A tutor cannot guarantee a grade. Anyone offering one is describing a result outside their control, since it depends on the student's work between sessions, the school's teaching, and the paper that turns up on the day.

A tutor cannot compensate for a subject choice that was wrong from the beginning. If a Grade 11 student is failing higher level Chemistry and has no interest in the subject, the useful conversation is with the school about levels, not with us about session frequency.

And a tutor cannot fix a student who is not sleeping or has stopped attending school. Adding hours to an already overloaded week makes that worse rather than better.

The smaller, honest promise is this. A screened tutor who has taught this subject at this level. A first session that diagnoses. A plan you can read and question. A match that changes when it is not working. Anyone offering you considerably more than that in writing is worth treating with suspicion. Ask them how they intend to deliver it, and watch how quickly the promise shrinks.
items: Exam technique and routine: realistic gains
Wrong level or wrong subject: a school conversation, not a tutoring one
Sleep and attendance problems come first
Match changes when the fit is wrong

Four lines are enough to begin. Grade and programme. Subject and level. School. The evening windows that actually work.

An advisor reads it and replies with a straight assessment: what can be arranged at home near Sector 44 and the surrounding central sectors, what is stronger online, and roughly how quickly each is likely to fill. faqs.question: Do I need a different tutor for Math AA and Math AI?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. The two courses share a name and little else at higher level. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic manipulation, proof and calculus fluency. Applications and Interpretation is built around modelling, statistics and interpreting context, with a Paper 3 investigation closer to a piece of applied research than a problem set. Some tutors teach both well, but many are noticeably stronger in one. Say which course your child is on in the request, because a mismatch here quietly wastes the first three sessions before anybody is willing to admit it.

faqs.question: How soon can a tutor start in Sector 44?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, the level and the hour you want. A common request with a five or seven o'clock slot is often filled within a few days. A higher level Diploma subject at half past eight on a weekday can take longer, and in the months before a May session longer still, because the specialists are already committed. If speed matters, widen either the format or the timing rather than both at once. Online availability is generally quicker than home tutoring in the central sectors, which is limited by who can realistically travel.

faqs.question: What does a first session actually cover?
faqs.answer: Mostly diagnosis. Expect the tutor to ask the student to attempt something rather than lecturing, to look at recent returned work and teacher comments, and to establish which parts of the syllabus the school has already covered. Some teaching usually happens too, but a session that is only teaching has skipped the point. Afterwards you should get a short account of what the student can do, what is missing, and what the next few sessions will address. If nothing like that arrives within a couple of days, ask for it directly.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum number of sessions we have to book?
faqs.answer: No minimum is imposed from our side, although individual tutors may have their own preference and will say so before you agree anything. Most families start with a small block, four sessions being common, and then review. That is long enough to see whether the student engages and whether the tutor is planning rather than improvising, and short enough that a poor fit does not turn into an expensive one. You can pause during holidays or heavy school weeks. Availability afterwards depends on the tutor's schedule at that point.

faqs.question: My child is in PYP. Is it too early for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but the reason matters a great deal. If the aim is to push a six-year-old ahead of the class, tutoring is usually the wrong instrument and can dent a child's willingness to try things at all. If a child is struggling to read fluently or has lost confidence with number work, short regular sessions help considerably at that age. Primary Years support should look like reading together and talking, not a worksheet routine. Ask any tutor what a typical thirty minutes looks like, and be sceptical if the answer sounds like a syllabus.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Theory of Knowledge on its own?
faqs.answer: Yes. Theory of Knowledge support is a recognised standalone request, usually concentrated around the essay and the exhibition. The work is unlike subject tutoring: choosing a prescribed title the student can genuinely argue, finding real-world examples that are not recycled from a website, and building an argument that considers counterclaims rather than listing opinions. It typically runs across a handful of sessions rather than a whole year. The school supervisor stays in charge of what is allowed, and the tutor works within that. Availability for TOK mentoring is narrower than for mainstream subjects.

faqs.question: How do you handle a student who needs two subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Sometimes one tutor covers both, more often two are better. Physics and Chemistry pair reasonably well, and so do Economics and a Math course at standard level. Higher level combinations across different faculties rarely sit comfortably with one person, and a tutor claiming all of them is worth questioning. Two tutors also cost more, so it is worth deciding which subject is genuinely urgent and starting there. A single subject handled properly usually improves the student's approach to the others more than splitting attention across three ever does.

faqs.question: Do tutors follow the school's syllabus or their own material?
faqs.answer: Good tutors work from the school's scheme of work and the student's own returned assignments rather than a private course of their own. In practice that means asking for the unit plan, reading teacher feedback, and using the school's rubrics. Some supplementary material is fine, particularly past papers and extra practice sets. A tutor running an entirely parallel syllabus creates two workloads instead of one. If your child comes home with tutoring homework bearing no relationship to what school is doing, raise it in week one rather than week six.

faqs.question: We live closer to South City 1 than to Sector 44 itself. Does this page still apply?
faqs.answer: Yes. South City 1 is close enough that the same tutors take requests from both, and the shortlist barely changes. The same holds for Nirvana Country, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4 and Sector 50. Distance starts to matter around Sector 65 and the further stretches of Golf Course Extension Road, where a tutor may prefer online or ask for a later start. Give your actual address area in the request rather than the nearest well-known sector, because it affects who is realistically willing to travel on a weekday evening.

IB Gram reviews both. contentBlocks.heading: The Weekly Routine That Decides Whether Sector 45 Students Cope With IB
contentBlocks.body:
Ask a Grade 11 student in Sector 45 how they revise and the honest answer is usually this: read through the notes the night before. That habit survives Grade 9 comfortably. It falls apart in the Diploma Programme, where a Paper 2 question can ask a student to apply something they last touched eleven months earlier, in a context their teacher never used in class.

So before booking anybody, look at the week rather than the marks. Does the student write anything down without being told to? Is there one place where unfinished doubts get parked instead of quietly forgotten? Has a past paper ever been marked against the real markscheme instead of a feeling that the answer looked about right?

Spaced review and honest self-marking shape a DP result more than the number of hours booked. They also change which tutor is worth paying for. A tutor who only re-explains content leaves the routine untouched, and the student understands the lesson, feels better, then repeats the same pattern four weeks later.

Ask any prospective tutor one plain question. What will my child do between our sessions? If the answer is vague, the sessions are company rather than teaching. That single question filters more candidates than any list of credentials.
items: Notes reread the night before: fine at MYP, not at DP
A running doubt list beats remembering to ask
Self-marking against the published markscheme
Ask what happens between sessions, not during them
Hours booked is the weakest predictor of a result

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or a Mix: What Travel Around Sector 45 Actually Allows
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition in Sector 45 works well in the early evening and gets harder after that. A tutor crossing from DLF Phase 5 or the Rapid Metro corridor at seven in the evening can lose thirty to forty minutes each way, and the family ends up paying for that fatigue without ever seeing it on the invoice. Slots before six, or on weekend mornings, tend to hold much better across a full year.

Online changes the arithmetic. The tutor pool stops being whoever lives within a short drive and becomes whoever teaches that subject at that level. For Math AA HL, higher level Physics or an Economics internal assessment, that usually matters more than being in the same room.

A hybrid pattern suits many DP families here. One in-person session a fortnight for work that benefits from a table, printed past papers and a pen, plus weekly online sessions for the routine grind of practice and correction.

The honest exception is younger children. A Grade 3 or Grade 4 student in PYP generally does better with a person in the room, and stretching an online slot past thirty-five minutes at that age rarely pays.
