Advisor call: diagnosis before logistics
Filter: level and assessment experience, then schedule
Shortlist of two or three, backgrounds stated
Trial session, four-week plan, written review

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP timelines as Gurugram schools run them
contentBlocks.body:
Primary Years Programme families in Sector 63 mostly want reading fluency and number sense, delivered without turning a seven year old evening into a worksheet factory. Inquiry units are collaborative, so a tutor often does better building the vocabulary a child needs before a unit starts than reteaching it afterwards.

Middle Years Programme is where criterion language starts to bite. A Grade 8 student can understand a concept and still score poorly because the task asked for analysis and the answer described. The criteria are published; a tutor who reads them with the student, against a returned assignment, moves marks quickly.

Diploma Programme runs on a two-year clock that is tighter than most families expect. Internal assessment briefs land in the first year, the Extended Essay supervisor conversation starts before the summer, Theory of Knowledge work sits alongside subject deadlines, and mocks arrive in the winter of the second year. The May 2026 cohort is already inside that window. The November 2026 cohort has slightly more room and generally uses it badly.

Support across all three programmes runs Grade 1 to Grade 12, subject to tutor availability.
items: PYP: fluency, number sense, vocabulary ahead of inquiry units
MYP: published criteria read against returned work
DP: IA briefs, EE supervisor meetings, TOK, winter mocks
May 2026 cohort already inside the crunch window

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor reaches your gate
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a checklist, not a promise. Before a tutor appears on a Sector 63 shortlist we confirm identity documents, the qualification claimed, and teaching history for the specific programme and level. We ask for evidence of IB work: which syllabus, which years, whether they have supervised internal assessment drafts or only taught content. A subject interview follows, run by somebody who knows the syllabus well enough to catch a bluffed answer about command terms.

References are requested where a tutor has taught privately before. Where examiner or moderator work is claimed, we ask which component and which session, since that particular claim is easy to make and easy to check.

What screening cannot establish is whether your child will like this person. Rapport is not testable in an interview, which is why the first session is treated as a trial and why swapping tutors early brings no argument from us.

We also check the practical claims, since a broken promise about timing does more damage than a weak first lesson. If a tutor says he can be at DLF Park Place by half past six on a Wednesday, we ask where he is starting from and what he does immediately before.

Travel claims tested against the actual starting point

contentBlocks.heading: The promises we will not make in Gurugram or anywhere else
contentBlocks.body:
Some things get promised in this market that nobody can deliver.

No tutor can guarantee a grade. Not a 7, not a two-point jump, not a specific Paper 2 mark. Anyone offering that is either misunderstanding how the assessment works or hoping you will not check afterwards.

We publish no roster counts, no success percentages and no invented parent reviews. There is no honest way to produce those figures for a matching service, so we do not produce them.

What can be described accurately is process. You will know a tutor teaching background before the first session. You will get a written plan for the first four weeks. You will get a review at the end of those four weeks stating plainly whether the agreed target moved.

And where the answer is uncomfortable, expect to hear it. A student beginning Chemistry HL revision eight weeks before a May sitting, having missed most of the year, can improve. Whether that improvement reaches the grade the family has in mind is a separate question, and we would rather raise it in week one than in week nine.
items: No promised grades, points or paper marks
No published roster counts or success rates
No invented reviews or ratings
Written four-week plan and an honest review against it

contentBlocks.heading: Booking a first session in Sector 63
contentBlocks.body:

An advisor calls, asks what has already been tried, and is candid about whether a tutor is the right instrument at all. Sometimes it is not. A Grade 11 student drowning across six subjects usually needs a timetable conversation before a Physics tutor.

If a match makes sense, expect a shortlist rather than a single name, with mode and availability stated. Home sessions in Sector 63 depend on tutor schedules. Online tutoring covers Gurugram and the wider region including Delhi, Noida and Faridabad, for every supported subject.

Fees are quoted alongside the shortlist rather than after the trial, with mode and weekly frequency written down, so nothing about cost arrives as a surprise in week three.

Then a trial session, a four-week plan, and a written checkpoint. If the checkpoint is bad, we change the tutor rather than defend the original choice.

faqs.question: We only need help until the March mocks. Is a short engagement fine?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the more common request. A six to eight week block aimed at mocks works when the gap is specific: paper technique, one topic cluster, or an internal assessment draft. It works badly as a general fix, because the first two sessions go on diagnosis and you have then spent a quarter of the block. Tell the advisor the end date at the start. The plan gets built backwards from it, and the tutor knows not to begin a scheme of work that cannot finish in time.

faqs.question: How are fees decided for IB tuition near Sector 63?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on level, subject and mode rather than on a single published rate. Higher level sciences and Math AA HL sit above SL support, and Extended Essay mentoring is usually priced per block of sessions instead of hourly. Home sessions on Golf Course Extension Road carry the tutor travel time, which is why the same person may quote differently for online work. You see the rate before the trial session, not after it. If a quoted figure looks out of step with the level, ask exactly what is included.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach Ireo Skyon or M3M Golf Estate for a seven in the evening slot?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on where the tutor starts from. Somebody already living on the Extension Road stretch, in Sector 57 or Sushant Lok 3, can usually hold that slot through the week. A tutor travelling from DLF Phase 1 or from Delhi will struggle at that hour and will eventually start arriving late, which is worse than not booking at all. We would rather offer an online tutor for a fixed evening slot than a home tutor who makes it three weeks out of four.

faqs.question: My son is fine in Math AA HL until Paper 3. What kind of tutor helps?
faqs.answer: You want somebody who has taught or marked the extended response paper specifically, not just a strong mathematician. Paper 3 rewards a student who picks an approach early, states assumptions, and keeps a running narrative through a long guided investigation. That is a technique problem, drilled through past-paper sets with feedback on the writing as much as on the algebra. Ask any shortlisted tutor which recent Paper 3 investigations they have worked through with students. A vague answer there tells you most of what you need.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring in Sector 63 worth the traffic in winter?
faqs.answer: Often it is not, between roughly six and eight in the evening. Golf Course Extension Road slows badly in the fog months, and a tutor arriving twenty minutes late twice a week costs you a full session every month. Two workable answers exist: shift the home session to a weekend afternoon, or keep weekday sessions online and save the home slot for teaching that genuinely benefits from paper and a shared table. Families near DLF Crest and M3M Golf Estate commonly settle on the second.

faqs.question: Our daughter is in the Primary Years Programme. Is a tutor premature?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, unless something specific is off. Reading fluency well behind the class, number facts that will not stick, or a child who changed curriculum mid-year are real reasons. General enrichment at that age tends to make school feel longer without making it easier. If you do start, keep sessions short, keep them oral, and expect the tutor to build vocabulary ahead of an inquiry unit rather than reteach it afterwards. Ask for a four-week review, and be willing to stop when the answer is that nothing more is needed.

faqs.question: We are starting in November for a May 2026 exam. What is realistic?
faqs.answer: Roughly six months of term time, minus school holidays and mocks, so about twenty usable weeks. That is enough to rebuild one weak subject properly, or to lift paper technique across two. It is not enough to relearn two years of Chemistry HL from nothing, and any tutor suggesting otherwise is selling. A good plan names what gets dropped: some topics are triaged out so the ones carrying the most marks get proper time. Expect that conversation in the first session rather than in March.

faqs.question: How do you check that a tutor has actually taught the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: By asking questions a content-only teacher answers badly. Which internal assessment criteria carry the most weight in their subject, how they would coach a student through Extended Essay supervisor meetings, what they do with a script full of describe answers where the command term was evaluate. We also confirm identity, qualifications and teaching history, and request references where private teaching experience exists. None of that establishes chemistry between tutor and student, which is exactly why the first session is a trial rather than a commitment.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics and Chemistry?
faqs.answer: At standard level, sometimes. At higher level, rarely well. The two subjects share mathematical habits and almost nothing else once you reach HL, and a tutor stretched across both usually turns out to be strong in one. If both are wobbling, ask for two specialists at one session a week each instead of one generalist twice a week. The cost lands in a similar place and the feedback is sharper. The exception is early Middle Years science, where a single well-taught sciences tutor is genuinely enough.

contentBlocks.heading: The short answer for parents in Sector 65, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The short answer: yes, IB tutors in Sector 65 Gurugram can be arranged from Grade 1 through Grade 12, at home where a tutor route makes that realistic and online everywhere else. The useful part of the conversation is not availability. It is fit.

Now the longer answer, because the short one hides all the work.

A parent asking for a tutor is usually holding one of three things: a report card that dropped, an internal assessment draft that came back covered in comments, or a general sense that the Diploma Programme is heavier than the Middle Years ever was. Those need different people. The first often needs a diagnostic session before any teaching happens. The second needs somebody who has supervised that subject internal assessment and can read a criterion sheet aloud with a student. The third needs a study-skills conversation more than a subject expert.

So the enquiry asks for level and deadline before it asks for a preferred time. This sector sits on the newer corridor off Sohna Road, near Emaar Emerald Hills and Central Park Resorts, and travel is real. But a tutor who arrives on time and teaches the wrong thing has still wasted your term.

Both the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions are supported.

contentBlocks.heading: How a request from Sector 65 turns into a shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
A shortlist gets built through four filters, applied in this order.

Level first. Higher level and standard level in the same subject are separate teaching jobs, and a tutor comfortable with SL Economics can be out of depth on the HL paper. Assessment second: has this person worked on internal assessments, Extended Essays or Theory of Knowledge, or only on content? Schedule third, which is where a Sector 65 address genuinely matters, because a slot the tutor cannot keep is not a slot. Preference last: gender of tutor, language of explanation, home or screen, and any request about pace.

You then receive two or three names with teaching background and availability, not one recommendation. A single name removes your judgement from the process, and you are the person who knows your child.

The advisor call sits ahead of all of this and is deliberately slow. Ten minutes on what has already been tried saves a fortnight of the wrong tutoring. Families looking for an IB private tutor near Sector 65 often arrive having tried a group batch or a school senior already, and what failed narrows the search faster than what is wanted.
items: Filter one: programme and level taught, evidenced
Filter two: IA, EE or TOK experience
Filter three: can the slot actually be kept
Filter four: pace, language, gender, mode preferences
Output: two or three names, never a single take-it-or-leave-it

contentBlocks.heading: Which programme your child is in, and what that changes
contentBlocks.body:
Programme shapes the help more than the subject does.

In the Primary Years Programme, tutoring is mostly confidence and fluency: reading aloud, number facts, writing a sentence that says what the child meant. Sessions here should be short and frequent instead of long and weekly.

The Middle Years Programme carries a quieter difficulty. Assessment is criterion-related, so a student is judged against published descriptors and not against a class average. Grade 9 and Grade 10 students lose most of their marks in the gap between knowing something and demonstrating it. The personal project in the final year catches families by surprise, and it needs planning support rather than content teaching.

The Diploma Programme is heaviest and most time-sensitive. Six subjects, three at higher level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the creativity, activity and service commitment. Internal assessment drafts cluster in the first year at many Gurugram schools, so the crunch arrives earlier than the exam date suggests.

The transition years, Grade 5 into Grade 6 and Grade 10 into Grade 11, produce the most enquiries from this corridor. Both are worth planning a term ahead rather than a fortnight after the first disappointing test.
items: PYP: short frequent sessions, oral work, fluency
MYP: criterion descriptors, personal project planning
DP: six subjects, three HL, EE, TOK, CAS
Transition years generate the most enquiries here

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or a mix: picking the format in Sector 65
contentBlocks.body:
Three questions settle the format, and they are worth answering honestly.

Does the student work when unsupervised? If the answer is no, home sessions do more than teach. They impose an hour of focus. A screen is easy to half-attend, and a student who has learned to keep the camera on and the mind elsewhere will not be caught by a tutor sitting two hundred kilometres away.

Is the subject rare at the level you need? Math AI HL, Economics HL and Theory of Knowledge support are thinner locally. Insisting on a home tutor for those from Sector 65 usually means accepting a weaker match, and searches for an IB online tutor Sector 65 Gurugram exist largely for that reason.

When is the slot? Anything after eight in the evening is a hard sell for travel from Golf Course Road or Sushant Lok, and a tutor who agrees to it in week one starts cancelling by week five.

Many families here end up mixed, home at weekends and online midweek. The weakness of that model is continuity of notes, so ask the tutor to keep one shared document across both formats.
items: Home: imposes focus, suits younger and distractible students
Online: wider specialist choice for HL and TOK
After eight in the evening: online is the realistic option
If mixing formats, insist on one shared notes document

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by subject, what a Gurugram IB tutor is being asked to fix
contentBlocks.body:
Requests arrive in fairly predictable shapes.

Math AA HL: calculus fluency and proof habits, plus the mathematics exploration, where students pick a topic too large to finish and too thin to earn marks. Math AI HL: statistics and modelling are handled competently and the written interpretation stays thin, which is precisely where the marks sit.

Physics: uncertainties, graph work and the internal assessment method section. Students can describe an experiment and cannot justify why a variable was chosen. Chemistry: organic reaction pathways, and anything demanding a multi-step calculation under time pressure.

Economics: real-world examples that are too old or too vague, and diagrams drawn from memory instead of built from the question in front of them. English A: structuring a comparative response, and handling an unseen extract in Paper 1 without sliding into device-spotting.

An IB science tutor Sector 65 request often turns out to be an assessment-writing request wearing a subject label. That is not a criticism of the student. Nobody sits you down and teaches you how to write a method section; you are expected to absorb it.

Which is why shortlists for these subjects favour tutors who have marked work, not only taught it.

Math AI HL: thin written interpretation
Physics: variable justification in the IA method
Chemistry: organic pathways under time pressure

contentBlocks.heading: What we cannot tell you, and why
contentBlocks.body:
Three claims are common in this market, and none of them survive scrutiny.

The first is a predicted grade improvement. Nobody can promise a 7 or a particular points total, because the result involves examiners, moderation, and a student performance on one particular morning. A tutor who commits to a number is telling you about a sales process rather than about teaching.

The second is a headcount. Pages advertising how many verified teachers sit on a roster are quoting a database, and a database is not a shortlist. What matters is whether one suitable person is free at your hour, in your subject, at your level.

The third is a wall of glowing parent reviews. We do not publish invented ones, so you will not find a wall here.

What replaces all three: a named teaching background before the trial, a written four-week plan, and a review at the end of those four weeks stating whether the agreed target moved. If it did not, the sensible response is to change the approach or the tutor. We would rather say that first than wait for you to raise it.

No invented reviews or star ratings

contentBlocks.body:

Identity is confirmed against a government photograph document. Qualifications are checked against the certificate rather than the claim. A subject interview follows, run by somebody who knows the syllabus. The questions stay practical: how would you plan a mathematics exploration with a student who has chosen a topic that cannot be finished, what would you do with a Paper 2 script full of unsupported assertions.

faqs.answer: Possibly, and it depends on subject, level and the hour you want. Standard level support in the sciences and mathematics can usually be arranged quickly. faqs.question: What is the difference between a subject tutor and an internal assessment mentor?
faqs.answer: A subject tutor teaches content and technique across the syllabus: topics, past papers, timing. An internal assessment mentor works on one piece of coursework, from research question to final draft, and spends the time on structure, method justification and criterion alignment rather than on teaching new material. Some tutors do both well. Many do not, so we ask which role you actually need before matching. A student who is fine in class but sinking in the draft needs the second, not the first.

faqs.question: My child attends a school in Sector 57. Does the tutor need to know that school?
faqs.answer: It helps and it is not essential. What a familiar tutor brings is calendar knowledge: when that campus issues internal assessment briefs, how detailed its draft feedback tends to be, when mocks land. That saves the first two sessions of guesswork. If no familiar tutor is available at your slot, send the school term calendar instead and a good tutor will work from it. IB Gram is independent and is not affiliated with any school, so this is about practical timing rather than any connection.

faqs.question: Is Middle Years tutoring worth paying for, or should we wait for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Waiting is usually the more expensive choice. The habits that decide Diploma results, reading a criterion before writing, showing working, using command terms precisely, are far easier to build at Grade 8 or Grade 9 than at Grade 11 under deadline pressure. The intensity should differ though: one session a week during Middle Years, aimed at method rather than marks, is normally enough. If your child is comfortable and engaged in class, there is no need to add anything at all.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week make sense for a Grade 11 student?
faqs.answer: Two per subject is rarely right at the start. One well-used session a week, with real work done between sessions, tells you more in a month than four hours of being taught at. Grade 11 is already heavy: six subjects, the Extended Essay beginning, and internal assessment briefs arriving. Adding six tutoring hours a week creates a second timetable that nobody can sustain. Start with one subject and one session, review at four weeks, and add only where the review shows the need.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is good but my child does not engage?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than waiting for the review. A capable tutor who does not connect with a particular student is a common outcome, not a failure of screening, because rapport cannot be interviewed for. We will change the tutor without an argument and without treating it as a complaint. Occasionally the real issue is the subject or the hour rather than the person, and the advisor will ask a few questions to work out which before simply substituting a name.

faqs.question: Do you help with the Extended Essay, or only with subjects?
faqs.answer: Extended Essay mentoring is supported, within a clear limit: a mentor guides, questions and reviews structure, and does not write or supply content. Useful work includes narrowing a research question that is far too broad, planning a realistic timeline against your school supervisor meetings, and reading a draft for argument rather than for grammar. This works well online because it is mostly conversation and document review. Availability depends on the subject area, since some fields have far fewer experienced mentors.

faqs.question: Are weekend slots easier to get in Sector 65 than weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Yes for home tutoring, no for online. Weekend travel from Golf Course Road, Sushant Lok or Sector 57 takes roughly half the time it takes at seven on a Tuesday, so tutors accept those bookings more readily. Weekend demand for online slots is heavier, because families across the city want the same hours. If your preference is a fixed weekday evening online session, book it well ahead. Everything remains subject to tutor availability and can be reviewed as schedules change.

faqs.question: How is progress measured if you will not promise a grade?
faqs.answer: Through things that can be observed inside four weeks. Timed past-paper scores under real conditions, not open-book practice. Whether an internal assessment draft comes back with fewer structural comments. Whether the student can now explain a topic without notes. Whether homework is being attempted before the session rather than during it. Those are written into the four-week plan at the start, so the review compares like with like. A grade in June is an outcome, and outcomes are not something anybody can commit to in advance.

contentBlocks.heading: The study week behind a Sector 66 student result
contentBlocks.body:
Look at a week rather than at a report card and the problem usually becomes obvious.

A Diploma Programme student in Sector 66 leaves home around seven, is back by four, has an activity twice a week, and sits down to work somewhere between eight and nine. That leaves perhaps two usable hours on a good evening. What fills those hours decides the grade far more than raw ability does.

Most students fill them with the wrong thing. They rewrite notes, which feels productive and teaches almost nothing. They read model answers instead of attempting questions cold. They revise the topics they enjoy, which are the topics they already know.

IB tutors in Sector 66 Gurugram are worth booking once that pattern is set and the student cannot break it alone. A good tutor does not simply add a third hour. He changes what happens in the other two: retrieval before review, past-paper questions attempted under time, command terms read properly before any writing starts.

Support runs Grade 1 to Grade 12 across PYP, MYP and DP, with the May 2026 and November 2026 sittings in scope. Home sessions along the Sohna Road extension depend on tutor schedules.

contentBlocks.heading: Six IB subjects, six habits that decide the grade
contentBlocks.body:
Every subject rewards a different weekly habit, and the habit is teachable.

Math AA HL rewards daily volume. Twenty minutes of mixed questions six days a week beats a two-hour Sunday session, because fluency decays fast and mixed practice forces topic recognition. Math AI HL rewards writing: after every modelling question, one sentence explaining what the answer means in the context given.

Physics rewards an errors book. Students who log each wrong answer with the reason, then revisit it a fortnight later, stop repeating whole categories of mistake. Chemistry rewards spaced revisiting of mechanisms, because organic chemistry is memory work dressed up as reasoning.

Economics rewards a running file of real examples collected through the year, so that commentary work is not invented the night before. English A rewards reading something unset every week and annotating it with no task attached.

None of that is exotic. It is simply nobody job at school to install it, and few students build it unaided. So when a parent asks for an IB maths tutor Sector 66 or a science specialist, the first four weeks often go on the working week as much as on the syllabus itself.

Chemistry: spaced return to organic mechanisms
Economics: a running file of dated real examples
English A: weekly unset reading, annotated

contentBlocks.heading: Turning a habit problem into a tutor brief in Sector 66
contentBlocks.body:
The brief a family writes and the brief a tutor needs are rarely the same document.

A parent writes: needs help with Chemistry, Grade 11, twice a week. An advisor turns that into something usable: higher level Chemistry, currently around a 4, weak on organic pathways and on calculation under time, no revision routine at all, internal assessment brief issued last month, target is the May 2026 session, free on Tuesday and Saturday. The second version can be matched against a real person. The first cannot.

Getting there takes one call of ten to fifteen minutes, plus two things you can supply: a recent marked script and the school term calendar.

Then the filtering. Programme and level experience, assessment experience, availability at your actual hour, and only then preferences about pace, language and gender of tutor. Two or three names follow, with backgrounds stated so you can compare them.

Where no suitable tutor near Sector 66 can make your slot, you will be told, rather than offered somebody who almost fits. Almost fits is how families end up changing tutors in week six.

Sector 66 sits further along the new sector corridor than its neighbours, past Sector 65, with Tata Primanti and M3M Golf Estate as the usual reference points and Emaar Emerald Hills and Central Park Resorts within the same belt. The distance from the older parts of the city looks modest on paper and turns expensive after five in the evening.

A tutor coming from Sushant Lok, DLF Phase 4 or Sector 57 does that trip comfortably at three in the afternoon and painfully at seven. Sohna Road towards Vatika Chowk backs up in both directions during the office exit, and going via Sector 50, Nirvana Country or South City 1 is no shortcut at that hour.

There is a straightforward consequence for a study routine. If your child works best between eight and ten at night, a home tutor is fighting traffic to arrive tired, and an IB online tutor Sector 66 Gurugram is generally the better arrangement for that slot.

Keep home sessions for the afternoon and the weekend, when a run from Golf Course Extension Road is a fifteen minute job rather than a forty minute one.

contentBlocks.heading: Habits that PYP, MYP and DP each reward in Gurugram schools
contentBlocks.body:
Each programme asks for a different working habit, and starting the right one early costs less than repairing the wrong one later.

Primary Years students need daily reading and conversation about what they read. Twenty minutes, aloud, with an adult asking one question at the end. A tutor at this stage should be building that habit, not setting worksheets to fill an hour.

Middle Years students need the habit of reading the criterion before starting a task. Most lost marks between Grade 8 and Grade 10 come from answering a slightly different question than the one asked. A tutor who opens every session with the assessment descriptor changes that inside a term.

Diploma students need a calendar habit. Internal assessment deadlines, Extended Essay checkpoints and Theory of Knowledge work do not arrive evenly, and in the second year they collide with mocks. Students keeping a single term planner survive that collision. Students working from memory do not.

Across Gurugram schools these patterns look similar even where the calendars differ, which is why a tutor programme experience matters as much as subject knowledge does.

contentBlocks.heading: Screening: what Gurugram parents should ask us to prove
contentBlocks.body:
Ask for evidence rather than adjectives. Before a tutor is recommended to a Sector 66 family we confirm identity against a photo document, check qualifications against certificates, and establish teaching history by programme and by level. A subject interview follows with somebody able to tell a rehearsed answer from a practised one. References are requested where previous private teaching exists. We also ask a tutor to name the last few internal assessment titles he has supervised, since people who did that work answer instantly and people who did not start generalising.

That is the checkable part. Here is the part parents should push on themselves: ask which years the tutor taught the current syllabus, ask whether they have seen internal assessment work through to submission, and ask what they would do in the first two sessions with your child specifically. Vague answers to that third question are the most reliable warning sign available to you.

What screening does not cover is temperament across months, or whether a fifteen year old will respect this particular adult. No interview reveals that. The trial session and the four-week review exist because of it, and changing a tutor after either one is treated as ordinary rather than as a complaint.

contentBlocks.heading: Which format supports a routine in Sector 66, and which breaks it
contentBlocks.body:
Format should follow the routine you are trying to build, not the other way round.

If the aim is discipline, home sessions help. An adult at the table at a fixed hour twice a week creates two anchor points in an otherwise chaotic evening, and younger students in particular work better when the tutor can see the notebook rather than a webcam view of a face.

If the aim is depth in one subject, online usually wins, because you are choosing from every available specialist instead of only those willing to drive out to the Sohna Road extension. Extended Essay supervision and Theory of Knowledge coaching work well on a screen, since both are conversation and document review.

A frank warning about the mixed model. Two tutors, one at home and one online, teaching the same subject, tend to produce contradictory advice on assessment structure. If you mix, mix formats with one tutor rather than tutors within one subject.

Each campus also runs its own internal deadline rhythm, and a tutor who has worked with students from that school arrives already knowing whether drafts are due in August or in October.

If your child has changed campus recently, mention it. The two calendars rarely line up, and the term after a move is where deadlines quietly get missed.

contentBlocks.heading: Honest limits on what a Gurugram tutor changes
contentBlocks.body:
Tutoring changes what happens in two to four hours of a student week. It does not change the other hundred and sixty.

So the honest list of limits is short. A tutor cannot make a disengaged student care, although a good one can sometimes make the subject interesting enough that caring follows. A tutor cannot recover two years of missed foundations in six weeks, and should say so in the first session rather than the fifth. And nobody can promise a grade outcome, because the mark depends on examiners and on one performance in one hall on one morning.

You will not find student success percentages or a roster count on this page, because neither figure can be produced honestly by a matching service.

What is measurable: whether the agreed weekly routine is being kept, whether timed past-paper scores move, and whether an internal assessment draft returns with fewer structural comments. faqs.question: My son studies for hours and the marks do not move. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually the method rather than the effort. Rereading and rewriting notes feel like work and produce very little retention, while attempting questions cold, getting them wrong, and correcting them produces a lot. Check three things before booking anyone: is he attempting past-paper questions under time, is he correcting them properly afterwards, and is he revising the weak topics rather than the comfortable ones. If the answer to any of those is no, a tutor has something concrete to fix in the first fortnight.

faqs.question: How long does it take to change a study routine?
faqs.answer: Four to six weeks before it holds without prompting, in most cases, and longer if the student is exhausted. The early sessions tend to feel slow because the tutor is watching the student work rather than teaching, which some parents find frustrating to pay for. It is the part that lasts. Once retrieval practice and timed questions are habitual, subject teaching moves much faster, and the tutoring hours themselves can often be reduced instead of increased later in the year.

faqs.question: Should we book two sessions a week or one longer one?
faqs.answer: For habit repair, two shorter sessions win, because the gap between them is where the student has to work alone and the tutor gets to see whether that happened. For internal assessment or Extended Essay work, one longer session works better, since drafting needs a run at it. Given a nine hour school day and travel along the Sohna Road extension, most Sector 66 families land on ninety minutes twice a week, one of those at the weekend.

faqs.question: Is an evening slot after eight practical in Sector 66?
faqs.answer: For online, yes. For a home tutor, rarely and not reliably. Anyone driving from Golf Course Road, Sushant Lok or Sector 57 at that hour is arriving after a long day and leaving very late, and those bookings tend to be quietly cancelled by the second month. There is also a learning argument against it: a tired student at half past eight retains little regardless of who is teaching. If eight is the only free hour, treat online as the default and keep the session short.

faqs.question: What should a first session with an IB tutor near Sector 66 look like?
faqs.answer: Mostly diagnosis. A good tutor spends the first hour finding out what the student can already do, usually by setting questions and watching how they are attempted rather than by asking what is difficult. Expect questions about the school calendar, recent marked work and the current revision routine. Expect very little teaching. By the end you should receive a short view of where the marks are being lost and what the first four weeks will target, in writing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay if the school has already assigned a supervisor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the roles need to stay separate. The school supervisor signs off on process and holds the formal meetings. A mentor works between those meetings on scope, structure and argument, and never supplies content or writing. Tell the tutor who the supervisor is and what has already been agreed, so advice does not conflict. Where a research question is too broad to finish, which is the most common problem, an early mentoring conversation saves months of wasted reading.

faqs.question: Are group batches cheaper and just as good?
faqs.answer: Cheaper, certainly. Just as good depends entirely on the problem. A batch works when a student needs more exposure to worked examples and is comfortable asking questions in front of others. It works badly for internal assessment support, for command-term technique, and for any student whose gaps are individual, because the pace is set by the group. faqs.question: My daughter is in Grade 6, her first year of Middle Years. What support makes sense?

mainEntity.name: My son studies for hours and the marks do not move. What is going wrong?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually the method rather than the effort. Rereading and rewriting notes feel like work and produce very little retention, while attempting questions cold, getting them wrong, and correcting them produces a lot. Check three things before booking anyone: is he attempting past-paper questions under time, is he correcting them properly afterwards, and is he revising the weak topics rather than the comfortable ones. If the answer to any of those is no, a tutor has something concrete to fix in the first fortnight.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to change a study routine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four to six weeks before it holds without prompting, in most cases, and longer if the student is exhausted. The early sessions tend to feel slow because the tutor is watching the student work rather than teaching, which some parents find frustrating to pay for. It is the part that lasts. Once retrieval practice and timed questions are habitual, subject teaching moves much faster, and the tutoring hours themselves can often be reduced instead of increased later in the year.

mainEntity.name: Should we book two sessions a week or one longer one?

acceptedAnswer.text: For habit repair, two shorter sessions win, because the gap between them is where the student has to work alone and the tutor gets to see whether that happened. For internal assessment or Extended Essay work, one longer session works better, since drafting needs a run at it. Given a nine hour school day and travel along the Sohna Road extension, most Sector 66 families land on ninety minutes twice a week, one of those at the weekend.

mainEntity.name: Is an evening slot after eight practical in Sector 66?

acceptedAnswer.text: For online, yes. For a home tutor, rarely and not reliably. Anyone driving from Golf Course Road, Sushant Lok or Sector 57 at that hour is arriving after a long day and leaving very late, and those bookings tend to be quietly cancelled by the second month. There is also a learning argument against it: a tired student at half past eight retains little regardless of who is teaching. If eight is the only free hour, treat online as the default and keep the session short.

mainEntity.name: What should a first session with an IB tutor near Sector 66 look like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mostly diagnosis. A good tutor spends the first hour finding out what the student can already do, usually by setting questions and watching how they are attempted rather than by asking what is difficult. Expect questions about the school calendar, recent marked work and the current revision routine. Expect very little teaching. By the end you should receive a short view of where the marks are being lost and what the first four weeks will target, in writing.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay if the school has already assigned a supervisor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and the roles need to stay separate. The school supervisor signs off on process and holds the formal meetings. A mentor works between those meetings on scope, structure and argument, and never supplies content or writing. Tell the tutor who the supervisor is and what has already been agreed, so advice does not conflict. Where a research question is too broad to finish, which is the most common problem, an early mentoring conversation saves months of wasted reading.

mainEntity.name: Are group batches cheaper and just as good?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cheaper, certainly. Just as good depends entirely on the problem. A batch works when a student needs more exposure to worked examples and is comfortable asking questions in front of others. It works badly for internal assessment support, for command-term technique, and for any student whose gaps are individual, because the pace is set by the group. heroSubtitle: Sector 67 sits along the Sohna Road extension, which makes tutor travel time a real variable rather than a footnote. introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 67 Gurugram are usually booked in one of two formats: a tutor who travels to your flat in M3M Golf Estate or Emaar Emerald Hills, or an online specialist who takes the session from anywhere. Online wins on subject depth and late slots. Home tutoring wins on younger children and on concentration. IB Gram helps you decide between the two first, then shortlists tutors against the actual subject, level and assessment your child is working on, from Grade 1 through Grade 12.

contentBlocks.heading: What IB tutoring in Sector 67 Gurugram usually looks like
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 67 sits on the far side of the Sohna Road extension, where the newer sector corridor is still filling in. Families moved here for space and for the schools they could reach from it. What most of them did not plan for was how a Diploma Programme timetable behaves once internal assessments start landing on top of school deadlines.

So the first question worth answering is not which tutor. It is which format.

Online tutoring genuinely does several things better. It removes travel from both sides, which means a tutor who specialises in Math AA HL can take an 8:45 pm slot in Sector 67 without a forty-minute drive against traffic. It makes session recordings possible, so a student can replay a derivation instead of half-remembering it. It makes an annotated past paper on screen easier to work through than a photocopy sliding around a dining table.

It also does several things worse. A Grade 4 student on a screen drifts, and drifts quietly. A teenager who hides confusion hides it more easily behind a camera. Handwritten working in Physics is harder to correct remotely unless the tutor insists on a document camera or clear photographs of the full page.

IB tutors in Sector 67 Gurugram are worth choosing on that trade-off first and on subject reputation second.

Online suits DP specialist subjects and late weeknight slots
Home visits suit PYP and early MYP concentration
Grade 1 to Grade 12, PYP through DP

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing a format that survives a Sector 67 Gurugram week
contentBlocks.body:
Take an ordinary Wednesday. School finishes, there is a co-curricular, the child reaches home around 6:30, eats, and is realistically available from 7:30. A home tutor coming from Sushant Lok or DLF Phase 4 has to leave by about 6:45 to make that work. On a bad evening near Vatika Chowk, they do not make it, and the session either shrinks or slides.

Online removes that risk completely. That is the strongest argument for it on this corridor, and it has nothing to do with teaching quality.

Where online falls short is supervision. No one is in the room to notice a student copying a worked example rather than attempting it. Good online tutors build around this. They ask for the notebook to be held to the camera. They set a silent six minutes and watch the pen move. They refuse to type the solution while the student watches.

Hybrid is where most Sector 67 families settle. One weekend session at home, where a tutor can go through a full paper with the student's actual handwriting in front of them. One or two shorter online sessions midweek, aimed at whatever went wrong in class that week.

Home tutoring around Sector 67 may be arranged subject to tutor availability. Online tutoring covers Gurugram for every supported IB subject.
items: Weeknight home visits depend on Vatika Chowk traffic
Online allows late slots and session recordings
Ask an online tutor how they check written working
Hybrid: weekend at home, midweek online

contentBlocks.heading: Subjects Sector 67 IB students most often ask for help with
contentBlocks.body:
Math AA HL is the most requested subject on this corridor, and requests usually arrive late, somewhere around the end of DP1 when calculus and proof stop rewarding memorised methods. Math AI HL enquiries look different. Those students are often comfortable with the modelling itself but lose marks on statistical interpretation and on writing reasoning in the register the mark scheme expects.

Physics splits into two problems: the derivations, and Paper 3 with its unfamiliar experimental setups. Chemistry tends to arrive as an internal assessment problem before it arrives as a content problem, usually a student who has chosen a topic that cannot generate enough quantitative data to analyse.

Economics is the subject where command terms decide the grade. Evaluate, examine, distinguish, discuss. A student who explains well and never evaluates can sit at the same mark for a full year without understanding why.

English A is the least searched and the most under-supported. The Paper 1 unseen commentary rewards a repeatable method, and that method can be taught to a student who currently freezes at the sight of an unfamiliar extract.

An IB maths tutor Sector 67 parents want and an IB science tutor Sector 67 parents want are rarely the same person.
items: Math AA HL: calculus and proof, usually flagged late in DP1
Math AI HL: statistical interpretation and written reasoning
Physics Paper 3 and derivation-heavy topics
Chemistry IA topics that cannot produce enough data
Economics command terms: evaluate, examine, discuss

contentBlocks.heading: Travel from Sector 67 to Sector 65, Nirvana Country and beyond
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 67 is bounded by the newer stretch of the sector corridor rather than by the older Gurugram grid, and that matters for tutor travel more than parents expect. Sector 65 is the nearest genuinely quick hop. Sector 50 and Nirvana Country are reachable, though the final kilometre after 7 pm is unpredictable. South City 1, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 sit far enough away that a tutor based there will either quote a fee reflecting the drive or quietly prefer to teach online.

Residents of M3M Golf Estate, Tata Primanti, Emaar Emerald Hills and Central Park Resorts have one advantage worth using. These are gated communities with several IB families inside them. Two students in the same tower, same subject, same level, can share a slot at a lower per-head fee.

It works when the two are genuinely close in ability. It fails badly when they are not, and a tutor who agrees to a pairing without asking about that is not thinking carefully about your child.

For families living closer to Sector 57 or Golf Course Extension Road, the pool of tutors willing to visit at home widens noticeably.
items: Sector 65: the shortest hop for home visits
Sector 50 and Nirvana Country: reachable, evening-dependent
DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, South City 1: usually online instead
Shared slots within one tower work only at matched ability

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP support for Gurugram families in Sector 67
contentBlocks.body:
Grade 1 to Grade 12 is a wide span, and the three IB programmes are not versions of one another.

Primary Years Programme students, roughly ages 3 to 12, need support that keeps inquiry intact. The common failure is a tutor who quietly converts a PYP unit into worksheet drilling because drilling is what they know how to do. Reading fluency, number sense and the confidence to ask a question in class are the honest targets at this stage.

Middle Years Programme students, ages 11 to 16, hit the criterion wall. They understand the content and still lose marks on Criterion C or D because nobody has shown them what the descriptors actually ask for. MYP support in Sector 67 is largely translation work: moving a student from what they know to what the criterion rewards.

Diploma Programme students, ages 16 to 19, are carrying subject content, an internal assessment and a revision plan pointed at the May 2026 or November 2026 session, all at once. Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge sit on top of that. Those two are usually the first commitments to slip, and they slip silently.
items: PYP: reading fluency, number sense, keeping inquiry intact
MYP: criterion descriptors and task-specific clarifications
DP: subject content plus IA plus a revision calendar
EE and TOK: planned early or missed late

contentBlocks.heading: How a shortlist gets built after you send an enquiry
contentBlocks.body:
An enquiry from Sector 67 is not answered with a directory. It starts with a short conversation that establishes four things: the exact subject and level, the school and its assessment calendar, what has already been tried, and what the family can realistically commit to each week.

Then a shortlist is put together. Usually two or three tutors, each with a note on why they are on the list and what their limitation is. A tutor may be strong on Math AA HL and free only after 9 pm. That gets said upfront rather than discovered in week three, when rearranging everything is far more painful.

A first session follows, and it should not be a lecture. It should be diagnostic. A good tutor spends most of it working out where the gap actually begins, which is frequently two chapters earlier than the parent assumed.

By week four you should be able to point at something concrete. A marked past paper with a better breakdown by question. An internal assessment moved from a vague topic to a defined research question. If nothing concrete exists, the match is wrong, and changing early costs far less than persisting out of politeness.
items: Subject, level, school calendar, realistic weekly hours
Two or three names, each with a stated limitation
First session is diagnostic, not a lecture
Week four: something concrete you can look at

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, cancellations and the awkward questions worth asking early
contentBlocks.body:
Fees for IB tuition near Sector 67 vary with level and mode, and anyone quoting one number without asking which subject and which year is guessing. HL Diploma subjects cost more per hour than MYP support. Home visits cost more than online, because the tutor is paid for travel time whether or not the invoice says so. Rare subject combinations cost more because the pool of people who can teach them is small.

Ask about the cancellation rule before the first session, not after the first missed one. Ask whether the fee is per session or per month, and what happens in a month with school examinations and fewer sessions. Ask what the process is if you want to change tutors.

Ask also what the tutor will not do. A tutor who offers to write the internal assessment has disqualified themselves in that one sentence. IB academic honesty rules are enforced by schools, and a student caught submitting over-tutored work loses considerably more than the marks on that piece.

Fees, availability and scheduling can be reviewed on a call before anything is committed.

Home visits carry unbilled travel time

A tutor offering to write the IA is the wrong tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Schools that Sector 67 Gurugram families commonly attend
contentBlocks.body:
Families in Sector 67 usually look at Scottish High International School in Sector 57 first, simply because it is the closest IB school on this side of the corridor. Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, GD Goenka World School in the Sohna Road region and Pathways World School also draw students from these communities, with the daily journey ranging from manageable to serious depending on the bus route.

Knowing the school changes the tutoring more than most parents expect. Assessment calendars differ. Some schools run Diploma mock examinations early in DP2, leaving room to react to a weak result. Others run them late enough that a poor mock is more of a verdict than a warning. Some MYP departments issue detailed task-specific clarifications with every assignment; others expect students to work directly from the generic descriptors.

A tutor who has already taught students from that school knows which of those situations they are walking into, and plans the first month differently as a result.

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor profile reaches you
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor profile reaches a family in Sector 67, several things are checked, and it is worth being precise about which.

Identity and qualification documents are reviewed. Subject and level claims are tested against what the tutor can demonstrate, so someone claiming Math AA HL is asked about HL-only content rather than general mathematics. IB-specific familiarity is assessed separately: criterion-related assessment, command-term language, internal assessment structure, and the gap between what a school department expects and what an examiner actually rewards.

Teaching is observed or discussed in enough depth to judge explanation quality rather than knowledge alone. Plenty of people who know Physics thoroughly cannot explain it to a tired sixteen-year-old at 8 pm on a Thursday, and the difference shows up quickly. References from earlier families are checked where a tutor can supply them, though these are treated as one input rather than as proof of anything.

What screening cannot do is predict rapport between one specific tutor and one specific student. That gets decided in the first two or three sessions and nowhere else. Which is exactly why those early weeks should be reviewed honestly, with the student in the room, rather than politely over a phone call after the fact.

Level claims tested on HL-only content
Criterion, command-term and IA familiarity assessed
Rapport is decided in sessions one to three, not on paper

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB tuition near Sector 67 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
If you live in M3M Golf Estate, Tata Primanti, Emaar Emerald Hills, Central Park Resorts, or anywhere else along this stretch of the Sohna Road extension, the useful next step is a short conversation rather than a form filled in at midnight.

Have three details ready. The subject and level. The school. The two or three time windows that genuinely work in your week, not the ones that would work in an ideal week. Those three answers narrow a shortlist faster than anything else you could tell an advisor.

Say plainly whether you want the tutor at home or online. If you are unsure, say that as well, because the recommendation changes depending on the answer and there is no benefit in pretending otherwise.

Home tutoring near Sector 67 depends on tutor schedules for that particular subject and slot. Online tutoring covers every supported IB subject across Gurugram, including several where a local specialist within driving distance may simply not exist this term.

Enquiries about IB tutors in Sector 67 Gurugram can be reviewed for both formats at the same time.

State a preference for home or online, or say you are unsure
Home slots subject to tutor availability

faqs.question: Is online IB tutoring really as good as a tutor coming to Sector 67?
faqs.answer: For Diploma Programme subjects, often better, because the pool of specialists is not limited to people willing to drive down the Sohna Road extension on a weeknight. For younger students it is usually worse, since a Grade 4 child needs someone in the room. The honest test is whether the tutor has a method for checking written working on screen. If they never ask to see the notebook or a photograph of the full page, the format is doing them a favour rather than your child.

faqs.question: How soon after enquiring can sessions actually begin?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the slot you need. Online support in commonly taught subjects can usually be arranged faster than a home visit in Sector 67, because home tutoring depends on a tutor already working near the Sohna Road extension with that exact time free. Rare subject and level combinations take longer, and anyone promising an immediate start for every request is not checking properly. A realistic timeline is given during the first call, subject to tutor availability.

faqs.question: What does IB tuition near Sector 67 cost per session?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and a quoted number that arrives before anyone asks the subject is not a real quote. Cost moves with the programme level, whether the subject is HL or SL, how scarce that subject is locally, and whether the tutor travels to you. Home sessions carry travel time inside the fee even when it is not itemised. Fees are discussed openly before a first session so you are comparing like with like rather than reacting to an invoice later.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and already lost in Math AA HL. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan changes. Starting in DP1 leaves room to go back and repair the algebraic fluency that usually sits underneath a calculus problem. Starting six weeks before the May session does not, and a tutor who claims otherwise is selling you something. Late starts get prioritised: the highest-weighted topics, the question types that recur, and exam technique on papers the student can realistically finish. Slower repair work is dropped deliberately rather than attempted badly alongside everything else.

faqs.question: Can two children from the same tower in Emaar Emerald Hills share one tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in gated communities along this corridor it is a common arrangement. It works when both students are in the same subject at the same level and are genuinely close in current standing. It stops working when one is chasing a grade boundary and the other is consolidating basics, because the session then serves neither properly. Ask the tutor to be blunt about the fit after two sessions. A tutor who agrees to any pairing to secure the booking is not the tutor you want.

faqs.question: What happens if my child and the tutor simply do not get on?
faqs.answer: You say so, early, and a different tutor is shortlisted. This is treated as ordinary rather than as a complaint. Personality fit cannot be screened for in advance, only observed once teaching starts, so the first fortnight is the point to raise it. Waiting three months out of politeness costs the student far more than an awkward message costs anyone. Where possible the incoming tutor is briefed on what was already covered so the student is not made to repeat topics.

faqs.question: Do tutors help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, or only taught subjects?
faqs.answer: Both, within limits. Extended Essay support means shaping a research question that can actually be answered in four thousand words, planning the sources, and reviewing structure and argument against the criteria. Theory of Knowledge support usually focuses on the exhibition and the essay prompts, and on building examples a student can defend. The supervisor at school remains the primary authority on both. A tutor supplements that relationship rather than replacing it, and never writes any part of the submitted work.

faqs.question: We have paid for a month and seen nothing change. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for evidence rather than reassurance. After four weeks there should be something you can look at: a past paper marked with a question-level breakdown, a corrected set of working, an internal assessment moved from topic to research question. If the only answer offered is that your child is improving in confidence, treat that as a warning. Sometimes the tutor is wrong for the student. Sometimes the student is not doing the work between sessions, and that needs a different conversation entirely.

faqs.answer: Students from Scottish High International School in Sector 57, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, GD Goenka World School in the Sohna Road region and Pathways World School do come through enquiries from this part of Gurugram. Knowing the school helps a tutor plan around its mock timetable and internal deadlines. mainEntity.name: What happens if my child and the tutor simply do not get on?

acceptedAnswer.text: You say so, early, and a different tutor is shortlisted. This is treated as ordinary rather than as a complaint. Personality fit cannot be screened for in advance, only observed once teaching starts, so the first fortnight is the point to raise it. Waiting three months out of politeness costs the student far more than an awkward message costs anyone. Where possible the incoming tutor is briefed on what was already covered so the student is not made to repeat topics.

mainEntity.name: Do tutors help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, or only taught subjects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both, within limits. Extended Essay support means shaping a research question that can actually be answered in four thousand words, planning the sources, and reviewing structure and argument against the criteria. Theory of Knowledge support usually focuses on the exhibition and the essay prompts, and on building examples a student can defend. The supervisor at school remains the primary authority on both. A tutor supplements that relationship rather than replacing it, and never writes any part of the submitted work.

mainEntity.name: We have paid for a month and seen nothing change. What should we do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask for evidence rather than reassurance. After four weeks there should be something you can look at: a past paper marked with a question-level breakdown, a corrected set of working, an internal assessment moved from topic to research question. If the only answer offered is that your child is improving in confidence, treat that as a warning. Sometimes the tutor is wrong for the student. Sometimes the student is not doing the work between sessions, and that needs a different conversation entirely.

contentBlocks.heading: Three moments when Sector 68 Gurugram parents start looking
contentBlocks.body:
There is a pattern to when enquiries arrive from this part of the Sohna Road extension, and it has almost nothing to do with the calendar the school publishes.

The first moment is a returned paper. Something came back on Friday, the mark was worse than expected, and the weekend has been tense. What that family needs is speed and diagnosis, not a six-month plan.

The second moment is a deadline three or four weeks out. Usually an internal assessment, sometimes a Theory of Knowledge exhibition, occasionally the first draft of an Extended Essay. Here the requirement is narrow and technical. The tutor has to know the criteria for that subject and be honest about what can still be changed in the time left.

The third moment is planning. A parent decides in July that DP2 will not be improvised, and asks for support before anything has gone wrong. This is the rarest call and by far the most effective one.

IB tutors in Sector 68 Gurugram get shortlisted differently for each of those. Treating all three as the same request is how families end up with a tutor who is competent and still wrong for them.

This term: planning DP2 before problems appear

contentBlocks.heading: From your first message to a shortlist for Sector 68
contentBlocks.body:
The opening call is short and mostly consists of questions. Which subject, and at which level. Which school, and what its assessment calendar looks like for the next eight weeks. What has already been tried, including tutors who did not work out and why. How many hours a week the family can actually protect, allowing for co-curriculars and travel.

That last answer is the one people overstate. Three sessions a week sounds committed in a phone call and collapses by the third Thursday.

A shortlist of two or three tutors follows, with a stated limitation against each name. One may be excellent on Economics but only free on Sundays. One may take students at home in Sector 68 but not before 8 pm.

The first session should be diagnostic. Expect the tutor to spend most of it finding where the difficulty begins rather than teaching forward from wherever the class happens to be. Expect a short written summary afterwards saying what they found.

If a shortlist arrives without any limitations mentioned, ask for them. Every real tutor has constraints, and the ones who name them tend to keep their commitments.

Two or three names with limitations stated in writing
Diagnostic first session, followed by a short summary

contentBlocks.heading: Which subjects come up most in Sector 68 enquiries
contentBlocks.body:
Economics and English A account for a surprising share of requests from these newer communities, and both are usually asked about late.

Economics goes wrong in a specific way. The student writes fluent explanation, draws the diagram correctly, and stops. The command term asked them to evaluate, and evaluation is a separate skill with its own structure. Once a student sees that, marks tend to move within a few papers. Getting there without a tutor pointing it out can take a year.

English A is harder to shop for because parents assume a strong reader will manage. The Paper 1 guided analysis punishes students who write about content rather than about technique and effect. Support here is mostly about building a method that survives an unseen text under time pressure.

Math AA HL and Math AI HL requests come in steadily, usually at the point where the student can no longer pattern-match from worked examples. Physics and Chemistry arrive in two waves: content help through the year, then a rush of internal assessment questions once data collection has begun and something has not worked.

An IB maths tutor Sector 68 families need is a different search from an IB science tutor Sector 68 families need.

contentBlocks.heading: What each IB programme asks for, from Grade 1 to Grade 12
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme runs roughly from ages 3 to 12. Support at this stage should be light-touch and frequent rather than long and heavy. Twenty-five focused minutes on reading or number work, several times a week, does more than a ninety-minute session that leaves a nine-year-old exhausted. Parents in Sector 68 sometimes ask for more intensity than a young child can absorb, and a good tutor will say so.

The Middle Years Programme covers ages 11 to 16. The recurring issue is not knowledge but presentation against criteria. A student can understand a scientific concept fully and still score poorly on Criterion B because the investigation was not designed the way the descriptor requires.

The Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, carries the heaviest load. Six subjects, internal assessments in most of them, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, and the creativity, activity and service requirement running underneath. Tutoring here works best when it is scheduled around the school's own deadlines rather than in competition with them, which is why the assessment calendar comes up on the very first call.
items: PYP: short frequent sessions beat long ones
MYP: designing work to match the criterion, not just knowing it
DP: six subjects, IAs, EE, TOK and CAS at once
Sessions planned around school deadlines, not against them

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 68 sits in Gurugram, and which tutors can reach it
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 68 belongs to the newer sector corridor off the Sohna Road extension. The roads are better than in older Gurugram; the distances are longer. That combination produces a specific outcome for home tutoring, which is that a tutor will happily travel here on a Saturday morning and think twice about a Tuesday at seven.

Tata Primanti and Central Park Resorts sit close enough that a tutor visiting one can often take a second student in the other on the same evening. M3M Golf Estate and Emaar Emerald Hills work similarly. Where two families coordinate slots, both usually get a better time than either would alone.

Sector 65 and Sector 50 are the nearest reference points for travel. Nirvana Country and South City 1 are further, and DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 further still, which is why tutors based in those areas tend to offer online sessions to Sector 68 rather than home visits.

Home tutoring may be available depending on tutor schedules. That phrasing is deliberate. Nobody can promise a home slot in this sector before checking who is actually free.

Coordinating slots between Tata Primanti and Central Park Resorts helps

contentBlocks.heading: Home or online in Sector 68 Gurugram, judged against your deadline
contentBlocks.body:
If the deadline is this month, online usually wins, because you can start sooner and you are not limited to tutors within driving distance. An internal assessment review does not need anyone in the room. It needs someone who can read a draft, mark it against the criteria, and talk through the changes on a shared screen.

If the work is long-term repair over a full term, home sessions have a real edge. Attention holds better. The tutor sees the student's actual desk, the actual pile of unfinished worksheets, and the phone that keeps lighting up.

For younger children the answer is almost always home, if a tutor is free.

Many families run both. A weekend home session for depth, where a full past paper can be worked through end to end, and a short online session midweek aimed at whatever came up in class that week. Others start online because it is faster to arrange, then move to home tutoring once a tutor with a workable route becomes available.

Online tutoring is available across Gurugram for supported IB subjects. Home tutoring near Sector 68 is subject to tutor availability for that subject and time.
items: Short deadline: online starts sooner and widens the pool
Long repair work: home sessions hold attention better

contentBlocks.heading: IB schools reached from Sector 68 Gurugram, and why it matters

GD Goenka World School in the Sohna Road region is the most natural fit geographically for families on this side of the corridor. Pathways World School, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and Lancers International School on Golf Course Road also take students from these communities.

A tutor who knows that a particular school runs Diploma mocks in the first half of DP2 will build the revision plan backwards from that date. A tutor who does not know will schedule as though the terminal examination is the only fixed point, and the student will hit the mock unprepared.

School policy on tutoring also varies. Some departments want to know a student has external support and will coordinate. Others prefer not to be involved. Asking your child's coordinator is worth ten minutes.

contentBlocks.heading: The checks that happen before a name is sent to you
contentBlocks.body:
Screening covers documents, subject depth and teaching ability, in that order, and each stage removes different people.

Documents come first: identity and the qualifications a tutor claims. That is the easy part. Subject depth is where most applications fail. Someone comfortable with school mathematics is not automatically able to teach Math AA HL, and the check is built around content that only appears at higher level. The same applies to Physics and Chemistry, where a tutor may be strong on theory and unfamiliar with what an internal assessment actually has to contain.

IB-specific knowledge is assessed on its own. Criterion-related assessment, command-term language, the structure of an internal assessment, the difference between a school's internal expectations and an examiner's mark scheme. A tutor from a board background who has never worked with any of this needs to learn it before teaching, not while teaching.

Teaching ability is judged on explanation rather than on qualifications. A tutor is asked to teach something difficult, briefly, to someone who does not already understand it, because that reveals more in ten minutes than a transcript does. The final piece, whether a tutor suits your particular child, cannot be tested in advance by anyone, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest.
items: Identity and qualification documents first
Subject depth tested at the level being claimed
IB assessment literacy assessed separately
Fit with your child is only visible after teaching starts

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, commitments and what to settle before session one
contentBlocks.body:
Fee levels move with the programme, the level within it, how scarce the subject is, and whether the tutor is travelling to Sector 68 or teaching online. An HL Diploma subject with a small local pool costs more than MYP support in a commonly taught subject. That is arithmetic, not a sales position.

Settle the practical terms before the first session. How much notice cancels a session without charge. Whether a missed session can be made up in the same month. What happens to the fee during school examination weeks when sessions naturally drop. Whether you are committing to a block or paying as you go.

One more question is worth asking directly: what will this tutor refuse to do. Any tutor willing to draft your child's internal assessment or Extended Essay is a liability. IB academic honesty procedures are handled by the school, and the consequences fall on the student, not on the tutor who offered.

Everything above can be reviewed on a call. Nothing is committed until the family agrees to it, and a trial session exists precisely so that the decision can be made with evidence.
items: Cost reflects level, scarcity and travel, not a fixed rate
Agree cancellation notice and make-up rules in advance

Nothing is committed before a trial session

contentBlocks.heading: Booking IB tuition near Sector 68 Gurugram this week
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the timeline. Tell an advisor whether the problem is a paper returned last week, a submission due this month, or a term you want to plan properly. That single answer changes the shortlist more than anything else.

Then the specifics. Subject and level, since HL and SL are staffed from different pools. School, because its mock timetable sets the plan. The grade your child is in. The two or three windows in the week that are genuinely free, allowing for the drive back from school and the co-curricular that always runs late.

Say whether you would prefer a tutor at home in Tata Primanti, Central Park Resorts, M3M Golf Estate, Emaar Emerald Hills or elsewhere in the sector, or whether online suits you better. If the deadline is close, online is usually the faster route to a start date, and you can move to home sessions later once a tutor with a workable route is free.
