contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Sent Your Way
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is not a badge. It is a set of checks, and it is worth knowing exactly what they cover so you can judge what they do not.

Identity and qualification documents are collected and read. A claim of teaching Physics at higher level has to line up with a degree, a teaching record, or both. Subject and level are recorded separately, because someone comfortable with standard level content is not automatically ready for Paper 3.

Experience with the IB specifically is asked about rather than assumed. Plenty of capable teachers have spent a decade on CBSE or Cambridge boards and have never marked against IB criteria or handled an internal assessment. That is a real gap and it shows up in the second week, not the first. Any IB private tutor near Sector 74 who cannot describe how they would guide an investigation does not go on a shortlist.

Tutors are also asked how they would approach a sample situation from the level they claim: an investigation that has gone off track, a student who cannot use command terms, a topic the class covered too fast.

Parent feedback after the early sessions carries more weight than any of this. If a match is not working, it is changed. No screening process catches everything.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Both: Picking a Mode That Survives Gurugram Traffic
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring wins on attention. A tutor at your dining table sees the notebook, the half-finished investigation, the phone that keeps lighting up. For younger students, particularly PYP and early MYP, that physical presence does work a screen cannot replicate.

But it is the fragile option in this part of Gurugram. One long meeting, one bad stretch on Sohna Road, and the session is gone. Parents who book IB home tuition in Sector 74 Gurugram at eight in the evening on weekdays often find the arrangement drifting within a month.

Online sessions are steadier and they widen the pool considerably. If your child needs Math AI HL or a narrow Economics focus, the strongest available teacher may sit in Delhi, Noida or Faridabad rather than anywhere near this corridor. An IB online tutor for Sector 74 Gurugram can start at nine without anyone worrying about the drive home. Screen sharing handles maths working and past-paper annotation well. It handles a distracted nine-year-old poorly.

The arrangement most families here settle into is mixed: a weekend home session where the tutor can afford the travel, and one or two shorter online sessions midweek for doubt-solving and homework review.

Parents comparing IB tutors in Sector 74 Gurugram do better to decide the mode after they know the subject and the hour, not before.

contentBlocks.heading: Honest Limits of Tutoring in a Newly Built Sector
contentBlocks.body:
A few things this page will not tell you, because they would not be true.

No tutor can promise a 7, a particular grade boundary, or a fixed percentage jump. IB grades depend on internal assessment moderation, examiner judgement across papers, and how a student performs in one week of a May or November session. Any IB coaching in Sector 74 that promises you a fixed outcome is selling something.

Availability here is genuinely uneven. Common combinations, Math AA HL or Physics on a weekend afternoon, are usually matchable. A Grade 12 Economics tutor for a nine-thirty weeknight home slot may simply not exist within travelling distance, and you deserve to hear that on the first call rather than in week three.

What can be described honestly is process. What the first session covers. What you should be seeing after four weeks: clearer written responses, fewer repeated errors on the same topic, homework finished without a fight. If none of that has shifted, the match is wrong and it should be changed rather than defended.

Fees depend on level, subject rarity and travel. They are discussed openly before anything is booked.

faqs.question: How long does it take to arrange an IB tutor for Sector 74?
faqs.answer: It depends on the combination. A common subject like Physics at standard level in a weekend afternoon slot is usually matched within a couple of days. Math AA HL for a nine o clock weeknight home session takes longer, because the pool of tutors willing to travel to the Sohna Road extension at that hour is small. An advisor will tell you which category your request falls into on the first call rather than leaving you waiting. Online requests generally move faster, because travel stops being a constraint at all.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring actually practical in Sector 74, or should we just go online?
faqs.answer: Both work, for different situations. Home tutoring suits younger students and weekend slots, where a tutor can absorb the travel time without wrecking the rest of the day. Weeknight evenings after seven are the difficult ones, because the drive in from Sohna Road, Sector 49 or Golf Course Road is unpredictable. Many families here run a weekend home session and keep midweek doubt-solving on screen. If a subject is rare at higher level, online usually gives you a better teacher even though a home tutor is technically available.

faqs.question: My child studies at Scottish High International School in Sector 57. Does the school matter for matching?
faqs.answer: Yes, for two practical reasons. The return time sets how much energy is left for a session, so a Grade 11 student getting home after four is better served by a shorter, sharper weekday slot. The school also sets the assessment calendar: when internal assessment drafts fall due, when mocks are scheduled, how a department sequences topics through the year. A tutor who knows that rhythm plans around it. IB Gram is not affiliated with any school named on this page and does not represent them in any way.

faqs.question: What does the first session with a new tutor actually cover?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis, mostly. The tutor looks at recent school assessments, marked work and the feedback comments that came with them, then asks the student to attempt something from the current topic while watching how it is approached. Errors that repeat matter more than errors that appear once. By the end there should be a plain statement of what is going wrong and a plan for the next four weeks: what will be covered, in what order, and what you should expect to see change first.

faqs.question: How are fees decided for a Sector 74 booking?
faqs.answer: By level, subject rarity and travel. A Grade 6 MYP maths session close to the home of the tutor costs less than a Grade 12 higher level Chemistry session that needs a specialist to drive across Gurugram at peak hour. Online rates are usually lower for the same tutor because the travel disappears from the calculation. Everything is discussed before you commit, and there is no charge for receiving a shortlist. If a quoted rate does not suit, say so early and the shortlist can be rebuilt at a different experience level.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two subjects, say Physics and Maths?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because it halves the scheduling problem. Physics and Math AA overlap enough that a strong teacher often covers both credibly at standard level. At higher level the overlap thins out, particularly around Math AA proof and analysis work, and a student may be better served by two specialists even though it complicates the week. Economics and English A rarely pair with anything else. The honest answer depends on the individual tutor rather than on the subject combination alone.

faqs.question: What if we only start Diploma Programme support in Grade 12?
faqs.answer: It can still help, but the plan changes shape. There is no longer time to rebuild foundations across a full syllabus, so the work becomes triage: identify the two or three topics costing the most marks, fix exam technique on those, and protect whatever internal assessment deadlines remain. A tutor who promises to cover everything before the May session is not being straight with you. Starting in Grade 11, or even the second half of it, leaves far more room to work with.

faqs.question: We live in Sector 65 rather than Sector 74. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: Very little. Sector 65, Sector 50, Nirvana Country and South City 1 sit on the same set of approach roads, and a tutor covering one of them can usually cover the others. What changes is the ordering of an evening. If someone already teaches in Sector 65 at six, a seven o clock slot nearby is realistic. The same tutor cannot promise a Golf Course Road session and a Sector 74 session inside the same hour band, and honest scheduling matters more than good intentions.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no visible progress after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Tell the advisor rather than waiting it out. Four weeks is enough to see whether written responses are getting clearer, whether the same mistakes keep returning, and whether the student is doing the work between sessions. If those signals stay flat, the usual causes are a mismatch of teaching style, a session length that does not suit the student, or a level the tutor is not genuinely strong in. A different tutor is arranged. There is no argument about it and no pressure to continue.

faqs.question: Do I need to know whether my child is doing standard level or higher level before calling?
faqs.answer: It helps enormously, and the school report or subject choice form will say. Higher level courses carry more content, an extra paper in several subjects, and a different depth of question. A tutor comfortable at standard level is not automatically ready for higher level work, so naming the level early prevents a mismatch that would otherwise surface in week two. If you genuinely do not know, bring a recent marked assessment to the first call and the level is usually obvious from the paper itself.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an IB student in Sector 75 usually need?
faqs.answer: For one subject, one longer session plus a short doubt-solving slot is a common pattern. Two full sessions a week suit a student who is behind on content rather than on technique. More than that is rarely useful during term, because the student also needs time to attempt work independently, and tutoring that removes that time hides the very gaps it should be finding. Closer to internal assessment deadlines or mock weeks, frequency can be raised temporarily and then dropped back.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the extended essay if the subject is not one they teach?
faqs.answer: Partly. Structure, research question framing, referencing, the reflection sessions with the supervisor and keeping to the word limit are transferable, and a strong tutor in a related area can help with all of it. Subject-specific analysis is different. An extended essay in History needs someone who reads historiography, not a Physics tutor with good essay instincts. The school supervisor remains the person responsible for the essay, and outside support should sit alongside that relationship rather than replacing it.

faqs.question: We live near Central Park Resorts. Will a tutor come inside the society?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, once entry is sorted. Large gated developments in this part of Gurugram control visitor access at the main gate, and a tutor without a standing pass can be held up long enough to eat into the session. Families who arrange a recurring visitor entry for the tutor in advance avoid the problem entirely. If society rules make regular entry awkward, the practical alternatives are a common area within the complex or moving that subject online.

faqs.question: What is the difference between tutoring for MYP and tutoring for the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: The work changes shape. Middle Years tutoring is largely about matching a response to criteria, so a student who understands the topic stops losing marks on presentation and structure. Diploma tutoring adds content depth, internal assessment supervision, past-paper technique and time management across six subjects at once. A tutor who is excellent with Grade 9 students is not automatically the right person for a Grade 12 higher level course, and the reverse is also true more often than people expect.

faqs.question: Is it a problem if the tutor has never taught at my child's school?
faqs.answer: Not in itself. What matters is that the tutor understands the IB assessment model and is willing to work from your school's calendar and its marked feedback. Ask them how they would use a returned assignment with teacher comments on it. A tutor who reads those comments carefully and builds the next month around them will be more useful than someone who happens to know the building. School familiarity is a small convenience, not a qualification.

faqs.question: What if my child needs help in two subjects at once?
faqs.answer: That is common in Grade 11, when several courses step up together. Two options exist. One tutor covering both subjects keeps the schedule simple and gives a single view of how the student works, which suits related subjects. Two specialists give better depth, particularly at higher level, at the cost of a more crowded week. Cost also differs, so it is worth asking for both versions of the shortlist and deciding once you can see the actual timings side by side.

faqs.question: How do we know the tutor is actually qualified and not just confident?
faqs.answer: Documents are checked before a name is recommended, and the trial session tells you the rest. During it, ask the tutor to explain one topic your child finds difficult and watch whether the explanation adapts when the student does not follow. Ask directly how many IB students they have taught and at which level. Confident vagueness usually shows up within ten minutes of a specific question about criteria or command terms.

faqs.question: Can sessions pause during school holidays or family travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better to plan the pause than to cancel week by week. Tell the tutor the dates as soon as you know them so the plan can be resequenced rather than interrupted. Many families use holiday weeks differently, running longer sessions on content that needs rebuilding while there is no homework competing for time. Fees and scheduling for a break are agreed in advance, and picking a slot back up afterwards depends on tutor availability at that point.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by Subject: Where New Gurgaon Students Usually Stall

In Math AA at higher level, the stall is normally proof and the algebraic manipulation underneath calculus. Students can differentiate and still not see why a step is allowed. In Math AI, the stall is written interpretation: a correct regression followed by a sentence that says nothing about the context. Physics stalls at translating a described situation into a diagram and then into equations. Chemistry stalls at mechanism and at the internal assessment, where a promising idea turns out to have no measurable variable. An IB science tutor in Sector 76 spends real time on investigation design, which is teaching, not admin.

Economics stalls on evaluation. Students write everything they know and never answer the question asked.

English A stalls on close analysis. Summarising a text is comfortable. Arguing about how a writer builds an effect, with evidence, is the part that earns marks and the part most students avoid.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP to DP: What Changes as Your Child Moves Up
contentBlocks.body:
Families asking about IB tutors in Sector 76 Gurugram often treat the three programmes as three difficulty settings of the same thing. They are not. Each asks for something different, and the transitions between them are where families most often ask for help.

The Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, is built on inquiry. Support at this stage should protect curiosity while building reading fluency and number confidence. Sessions of thirty to forty minutes work better than long ones.

Moving into the Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, the change is assessment. Work is judged against four criteria per subject, and a student used to being told they got the answer right now has to show process, communication and reflection. This transition surprises capable students most, because effort no longer maps neatly onto marks.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, adds volume and permanence. Internal assessments count towards the final grade. The extended essay runs across months. Theory of Knowledge asks for a kind of thinking nobody has explicitly taught them. And the May 2026 or November 2026 papers sit at the end of it with no reschedule available.

A student entering the Diploma from a different curriculum needs a term of adjustment, not a crash course.

contentBlocks.heading: The distance between a predicted 5 and a final 7 in Sector 77, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
A predicted grade is a forecast. A subject teacher writes it from classwork, mocks and internal assessment drafts, and a university admissions office then reads it as though it were a promise. It is not one.

Every year some students finish above their prediction and some finish two grades below it, and the reason is rarely raw ability. The reasons are narrow and unglamorous. Marks lost because a command term was skimmed instead of answered. An internal assessment stuck at fourteen out of twenty-four because the research question was too broad back in September and nobody said so. Paper 2 questions half finished because the student had never sat one against a clock.

A tutor working with one child can chase those losses directly. A class teacher carrying thirty students, a unit plan and a reporting calendar cannot, and it would be unfair to expect it. So the useful question for a parent here is not whether the child is capable. It is which four or five recurring errors keep appearing in the marked scripts, and whether anyone has written them down in one place.

That list is what a workable tutoring arrangement is built on. Without it, sessions become supervised homework and the prediction stays exactly where it was.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 77 Gurugram students lose marks between prediction and result
contentBlocks.body:
Math AA HL predictions slip when the algebra underneath the calculus was never secure. A student follows the lesson, reproduces the method and then loses method marks in a paper because a trigonometric identity was memorised in Grade 10 rather than understood. Math AI HL fails in a different place. The modelling looks approachable, and marks disappear in the sentence that has to say what the model means for the situation it came from.

Physics predictions tend to be generous about experimental work. A student fluent with equations can still write a thin uncertainty analysis, and that shows up in Paper 3 and in the internal assessment long before it shows up in a class test.

Chemistry has organic mechanisms as its fault line. Pathways learned as pictures collapse the moment a paper asks for curly arrows and a written justification.

Economics loses marks on diagrams and on evaluation. Students describe a policy carefully when the command term asked them to weigh it against an alternative.

English A moves more on the analysis paper than on the oral. A student can speak intelligently about a text and still submit a Paper 1 commentary that retells the extract instead of arguing about how it has been constructed.

Six subjects, six different repairs. Choosing an IB maths tutor in Sector 77 by subject name alone misses most of that.

Physics: uncertainties, Paper 3 and the IA

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and Diploma needs across Sector 77 households

The Primary Years Programme runs from ages three to twelve and produces no grade a university will ever see. Support at this stage is about reading stamina, number sense and the habit of asking a question before answering one. Good early tutoring here looks slow. It should not turn inquiry into worksheet drilling, which is the most common complaint parents bring after a poor experience elsewhere.

The Middle Years Programme covers ages eleven to sixteen and is where the first honest signal appears. Criterion-related assessment tells you a great deal if you read it properly. A child scoring well on Criterion A and poorly on Criterion D is not weak at the subject. They are weak at applying it to unfamiliar contexts, and that is a specific, teachable thing.

The Diploma Programme runs from sixteen to nineteen and carries the predicted grade that matters for applications. Here the work is specialist: subject depth at HL and SL, internal assessment direction, extended essay reading alongside the school supervisor, theory of knowledge essay planning, and a revision plan that survives contact with school deadlines.

Grade 1 through Grade 12 can be supported. What changes is who counts as a sensible match, and a Diploma physics specialist is often the wrong person for a Grade 4 reader.

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a name reaches a Sector 77 parent
contentBlocks.body:
Identity comes first, against a government photo document. Then qualifications, which means seeing the certificate rather than accepting a line on a profile. Then the teaching claim itself, which is the part most platforms wave through.

A tutor saying they teach Chemistry HL is asked what they have taught recently, at which level, for how long, and what an internal assessment they supervised was actually about. Vague answers to that question are informative. Specific answers usually come from people who have done the work.

Where a tutor offers references from previous families, those are followed up. Where they do not, that is recorded rather than quietly dropped.

And here is the honest limit. A check confirms what someone has done in the past. It cannot tell you how your particular child will respond to their manner, their pace or their handwriting on a whiteboard. Nothing on paper predicts that.

contentBlocks.heading: What a tutor cannot fix, said plainly
contentBlocks.body:
No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does should be declined on the spot. Marks are awarded by external examiners against published criteria, and no arrangement made in a flat in Sector 77 has any influence over that.

Time is the real constraint. A student starting focused work in March of Grade 12 has a handful of weeks and can usually repair exam timing, technique and one or two specific topics. Rebuilding two years of shaky foundations inside that window is not realistic, and hearing so on the first call is more useful than being sold optimism.

Attendance is the second constraint. Two cancelled sessions a month undo most of what the other two achieved.

There is a third, quieter one. Some students do not want a tutor and will sit through sessions politely without engaging. Naming that early matters, because a different approach, a different person or a short pause often works better than adding hours.

faqs.question: The school predicted a 5 in Math AA HL. Can that realistically change before the May session?
faqs.answer: It can move, and it also may not. What tutoring addresses is the part of the loss that comes from technique: method marks dropped through weak algebra, questions abandoned under time pressure, answers that ignore what the command term asked for. Those are repairable within a term if sessions run regularly. What cannot be repaired in a few weeks is a two-year foundation gap in a subject built cumulatively. An honest tutor will tell you which of the two you are dealing with after reading marked papers, and nobody should be promising you a number.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma student here usually take?
faqs.answer: Two a week per subject is the common pattern during term, dropping to one when things are stable and rising during an internal assessment window or the run-up to mocks. Some families start with a single weekly session to test the fit before committing further. More is not automatically better. A student already doing seven hours at school plus activities has a ceiling, and past that point sessions turn into supervised sitting rather than learning. Review the plan roughly monthly against actual marked work, not against how the week felt.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually travel to Godrej Air or Vatika India Next in the evening?
faqs.answer: Some will, depending on where they live and what else they are teaching that day. Tutors already working with a student inside the same township are the most likely to offer a workable slot. Those driving from the Golf Course Road or DLF side face a long return journey and often decline late bookings or price them higher. Availability changes week to week and is confirmed at the point of matching rather than promised in advance. If home sessions cannot be arranged at a sensible hour, online is usually the better trade.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in this sector actually depend on?
faqs.answer: Four things, mostly. The level, because HL Diploma teaching costs more than Middle Years support. The subject, since rare HL combinations have fewer available specialists. The mode, as home visits carry travel time that online sessions do not. And the tutor's own experience with the specific assessment you need help with. Fees are discussed openly before any session is booked, and no standard rate applies to every enquiry. Ask what is included as well: some tutors mark practice papers between sessions, others do not.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely good enough for higher level subjects?
faqs.answer: For Diploma students it is often the stronger option. A shared screen with an annotated past paper is a better teaching surface than a notebook on a dining table, work can be marked and returned between sessions, and the pool of specialists for something like Math AA HL or Physics HL widens well beyond driving distance. The trade is presence. A student who needs someone physically alongside to stay on task will do better in person, and that describes younger learners far more often than sixteen-year-olds.

faqs.question: We want help with the extended essay rather than a subject. Is that possible?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common request around the drafting stages. A tutor can help narrow a research question that is currently too broad, build a workable structure, sort out referencing and read a draft critically before it goes to the school supervisor. What they will not do is write it, supply arguments as though they were the student's own, or contradict the supervisor's instructions. The school owns the process and the deadlines. Support of this kind works best when it starts before the first draft rather than during the final week.

faqs.question: What happens if we simply do not get on with the first tutor?
faqs.answer: You say so and ask for another name. Two sessions is usually enough to know whether the manner and pace suit your child, and changing early costs far less than persisting for a term out of politeness. No explanation is needed beyond the fact that the fit is not working. The shortlist normally has other names on it. If you can say what specifically did not work, the next suggestion becomes a genuine improvement rather than a coin toss between two similar profiles.

faqs.question: Do you work with Middle Years students or only with the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Both, and the Primary Years Programme as well, across Grade 1 to Grade 12. Middle Years work is often the more valuable investment because problems caught at Year 3 or Year 4 are still small. Criterion-related feedback gives a precise picture of what is going wrong, and a tutor who reads those strands properly can target one weak criterion instead of reteaching an entire subject. Parents who wait until Grade 11 to act usually find the same gap has grown considerably harder to close.

faqs.question: How soon after we get in touch can sessions realistically begin?
faqs.answer: Common subjects at common times can often be arranged within a few days. Rare higher level combinations, or requests for a specific evening slot with a home visit in Sector 77, take longer because fewer people meet both conditions at once. Everything is subject to tutor availability at that moment, so nothing is confirmed until a name has accepted. If timing is urgent because of a deadline, say so at the start, since that changes which tutors are worth approaching first.

contentBlocks.heading: How to compare two IB tutors in Sector 78 Gurugram without guessing
contentBlocks.body:
Two profiles arrive. Both look credible. One has a stronger university on the page and the other charges four hundred rupees less an hour, and most families pick on one of those two facts.

Both are poor predictors. A degree tells you somebody once passed their own exams. It says nothing about whether they can watch a Grade 9 student write a paragraph and identify, in real time, which misunderstanding produced it. A lower rate often reflects less experience with the specific assessment you need, which is expensive later.

There is a cheaper test. Send both candidates the same piece of your child's marked work and ask each one what they would do first. The answers separate quickly. One will describe a syllabus and offer to revise the chapter. The other will point at two lines on the script and explain what the student appears to believe that is not true.

That second answer is the one worth paying for. It is also the only comparison that survives contact with a real child, because it tests diagnosis rather than knowledge.

Everything below is written to help a parent in Sector 78 run that comparison properly.

Ask what they would do in week one, not what they can teach

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or Diploma: know which one you are hiring for
contentBlocks.body:
These are three different jobs, and a person excellent at one can be mediocre at another.

Primary Years work, ages three to twelve, needs patience and a light touch with inquiry. The tutor has to build reading stamina and number confidence without converting a child's curiosity into a stack of worksheets. Ask a candidate how they would handle a seven-year-old who says maths is boring. Listen for whether the answer involves the child's own questions.

Middle Years, ages eleven to sixteen, is the criterion-reading job. A good MYP tutor asks to see the criterion breakdown before the overall grade, because a student weak on Criterion C and fine on Criterion B needs communication practice, not more content.

The Diploma, sixteen to nineteen, is the specialist job. HL depth, internal assessment direction, extended essay reading, theory of knowledge planning and exam technique under time pressure.

When comparing two names, ask which of these three they have taught in the last twelve months, not which they are willing to teach. Willingness is abundant. Recent practice is not. Support runs across Grade 1 to Grade 12, but the right person changes at each boundary.

DP, ages 16 to 19: HL depth, IA, EE and TOK

Sector 78 sits in the newer western residential belt, with Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and the Vatika India Next township as the main addresses families write on an enquiry form. A tutor living inside that belt, or already teaching a student in one of those towers, can hold a weekday slot at half past six and keep it all term.

A tutor coming from Golf Course Road, DLF Phase 1 or Phase 4, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sector 50, Sector 65, Nirvana Country or South City 1 is looking at a long return drive in evening traffic. They may still take the booking. They will cancel more often than the nearby one, and both of you will pretend the reason is something else.

So weigh it honestly. If the two candidates are close in ability, take the near one. If the distant one is clearly stronger for an HL subject, take them online rather than asking them to drive. contentBlocks.heading: Subject questions that separate a good candidate from a plausible one
contentBlocks.body:
For Math AA HL, ask which topic students most often fake fluency in. A candidate who says trigonometric identities, or the algebra that sits underneath integration by substitution, has marked real scripts. A candidate who says calculus is difficult has not.

For Math AI HL, ask how they teach a student to write the interpretation sentence after a regression. The modelling itself is rarely the problem.

For Physics, ask what they do about uncertainties. Weak answers treat it as a formula. Strong answers treat it as a habit built across a term, because it decides marks in Paper 3 and in the internal assessment.

For Chemistry, ask them to explain a mechanism out loud. If curly arrows do not appear in the explanation, the student will memorise pictures.

For Economics, ask how they train evaluation. Watch for whether they mention command terms by name.

For English A, ask what a Paper 1 commentary should do that a summary does not. This one exposes people quickly.

Ask the same question to both candidates and write the answers down. Comparing an IB science tutor in Sector 78 against another becomes straightforward once you have two answers side by side on paper.

Local students commonly attend Pathways World School in the wider Gurugram region, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and GD Goenka World School towards Sohna Road.

A tutor who has worked with students from your child's school knows the rhythm of its internal assessment deadlines and how its reports are worded. That saves a fortnight of orientation. It is a genuine advantage and worth asking about.

But treat it as a tiebreaker, never as the deciding factor. Familiarity with a school is not the same as skill with a student, and a tutor who names your school warmly may simply be good at conversation. A tutor from an unfamiliar school who reads a marked script accurately is the better hire every time.

One more caution. No tutor speaks for a school, negotiates a deadline, or overrules an extended essay supervisor. If a candidate implies otherwise during a call, that is a reason to remove them from your shortlist rather than a reason to be impressed.

contentBlocks.heading: Weighing a nearby home tutor against a stronger online one
contentBlocks.body:
This is the trade most Sector 78 families end up making, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a preference.

Home sessions win on presence. A younger child stays on task because an adult is sitting beside them, materials are physical, and a parent can glance in. For Grade 1 through roughly Grade 7, this usually outweighs a modest gap in tutor quality.

Online wins on selection and on marking. The pool for a rare HL combination stops being limited by driving distance. A shared screen with an annotated past paper is a better working surface than a notebook, and work can be marked between sessions rather than during them. For Diploma students, particularly after nine in the evening, it is often the stronger choice.

Online loses badly with a distractible child left alone in a room. That is worth saying because it is the failure families report most.

A hybrid settles the argument for many households: one visit a week for accountability, one online session for the technical work. Home availability across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and Sohna Road depends on tutor schedules and is confirmed case by case.

Families continue with a poor match far longer than they should, usually out of politeness. A term of that costs more than any fee difference between two candidates.

Set the exit criteria before the first session, while everyone is calm. Something like this: after four weeks there should be a written list of the child's recurring errors, a visible change in how an unfamiliar question is approached, and at least one piece of marked school work you can hold against the month before. If none of the three has appeared, the arrangement is not working.

Also worth naming honestly: nobody can promise a grade, and a tutor who offers one is telling you something about themselves. External examiners award marks against published criteria and no session in Sector 78 changes that.

When you do stop, say it directly and give reasonable notice. Tutors here largely know each other, and a clean ending is better for everybody than a slow fade of cancelled sessions.

Then ask for the next name. Changing at week five is ordinary. Changing at week twenty is expensive.

contentBlocks.heading: What a background check proves, and what it leaves to you
contentBlocks.body:
Before a name reaches your shortlist, identity is confirmed against a government photo document and qualification certificates are seen rather than assumed from a profile line.

The teaching claim is then tested with specifics. What did you teach last year, at which level, for how long. Describe an internal assessment you supervised and what the student's research question was. People who have done the work answer these easily. People who have not become general.

References from previous families are followed up where a tutor offers them, and where none are offered, that absence is noted rather than hidden.

Here is what none of that establishes. Whether your child will listen to this person. Whether the pace suits them. Whether a quiet manner reads as calm or as disinterest to a fifteen-year-old. Documents cannot answer any of it, and no platform should suggest otherwise.

So the checks remove the candidates who should never have been on a list. Your comparison, run over the first two sessions, decides the rest. Keep it that way round.

faqs.question: We have two names and cannot decide between them. What should we compare first?
faqs.answer: Recent teaching at the exact level your child studies, ahead of everything else. A tutor who taught Physics HL last year is a different proposition from one who taught Physics SL three years ago, even if both profiles say Physics. After that, compare how each responds to a piece of marked work. Ask both what they would tackle in week one and write the answers down. A candidate who names two specific errors is more useful than one who offers to revise the chapter from the beginning.

faqs.question: Is it sensible to run a trial session with both candidates before choosing?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you can afford the time, and it is the cleanest comparison available. Give both the same brief and the same material so the sessions are genuinely comparable. Afterwards ask your child a narrow question rather than a broad one: not whether they liked the tutor, but whether they understood something today that they did not understand yesterday. Children are generous about likeability and accurate about clarity. Two trials cost a few hours and prevent a term spent with the wrong person.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who teaches at an IB school automatically make the better choice?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Classroom teaching and one-to-one teaching reward different skills. A serving teacher brings current familiarity with syllabus changes and marking standards, which is genuinely valuable. But managing thirty students is not the same as sitting with one and working out what a single child has misunderstood. Some teachers are outstanding at both and some are not. Judge on the diagnostic answer rather than on the employer, and ask how many individual students they have worked with recently.

faqs.question: How do fees usually differ between a nearby home tutor and an online specialist?
faqs.answer: Home visits carry travel time, and in this part of the city that travel can run to well over an hour in total. Tutors price that in, so a home rate typically sits above an online rate for comparable experience. Working the other way, a scarce higher level specialist can charge more online than a generalist charges at your door. Level, subject rarity, mode and assessment experience all move the number. Rates are discussed openly before a booking, and asking what is included between sessions is worth doing.

faqs.question: My daughter is in MYP Year 4. Does the tutor need Diploma experience as well?
faqs.answer: It helps, though it is not essential. A tutor with Diploma experience can see where the subject is heading and prepare a Year 4 or Year 5 student for the jump in expectations. What matters more right now is comfort with criterion-related assessment, since that is how her work is judged. Ask any candidate to look at a recent task sheet and explain what a stronger response to one criterion would contain. Vague reassurance is a warning sign at this stage.

faqs.question: Can we ask a tutor for references from other families in Gurugram?
faqs.answer: You can ask, and many tutors will offer them. Where references are provided they are followed up during vetting, and you are welcome to speak to a family directly if the tutor is comfortable arranging it. Keep expectations sensible. References confirm reliability and manner, which is useful, and they cannot tell you how the person will suit your particular child. Some good tutors have few references simply because they are early in independent work. Weigh the absence, do not treat it as disqualifying.

faqs.question: How much notice should we give if we decide to stop?
faqs.answer: A week is courteous and usually enough, though it is worth agreeing the terms at the start rather than at the awkward moment. Say plainly why you are stopping, because tutors improve from specifics and a vague ending helps nobody. If the issue is fit rather than quality, saying so protects a decent tutor's reputation and helps an advisor suggest a better next name. Avoid the slow fade of repeatedly rescheduled sessions, which costs both sides more than a direct conversation.

faqs.question: Do sessions have to happen at the same time every week?
faqs.answer: A fixed slot works better for most students because it removes a weekly negotiation and protects the time from being eaten by other commitments. It is not compulsory. Families with irregular activity schedules often run one fixed session and one floating one arranged a few days ahead. The floating one is harder to keep, especially with a tutor who travels, so expect less consistency there. During examination periods most families move to a denser and more flexible pattern for a few weeks.

faqs.question: What if both shortlisted tutors turn out to be unavailable?
faqs.answer: You get further names. Availability moves constantly, since tutors fill slots, take on examination-season commitments or reduce their travel radius. A name that was open on Monday may not be open on Friday, which is why nothing is confirmed until a tutor has accepted the brief. If the constraint is a specific evening hour with a home visit, loosening either the hour or the mode usually reopens several options at once. Say which of the two you can flex.

contentBlocks.heading: What changes for a Sector 79 Gurugram student between August and May
contentBlocks.body:
In August everything feels manageable. New timetable, fresh notebooks, deadlines that sit comfortably far away. Most families do not think about tutoring at all in August, which is a shame, because it is the cheapest month to start.

By the middle of October the first reports land and the picture changes. A grade that felt like a blip in a class test is now written down. Around the same time the Diploma internal assessment calendar starts to bite, and Grade 11 students discover that data collection has to happen weeks before a draft is due.

December and January are the compression point. Draft deadlines stack against winter break, the extended essay wants attention, and nobody has done a full past paper under timed conditions.

February brings mocks and, with them, the first realistic estimate of where a student stands. March and April are technique and revision months, not content months. By then the syllabus is what it is.

So the honest way to think about a tutor is not as a permanent fixture, but as something whose shape should change four or five times between one August and the next May.

October: first reports turn a hunch into evidence
December and January: internal assessment drafts compress
February: mocks give a realistic estimate
March to May: technique and timed practice, not new content

Enquiries from here come mostly from Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and the Vatika India Next township, all sitting in the newer residential belt on the western side of the city.

The practical geography changes with the calendar, which is something families discover rather than plan for. Through the monsoon months of July to September the approach roads take on water and a tutor driving in from Sector 57 or the DLF phases will occasionally arrive forty minutes late or not at all. December and January bring morning fog on the northern corridors and a general reluctance to make long evening journeys.

March onwards is easier for travel and harder for scheduling, because school revision programmes and extra classes eat the slots that were free in September.

Nearby areas such as Sector 65, Sector 50, Nirvana Country, South City 1 and DLF Phase 1 and Phase 4 all lie across that commute rather than beside it. A tutor already teaching inside the same township is worth a great deal in January for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching. Families moving in from Delhi, Noida or Faridabad often keep an existing tutor and shift the sessions online.

contentBlocks.heading: Why the mode that works in September often fails by February
contentBlocks.body:
A home tutor arriving twice a week suits the early part of the year. There is time, the roads are cooperative by October, and a younger student benefits from someone physically present while habits are being built.

That arrangement gets fragile later. In the middle of a mock exam fortnight a student may need forty minutes on Tuesday and two hours on Saturday, and no visiting tutor can restructure their week that quickly. During the January drafting period a student often needs a document read and annotated between sessions rather than another hour of talking.

Online handles both of those better. A shared screen with a marked paper on it is a serious working surface, files move instantly, and a tutor two suburbs away can add a short session on a Thursday night without a car being involved.

The reverse is also true and worth stating. A Grade 5 student left alone with a laptop in November learns very little, whatever the tutor's quality.

Many households settle on a home session for continuity plus online capacity during crunch periods. Home availability across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and Sohna Road depends on tutor schedules and is checked at the time of matching.

contentBlocks.heading: When each subject turns difficult during the year
contentBlocks.body:
Math AA HL gets hard in the second half of Grade 11, when calculus arrives and every unresolved weakness in algebra and trigonometry surfaces at once. Students who coasted through the first term often stall here, and the repair takes longer in January than it would have in September.

Math AI HL peaks around the exploration. The modelling is approachable all year, and then a student has to write about what a model actually says, which is a different skill practised too late.

Physics concentrates its difficulty in the internal assessment window, where uncertainty analysis decides marks that no amount of equation fluency can recover.

Chemistry usually breaks in the first term of Grade 12 when organic mechanisms arrive and memorised diagrams stop working.

Economics tightens just before mocks, because evaluation cannot be crammed. It is a habit of weighing one policy against another, and it needs several months of practice.

English A becomes urgent in the Paper 1 run-up, when students realise that describing a text and analysing how it works are not the same activity.

Matching an IB science tutor in Sector 79 in October is a very different request from making the same request in March.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting a Sector 79 Gurugram search mid-term rather than in June
contentBlocks.body:
Most families call in October or January, not in June, and the process is built for that reality.

An advisor asks first what point in the year you are at and what is closest on the calendar. A draft due in three weeks, a mock in six, a set of reports that arrived yesterday. That single answer changes which tutors are worth approaching, because a tutor free for a long steady build is not necessarily the right person for a compressed piece of work.

Next comes evidence. A marked script, the report itself, or the assessment brief the school issued. Sending it before the call saves a week.

Then the search narrows on level, on experience with the specific piece of work in question, and on whether anybody can reach Sector 79 at the hour you need. Where the third condition fails, online is offered rather than a compromise on the first two.

You receive two or three names with a note on what each has taught, and you choose. The first session diagnoses rather than teaches, and it should end with a plan tied to the dates you gave. Availability depends on level and schedule.

contentBlocks.heading: The year has a different shape in PYP, MYP and the Diploma
contentBlocks.body:
For a Primary Years child, ages three to twelve, the year is mostly continuous. There is no external examination pulling at the calendar, so support can be steady and unhurried: reading built across months, number sense allowed to settle, curiosity protected from worksheet fatigue. Progress is judged by whether a seven-year-old reads for longer in April than in September.

Middle Years, ages eleven to sixteen, runs in units. Each one closes with criterion-related assessment, which means the useful checkpoints are unit ends rather than term ends. A tutor who reads those criterion strands can spot a pattern by the third unit, well before a report says anything alarming.

The Diploma, ages sixteen to nineteen, runs on deadlines that arrive in clusters. Internal assessments, the extended essay, the theory of knowledge essay and exhibition, plus mocks and the May or November session. Grade 11 is where the groundwork is either laid or postponed, and postponing it makes Grade 12 considerably worse.

Grade 1 to Grade 12 is covered. What differs is how often the plan needs revisiting, which is roughly termly for younger students and roughly monthly during the Diploma.

Each runs its own internal calendar, and the collisions are predictable once you have seen a few. A school trip in the last week of November against a Chemistry draft due in the first week of December. A creativity, activity and service commitment that eats the Saturday a student had earmarked for past papers. A tutor who has worked with students from that school anticipates the pile-up and plans backwards from it. That is most of the practical value of school familiarity, and it is worth asking about in October rather than discovering in December.

What a tutor cannot do is move a school deadline, speak for a department or overrule an extended essay supervisor. The school owns the calendar and the tutor works inside it.

The part families forget is the review that should happen again in the middle of the year. Sometimes it does and nothing changes. Sometimes a second tutor for one subject makes more sense than stretching the first across two. Occasionally the honest answer is that the student needs fewer hours and more sleep.

contentBlocks.heading: Four weeks in: what a Sector 79 Gurugram parent should see change
contentBlocks.body:
Set a checkpoint one month after the first session and judge it on three things, none of which is your child's mood.

First, a written list of recurring errors. Not a general comment about needing to work harder, but named mistakes: consistently misreading compare as describe, dropping units in calculations, writing conclusions that restate the introduction.

Second, a visible change in approach to an unfamiliar question. A student who now reads the command term before starting is progressing even if the mark has not moved yet.

Third, a piece of marked school work you can hold against something from the previous month. Marks move slowly and unevenly, so read the teacher's comments rather than the number.

If none of the three has appeared after four weeks, change something. Frequency, mode or the tutor.

And the plain limits, which matter more the later in the year you start. No tutor can guarantee a grade, since external examiners award marks against published criteria. A student beginning in March of Grade 12 can repair technique and a couple of topics, not two years of foundations. Missed sessions cost more progress than most parents expect.

faqs.question: It is already November. Is it too late to start for the May session?
faqs.answer: No, though what is achievable narrows from here. November to May gives roughly six working months once holidays and mocks are removed, which is enough to repair exam technique, rebuild two or three weak topics properly and improve internal assessment work that has not yet been submitted. What it does not allow is a full reconstruction of Grade 11 content alongside Grade 12 teaching. A tutor should tell you which of those you are facing after reading a marked paper, and should decline to promise a grade either way.

faqs.question: How should tutoring change during mock exam weeks?
faqs.answer: It should get shorter and more frequent rather than longer. During mocks a student has limited capacity, so forty-five focused minutes on the paper sat yesterday is worth more than a two-hour session covering new ground. Useful work in that fortnight is almost entirely reactive: go through what went wrong this morning while it is still fresh, then practise that specific question type. New content in mock weeks tends to be wasted. Afterwards, the marked mock papers become the most valuable planning document of the whole year.

faqs.question: Do sessions carry on through the school holidays?
faqs.answer: That depends on the family and the tutor, and both should agree it in advance rather than assume. Winter break is genuinely useful for Diploma students because the internal assessment drafting period sits right beside it and there is uninterrupted time to write. Longer summer breaks are better used lightly, with a weekly session to hold the habit rather than a full schedule. Younger students usually benefit from a real rest. Tutors often travel during holidays themselves, so confirm availability before planning around it.

faqs.question: My son has an internal assessment due in three weeks. Can a tutor help with just that?
faqs.answer: Yes, and short focused engagements of this kind are common. A tutor can help tighten a research question that is too broad, sort out the structure, check that the data or evidence supports the argument being made, and read a draft critically before the school supervisor sees it. What they will not do is write sections, supply the analysis, or work against the supervisor's instructions. Three weeks is workable. Three days is mostly damage limitation, and the tutor should say so plainly.

faqs.question: Are evening home sessions realistic here during the winter months?
faqs.answer: Less so than in October, and it is better to plan for that than to be surprised by it. Morning fog on the northern corridors makes long evening drives slow and occasionally unsafe, so tutors travelling from the older parts of the city cancel more often in December and January. Somebody already teaching inside the same township is far more reliable in those weeks. Many families in this sector keep a home slot for the milder months and switch to online for the winter, which removes the problem entirely.

faqs.question: How often should the plan be reviewed over the course of the year?
faqs.answer: Monthly during the Diploma and roughly termly for younger students. The natural review points are the ones the school already provides: the first reports, the end of an internal assessment cycle, the mock results and the start of the revision period. At each of those, ask whether the frequency, the mode and the person still suit the months ahead. Plans that were sensible in September are often wrong by February, not because anything failed but because the demands changed underneath them.

faqs.question: Can we pause after the May session and restart later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many families do exactly that. A Grade 11 student who has finished the year's examinations often takes a genuine break and resumes in late July or August, which is a reasonable rhythm. Do tell the tutor your intention early rather than at the last session, since they plan their own schedules around returning students and may not hold a slot indefinitely. If you expect to return to the same person, agree roughly when. Restarting with a familiar tutor saves several weeks of re-diagnosis.

faqs.question: Which subjects should a Grade 11 student start early on?
faqs.answer: Anything cumulative, which mostly means the mathematics courses and the sciences. Math AA HL in particular punishes delay, because Grade 12 content assumes fluency that a struggling student never built. Chemistry is worth starting before organic mechanisms arrive rather than after. Subjects that reward long practice rather than content coverage, such as Economics evaluation or English A analysis, also benefit from an early start because the skill accumulates slowly. Subjects that are largely content recall can be addressed later without the same penalty.

mainEntity.name: It is already November. Is it too late to start for the May session?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, though what is achievable narrows from here. November to May gives roughly six working months once holidays and mocks are removed, which is enough to repair exam technique, rebuild two or three weak topics properly and improve internal assessment work that has not yet been submitted. What it does not allow is a full reconstruction of Grade 11 content alongside Grade 12 teaching. A tutor should tell you which of those you are facing after reading a marked paper, and should decline to promise a grade either way.

mainEntity.name: How should tutoring change during mock exam weeks?

acceptedAnswer.text: It should get shorter and more frequent rather than longer. During mocks a student has limited capacity, so forty-five focused minutes on the paper sat yesterday is worth more than a two-hour session covering new ground. Useful work in that fortnight is almost entirely reactive: go through what went wrong this morning while it is still fresh, then practise that specific question type. New content in mock weeks tends to be wasted. Afterwards, the marked mock papers become the most valuable planning document of the whole year.

mainEntity.name: Do sessions carry on through the school holidays?

acceptedAnswer.text: That depends on the family and the tutor, and both should agree it in advance rather than assume. Winter break is genuinely useful for Diploma students because the internal assessment drafting period sits right beside it and there is uninterrupted time to write. Longer summer breaks are better used lightly, with a weekly session to hold the habit rather than a full schedule. Younger students usually benefit from a real rest. Tutors often travel during holidays themselves, so confirm availability before planning around it.

mainEntity.name: My son has an internal assessment due in three weeks. Can a tutor help with just that?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and short focused engagements of this kind are common. A tutor can help tighten a research question that is too broad, sort out the structure, check that the data or evidence supports the argument being made, and read a draft critically before the school supervisor sees it. What they will not do is write sections, supply the analysis, or work against the supervisor's instructions. Three weeks is workable. Three days is mostly damage limitation, and the tutor should say so plainly.

mainEntity.name: Are evening home sessions realistic here during the winter months?

acceptedAnswer.text: Less so than in October, and it is better to plan for that than to be surprised by it. Morning fog on the northern corridors makes long evening drives slow and occasionally unsafe, so tutors travelling from the older parts of the city cancel more often in December and January. Somebody already teaching inside the same township is far more reliable in those weeks. Many families in this sector keep a home slot for the milder months and switch to online for the winter, which removes the problem entirely.

mainEntity.name: How often should the plan be reviewed over the course of the year?

acceptedAnswer.text: Monthly during the Diploma and roughly termly for younger students. The natural review points are the ones the school already provides: the first reports, the end of an internal assessment cycle, the mock results and the start of the revision period. At each of those, ask whether the frequency, the mode and the person still suit the months ahead. Plans that were sensible in September are often wrong by February, not because anything failed but because the demands changed underneath them.

mainEntity.name: Can we pause after the May session and restart later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and many families do exactly that. A Grade 11 student who has finished the year's examinations often takes a genuine break and resumes in late July or August, which is a reasonable rhythm. Do tell the tutor your intention early rather than at the last session, since they plan their own schedules around returning students and may not hold a slot indefinitely. If you expect to return to the same person, agree roughly when. Restarting with a familiar tutor saves several weeks of re-diagnosis.

mainEntity.name: Which subjects should a Grade 11 student start early on?

acceptedAnswer.text: Anything cumulative, which mostly means the mathematics courses and the sciences. Math AA HL in particular punishes delay, because Grade 12 content assumes fluency that a struggling student never built. Chemistry is worth starting before organic mechanisms arrive rather than after. Subjects that reward long practice rather than content coverage, such as Economics evaluation or English A analysis, also benefit from an early start because the skill accumulates slowly. Subjects that are largely content recall can be addressed later without the same penalty.

finalCta: Tell an advisor which month you are in and what deadline is nearest, then attach a recent report or marked script. Two or three names come back with reasoning, and the first session ends with a plan tied to your actual dates rather than a standing weekly hour nobody has thought about.

introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 80 Gurugram are available for Grade 1 to Grade 12, covering PYP inquiry work, MYP criterion assignments and DP subjects with IA, EE and TOK support. IB Gram is a matching platform: you describe the level, the subject and the slot you can protect each week, and a shortlist is proposed subject to tutor availability. Home sessions depend on which side of Gurugram a tutor lives on. Online covers the whole city, including specialist HL subjects that Sector 80 cannot always staff locally.

contentBlocks.heading: What an hour of IB tutoring in Sector 80 Gurugram should actually buy
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the hour, not the month. A tutoring hour has a market rate, and in Gurugram that rate varies more by subject scarcity and level than by how far the tutor drives. So the useful question is what the hour contains. An hour that opens with fifteen minutes of setting up, drifts through a textbook chapter and ends with a promise to look something up is not cheap at any price.

A good IB hour looks different. The tutor arrives knowing which criterion or paper the work is being marked against. There is a piece of the student's own writing or working on the table, not a fresh worksheet. The correction is specific, in the language the examiner uses, and the student leaves with one task small enough to finish before the next session.

Parents in Sector 80 often compare quotes across three tutors and pick the middle one. A better comparison is what each tutor asks you before quoting. Someone who asks for the subject, the level, the school's internal deadline and a sample of recent work is pricing a job. Someone who quotes a flat rate for "IB" has not yet met the problem.

Fees on IB Gram depend on level, subject and schedule, and are confirmed with the tutor before anything begins.
items: Rate driven by level and subject scarcity, not distance alone
Session built around the student's own work, not fresh worksheets
Command-term language used during correction
One finishable task set per session
Fee confirmed before the first paid hour

contentBlocks.heading: How a shortlist gets built for a Sector 80 Gurugram family
contentBlocks.body:
The intake conversation is short and deliberately narrow. Grade and programme first, because PYP, MYP and DP need different people. Then the subject and level, because Math AA HL and Math AI HL are not interchangeable requests. Then the part most families skip: which two hours in the week are genuinely protected, after school transport, activities and homework are accounted for.

That last answer decides more than parents expect. Sector 80 sits far enough from the Golf Course Road side that a 7pm home session and a 5pm home session are effectively different jobs, and they draw from different pools of tutors. When the protected slot is late, the shortlist tilts towards online.

After that, subject fit is checked against what the student is actually being assessed on. A DP1 student three weeks from a first IA draft needs a tutor comfortable with methodology and referencing. A DP2 student in January needs someone who marks past papers quickly and honestly.

A shortlist is then shared, usually with two or three profiles, and you choose who to speak with. Availability is never assumed. Every profile is subject to the tutor confirming the slot, and a slot that looked open on Monday can be gone by Thursday.
items: Programme and grade captured before subject
HL and SL treated as separate requirements
Two protected weekly slots identified
Two or three profiles shared, not a directory
Slot confirmed with the tutor before scheduling

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: where the fees go at each stage
contentBlocks.body:
Cost tracks scarcity, and scarcity changes across the three programmes. PYP support in Sector 80 is usually about reading fluency, number sense and helping a child hold an inquiry question without an adult rewriting it for them. The tutor pool for that is wider, sessions are shorter, and the sensible rhythm is two brief sessions a week rather than one long one.

MYP is the stage families underestimate. The content is manageable; the marking is not. Students lose marks because they answer the question they understood rather than the criterion strand being assessed. Tutoring here is largely translation work, and a tutor who has read the criteria descriptors is worth more per hour than one who simply knows the topic.

DP is where fees rise, and for a defensible reason. HL sciences, Math AA HL and Economics at HL need subject specialists who can handle the IA and the externals, and there are fewer of them. Add the EE supervision, TOK essay planning and the exam-session pressure of May 2026 or November 2026, and the job is closer to academic mentoring than tuition.

Grade 1 to Grade 12 is covered. What changes is how many hours a week are worth paying for.
items: PYP: short, frequent sessions; reading and number sense
MYP: criterion translation, not extra content
DP HL: specialist subject knowledge, higher rate
EE and TOK support planned across terms, not weeks
Hour count matched to stage, not to worry

contentBlocks.heading: Travel time is part of the fee for IB tutors in Sector 80 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Nobody itemises it, but travel is priced in. A tutor living near Sushant Lok or Sector 57 who agrees to a 6pm home session in Sector 80 is giving up close to two hours of road either side of the lesson on a bad evening. That tutor either charges for it, takes fewer students, or quietly starts arriving late in the second month.

Home tutoring in Sector 80 works best when the tutor already lives on the New Gurgaon side, near Sector 79, 81, 82 or the Vatika India Next stretch. Those matches are worth waiting a week for. Home tutoring may also be arranged from Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 or Sohna Road depending on tutor schedules, but the further the origin, the narrower the timing options.

Online changes the arithmetic. The specialist pool opens across all of Gurugram and beyond, late slots become possible, and a cancelled session can often be moved rather than lost. For Math AA HL, Physics HL or a rare subject combination, online frequently produces the stronger tutor.

Many Sector 80 families end up hybrid: one home session on a weekend, one online midweek. It is not a compromise so much as an honest reading of the road.

Longer commutes narrow the timing choices
Online widens the specialist pool for HL subjects
Missed online sessions easier to reschedule
Hybrid: weekend at home, midweek online

contentBlocks.heading: Math AA HL, Physics and the subjects that cost more to staff
contentBlocks.body:
Six subject areas come up most often from this part of Gurugram: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A. They do not carry the same price or the same waiting time.

Math AA HL is the hardest to staff and the easiest to get wrong. A tutor who can do the mathematics but cannot read a Paper 3 question stem will keep a student busy without moving the grade. Math AI HL needs someone comfortable with modelling and interpretation, which is a different instinct entirely, and asking one tutor to cover both is usually a mistake.

Physics and Chemistry are demanding for a different reason. The IA is a graded investigation with a real methodology, and a lot of the tutoring hours go into narrowing a research question that is actually measurable in a school lab. Chemistry students often need organic mechanisms drilled separately from the IA work.

Economics at HL sits on command terms. Evaluate, examine, discuss and to what extent all mean different things to an examiner, and diagram accuracy carries marks students routinely give away.

English A is the quiet one. Paper 1 unseen analysis improves with volume, and there is no shortcut around reading widely.
items: Math AA HL and Math AI HL treated as separate matches
Physics and Chemistry: research question shaped before data
Chemistry organic mechanisms drilled apart from IA time
Economics HL: command terms and diagram accuracy
English A Paper 1: volume of unseen practice

contentBlocks.heading: School runs from Sector 80 to Golf Course Road and Sohna Road
contentBlocks.body:
Families in Sector 80 tend to send children some distance for IB. Scottish High International School sits in Sector 57, Lancers International School is on the Golf Course Road side, GD Goenka World School is out towards the Sohna Road region, and Pathways World School draws from across the Gurugram region. None of them is a short hop from Vatika India Next.

That commute is the single biggest constraint on tutoring here. A child leaving home before 7am and getting back after 4pm has already worked a longer day than most adults, and the first hour home is close to useless for learning. Parents who book a 4:30pm session and wonder why it goes badly are usually fighting fatigue rather than a weak tutor.

The practical fixes are unglamorous. Push weekday sessions later and keep them to sixty minutes. Move the heavier subject to a weekend morning when the student is fresh. Use the school's own assessment calendar to decide which weeks need two sessions and which need none.

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 80 and the New Gurgaon belt around it
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 80 belongs to the newer residential sectors rather than the older Gurugram core. The immediate neighbours are Sector 79, Sector 81 and Sector 82, with the Vatika India Next development running alongside and condominium clusters such as Godrej Air, Godrej Summit and Mapsko Casa Bella forming most of the family housing.

This matters for tutoring in a specific way. Density here is vertical and concentrated, so a tutor who takes one student in a Godrej Air tower can often take a second in the same complex on the same evening. Those back-to-back arrangements are what make home tutoring viable this far out, and they are worth asking about.

The older premium pockets sit on the other side of the city. Golf Course Road, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, DLF Phase 5, Sushant Lok, Sector 50, Sector 57, Sector 65, Nirvana Country and South City 1 all have deeper local tutor pools built up over years. Sector 80 does not yet, which is why online carries more weight here than it would in Sushant Lok.

For families with a parent commuting to Delhi, Noida or Faridabad, weekday evening logistics are tighter still, and weekend scheduling usually holds better.
items: Neighbouring sectors: 79, 81, 82 and Vatika India Next
Condominium clusters allow back-to-back home sessions
Older tutor pools sit around Golf Course Road and DLF phases
Online carries more weight in newer sectors

contentBlocks.heading: Four weeks in: what progress should look like in Sector 80 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks is roughly eight sessions. That is not long enough to move a predicted grade, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something. It is long enough to see whether the arrangement is working.

By the end of the first month you should be able to see three things without asking your child directly. There should be marked work with the tutor's corrections on it, dated. There should be a short written plan naming the next assessment and the weeks leading to it. And the student should be able to say what they are currently bad at, in specific terms, which is a sharper signal than confidence.

What you will not see is a grade jump. IB assessment is criterion-related and slow to move, particularly in DP2 where the externals dominate. Early progress shows up as fewer wasted marks: a conclusion that answers the question asked, a diagram that is labelled, a method section that a moderator could follow.

If none of that has appeared by week four, say so plainly. A tutor change early costs a fortnight. The same change made in March of DP2 costs far more, and the student absorbs most of it.
items: Dated, marked work you can look at
A written plan naming the next assessment
Student can name a specific weakness
Fewer marks given away, before any grade movement
Raise concerns at week four, not at week twelve

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor sits at your dining table
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a filter, not a promise. What IB Gram checks before proposing anyone is documentary and practical: identity, claimed qualifications, and teaching or tutoring history at the level requested. A tutor who has taught SL Chemistry for years is not automatically proposed for HL Chemistry.

The subject conversation goes further than a CV. Tutors are asked how they approach an IA at the level they are applying for, how they handle a student who has drafted a research question that cannot be measured, and what they do in the last six weeks before a May or November session. The answers separate people who have run a DP cycle from people who have read the syllabus.

For home tutoring, contactability and punctuality carry real weight, because a tutor who is unreliable about arriving in Sector 80 will be unreliable in month three regardless of subject skill.

What screening cannot do is guarantee chemistry between a tutor and a fifteen-year-old. So the first session is treated as a trial by both sides, and changing after it is normal rather than awkward.

No count of tutors is published, because the number that matters is how many are free for your slot.
items: Identity and qualification documents reviewed
Teaching history checked at the specific level
Subject interview covering IA and exam-period approach
Punctuality weighted for home sessions
First session treated as a trial by both sides

contentBlocks.heading: Booking IB tutors in Sector 80 Gurugram: the first call
contentBlocks.body:
The first conversation takes about ten minutes and is mostly listening. You will be asked for the grade, the programme, the subjects and levels, the school's next internal deadline, and the two weekly slots you can genuinely hold. If you have a recent piece of marked work, keep it handy, because it tells an advisor more than any description of the problem.

From there a shortlist is prepared, usually two or three tutors, with fee ranges attached to each. Nothing is charged for that stage. You speak to whoever you want to speak to, and you decide whether to run a first session.

Some requests take longer to fill than others. A weekday evening home session in Sector 80 for Math AA HL is a narrow ask, and it may sit for a week before the right person is free. An online SL slot usually moves faster. Availability is checked at the time, not assumed from a list.

If nothing suitable exists this month, you will be told that rather than matched with someone who nearly fits.

Bring a recent piece of marked work
Two or three profiles with fee ranges
