faqs.question: What do IB tutors in Sector 80 Gurugram usually charge per hour?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate. Fees move with the programme, the subject and the level, and DP HL subjects such as Math AA HL or Physics HL sit at the higher end because fewer tutors can teach them well. PYP and MYP support is generally lower. Home sessions in Sector 80 can carry a premium when the tutor travels from the Golf Course Road side, since the journey costs them time they cannot teach in. Exact fees are confirmed with the tutor before the first paid session, so you agree the number before anything starts.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book online tutoring instead of home tuition here?
faqs.answer: Often, though the saving is not the main reason to choose it. Online removes the tutor's travel from the equation, which can bring the rate down and opens up late-evening slots that a home tutor cannot realistically offer in Sector 80. The stronger argument is choice: online gives you access to specialists across Gurugram rather than only those willing to drive out to New Gurgaon. For younger PYP children who need an adult physically present to hold attention, home sessions usually still work better even at a higher rate.

faqs.question: My child studies at a school near Golf Course Road but we live in Sector 80. Does that complicate matching?
faqs.answer: It affects timing more than tutor quality. A long school run means your child gets home late and tired, so early-evening sessions tend to underperform. Most families in this position push weekday sessions towards 7pm or later, keep them to an hour, and move the demanding subject to a weekend morning. Tutors are matched to your home location rather than the school, and they work to whatever coursework and deadlines the school has set. IB Gram is not affiliated with any school and does not act on a school's behalf.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP student actually need?
faqs.answer: For most DP students, one session per subject per week is the working default, rising to two in the weeks around an IA deadline or a mock. Three or more per subject usually signals a different problem: a gap from MYP, a subject chosen at the wrong level, or a scheduling issue at home. Booking more hours rarely fixes those. An honest tutor will tell you when the timetable is already full and the issue is how the existing hours are being used rather than how many there are.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both Math AA HL and Physics HL?
faqs.answer: Some can, but it is worth checking rather than assuming. The overlap in content is real, yet the assessments pull in different directions: Physics HL involves a practical investigation with data handling and uncertainty analysis, while Math AA HL leans on proof, technique and Paper 3 style extended problems. A tutor strong in one is not automatically strong in the other. Where a single tutor covers both credibly, it saves scheduling effort. Where they do not, two specialists usually produce better work than one generalist stretched across both.

faqs.question: We are starting in DP2 in January. Is it too late to be useful?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the goals change. With a May session ahead, there is no time to rebuild foundations across a whole subject. The work becomes triage: identify which papers are losing the most marks, drill those question types, tidy up any IA still open, and build an exam-week plan the student can follow when tired. That can make a real difference to marks lost through technique. What it cannot do is close a two-year content gap, and any tutor promising that is overselling.

faqs.question: What happens if we do not get on with the first tutor?
faqs.answer: You say so and a replacement is looked for. The first session is treated as a trial by both sides, and mismatches at that stage are common and unremarkable. Personality matters more than parents expect with teenagers, and a tutor who works beautifully with a quiet DP1 student can struggle with a defensive one. Tell the advisor what specifically did not work, since that detail sharpens the next match considerably. Availability for a replacement depends on the slot and the subject, so a change may take a week or two.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to the Godrej Air and Vatika India Next side of Sector 80?
faqs.answer: Some do, and those matches are worth waiting for. Tutors already living in the New Gurgaon sectors, around Sector 79, 81 or 82, handle this area comfortably. Tutors coming from Sushant Lok, Sector 57 or the DLF phases can be arranged but their available windows are narrower and traffic-dependent. Large complexes help, because a tutor with two students in the same tower can justify the trip. Home availability is always subject to the individual tutor's schedule and is confirmed before you commit.

faqs.question: Which grades and IB programmes are covered from this area?
faqs.answer: Grade 1 through Grade 12, spanning the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma Programme. Support includes IA structure, Extended Essay mentoring, TOK, past-paper revision, school assignment review and exam planning for the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions. Younger DP cohorts are encouraged to plan earlier rather than arriving in DP2 with an open Extended Essay. What is available in any given month depends on which tutors have free slots at your level, so it is checked at the time of enquiry.

contentBlocks.heading: Changing IB tutors mid-course: what Sector 81 Gurugram families lose
contentBlocks.body:
Almost nobody keeps the same tutor from MYP4 to the final exam. Tutors relocate, take school jobs, get overloaded in January, or simply stop suiting a student who has changed. The switch itself is normal. What costs money is the gap around it.

Here is what disappears when a tutor leaves without a handover. The mental map of which topics were actually covered, as opposed to which appear in the syllabus. The half-corrected IA draft that lives in a shared folder nobody now has access to. The knowledge that the student panics with unseen data but is fine once the first line is written. A replacement rebuilding all of that from scratch spends three or four sessions diagnosing before any teaching happens, and those sessions are billed like any other.

Parents rarely see this cost because it is invisible on the invoice. It shows up later, as a term that produced no visible movement.

So the enquiry from a Sector 81 family is treated differently when it is a replacement. Before profiles are shared, an advisor asks what the previous arrangement covered, where it broke down, and what is currently sitting unfinished. That conversation shortens the new tutor's first month considerably.
items: Topic coverage map lost with the previous tutor
Drafts and corrections stranded in old folders
Three or four billed sessions spent re-diagnosing
The cost appears as a lost term, not a line item
Replacement enquiries start with what broke

contentBlocks.heading: Subject handovers that go wrong most often
contentBlocks.body:
Not every subject suffers equally when a tutor changes. Some transfer cleanly. Others do not.

Math AA HL is the least forgiving. Two tutors can use different notation, different proof conventions and a different order for the option content, and a student caught between them often loses confidence in work they had already understood. Math AI HL suffers less on notation and more on modelling style, since the second tutor tends to rebuild the student's approach to interpreting a context question.

The experimental sciences break at the IA. A Physics or Chemistry investigation half-designed by one tutor and inherited by another usually gets redesigned, because the incoming tutor cannot vouch for a method they did not see chosen. That is defensible but expensive in weeks, which is why an incomplete science IA should be flagged at the very first call.

Economics transfers reasonably well, provided the new tutor sees the commentary work and knows which command terms the student mishandles. English A transfers best of all: the reading list moves with the student, and Paper 1 technique is largely cumulative.

Across all six, the new tutor is asked to review existing work before proposing a plan rather than after.
items: Math AA HL: notation and proof conventions clash hardest
Math AI HL: modelling and interpretation style resets
Physics and Chemistry IAs often need redesign after a switch
Economics: commentary drafts plus command-term weak points
English A: cumulative technique, transfers most easily

contentBlocks.heading: Matching that begins from the last tutor's notes, not a blank form
contentBlocks.body:
The intake for a replacement request asks four things the usual form does not. What was the previous tutor doing well, since something usually worked. What specifically stopped working, described as behaviour rather than as a verdict. What is unfinished right now, with dates attached. And what the student themselves says about the change, which is often more accurate than the parent's version.

Only then does the search narrow by subject and level. A student who left a tutor because sessions had become passive needs someone who works from the student's pen rather than their own. A student who left because the tutor could not handle HL depth needs a genuine specialist, and that shortlist may be shorter and slower to fill.

Timing is checked in the same conversation. Sector 81 sits out in the newer sectors, so the pool willing to travel here on a weekday evening is narrower than it would be closer to Sushant Lok.

Two or three profiles follow, each with a note on why that person suits this particular restart. Availability is confirmed with the tutor before you commit to anything.
items: What worked previously, recorded before what failed
Unfinished work listed with real dates
Student's own account taken seriously
Specialist searches take longer to fill
Each profile carries a reason for this restart

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 81 Gurugram sits and who can realistically reach it
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 81 belongs to the New Gurgaon residential sectors, hemmed in by Sector 80 on one side and Sector 82 on the other, with Vatika India Next running through the area and towers including Godrej Air, Godrej Summit and Mapsko Casa Bella holding most of the resident families.

Geography decides a lot about handovers here. Because the sector is newer, the local tutor pool is thinner than in the established parts of the city, and a departing tutor cannot always be replaced by somebody two streets away. Tutors who already teach in Sector 80 or Sector 82 are the most natural successors, and a request that allows a small shift in timing often unlocks one of them.

The deeper pools sit east and south: Golf Course Road, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, DLF Phase 5, Sushant Lok, Sector 50, Sector 57, Sector 65, Nirvana Country and South City 1. Tutors from those areas do travel out, though usually for weekend blocks rather than scattered weekday hours.

Where a parent commutes daily to Delhi, Noida or Faridabad, the household evening is already compressed, and an online replacement often restores continuity faster than waiting for a local one.

Vatika India Next and Godrej towers hold most families
Neighbouring-sector tutors are the natural successors
Tutors from DLF and Sushant Lok prefer weekend blocks
Online restores continuity faster than waiting locally

contentBlocks.heading: Keeping continuity across PYP, MYP and DP
contentBlocks.body:
A change of tutor lands differently depending on where the child is.

In PYP, continuity is mostly about the adult, not the content. A seven-year-old who has settled with one person may take three or four sessions to warm to another, and pushing academic work too fast during that window wastes it. Shorter, more frequent sessions help the new tutor build rapport without a long unproductive hour.

In MYP, the risk is that criterion feedback resets. Two tutors can grade the same piece of work differently if one is reading the criteria carefully and the other is marking on instinct, and the student ends up unsure which standard applies. Asking a new MYP tutor to re-mark one recent assignment against the published strands, and to explain the difference, settles this quickly.

In DP, continuity is a calendar problem. The Extended Essay has supervisor deadlines at school, the TOK essay has its own timeline, and IA drafts sit in between. A tutor joining in DP2 with a May 2026 session ahead has limited room to change direction, and honest planning matters more than ambition. Younger DP cohorts have the luxury of starting earlier, and generally should.
items: PYP: rapport before content after a switch
MYP: re-mark one assignment against published strands
DP: EE, TOK and IA deadlines set the pace
Late DP2 joins mean triage, not redirection
Earlier planning for younger DP cohorts

contentBlocks.heading: The checks that happen before a replacement tutor is proposed
contentBlocks.body:
A family on their second or third tutor has less patience for surprises, so screening is stated plainly rather than implied.

Identity documents and claimed qualifications are reviewed. Teaching or tutoring history is checked against the exact level requested, since experience with SL Economics does not stand in for HL. Tutors are then asked to talk through a realistic scenario at that level: how they would handle a student arriving with a weak IA draft and four weeks left, or how they decide when a research question is not going to survive moderation.

Candidates who describe only content coverage tend not to progress. The people who help mid-course students are the ones who talk about diagnosis, sequencing and what they would drop.

Reliability is weighted heavily for home tutoring, because a second failed arrangement damages a student's willingness to try a third.

None of this is a guarantee. Screening removes obvious risk; it cannot predict whether a particular teenager will open up to a particular adult. The first session is therefore treated as mutual assessment, and no long commitment is expected before it happens. No tutor headcount is quoted anywhere on this site, because it would tell you nothing about your slot.
items: Documents and qualifications reviewed
History checked at the exact level requested
Scenario questions on diagnosis and sequencing
Reliability weighted heavily for home visits
First session treated as mutual assessment

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or both for IB tutors in Sector 81 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
For a restart, the mode question is really a speed question. How quickly can somebody competent be in front of the student.

Home tutoring suits students who need supervision as much as instruction, and it works well in Sector 81 when the tutor lives within the New Gurgaon sectors. Where the tutor is coming from Sohna Road, Sector 57 or the DLF phases, expect fewer available windows and a real dependency on traffic. Home sessions may be arranged from those areas subject to tutor schedules, but they are harder to hold at short notice.

Online is usually faster to start. It also removes one common cause of the previous breakdown: sessions quietly cancelled because the tutor could not make the drive twice in a week. Screen sharing suits mathematics and sciences reasonably well, and recorded working can be revisited before a test.

Hybrid is the arrangement most restarts settle into. An online session begins within days, keeping the deadline work moving, and a home slot is added later once a nearby tutor frees up.

One caution. Online demands more from a distracted student, and for a child who lost focus with the previous tutor, a supervised home session is often the better bet.
items: Online typically starts within days
Home suits students needing supervision, not only teaching
Distant tutors mean fewer and less reliable windows
Hybrid: online now, home slot added later
Distracted students usually do better in person

contentBlocks.heading: School-side deadlines a new tutor has to inherit
contentBlocks.body:
Whichever campus your child attends, the school sets the clock. Scottish High International School in Sector 57, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, GD Goenka World School towards the Sohna Road region and Pathways World School across the Gurugram region all run their own internal submission calendars, and those dates rarely match the tutor's assumptions.

An incoming tutor should ask for three things in the first week: the subject's internal deadline sheet, the last piece of marked school work, and the teacher's written feedback if any exists. That feedback is the single most useful document in a handover, because it tells the tutor what the school already believes about the student.

Where a school has flagged academic honesty expectations on an IA or Extended Essay, the tutor's role narrows deliberately. A tutor may explain methodology, question a claim, and point at a weak paragraph. Writing the paragraph is not tutoring, and a good tutor will refuse.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. No tutor speaks to a school on your behalf or represents any campus.
items: Internal deadline sheet requested in week one
Last marked school work and teacher comments reviewed
Academic honesty limits stated openly
Tutors question and explain, they do not draft
Independent platform, no school affiliation

contentBlocks.heading: Judging a second attempt at IB tuition in Sector 81 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Judge the restart faster than you judged the first arrangement. You already know what the failure mode looked like, so you can watch for it.

In the first fortnight, look for evidence that the new tutor read the old work. They should be able to name a specific weakness the previous tutor missed, or agree with something the previous tutor was doing and continue it. Either answer is fine. A tutor with no view on the earlier work has not looked.

By week four, expect the unfinished item to have moved. Not finished necessarily, but visibly further: a research question narrowed, a commentary redrafted, a paper section attempted under timed conditions. And the student should complain less about being confused, which is a low bar but a real one.

What you should not expect is a grade change. IB assessment is criterion-related, and a predicted grade responds to accumulated evidence rather than to effort in a single month.

If the second arrangement is also drifting by week five, the problem may not be the tutor. Sometimes the timetable is wrong, sometimes the subject level is wrong, and that is a harder conversation worth having early.
items: New tutor should have a view on the previous work
Unfinished item visibly further along by week four
Less confusion reported by the student
Predicted grades move slowly, on accumulated evidence
Repeated drift may point to level or timetable, not tutor

contentBlocks.heading: Restarting IB tuition in Sector 81 Gurugram without losing a term
contentBlocks.body:
Come to the first call with three details and the rest is quick: what subject and level, what is currently unfinished and when it is due, and why the last arrangement ended. Ten minutes is usually enough.

A shortlist of two or three tutors follows, chosen for this particular restart rather than pulled from a list. Fee ranges are included so nothing is discovered later. You speak to whoever you like, and run one session before deciding anything.

Some slots take time. A weekday home session in Sector 81 for an HL science is a narrow request, and it may sit unfilled while a nearer tutor finishes another commitment. An online slot generally opens sooner. Availability is checked when you enquire rather than assumed, and if nothing suitable is free, you will hear that plainly instead of being handed somebody who nearly fits.

Bring the school calendar too, even a photograph of it. Knowing that a commentary is due in eleven days changes which tutor is right far more than knowing the subject does. Where a deadline is genuinely close, an advisor will say whether starting now is worth it or whether the sensible move is to get through this submission and begin properly the week after. That answer is free, and occasionally it is no.
items: Bring subject, level, unfinished work and its deadline
Say why the previous arrangement ended
Two or three profiles with fee ranges
One session before any longer commitment
Narrow home slots may take longer to fill

faqs.question: Our tutor stopped mid-DP1. How much ground do we lose by changing now?
faqs.answer: Usually two to four sessions, spent letting the new tutor work out what has genuinely been covered and where the gaps are. You can shrink that considerably by handing over the student's notebooks, any marked drafts, and the school's deadline sheet at the first meeting. DP1 is actually a reasonable point to change, since there is still time before the externals dominate. Changing in the final months of DP2 costs far more, because the new tutor has to accept whatever foundation exists and work only on technique and exam strategy.

faqs.question: Should we tell the new tutor why the previous one did not work out?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in behavioural terms rather than as a character judgement. Saying sessions had become a monologue, or that homework was never checked, or that the tutor could not handle HL depth, gives the next person something to act on. Saying the tutor was simply not good does not. It is also worth passing on what did work, because there is nearly always something. Students form habits around a tutor, and preserving the useful ones while replacing the rest is faster than starting from nothing.

faqs.question: Can a new tutor take over a Physics or Chemistry IA that is already half done?
faqs.answer: They can, but expect them to question the design before helping with data. A science investigation is graded partly on how the research question and method were framed, and an incoming tutor who did not see those decisions being made will want to check that the experiment can produce meaningful data at all. Sometimes it can and the work continues. Sometimes a narrowing or a change of variable is needed, which costs a fortnight. Flagging an open IA at the first enquiry lets the shortlist be built accordingly.

faqs.question: Are there IB tutors living in the New Gurgaon sectors themselves?
faqs.answer: Some, though fewer than in the older parts of the city. Tutors already teaching in Sector 80, Sector 82 or the Vatika India Next area are the most practical for home sessions, since an existing trip can be extended. Tutors based around Sushant Lok, Sector 57 or the DLF phases do travel out here, usually preferring weekend blocks over scattered weekday hours. Because the local pool is thinner, families in Sector 81 who insist on home-only tutoring often wait longer than those open to online or hybrid.

faqs.question: How soon can sessions restart after we enquire?
faqs.answer: Online restarts are typically the quickest, since no travel has to be arranged and evening slots are wider. Home tutoring depends entirely on who is free in the surrounding sectors at your preferred hour, and a specific weekday evening request for a Higher Level subject can sit for a week or more. Nothing is confirmed until the tutor themselves accepts the slot, so an advisor will give you a realistic window rather than a comfortable one. If the timeline does not work for a live deadline, say so early.

faqs.question: Will a new tutor rewrite work my child has already submitted feedback on?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of one who offers to. A tutor can explain why a paragraph is weak, ask the questions that expose a thin argument, and show what a stronger structure looks like using different material. Producing the text itself crosses into academic honesty territory that schools take seriously and that can put a diploma at risk. Where a school has issued authenticity declarations for an internal assessment or Extended Essay, tutors are expected to stay clearly on the coaching side of that line.

faqs.question: Is it worth changing tutors if the fee is the only problem?
faqs.answer: Sometimes the cheaper route is fewer hours with the same person rather than the same hours with somebody cheaper. A strong tutor at one session a week, with the student doing the follow-up work independently, often beats two weaker sessions. Discuss the hour count before discussing the rate. If the fee genuinely does not work, say so plainly at the enquiry stage and the shortlist can be built within that range, though a Higher Level specialist at a low rate may simply not be available.

faqs.question: What if my child does not want another tutor at all?
faqs.answer: That reluctance is worth listening to before booking anyone. Students who have been through a poor arrangement often associate tutoring with being managed rather than helped, and forcing a third person into the same slot repeats the experience. A short trial with a clear end point works better than an open commitment. Letting the student sit in on the choice, and hear the tutor talk about the subject before agreeing, changes the dynamic more than parents expect. If the resistance is really about workload, more hours will not help.

faqs.question: Which programmes, grades and exam sessions do you support from this area?
faqs.answer: Grade 1 to Grade 12, covering the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma Programme. Support spans internal assessment structure, Extended Essay mentoring, Theory of Knowledge, past-paper revision, review of school assignments and exam planning aimed at the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions. Common subject requests include Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A. What can actually be staffed in a given month depends on tutor availability at your level and preferred timing.

contentBlocks.heading: The assessment calendar that sets the timetable in Sector 82 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
IB does not test a student once. It tests them repeatedly, in different formats, spread across two years, and a good tutoring plan is built from those dates rather than from a habit of meeting on Tuesdays.

Work backwards through a Diploma Programme cycle and the shape is clear. In DP1 the science and mathematics internal assessments are proposed, refined and drafted, usually with a school checkpoint before the summer. The Extended Essay begins around the same period, with a supervisor meeting and a research question that has to survive scrutiny. Theory of Knowledge runs alongside, producing an exhibition and later an essay on a prescribed title. DP2 opens with mock preparation, closes the remaining internal work, then hands everything to the externals.

MYP has its own rhythm. Criterion-assessed tasks arrive through the year and the personal project dominates the final year.

So the first question asked of a Sector 82 family is not what subject the student struggles with. It is what is due next, and after that. Two hours a week spent on general revision in the month a Chemistry IA is due is two hours misplaced, however good the tutor.
items: DP1: IA proposals, EE research question, TOK exhibition

contentBlocks.heading: Late sessions, deadline weeks and the online option
contentBlocks.body:
Assessment weeks distort a schedule, and the mode of tutoring decides how well you cope with that.

A home tutor gives you presence and attention, which matters most for younger students and for anyone who quietly stops working the moment an adult leaves the room. In Sector 82 the practical constraint is where that tutor lives. Somebody already teaching in the surrounding New Gurgaon sectors can hold a weekday evening slot reliably. Somebody driving from Golf Course Road, Sushant Lok or the Sohna Road side can be arranged subject to their schedule, but a 9pm finish and a long drive back is not something most tutors sustain across a full term.

Online behaves differently under deadline pressure. An extra forty minutes the night before a draft is due is realistic online and rarely realistic in person. Specialists in narrower subjects become reachable. Sessions can be rescheduled instead of cancelled when a school event moves.

The honest limitation is attention. A student who drifts on a screen will drift more in an exam term, not less. For those students the home session is worth the extra cost and the narrower choice of tutors.
items: Home sessions strongest with tutors already in New Gurgaon
Long-distance evening slots are hard to sustain across a term
Online allows short extra sessions in deadline weeks
Rescheduling is easier than cancelling online
Screen tutoring suits focused students, not distracted ones

contentBlocks.heading: Where the marks actually sit: IA, Paper 1, Paper 2 and Paper 3
contentBlocks.body:
Subject choice determines what a tutor has to be good at, and the six requested most often from this area split along useful lines.

Mathematics at Analysis and Approaches HL is dominated by the papers. Technique, speed and the extended problem solving in the third paper are where marks are made and lost, and the exploration, while graded, is a smaller share. Applications and Interpretation HL leans harder on modelling with real data and on explaining what a result means in context, which is a different skill from computing it.

Physics and Chemistry both carry a practical investigation graded on personal engagement, exploration, analysis and evaluation. A tutor who only revises content will not move that mark. The written papers reward precise use of terminology and, in Chemistry, fluent handling of mechanisms and calculations under time.

Economics is built around command terms and diagram accuracy. An answer that explains without evaluating caps itself, whatever the quality of the explanation.

English A rests on the unseen analysis, the comparative essay and the individual oral, and progress there is slow, cumulative and dependent on reading the student does alone.
items: Math AA HL: paper technique and extended problem solving
Math AI HL: modelling with data, interpretation in context
Sciences: investigation graded on method and evaluation
Economics: command terms plus accurate diagrams
English A: unseen analysis, comparative essay, individual oral

What works in practice is grouping. A tutor who visits the same complex twice on one evening treats the journey as worthwhile, so families in adjacent towers sometimes find that timing flexibility gets them a stronger tutor than insistence on one fixed hour would.

Households with a parent commuting to Delhi, Noida or Faridabad tend to find weekday assessment-week sessions hardest to protect, and weekend mornings hold up better across a whole term.

contentBlocks.heading: Assessment shapes across PYP, MYP and the Diploma Programme
contentBlocks.body:
The three programmes are assessed so differently that treating them as one service would be careless.

Primary Years, for ages three to twelve, has no external examination. Judgement is continuous and inquiry-led, and the useful tutoring is quiet groundwork: reading stamina, number fluency, and helping a child ask a question they can actually investigate rather than one an adult has phrased for them. Worksheet drilling here does more harm than good.

Middle Years, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, introduces criterion-related marking with published strands. A student can know the material and still score poorly by answering a different question from the one being assessed. Tutoring at this stage is largely about reading the task, identifying the strand, and structuring a response that lets a marker find the evidence.

Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, combines internal assessment with heavy external examination and the core of Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and creativity, activity and service. Planning here spans terms rather than weeks, particularly for students aiming at the May 2026 or November 2026 sessions. Younger cohorts benefit from starting subject support before the first draft deadlines arrive.
items: PYP: continuous, inquiry-led, no external exam
MYP: published criterion strands drive the marking
DP: internal assessment plus externals plus the core
EE and TOK planned across terms
Earlier starts for younger DP cohorts

contentBlocks.heading: Matching an IB tutor in Sector 82 Gurugram to a deadline
contentBlocks.body:
The intake is deliberately dull. Grade, programme, subjects with levels, then the dates. A school assessment sheet or even a photograph of the term calendar is more useful than a description of the difficulty.

With dates in hand, the search narrows quickly. A student six weeks from a Chemistry investigation deadline needs someone comfortable supervising a method, discussing uncertainty and reading a draft against the published criteria. A DP2 student in February needs a marker: someone who works through past papers at speed and explains the marks lost rather than reteaching the topic. Those are different tutors, and asking for both from one person usually produces neither.

Schedule comes next. You are asked for the hours you can genuinely hold, including whether a second short session is possible in a deadline week, because that flexibility widens the shortlist noticeably.

Two or three profiles are then shared with a note on why each fits the coming assessment. Nothing is scheduled until the tutor confirms the slot themselves, and if the calendar shown is unrealistic, an advisor will say so instead of accepting the booking.
items: Term calendar requested at the first call
Draft supervision and past-paper marking treated as different jobs
Deadline-week flexibility widens the shortlist
Profiles annotated against the coming assessment
Unrealistic timelines flagged rather than accepted

contentBlocks.heading: Reading the first month of IB tutoring in Sector 82 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
One month is about eight sessions. Enough to judge the arrangement, nowhere near enough to move a predicted grade, and any promise of a number should end the conversation.

What you can reasonably check is documentary. Is there a written plan naming the next assessment and the steps between now and it. Has the student's own work been marked with comments a stranger could follow. Has anything that was stuck become unstuck, even in a small way: a research question narrowed, a paper section attempted under timed conditions, a mechanism finally drawn correctly.

A second, quieter test. Ask your child what the tutor thinks they are weakest at. A student who can answer precisely is being taught. A student who says the tutor thinks they are doing fine, three weeks before a draft, probably is not.

Progress in IB shows up first as fewer avoidable losses. Conclusions that answer the question set. Diagrams labelled. Evaluation actually written rather than implied. Grades follow later, and not always in the month you hoped. If nothing has shifted by week five, raise it directly.
items: Written plan tied to the next submission
Marked work a third party could follow
Student can state their own weakest area
Avoidable mark losses fall before grades move
Say something at week five, not week twelve

contentBlocks.heading: What Gurugram IB schools expect before a draft is accepted

Schools around this city set their own internal checkpoints, and they are stricter than most families expect. Scottish High International School in Sector 57, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, GD Goenka World School out towards the Sohna Road region and Pathways World School across the Gurugram region each publish submission calendars, and a missed internal deadline can limit how much feedback a student is entitled to receive.

There is also an authenticity requirement running through all of it. Internal assessments and the Extended Essay are declared as the student's own work, and supervisors are expected to be able to vouch for the process. A tutor operating properly stays on the coaching side of that line: asking why a claim holds, pointing at an unsupported paragraph, explaining what an evaluation looks like. Drafting sentences for the student is not tutoring and puts the submission at risk.

Tutors here work to your child's own school calendar and assignments rather than to a generic scheme, so bring the school's documents to the first session.

contentBlocks.heading: Screening before a Sector 82 shortlist is sent out
contentBlocks.body:
Checks happen before names reach you, not after.

Identity and claimed qualifications are reviewed against documents. Teaching or tutoring history is confirmed at the level being requested, because a strong Standard Level Physics tutor is not automatically an appropriate Higher Level one, and the honest tutors say so themselves.

The subject conversation is where most candidates separate. Tutors are asked how they would respond to a research question that cannot generate enough data, how they sequence revision in the final eight weeks before a session, and what they would tell a student who has left an Extended Essay untouched for a term. Answers about coverage are weaker than answers about triage.

For home tutoring, punctuality and communication matter as much as subject depth, since a tutor who cancels twice in a deadline month causes more damage than a slightly less expert one who turns up.

What screening does not do is guarantee a personal fit, and no vetting process can. The first session functions as a two-way trial, and changing after it is expected rather than difficult. No figure for tutor numbers is published here, because the only number that affects you is how many are free at your hour.
items: Documents and qualifications reviewed before shortlisting
Level-specific teaching history confirmed
Triage questions asked, not coverage questions
Punctuality weighted for home sessions
First session works as a two-way trial

contentBlocks.heading: Getting IB tutors in Sector 82 Gurugram onto your calendar
contentBlocks.body:
Begin with the dates. Tell us the grade and programme, the subjects and their levels, what is due in the next eight weeks, and the hours you can hold each week without a fight. A photograph of the school's assessment calendar saves ten minutes of conversation.

We check who is genuinely free for those hours and send two or three profiles, each with a short note on why that tutor suits the assessment ahead, and a fee range so nothing surprises you later. You talk to them directly and run one session before committing to anything longer.

Some requests are narrow. A weekday evening home slot in Sector 82 for a Higher Level science can take a week or more to fill, and a request during a peak revision month can take longer still. Online usually opens sooner.

If your timeline is too tight for tutoring to help, we will tell you that and suggest waiting until after the submission. Availability is confirmed with the tutor at the time, never assumed from a list.

Two or three annotated profiles with fee ranges

faqs.question: When in the IB two years is the best time to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Early in DP1, before the first internal assessment proposals are due, is the most productive point. There is still room to fix habits, choose a workable research question and build paper technique gradually. Starting in DP2 is common and still useful, though the work becomes narrower: past papers, marks lost through technique, and closing whatever internal work remains. Starting after the mocks limits things further. For MYP students, the year before the personal project is a sensible window, since criterion writing habits carry forward into the Diploma.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay if my child already has a school supervisor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the roles are different. The school supervisor approves the topic, holds the formal reflection sessions and signs off on authenticity. A tutor works between those meetings on the parts students find hardest: narrowing an unmanageable question, building a reading strategy, structuring an argument that sustains four thousand words, and keeping to a realistic writing timetable. What a tutor should never do is write or rewrite passages. Schools take authenticity declarations seriously, and the risk sits entirely with the student rather than the tutor.

faqs.question: How much tutoring does a Chemistry or Physics internal assessment need?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect if the research question is right, far more if it is not. The heavy work sits at the start: choosing a variable that can actually be measured in a school laboratory, planning enough repeats to say something about uncertainty, and checking the method survives contact with the equipment available. Get that right and three or four sessions may carry the write-up. Get it wrong and the investigation is often redesigned weeks later, which is the most expensive mistake in the whole internal assessment process.

faqs.question: Do you offer extra sessions in the weeks before a submission?
faqs.answer: Where a tutor has room, yes, and online makes it far more likely. A short additional session two days before a draft is due is easy to arrange on a screen and difficult to arrange in person in Sector 82, given the drive most tutors face. It is worth agreeing this possibility when you first book rather than requesting it in a panic. Some tutors keep deliberate slack for their existing students during peak months; others are fully committed, and that is checked at the time.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge worth paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: For some students, clearly yes. The essay is written on a prescribed title and rewards precision about knowledge claims, examples and counterexamples rather than general opinion, and strong writers in other subjects often score poorly because they argue instead of analysing. A few focused sessions on structuring the essay and choosing usable real-life situations can help a lot. For a student already comfortable with the format and keeping to school deadlines, the same hours are usually better spent on a Higher Level subject.

faqs.question: We live near Godrej Summit. Will a tutor actually travel here on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: Some will, particularly tutors already working in the surrounding New Gurgaon sectors, where an existing evening trip can be extended. Tutors based around Sector 57, Sushant Lok or the DLF phases are more likely to offer weekend blocks than scattered weekday hours, because the return drive after a late session is difficult to repeat through a term. Larger complexes help: where a tutor has two students in the same tower, weekday visits become realistic. Home availability is always confirmed with the individual tutor before scheduling.

faqs.question: What does a first session usually cover?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis more than teaching. A good tutor will ask to see recent marked work, the school assessment calendar and any draft in progress, then spend most of the hour finding out where marks are being lost rather than covering new content. Expect them to end with a short plan naming the next submission and what happens between now and then. If the first session is spent lecturing on a topic without looking at anything the student has produced, that is a fair reason to try someone else.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both a Higher Level and a Standard Level subject for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it does simplify scheduling. The question to ask is whether they have taught or tutored at the Higher Level specifically, since the additional content and the extra paper change what is needed. Many tutors are honest about this and will tell you which level they are strongest at. Where the two subjects are unrelated, such as a science and an essay subject, a single tutor covering both is less common and worth verifying carefully before booking a combined arrangement.

faqs.question: Which grades, subjects and exam sessions are supported from this part of Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Grade 1 through Grade 12, across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes. Frequent requests include Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A, alongside internal assessment structure, Extended Essay mentoring, Theory of Knowledge, review of school assignments and past-paper revision aimed at the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions. Whether a particular combination can be staffed in a given month depends on tutor availability at that level and your preferred timing, so it is checked when you enquire.

contentBlocks.heading: What a first IB session in Sector 83 Gurugram should actually produce
contentBlocks.body:
A first session is a diagnostic, not a lesson. Sixty to ninety minutes in, you should have something written down: which topics the student is genuinely shaky on, which ones only look shaky because a command term was misread, and what the next four weeks will cover.

Parents looking for IB tutors in Sector 83 Gurugram usually arrive with a school report and a vague worry. The report says a 4 in Chemistry. It does not say whether the problem is bonding, mole calculations, or the fact that the student writes an answer to "explain" when the paper asked them to "evaluate". Those are three different fixes and often three different tutors.

So the first hour should end with a short written summary you can read. Not a pitch. A note that gives current level, target level, the two or three specific gaps, and the order they will be tackled in.

If a tutor cannot produce that after the first meeting, the match is probably wrong. Ask for it before committing to a monthly schedule. Families in the Godrej Air and Godrej Summit blocks often book a single trial before deciding anything, which is sensible and costs very little.

contentBlocks.heading: How a shortlist gets built for a Sector 83 family
contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts with three inputs: the programme, the subject at its exact level, and the calendar. A Grade 11 student taking Math AA HL and sitting May 2026 papers needs a different tutor from a Grade 9 student who is losing marks on criterion C in a related subject area.

Then comes the practical layer. Where in Sector 83 do you live, and are you asking for someone to travel? Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next each sit at slightly different points on the same stretch of the New Gurgaon residential sectors, and a tutor coming from Sushant Lok at seven in the evening is making a very different journey from one already living inside these sectors.

Once those are clear, a short list is put together rather than a long one. Three or four names, each with the reason it was included. You see why the match was made, which is more useful than seeing a bigger set of profiles.

Availability is never promised in advance. A tutor free on Tuesdays in October may not be free in January, and Diploma Programme subjects at HL fill first.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject support from Math AA HL to English A
contentBlocks.body:
Six subject areas come up most often from this part of Gurugram: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A. They go wrong in different ways, and a tutor who is strong in one is not automatically useful in another.

Math AA HL trouble is usually proof and Paper 3. Students can differentiate cleanly and still lose marks because they never wrote a justification line. Math AI HL is a different animal: modelling, technology use, and working out which statistical test a question is quietly asking for.

Physics tends to break at the point where algebra meets a described situation. Chemistry breaks at the internal assessment, where a student picks a research question that cannot generate enough usable data.

Economics is a writing subject wearing a numbers costume. Diagram, definition, real-world example, evaluation. Students who treat it as arithmetic lose the evaluation marks every time.

English A rarely needs content teaching. It needs somebody to sit with a Paper 1 unseen extract and push the student to say something arguable about it, then defend it under questioning.

An IB maths tutor near Sector 83 and an IB science tutor for the same family are usually two separate people. Plan for that.
items: Math AA HL: proof discipline and Paper 3
Math AI HL: modelling and choosing the right test
Chemistry IA: research questions that produce data
Economics: evaluation marks, not calculation
English A: arguable readings of unseen extracts

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP support across Grade 1 to Grade 12
contentBlocks.body:
Support runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, and the three programmes need genuinely different handling.

Primary Years Programme children, roughly ages three to twelve, should not be handed worksheet packs. What helps at that stage is reading fluency, number sense, and inquiry habits that survive contact with a unit of inquiry. A tutor who only drills sums produces a child who does sums and stops asking why.

Middle Years Programme students, ages eleven to sixteen, are usually stuck on translation. They understand the science. They cannot turn that understanding into criterion-based writing. Criterion A and criterion D look similar to a fourteen-year-old and are marked very differently. Most of the work here is reading the rubric aloud and rewriting one paragraph until it matches.

Diploma Programme students, ages sixteen to nineteen, need specialists. Internal assessment direction, extended essay mentoring, theory of knowledge support, past-paper drilling and a weekly plan that respects the school's own deadlines instead of competing with them.

For DP especially, starting in Grade 11 leaves room. Starting in February of Grade 12 does not. Better to hear that early than after fees are paid.
items: PYP: reading, number sense, inquiry habits
MYP: rubric literacy across criteria A to D
DP: IA, EE, TOK and past-paper strategy
Grade 11 starts leave room; February of Grade 12 does not

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or a mix: what works from Sector 83 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Three modes, and the honest answer is that they are not equal for every situation.

Home tutoring suits younger students, PYP and early MYP especially, where a person in the room does more than a screen can. It also suits families who want the session to be visible. Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules, and that qualification is real rather than legal decoration.

An IB online tutor for Sector 83 Gurugram wins for rare subjects and late slots. If you need Math AA HL Paper 3 work at half past eight on a Thursday in exam term, the specialist who can do it is probably not driving to New Gurgaon for it. Shared documents, annotated past papers and screen-shared graphing tools cover most of what an IB session needs.

Hybrid is what most DP families settle into. One in-person session a week for the heavier subject, online for doubt-solving and IA drafts.

The mode should follow the student. A Grade 5 child who fidgets through a video call should not be online because it suits the schedule.

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor reaches your shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is boring and it should be. Identity documents, qualification records, and a check on the subjects and levels a tutor actually teaches rather than the ones listed on a generic profile.

Then teaching evidence. Someone who says they teach Chemistry HL is asked how they would handle a student whose internal assessment has a research question yielding only three data points. The answer reveals more than a degree certificate does.

Programme familiarity is checked separately from subject knowledge. A strong graduate physicist who has never read an IB subject guide will teach physics well and mark it wrongly. Command terms, criterion descriptors, assessment objectives: all learnable, but a tutor who has not learned them will cost the student marks in the exam hall.

References are requested where available. Trial feedback is collected after the first session, and a family can ask for a different tutor without writing an essay about why.

What screening cannot do is predict the chemistry between one tutor and one fifteen-year-old. That only shows up in week two, which is why the first month is treated as a review period rather than a settled arrangement.

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB tutoring in Sector 83 Gurugram falls short
contentBlocks.body:
Some honesty is more useful here than reassurance.

Tutoring cannot fix a subject choice that was wrong from the start. A student who picked Math AA HL because a counsellor suggested it, and who has been quietly drowning since September of Grade 11, may need a level change rather than more hours. A good tutor says that out loud. A weak one sells you extra sessions.

Tutoring also cannot replace attendance. If the student is missing school classes, the tutor spends the session re-teaching content instead of building skill, and progress stalls at a cost.

There are no guaranteed grades here. Nobody can promise a 7, and any platform that does is describing something it does not control. What can be described is process: what gets covered, in what order, with what evidence of movement.

A reasonable checkpoint is four weeks. By then you should see past-paper questions attempted without prompting, command terms used correctly in written answers, and a student who can explain what their internal assessment is investigating. If none of that has shifted, change something. The tutor, the mode, or the plan.

contentBlocks.heading: The school week behind an IB tutoring request in Sector 84 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Look at an IB student's week before looking at their marks. School from early morning, a bus that leaves the New Gurgaon sectors well before the traffic builds, six subjects on a rotating timetable, CAS commitments, and in Grade 11 an extended essay supervisor asking for a first draft.

Parents searching for IB tutors in Sector 84 Gurugram are usually not asking for more teaching. They are asking for someone to make the existing load survivable.

Schools around here run demanding calendars. Internal assessment deadlines cluster. Two subjects will want drafts in the same fortnight, and a fifteen-year-old handles that by doing neither of them well.

So the useful opening question is not which topics are weak. It is what this week actually contains, and where the hour is going to come from. A tutoring slot that ignores school timings and CAS produces cancelled sessions and an irritated teenager.

Which is why an enquiry generally begins with the timetable rather than the report card. Fix the schedule first. Subject work becomes far easier once there is somewhere real to put it.

Slots that survive a bad traffic week

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects Sector 84 parents ask about most
contentBlocks.body:
Enquiries from this part of Gurugram cluster around Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A, though the reasons shift by grade.

In Grade 9 and 10 the request is usually confidence. The student was comfortable in middle school, then the science turned quantitative and the maths turned abstract, and the gap between understanding a lesson and answering a question opened up.

By Grade 11 and 12 it narrows to assessment. Economics students want help structuring a fifteen-mark evaluation. Physics students want an internal assessment investigation that is manageable and still worth good marks. English A students want somebody to argue with them about a text until their reading holds up.

Level matters more than subject name. Chemistry SL and Chemistry HL share content and then diverge sharply in depth and paper structure, and a tutor comfortable with one is not automatically comfortable with the other.

A parent asking for an IB maths tutor for Sector 84 students should say AA or AI, HL or SL, in the first message. It removes about a week of back and forth.

Grade 11 and 12: assessment structure and marks

State AA or AI, HL or SL, up front

contentBlocks.heading: Ages three to nineteen: what changes between PYP, MYP and DP
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme covers roughly ages three to twelve, the Middle Years Programme ages eleven to sixteen, and the Diploma Programme ages sixteen to nineteen. Support across Grade 1 to Grade 12 means three quite separate jobs.

PYP work is quiet and slow. Reading aloud, estimating before calculating, asking a child what they expect to happen before telling them. Parents sometimes want visible output. The visible output at this stage is a child who reads for pleasure, and that does not photograph well on a worksheet.

MYP is where the assessment shock lands. Criterion-related marking rewards process. A student who reaches the right answer with no method statement can score lower than one who reasons carefully to a wrong number. Families used to board marking find this genuinely confusing, and explaining it properly is half the tutoring.

DP is a two-year project with fixed dates. Internal assessments, the extended essay, theory of knowledge, and final papers in May 2026 or November 2026. Planning backwards from the session date, rather than forwards from today, is what separates a calm Grade 12 from a frantic one.
items: PYP: reading aloud, estimation, curiosity kept alive
MYP: process marks and method statements
DP: two-year plan anchored to the exam session
Backward planning from May 2026 or November 2026

contentBlocks.body:
In-person tutoring in Sector 84 Gurugram is genuinely good when the timing is genuinely possible. A weekend morning session, or a six o'clock slot that does not collide with the bus and dinner, works well for younger students and for subjects where writing gets checked line by line.

Online is the sensible default for narrow requirements. Math AI HL, theory of knowledge essay feedback, or extended essay mentoring are specialist asks, and the pool of people who can do them well is not limited to those willing to reach New Gurgaon on a weekday evening.

Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules. Online tutoring remains available across Gurugram for all supported IB subjects. Read that as a plain statement: mode is a scheduling decision, not a quality ranking.

One caution worth taking seriously. Online sessions fail when the student joins on a phone with no second screen. Past papers need to stay visible while the tutor annotates them. Sort the setup before blaming the format.

The sequence is short and it runs in this order.

You describe the situation: grade, programme, subjects with levels, the exam session in view, and the weekly windows that are actually free. Not the windows that would be free in an ideal week.

Filtering then happens on level and programme familiarity before anything else, because a tutor who has not taught at that level is a poor match no matter how convenient their address. Location and mode come next, and fees are discussed openly rather than after a trial.

You receive a short list with reasons attached. A trial is arranged with one tutor, not four, because comparing three strangers across three weeks exhausts the student and tells you less than you would expect.

After the trial there is a conversation about whether it fits. Continuing is a decision, not a default.

Availability can be reviewed but not reserved indefinitely. Grade 12 slots in HL sciences tighten from October onwards, and a family that waits for mock results is choosing from a smaller set of people.

If nothing suitable exists at your preferred hour, you are told that plainly rather than handed whoever happens to be free.

contentBlocks.heading: The screening a tutor passes before you meet them

Before a name reaches you, a few things are established.

Identity and academic credentials are checked against documents rather than claims. Teaching history is reviewed for the specific programme, since experience with a national board does not transfer automatically to criterion-related marking.

Subject-level competence is probed with practical questions. For a Physics applicant: how would you help a student whose internal assessment has no controlled variable worth measuring. For English A: what would you do with a student who summarises an extract instead of analysing it. Vague answers end the conversation there.

Communication is assessed too, which sounds soft and is not. A tutor who cannot explain their plan to a parent in two minutes will not explain covalent bonding to a fourteen-year-old either.

Feedback continues after matching. If sessions stop producing anything the student can show you, that is worth raising early rather than at the end of a paid month. Reassignment is possible and does not require justifying yourself at length.

Nothing here is a background check in the legal sense, and it is not presented as one. It is a screen designed to catch people who cannot teach at the level they list, because that is the failure families actually run into.

contentBlocks.heading: Honest limits of IB tuition near Sector 84
contentBlocks.body:
A few things worth saying plainly before money changes hands.

Tuition is a supplement. It does not replace the classroom, and a student who has disengaged from school will not be rescued by two hours a week. That situation needs a conversation with the school first, and a tutor who pretends otherwise is selling something.

Progress is uneven. A student can work well for three weeks and still produce a poor mock, because mocks test recall across a whole year while the sessions were fixing one unit. Judging a tutor on a single mock is unfair to both of them.

No score is guaranteed. There are no promised grade jumps and no published success rates, because a platform cannot control what happens in an exam hall in May.

What is reasonable to expect after a month: clearer written answers, a specific plan for each internal assessment, and a student who can name their own weak areas. If those are missing, the arrangement needs changing, and saying so is not rude.

Tutoring is also not therapy. A student who freezes in assessments through anxiety needs help a subject tutor is not qualified to give, and the honest move there is to say so rather than book more hours.

faqs.question: Should we wait for the mock results before arranging a tutor?

Mocks confirm what a careful parent already suspects, and by the time results arrive the calendar has shortened and the better Diploma Programme tutors have filled their evenings. faqs.question: What is the difference between Math AA and Math AI, and which tutor do we need?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the more traditional route, heavy on algebra, calculus and proof, with Paper 3 at higher level demanding sustained reasoning. Applications and Interpretation leans towards modelling, statistics and technology use, and its questions are wrapped in real contexts. faqs.question: Are online sessions really as effective for IB as sitting in the room?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma Programme work, yes, provided the setup is right. Annotated past papers, shared documents and screen-shared graphing tools cover what a session needs, and the wider pool means a better subject-level match. Online underperforms in two situations: young children who need physical presence to stay focused, and students joining from a phone with nowhere to keep the question paper visible. faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the extended essay if the school has already assigned a supervisor?

contentBlocks.heading: Exam-season rescue versus year-long support in Sector 85 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Two very different requests hide behind the same search. One arrives in February with a mock result and six weeks to go. The other arrives in July, before anything has gone wrong.

Both are legitimate. They are not the same job.

Crisis work is triage. Pick the three highest-yield topics, drill past papers under timing, fix exam technique, and accept that some units will not be covered at all. It can move a grade. It cannot rebuild two years of foundation, and pretending otherwise wastes a family's money.

Year-long support is slower and quieter. Weekly sessions that track the school's sequence, internal assessment drafts reviewed while there is still time to change the research question, and revision starting in December rather than April.

Parents looking for IB tutors in Sector 85 Gurugram should decide which of the two they are asking for, because it changes the tutor, the frequency and the cost. The answer is often that they meant to do the second one and ran out of time. That happens constantly. Say it plainly and the plan gets built for the time that actually remains.
items: Triage: three high-yield topics and timed papers
Year-long: school sequence tracked week by week
IA research questions changed while change is still possible
Revision starting in December, not April

contentBlocks.heading: How support changes from Grade 1 through Grade 12
contentBlocks.body:
Grade 1 to Grade 12 is a long stretch and the calendar pressure varies enormously across it.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, there is no exam clock at all. Sessions can follow the child. If reading is slow in October, spend October on reading. Nobody is losing marks, and the only real risk is boring a seven-year-old into disliking the subject.

The Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, introduces deadlines that matter without being final. Criterion-marked tasks land through the year, and the personal project in the final year consumes far more time than most families expect. A student who learns to plan here reaches the Diploma Programme with a skill many classmates lack.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, runs on fixed dates. May 2026 and November 2026 sessions anchor everything behind them: internal assessment deadlines, the extended essay, theory of knowledge components, mocks, and a study leave period shorter than students imagine.

Younger DP cohorts benefit from earlier planning. Term one of Grade 11 is when a subject level can still be revisited without damage.
items: PYP: no exam clock, follow the child
MYP: personal project eats more time than expected
DP: fixed May and November session dates
Grade 11 term one is the last easy point to change level

The question that decides everything about in-person tutoring is who can reach it, and when. Tutors based near Golf Course Road, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, Sushant Lok, Sector 50, Sector 57, Sector 65, South City 1, Nirvana Country or Sohna Road are crossing the width of the city to get here in the evening.

Some will. Many will do it once and then quietly ask to move online in week five.

For a family planning a full academic year rather than six weeks of revision, that pattern matters more than the format itself. Consistency beats presence. An online tutor who appears every Tuesday for eight months is worth more than an in-person tutor who cancels twice a month because Vatika Chowk was bad again.

Tutors in Delhi, Noida or Faridabad are viable online and rarely viable in person, whatever anyone promises at the enquiry stage.

Worth asking before you commit to in-person sessions: how will the tutor get here, and what time would they need to leave home. Someone who has thought that through will hold the slot. Someone who has not will discover the journey in week two and start rescheduling.

contentBlocks.heading: The subjects Sector 85 parents ring about
contentBlocks.body:
Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A account for most requests from these sectors, and each has a natural point in the year where it starts to hurt.

Maths goes wrong early and silently. A Grade 11 student who never consolidated functions in term one will still be paying for it in Grade 12 calculus. Catching that in November is cheap. Catching it in March is not.

The sciences go wrong at the internal assessment. Physics and Chemistry investigations tend to be chosen in a rush, and a weak research question caps the marks no matter how carefully the report is later written.

Economics goes wrong at Paper 2 and the evaluation command terms, usually right around the first mock, when students discover that a correct diagram earns fewer marks than they assumed.

English A is different again. It rarely collapses. It plateaus, and a plateau is hard to notice until a comparative essay comes back at a 4 for the third time.

Knowing the timing lets a family book the right help before the damage compounds.
items: Maths: term one gaps surface a year later
Sciences: the IA research question caps the mark
Economics: evaluation terms exposed by the first mock
English A: silent plateaus rather than sudden drops

Their calendars do not align. One school may finish Diploma Programme content in January and give a long revision run. Another may still be teaching an option topic in February. Mock weeks differ by a month. Internal assessment submission windows differ by more than that.

Which is why a generic revision timetable copied from the internet is close to useless. The plan has to be built against the school's own dates, and the first thing a tutor should ask for is the assessment calendar the school has published to parents.

contentBlocks.heading: What happens after you describe the problem
contentBlocks.body:
Once the situation is described, three filters run in sequence.

Time remaining comes first, because it dictates everything else. Eighteen months to an exam session allows foundation work. Ten weeks does not, and the tutor best suited to a long build is often not the one you want for triage.

Level and programme come second. Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics HL, Chemistry SL, Economics HL, English A: each needs someone who has taught that exact combination rather than something adjacent to it.

Logistics come third. Where you are within Sector 85, which evenings genuinely exist, whether anyone is realistically travelling.

The output is a small shortlist with the reasoning attached, not a directory. You are told why each person is on it and what their limitation is, because every tutor has one and hiding it only delays the discovery.

Fees, timing and mode are settled before a first session. Availability is subject to tutor schedules and tightens as May approaches, which is a decent argument for asking in August rather than February.

No money changes hands during any of this. The shortlist and the conversation around it cost nothing, and the first fee attaches to the first scheduled session.

Each shortlisted tutor's limitation stated openly
Ask in August rather than February where possible

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing between a tutor at your door and one on screen
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor at your door and a tutor on a screen solve different problems.

In the room is better for supervision. A twelve-year-old who drifts, a student whose handwriting and working need watching, a parent who wants to hear what is happening: all arguments for in-person. Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules.

On screen is better for precision and continuity. Online tutoring remains available across Gurugram for all supported IB subjects, and it survives the monsoon, the exam term, a family trip to Delhi and the fortnight when the approach road is dug up.

For year-long arrangements from Sector 85, online usually wins on reliability alone. For six weeks of crisis work with a younger student, in-person often wins on attention.

Plenty of families run both. Fortnightly in person, weekly online. It takes marginally more effort to arrange and it holds together across a full year better than either format used on its own.

A smaller point decides more sessions than people expect: where in the house the session happens. A dining table with family moving past suits most teenagers better than a closed bedroom door, and suits a few of them considerably worse. Try both arrangements before assuming the format is the problem.
items: In person: supervision, working shown, parent visibility
Online: continuity through monsoon, travel and exam term
Fortnightly in person plus weekly online as a middle path
Reliability matters more than format over eight months

contentBlocks.heading: What IB tuition in Sector 85 Gurugram will not do
contentBlocks.body:
Some limits, stated before you spend anything.

Six weeks of tutoring before a May session will not turn a 3 into a 7. It can defend a grade boundary. It can fix technique that is costing marks the student has already earned in their head. That is a real result, and it is not a transformation.

Nobody here guarantees grades, and no percentage improvements are published, because those numbers would have to be invented.

Starting late carries a cost that no amount of intensity removes. Four sessions a week in April produces a tired student, not four times the progress, and tired students underperform in exactly the papers you were worried about.

There is a limit on the platform's side too. Tutor availability is not unlimited, particularly for higher level sciences in the months before an exam session, and a preferred slot may simply not exist.

What can be offered is transparency: what will be covered, in what order, and an honest read at four weeks on whether it is working.

A tutor is also no substitute for talking to the school. If a predicted grade looks wrong, that conversation belongs with the Diploma Programme coordinator, not with someone paid by the hour to teach one subject.

contentBlocks.heading: How tutors are screened
contentBlocks.body:
Screening happens before any name is shared.

Documents first: identity, degrees, and any teaching qualification claimed. Then programme-specific checking. A tutor is asked which command terms students most often misread, and what they do about it. There is no single correct answer, but there is a visible difference between someone who has thought about it and someone who has not.

Subject and level are verified separately. Teaching Chemistry SL well says little about handling HL option topics under exam conditions.

For anyone offering internal assessment or extended essay support, the boundary is checked explicitly. Guidance on structure, method and argument is legitimate. Writing any part of a student's submission is not, and academic honesty rules make that a serious matter for the student rather than the tutor.

After matching, the first month is treated as provisional. Feedback gets collected, and a change of tutor can be requested without an argument. Most families never need it. The ones who do should not have to fight for it.

What none of this predicts is rapport. A tutor can hold every credential on the list and still fail to hold the attention of one particular sixteen-year-old on a Thursday evening. The trial session exists because paperwork cannot answer that question.

contentBlocks.body:
Start by telling us how much time is left. The exam session in view, the grade, the programme, the subjects with their levels, and whether you are asking for steady weekly work or focused revision before a specific date.

A shortlist can then be reviewed, with fees and timing confirmed before anything is scheduled and availability subject to tutor schedules.

If you are unsure which of the two situations you are in, describe the last three months instead. What the school has said, what the marks have done, and what your child says when asked directly. The right plan is usually obvious from that, and it is a quicker conversation than trying to specify a package in advance. Advisors here are used to that version of an enquiry, and it tends to produce a better match than a tidy one-line brief.

The conversation costs nothing. The delay does.
