faqs.question: When in the year should we actually start looking for an IB tutor?
faqs.answer: For Diploma Programme students, the strongest point is the start of Grade 11, when subject levels can still be changed and internal assessment topics have not been chosen badly yet. The second-best point is immediately after any assessment that surprised you. Middle Years families often start when criterion marking first confuses everyone at home. Waiting until Grade 12 mocks is common and it costs options, because the tutors who handle higher level sciences fill their evenings well before then.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks before the May session. Is there any point starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the goal is realistic. Eight weeks is enough to fix exam technique, drill timed past papers, and target two or three topics that carry disproportionate marks. It is not enough to rebuild a subject from the ground up, and any tutor who says otherwise is selling. Ask them in the first session which units they intend to leave uncovered. A straight answer to that question is a good sign; an evasive one tells you plenty about the months ahead.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week is sensible?
faqs.answer: For year-long support, one session per subject per week is usually the right rhythm, with the student doing independent work in between. Two per subject is worth considering only for a genuinely weak foundation or a compressed timeline. Beyond that, returns fall quickly. A student attending five tutoring hours a week alongside school and CAS has no time left to consolidate anything, and consolidation is where the marks actually come from. More hours is often the least effective response to a poor result.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help us decide between higher level and standard level?
faqs.answer: A tutor can give you a useful second opinion on whether the workload is realistic, based on how the student handles the material in front of them. What they cannot do is make the decision or change the registration, which sits with the school and its Diploma Programme coordinator. The most valuable input a tutor offers is honest: if a student is spending three times longer than peers on higher level problem sets, that is information the family and school should have early.

faqs.question: Most tutors seem to be based near Golf Course Road. Is that a problem for Sector 85?
faqs.answer: It is a scheduling constraint rather than a barrier. Many experienced tutors do live and teach around Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok and Sohna Road, and reaching the New Gurgaon sectors on a weekday evening is a long journey. Weekend slots are usually easier to secure than weekday ones. If continuity across a full academic year matters more than physical presence, online removes the problem completely and widens the set of people who can teach the exact level you need.

faqs.question: Is there a fee difference between short revision help and year-long support?
faqs.answer: The hourly rate is broadly similar, driven by subject, level and mode rather than duration. The total differs sharply. Intensive revision packs many hours into a few weeks, so the monthly outlay feels heavy even though the overall commitment is short. Year-long support spreads a lower monthly figure across eight or nine months and generally costs more in total while producing steadier results. Whichever route you choose, the rate is confirmed before the first scheduled session.

faqs.question: How much can a tutor help with an internal assessment without crossing an academic honesty line?
faqs.answer: Quite a lot, as long as the words and the data stay the student's. A tutor can question whether a research question is answerable, point out that a method will not generate enough data, explain why an evaluation paragraph is not scoring, and ask what a particular sentence is meant to prove. What they must never do is draft, rewrite or supply content. Schools require declarations of authenticity, and the consequences of a breach fall on the student.

faqs.question: What should we expect to see after four weeks?
faqs.answer: Concrete things, not a feeling. The student attempting past-paper questions without being told to. Written answers that respond to the command term rather than restating content. A named plan for each internal assessment, with dates. And the student able to describe their own weak areas without checking with you first. If none of that has appeared after a month of regular sessions, something needs changing, and raising it then costs far less than raising it in month four.

faqs.question: Do you support November session students as well as May?
faqs.answer: Both sessions can be supported, though the rhythm differs. May 2026 candidates work through a long build across two academic years with mocks in the winter. November 2026 candidates run on a shifted calendar, which means their internal assessment deadlines and revision windows fall at different points, and demand for tutors is spread differently across the year. Say which session applies when you enquire, because assuming May is the default has caused more than one badly timed revision plan.

mainEntity.name: When in the year should we actually start looking for an IB tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Diploma Programme students, the strongest point is the start of Grade 11, when subject levels can still be changed and internal assessment topics have not been chosen badly yet. The second-best point is immediately after any assessment that surprised you. Middle Years families often start when criterion marking first confuses everyone at home. Waiting until Grade 12 mocks is common and it costs options, because the tutors who handle higher level sciences fill their evenings well before then.

mainEntity.name: We have eight weeks before the May session. Is there any point starting now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, provided the goal is realistic. Eight weeks is enough to fix exam technique, drill timed past papers, and target two or three topics that carry disproportionate marks. It is not enough to rebuild a subject from the ground up, and any tutor who says otherwise is selling. Ask them in the first session which units they intend to leave uncovered. A straight answer to that question is a good sign; an evasive one tells you plenty about the months ahead.

mainEntity.name: How many sessions a week is sensible?

acceptedAnswer.text: For year-long support, one session per subject per week is usually the right rhythm, with the student doing independent work in between. Two per subject is worth considering only for a genuinely weak foundation or a compressed timeline. Beyond that, returns fall quickly. A student attending five tutoring hours a week alongside school and CAS has no time left to consolidate anything, and consolidation is where the marks actually come from. More hours is often the least effective response to a poor result.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help us decide between higher level and standard level?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tutor can give you a useful second opinion on whether the workload is realistic, based on how the student handles the material in front of them. What they cannot do is make the decision or change the registration, which sits with the school and its Diploma Programme coordinator. The most valuable input a tutor offers is honest: if a student is spending three times longer than peers on higher level problem sets, that is information the family and school should have early.

mainEntity.name: Most tutors seem to be based near Golf Course Road. Is that a problem for Sector 85?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a scheduling constraint rather than a barrier. Many experienced tutors do live and teach around Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok and Sohna Road, and reaching the New Gurgaon sectors on a weekday evening is a long journey. Weekend slots are usually easier to secure than weekday ones. If continuity across a full academic year matters more than physical presence, online removes the problem completely and widens the set of people who can teach the exact level you need.

mainEntity.name: Is there a fee difference between short revision help and year-long support?

acceptedAnswer.text: The hourly rate is broadly similar, driven by subject, level and mode rather than duration. The total differs sharply. Intensive revision packs many hours into a few weeks, so the monthly outlay feels heavy even though the overall commitment is short. Year-long support spreads a lower monthly figure across eight or nine months and generally costs more in total while producing steadier results. Whichever route you choose, the rate is confirmed before the first scheduled session.

mainEntity.name: How much can a tutor help with an internal assessment without crossing an academic honesty line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quite a lot, as long as the words and the data stay the student's. A tutor can question whether a research question is answerable, point out that a method will not generate enough data, explain why an evaluation paragraph is not scoring, and ask what a particular sentence is meant to prove. What they must never do is draft, rewrite or supply content. Schools require declarations of authenticity, and the consequences of a breach fall on the student.

mainEntity.name: What should we expect to see after four weeks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Concrete things, not a feeling. The student attempting past-paper questions without being told to. Written answers that respond to the command term rather than restating content. A named plan for each internal assessment, with dates. And the student able to describe their own weak areas without checking with you first. If none of that has appeared after a month of regular sessions, something needs changing, and raising it then costs far less than raising it in month four.

mainEntity.name: Do you support November session students as well as May?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both sessions can be supported, though the rhythm differs. May 2026 candidates work through a long build across two academic years with mocks in the winter. November 2026 candidates run on a shifted calendar, which means their internal assessment deadlines and revision windows fall at different points, and demand for tutors is spread differently across the year. Say which session applies when you enquire, because assuming May is the default has caused more than one badly timed revision plan.

heroSubtitle: Sector 86 sits in the New Gurgaon belt near Godrej Air, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next, a fair drive from the older international school corridor. This page explains what that distance means for home tutoring, when online is the better call, and how a shortlist gets built.
introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 86 Gurugram are arranged two ways: a tutor travels to the flat when one with the right subject and level is free in this part of New Gurgaon, or the sessions run online, which is what happens more often at higher level. Support covers Grade 1 to Grade 12 across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes. Diploma planning is currently built around the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions. contentBlocks.heading: The short answer for families searching for IB tutors in Sector 86, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the plain version. A tutor can come to your flat in Sector 86 when someone with the right subject and level happens to be free in this part of New Gurgaon, and online sessions cover everything else. Diploma-level requests here tend to end up online. Primary Years requests tend to stay at home.

That is the answer. What follows is the reasoning, because the answer shifts depending on which year your child is in and how far your evening timetable can bend.

Sector 86 is a residential pocket west of the national highway, surrounded by Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next. Households here are mostly high-rise, mostly recent, and mostly running a long school commute. Support through IB Gram runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes, with Diploma work planned around the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions and earlier groundwork for cohorts who have just chosen their subjects.

One thing worth saying before you read further. No tutor is confirmed until a specific person agrees to a specific slot, so treat every timing mentioned on this page as something to be reviewed rather than something already booked.

Home visits subject to tutor availability in New Gurgaon

contentBlocks.heading: Godrej Air, Vatika India Next and the roads that decide your slot
contentBlocks.body:
Geography here is simple and it matters. Sector 86 lies in the newer western sectors, with Vatika India Next spread across the sectors just beside it and the Godrej towers a short hop away. Movement between these communities is quick. A tutor already teaching in Mapsko Casa Bella can reach a flat in Sector 86 in the time it takes to park, which is why a second student in a neighbouring tower is easy to add and a first student is the hard one to arrange.

Travel in the other direction is the problem. The older residential belt where many experienced Diploma tutors live, around DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, South City 1, Nirvana Country, Sector 50 and Sector 65, sits across the city. At half past five on a weekday that crossing is not a twenty-minute drive.

So the practical pattern looks like this. Afternoon and weekend-morning home slots are realistic. Weekday evening home slots at higher level are thin, and pretending otherwise wastes a fortnight of your time.

Families who accept an online evening slot and keep the home slot for weekends generally get a better tutor than families who insist on home visits only.
items: Vatika India Next and the Godrej towers within minutes
Afternoon and weekend-morning home slots most realistic
Southern belt tutors mean a genuine cross-city drive
A second student in the same tower is easier to place
Peak-hour traffic decides more than the fee does

contentBlocks.heading: Home visits, online sessions and the hybrid week in Sector 86
contentBlocks.body:
Three shapes come up, and each suits a different child.

Home tutoring works best for younger students and for anyone whose real problem is starting work rather than understanding it. A Middle Years student who opens the laptop and then opens six other things needs a person in the room. Primary Years reading and numeracy support also belongs at home, where a tutor can watch a child work on paper.

Online tutoring wins on choice. Higher level Mathematics, Physics and Economics are specialist matches, and restricting the search to tutors willing to drive to Sector 86 on a Tuesday cuts the shortlist to almost nothing. Screen-shared past papers, a shared document for an internal assessment draft and a written record of every worked solution are genuine advantages, not consolation prizes.

The hybrid week is what many Diploma families settle into by the second term: one longer session at home on a weekend when concentration is available, one shorter online session midweek for doubt-solving and marking feedback.

Where online struggles is with the child who needs supervision more than instruction. If you are paying a tutor to keep your son at the desk, pay for a person at the desk.
items: Home suits PYP and students who avoid starting
Online widens the pool for HL Maths, Physics and Economics
Weekend home plus midweek online is the common settlement
Screen-shared past papers and a written solution record
Supervision needs a person in the room

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB subjects Sector 86 families ask about first
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics arrives first and loudest. Math AA HL enquiries usually follow a calculus assessment, and the diagnosis is often unglamorous: the calculus was understood and the algebra underneath it was slow. Math AI HL enquiries arrive later in the year and sound different, because the difficulty there lies in choosing a model, justifying the choice and writing about what the technology produced.

Physics and Chemistry follow the internal assessment calendar rather than the teaching calendar. A Physics request in October is usually about mechanics and uncertainty; the same student writes again in February about fields. Chemistry enquiries cluster around organic mechanisms and around the write-up itself, which trips up students who did the practical work perfectly well.

Economics is the quiet one. Students who write fluently still lose marks because a definition is missing, a diagram is unlabelled, or the command term asked them to evaluate and they described. English A requests are about the individual oral and about commentary structure far more often than about reading ability.

Younger students ask for something else entirely: reading fluency, number sense, and help turning a Middle Years task sheet into work that satisfies the criterion strands rather than the topic.
items: Math AA HL: algebraic fluency underneath the calculus
Math AI HL: modelling choices and justification
Physics and Chemistry internal assessment write-ups
Economics command terms and diagram labelling
English A individual oral and commentary structure

contentBlocks.heading: From enquiry to first lesson: how a Sector 86, Gurugram match is made
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is short enough to describe in full.

One. You tell an advisor the grade, the programme, the subject and level, the school, and what the last two pieces of assessed work looked like. That last part carries more information than anything else you can give.

Two. The requirement is written down as a teaching problem rather than a subject name. Chemistry HL, weak on organic, internal assessment draft due in five weeks is a brief a tutor can answer. Needs Chemistry help is not.

Three. Availability is checked against your actual week. School timings, the commute back to Sector 86 and any activity that eats a weekday evening are treated as fixed, because they are.

Four. A shortlist of profiles comes back with subject history, level experience and the modes each tutor will teach in. You choose.

Five. The first session is diagnostic. The tutor works through recent marked work, finds where the understanding stops, and tells you what the next four weeks will target.

If the fit is wrong after that session, say so early. Changing in week one costs nothing. Changing in week seven costs a term.
items: Advisor call: grade, level, school, last marked work
Requirement written as a teaching problem
Availability checked against your real week
Shortlist with subject and level history
Diagnostic first session, then a four-week target

contentBlocks.heading: Three programmes, three different ways a student gets stuck
contentBlocks.body:
The programmes fail in different places, so they are tutored differently.

In the Primary Years Programme the risk is over-correction. A six-year-old who is behind on decoding does not need worksheets lifted from a board syllabus; she needs short, frequent reading with someone patient, and number work that stays concrete. Parents in Sector 86 sometimes ask for drilling because it looks like progress. It usually is not.

The Middle Years Programme is where most families first feel lost, because the report mentions criterion B and nobody at home is sure what that means. Tutoring here is largely translation: reading the task sheet properly, understanding what each criterion strand actually rewards, and planning a response before writing it.

The Diploma Programme is the heaviest and the most time-bound. Internal assessments across six subjects, an extended essay that needs a supervisor conversation and a research question narrow enough to finish, theory of knowledge, and past-paper work under real timing. A student who starts in Grade 11 has room to build. A student who starts in the January of Grade 12 is triaging, and an honest tutor will say which topics are worth the remaining hours and which are not.
items: PYP: reading fluency, number sense, inquiry habits
MYP: criterion strands and careful task-sheet reading
DP: internal assessments, extended essay, TOK, timed papers
Grade 11 builds; Grade 12 triages
Programme-aware planning rather than topic drilling

contentBlocks.heading: The school run from Sector 86 to Gurugram's IB campuses
contentBlocks.body:
Children living in Sector 86 are not walking to an IB campus. The schools that come up in enquiries here, Pathways World School, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and GD Goenka World School out towards Sohna, are all a proper bus journey away.

That journey shapes the tutoring week more than most parents expect. A bus leaving before seven and returning after four produces a student who is tired at five, functional at six, and finished by half past eight. Booking a demanding higher level session at nine in the evening is a decision to waste money.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Tutors are not recruited from them and no claim about their internal marking is made here.

What the school name does tell an advisor is useful anyway: the assessment calendar, the subject combinations that campus typically offers, and how early internal assessment deadlines tend to land. A tutor who has taught students from the same campus arrives already knowing the rhythm of the term.

Six to eight in the evening is the usable window

contentBlocks.heading: Boring checks that keep a bad match away from your child
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is deliberately dull, and it should be.

Identity is confirmed against government photo identification. Qualifications are checked against the documents themselves rather than a claim on a profile. Teaching history is examined for the thing that matters, which is not years of experience but years of experience at the level you need. Somebody who has taught Mathematics for a decade to board students has not necessarily marked a single Math AA HL script.

Subject knowledge is tested through IB material: a past-paper question, a markscheme applied to a student answer, an internal assessment sample judged against criteria. Command-term precision shows up quickly in that exercise. So does the habit of explaining by telling rather than by asking.

References are followed up where a tutor supplies them, and the first weeks of any placement are reviewed with the family rather than assumed to be fine.

None of this guarantees an outcome, and any platform saying otherwise is selling. What it does is remove the failure mode families dread most: a confident, pleasant person who does not actually know the syllabus and takes six weeks to be found out.
items: Government photo identification verified
Degree and teaching documents seen, not claimed
Level-specific IB experience, not years alone
Markscheme and internal assessment sample exercise
Early placement review with the family

contentBlocks.heading: Where an IB tutor in Sector 86, Gurugram will not help
contentBlocks.body:
A page like this is more useful if it says what tutoring does not fix.

It does not fix a student who is not doing the work. A tutor can build a plan, mark it and chase it, but two hours a week set against fifteen hours of avoidance is arithmetic that does not resolve. If the real problem is sleep, screens or a subject chosen for the wrong reasons, tutoring will delay the reckoning rather than remove it.

It does not fix a subject choice made in Grade 11 that was wrong from the start. Sometimes the honest advice is to talk to the coordinator about a level change, and a tutor who never mentions that option is protecting the booking.

It does not substitute for the class teacher, who marks the internal assessment and knows the school's reading of the criteria.

And no tutor can promise a grade. Nobody is able to. What a good placement gives you is a clearer picture within four weeks: what the student can do unaided, what is missing, and whether the gap is closing at a rate the remaining calendar supports.
items: Cannot compensate for work not done at home
Not a replacement for the class teacher
No promised grades or score jumps
A level change is sometimes the better advice
Four weeks is a fair review point

contentBlocks.heading: Starting a tutor search in Sector 86, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started takes one conversation and about fifteen minutes of preparation on your side.

Have three things ready. The subject and level, written exactly as the school writes it. The last two marked pieces of work, including the teacher comments you would rather not show anyone. And an honest map of the week, with school timings, the commute back to Sector 86 and the activities that are not moving.

The advisor call covers what has been tried already, what the student says the problem is, which is frequently different from what the report says, and which mode is realistic given where you live in New Gurgaon.

A shortlist follows. Home availability near Godrej Air, Vatika India Next and the surrounding communities depends on which tutors are free that term, so it can be reviewed but not promised. Online options are wider and usually faster to start.

Then a diagnostic first session, and a decision after it. If the fit is wrong, replacement is straightforward and early. Nothing on this page is a commitment until you have met the tutor and agreed the slot.
items: Subject and level as the school writes it
The last two marked assignments to hand
A weekly timetable including the commute
Shortlist reviewed, not promised
Diagnostic session before committing

faqs.question: Is it realistic to get a higher level Maths tutor to come to Sector 86 on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being blunt about the odds. Many tutors with deep higher level Mathematics experience live in the older southern parts of Gurugram, and a six o'clock crossing to Sector 86 costs them an hour each way. Afternoon slots and weekend mornings are far more likely to be filled. If your requirement is a weekday evening at higher level, an online tutor will usually be both stronger on the syllabus and easier to keep. Home availability can be reviewed, but do not build the whole term around it.

faqs.question: We live in Vatika India Next. Does that make finding a tutor easier than a standalone flat?
faqs.answer: It helps. A tutor already visiting one tower in a large community will often take a second student in the same complex, because the travel is already paid for in time. Families in Vatika India Next, Godrej Air, Godrej Summit and Mapsko Casa Bella therefore tend to see slightly better home availability than a single household further out. It does not change the fee, and it does not create a tutor where none exists for a rare subject combination. What it mainly improves is which slot you are offered.

faqs.question: How much does IB tuition in Sector 86 cost, and what changes the price?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the level, the subject and how scarce that combination is locally. Higher level Diploma sciences and Mathematics sit at the top; Primary Years support sits well below. Mode matters too, since a tutor travelling to Sector 86 is pricing an hour of driving alongside the teaching hour. You are quoted per session before anything begins, and the quote belongs to the tutor rather than being a platform average. Ask specifically whether marking of drafts between sessions is included, because that varies and it is the part parents assume.

faqs.question: My son has fallen behind in two subjects at once. Do we need two tutors?
faqs.answer: Not always, and starting with two is usually a mistake. Two tutors means two schedules, two sets of homework and a student with no unsupervised evening left, which is often what caused the slide in the first place. Begin with the subject whose next assessment falls soonest, or the one he has stopped attempting altogether. Four weeks later you will know whether the problem was subject-specific or a working method failing across the board. The second answer needs a different remedy from a second tutor.

faqs.question: Our daughter wants to move from Math AA HL down to standard level. Can a tutor advise on that?
faqs.answer: A tutor can give you a view, and it should be an honest one rather than a comfortable one. After a diagnostic session and a look at recent scripts, someone who has taught both routes can say whether the gap is fixable in the time remaining or whether the higher level demand is genuinely beyond what her schedule allows. The decision itself sits with the school coordinator, who knows the timetable constraints and the deadline for changes. Ask early, because level changes have cut-off dates.

faqs.question: What happens if we do not like the first tutor?
faqs.answer: Say so quickly. The first session is diagnostic partly so that a mismatch surfaces before anyone has invested a month in it. Tell the advisor what specifically did not work, whether it was pace, explanation style, level depth or simply the timing, and a different profile is put forward. Changing tutors in the first fortnight is ordinary and costs the student almost nothing. Changing in the middle of an internal assessment cycle is genuinely disruptive, which is the reason for reviewing early rather than waiting politely.

faqs.question: Do you teach the Primary Years Programme, or only Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Both. Support runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, so Primary Years reading, inquiry work and number sense are covered alongside Middle Years criterion tasks and full Diploma subjects. The tutor profile differs a great deal between them. Younger students need patience, short sessions and a person physically present more often than not; Diploma students need subject specialists who have marked at that level. Ask for the age band explicitly when you enquire, because a strong Physics HL tutor is not automatically the right choice for a Grade 3 reader.

faqs.question: How will I know after a month whether this is working?
faqs.answer: Four weeks is a fair checkpoint. By then you should be able to see three things: whether the student can attempt a question type unaided that previously stopped him, whether homework is being started earlier, and whether the tutor can describe the remaining gaps precisely. Marks may not have moved yet, and a single term test can hide real progress. What should have moved is the specificity of the conversation. If the tutor still speaks in general terms about effort after a month, that is your signal to change.

faqs.question: Are your tutors from the schools my son's friends attend?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with Pathways World School, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School or any other campus unless specifically stated. Tutors are matched on verified qualifications and level experience, not on a school connection. Familiarity with how a particular campus sequences deadlines can be useful, and an advisor will mention it where it exists, but no claim is made about influence over school marking of any kind.

contentBlocks.heading: Study habits come first, then the tutor: IB tutoring in Sector 87, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Parents in Sector 87 usually open with a subject. My son needs Physics. Fair enough, and often true. But when the last three assessments are laid out on a table, the pattern is rarely a topic that was never taught. It is a working habit that stopped coping once the workload changed.

Four habits carry most of the damage. Notes that record what the teacher said instead of what the student did not follow. Revision that means rereading rather than attempting questions from memory. Deadlines met in the final twenty-four hours, which is survivable in Grade 9 and fatal across six Diploma internal assessments. And answers written without reading the command term, so a student who knows the content still writes a description where an evaluation was asked for.

Tutor selection follows from that diagnosis. A student whose problem is timing under exam conditions needs someone willing to sit with a clock and a past paper. A student whose problem is conceptual needs a different person entirely.

Support here runs Grade 1 to Grade 12 across all three programmes, with Diploma work planned around the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions, arranged at home in Sector 87 when a suitable tutor is free nearby or online when nobody is.

contentBlocks.heading: How a request from Sector 87 turns into a named tutor
contentBlocks.body:
The intake conversation is built around questions that are more specific than they first sound.

What did the last report actually say, in the teacher's words rather than the grade? Which piece of work took longest for the least return? What does the student do first when he sits down, and how long before he stops? Which subject is he avoiding, and since when?

Answers to those produce a written requirement: programme, subject, level, the assessment cycle ahead, the working habit that needs rebuilding, and the days and times that genuinely exist in your week once school timings and the journey back to Sector 87 are subtracted.

Profiles are shortlisted against that requirement. You see each tutor's subject history, the levels taught, the modes offered and the slots open, and you pick. An advisor recommends but does not assign.

The first session is spent diagnosing rather than teaching a topic. Recent marked work is read closely, the student is asked to attempt something unaided, and the tutor comes back with what the coming month will target.

If that plan sounds vague when you hear it, ask for it in writing before agreeing to a second session.

Written requirement naming the habit to rebuild
Real availability after the school run and activities
You choose from profiles; nobody is allocated to you
A month-one plan stated before session two

contentBlocks.heading: What changes between PYP, MYP and DP habits
contentBlocks.body:
Habits look different at each stage, which is why the same tutor rarely suits a Grade 4 student and a Grade 12 one.

Primary Years students are building attention and fluency. Twenty-five focused minutes of reading or number work beats an hour of drifting, and a tutor who understands inquiry-based classrooms will connect practice to the unit the child is already exploring rather than running a parallel syllabus at home.

Middle Years students hit the criterion wall. The task sheet lists strands, the marking is criterion-related, and a student who writes a decent essay by instinct starts losing marks because the essay never answered what strand C asked for. Habit repair here means planning against the criteria before writing, then rereading the task sheet after the first draft.

Diploma students are managing a calendar as much as a syllabus. Six subjects, internal assessments that overlap, an extended essay that quietly slips, theory of knowledge sitting outside the subject timetable, and past papers that need to be attempted under real timing rather than open-book. Students who log which questions they got wrong, sorted by topic, improve faster than students who work through more papers and record nothing.
items: PYP: short sessions, fluency, inquiry-linked practice
MYP: plan against criterion strands before writing
DP: calendar management across six subjects
Past papers under timing, with an error log by topic
Extended essay and TOK need their own slots, not leftovers

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing between a tutor at your door in Sector 87 and one on screen
contentBlocks.body:
The choice between a tutor at your door and one on a screen is usually settled by age and by self-management, not by preference.

Below about Grade 8, physical presence does most of the work. A younger student in Sector 87 will read aloud, write on paper and be redirected when attention drifts, and none of that survives a video call as well as parents hope.

From Grade 9 upward the calculation flips. Specialists who have taught higher level Chemistry or Economics repeatedly are scattered across the city, and requiring them to drive out to New Gurgaon in the evening removes most of them from consideration. Online sessions also suit habit work unusually well: a shared document holds the revision log, the tutor watches a question being attempted in real time, and everything worked through stays available the following week.

A mixed week is common. Home on Saturday for the long, demanding session. Online on Wednesday for marking, doubts and a check that the plan is being followed.

The honest failure case is the student who books online sessions and attends them with the camera off and a game open. If that describes your child, buy the person in the room instead.

Grade 9 upward, specialist choice widens online
A shared document keeps the revision log visible
Saturday at home plus a midweek online check-in
Camera-off attendance is a real failure mode

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by subject: the habit that usually breaks first
contentBlocks.body:
Taking the common requests in turn, along with the habit each one tends to expose.

Mathematics at higher level punishes gaps in fluency more than gaps in understanding. Students following Math AA HL often need timed practice on the mechanical steps so that the thinking has room to happen. Math AI HL students more often need teaching on how to write about a model, defend the choice of it, and interpret the output rather than only produce it.

In Physics the recurring failure is skipping the diagram and the units. Chemistry loses marks in the write-up, where a well-run practical becomes a weak internal assessment because uncertainty, variables and evaluation were treated as an afterthought.

Economics rewards precise definitions and correctly labelled diagrams, and the student who writes essays quickly is often the one dropping those easy marks. English A needs an active reading habit: annotation, tracking a technique across a text, preparing properly for the individual oral rather than improvising on the day.

Younger students ask for reading fluency and number sense. Middle Years students most often need help converting a task sheet into a plan.

contentBlocks.heading: Honest limits on what tutoring in Sector 87, Gurugram can change
contentBlocks.body:
Some limits are worth stating before you spend money.

Habits take longer to change than content. A missing topic can be taught in two sessions. A student who has never made notes he can revise from will need most of a term to build the habit, and there will be weeks where nothing visible improves. Families expecting the second kind of change on the first kind of timetable usually give up a fortnight before it would have worked.

Tutoring cannot manufacture time either. A Grade 12 student with five weeks left and three untouched internal assessments has an arithmetic problem, and the useful response is prioritising rather than optimism.

No grade, score or percentage improvement is promised here, by any tutor on this platform. Anyone offering you one is guessing.

contentBlocks.heading: The checks that happen before a profile reaches you

Identity is confirmed against official photo identification. Academic documents are seen in original form rather than accepted as a line on a CV. Teaching history is read for level specificity, because experience with the Diploma at standard level does not automatically transfer to higher level, and neither transfers automatically to Middle Years criterion marking.

Then a practical assessment. A tutor is asked to work through a past-paper question, apply a markscheme to a real student response, and comment on an internal assessment extract. That exercise reveals two useful things quickly: whether the tutor uses command-term language accurately, and whether they can explain by questioning rather than by lecturing.

Where references are provided, they are followed up. Once a placement starts, the early sessions are reviewed with the family rather than left alone.

Screening is not a promise about results. It is a filter that removes the most common and most expensive mistake, which is discovering in week six that the tutor has never actually taught the level your child is sitting.

faqs.question: My daughter revises for hours and still underperforms in tests. Would a tutor help with that?
faqs.answer: Very likely, though not in the way you expect. Hours spent rereading feel like revision and produce little recall, because the brain is recognising material rather than retrieving it. A tutor working on method will move her to attempting questions from memory first and checking against the markscheme second, keeping a log of which topics keep failing. That log is the useful artefact. Expect the change in test scores to lag the change in method by a few weeks, which is why the first month should be judged on behaviour.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week make sense for a Diploma student in Sector 87?
faqs.answer: Two is the common answer for a single subject at higher level, and one of those is often shorter. More than three sessions a week across subjects usually backfires, because the student then has no unsupervised time in which to discover what he cannot do alone. The pattern that works in Sector 87 households tends to be one longer weekend session when concentration is available, plus one midweek check on marking and doubts. Frequency should be reviewed after a month rather than fixed at the start.

faqs.question: Is theory of knowledge worth arranging a tutor for, or is it purely a school subject?
faqs.answer: It is taught at school and the essay is submitted through the school, so a tutor works alongside that rather than replacing it. Useful support looks like unpicking a prescribed title, testing whether a real-life situation actually illustrates the knowledge question, and pushing a student to argue against his own position. Many students write fluently and still score poorly because the essay never engages a counterclaim. Availability of tutors comfortable with theory of knowledge is narrower than for mainstream subjects, so ask early.

faqs.question: We want a tutor who comes home. How far in advance should we ask?
faqs.answer: Ask two to three weeks before you want to begin, and earlier if the requirement is a higher level science on a weekday evening. Home slots in Sector 87 open when a tutor's existing schedule across the newer sectors allows another visit, which means availability moves term by term. If the timing is urgent, starting online while a home slot is being sought beats waiting for one. Any home slot mentioned before a named tutor confirms it should be treated as provisional.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who teaches CBSE Maths acceptable for Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and the difference is not a small one. A strong board Mathematics teacher may be excellent on technique and still unfamiliar with the exploration, its criteria, the calculator paper conventions and the command-term wording that Diploma markschemes use. Some teachers have taught both and are genuinely fluent in each. Ask directly how many Diploma cohorts the tutor has taught at that level and whether they have marked exploration drafts. The answer should be specific rather than reassuring.

faqs.question: What do you need from us before the first session?
faqs.answer: Three things. The subject and level exactly as the school writes it, since standard and higher level differ substantially. The last two marked assignments with the teacher's comments, which tell a tutor more in five minutes than a phone call does in thirty. And a realistic picture of the week, including school timings and the journey back to Sector 87. With those in hand, the first session can be spent diagnosing rather than gathering information you already had.

faqs.question: Are sessions available during school holidays and ahead of the November session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and holidays are often the most productive period, particularly for students preparing for the November session or wanting to start an internal assessment before term pressure arrives. Availability shifts during holidays because some tutors travel, so schedules are confirmed session by session rather than assumed for the whole break. Intensive blocks work well for content catch-up and badly for habit building, which needs the rhythm of a normal week. A mix of both across a long break is usually the better plan.

faqs.question: My son is in Grade 9 and starts the Diploma next year. Is tutoring premature?
faqs.answer: Not premature, though the purpose is different. Grade 9 and 10 are when note-taking, revision method and deadline behaviour can still be rebuilt without an exam calendar pressing down. Work at this stage focuses on strengthening the mathematics and writing foundations that higher level subjects assume, and on testing how the student copes with subjects he is considering. Families who use these two years for method rather than content often need less intensive help later, though nothing about that can be guaranteed.

faqs.question: How are fees handled, and can we stop after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Fees are set by the tutor and quoted per session before you begin, with level and subject scarcity driving most of the difference. You are not locked into a term. Most families review after four sessions, which is roughly the point where a diagnosis has been made and a plan is visible. If you want to stop, tell the advisor rather than only the tutor, so the placement is closed properly. Ask upfront whether marking of drafts between sessions is charged separately.

contentBlocks.heading: What online IB tutoring in Sector 88, Gurugram does better than a home visit
contentBlocks.body:
Take the argument for online tutoring at its strongest first, because in Sector 88 it is usually the right call at Diploma level.

A screen removes distance from the equation. The tutor who has taught Physics HL for years and marked internal assessment drafts repeatedly does not have to live nearby, and in this part of New Gurgaon that matters, because most of them do not.

A screen also leaves a record. Everything written on a shared board during the session is still there on Sunday, which is more than can be said for a notebook page filled in a hurry during a home visit. Past papers open side by side with a markscheme. A draft gets annotated live while the student watches the reasoning behind each comment appear.

And short sessions become possible. A twenty-minute doubt-clearing call before a test is not worth a tutor's travel, but it is easy to arrange on a screen.

contentBlocks.heading: How each IB subject behaves on a screen
contentBlocks.body:
Subjects do not all behave the same way through a screen, so it is worth being specific.

Mathematics transfers almost perfectly. A shared writing surface with a stylus is closer to a notebook than a classroom board is, and both Math AA HL and Math AI HL work well this way, with the graphing software the student already uses open in the same window.

Economics and English A also transfer cleanly. Both are about the structure of an argument, and a document two people can edit at once is a better teaching tool than a printed essay covered in red ink.

Physics is fine for theory and weaker for practical intuition. A tutor can talk through an experimental design and pick apart an uncertainty calculation, but cannot hand a student a metre rule.

Chemistry is the hardest case. Organic mechanisms need drawing slowly and repeatedly, which works on a tablet and badly with a mouse, and equipment familiarity does not translate at all. Where the internal assessment involves apparatus the student has already used at school, the write-up support is unaffected.

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 88 inside the New Gurgaon belt: what is close and what is not

Density creates supply. Where enough students in one cluster of towers want the same programme, tutors begin including the area in their weekly route and home slots appear. In parts of the older city that process finished years ago. Here it is still happening, sector by sector.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: which ones survive a video call
contentBlocks.body:
Each programme sits differently with a screen between tutor and student.

The Primary Years Programme sits worst. A young child in Sector 88 learning to read needs someone beside her, tracking the finger under the word and catching the guess before it hardens into a habit. It can be done online with a very patient tutor and a parent nearby for the first few weeks, but it is second best and deserves to be described that way.

The Middle Years Programme sits in the middle. Criterion-based tasks are planned and drafted in documents anyway, so a tutor who can see the task sheet and the draft on one screen loses very little. What does get lost is the ability to notice a fifteen-year-old quietly disengaging.

The Diploma Programme sits best. Extended essay conversations, internal assessment drafting, past-paper walkthroughs and theory of knowledge argument work all happen through documents and questions. Timed practice works too, provided the student photographs the paper afterwards and the tutor marks it properly against the criteria instead of glancing at the answers.

contentBlocks.heading: Checks that matter more when the tutor is remote

Remote teaching raises the cost of a bad hire, since the parent is not in the next room to notice. So the checks come first.

Identity is confirmed against official photo identification, and the person appearing on the call must be the person on the profile. Qualifications are verified from documents. Teaching history is examined for the level in question rather than for total years, because a decade of standard level experience is not the same qualification as a year of higher level marking.

A subject exercise follows: a past-paper question worked through, a markscheme applied to a student script, and an internal assessment extract commented on. Two things become obvious quickly in that exercise. Whether the tutor's command-term usage is precise. And whether they explain by asking questions or by talking.

For online placements there is a practical layer as well: a stable connection, a writing surface the student can actually read, and the habit of sharing the session record afterwards. Early sessions are reviewed with the family. No screening promises a result, and any claim otherwise should be read as marketing.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or both for students in Sector 88, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Three arrangements, and a simple way of choosing between them for a student living in Sector 88.

Home tutoring is the right answer when the obstacle is behaviour rather than knowledge, when the student is young, or when a subject needs paper, apparatus and someone watching the hand that holds the pen. It costs more in practice, because you are also buying the tutor's travel time, and it narrows the choice of tutor severely at higher level.

Online tutoring is the right answer when the obstacle is subject knowledge at a level that is scarce nearby, when the timetable is tight and a short session is worth having, or when continuity through holidays and family travel matters.

Hybrid is what many Diploma families in New Gurgaon actually end up with, and it is less a compromise than a division of labour: the long conceptual session in person when a tutor is available, the frequent short reviews on screen.

Pick on the obstacle, not on the preference. Parents who choose the mode first and the tutor second usually end up changing one of them.

contentBlocks.heading: What no IB tutor in Sector 88, Gurugram should promise you

Some sentences you should not hear from a tutor, and what to make of them if you do.

A promised grade. Nobody can see a markscheme applied to a paper that has not been written, so a promise of a specific score is either ignorance or sales. The same goes for promised percentage improvements.

A claim of influence at a school. Internal assessments are marked by teachers and moderated externally, and any suggestion of a shortcut through that is a reason to end the conversation.

A refusal to discuss what is not working. If four weeks pass and the tutor cannot name the topics still failing, the diagnosis never happened.

An assurance that a home slot is confirmed before a named tutor has agreed to it. Availability in Sector 88 can be reviewed each term and depends on tutor schedules that shift.

The honest version is duller. A tutor can find the gap, plan the recovery and hold a student to a weekly routine. Whether that becomes a better grade depends heavily on how much work gets done when nobody is watching.

contentBlocks.heading: Arranging the first session from Sector 88, Gurugram

Starting is not complicated, and the first conversation carries no obligation.

Tell an advisor four things: the grade and programme, the subject and level exactly as the school writes it, what the last marked piece looked like, and when in the week the student is genuinely able to concentrate. That last one is the most commonly skipped and the most useful.

Say also whether you would prefer a tutor at home. It can be looked into for Sector 88 and the surrounding communities, and the answer depends on which tutors are covering this side of Gurugram that term. Online options are broader and can normally begin within days.

Bring the school report if you have a recent one. A tutor reads more from two lines of teacher comment than from a long description of what has been going wrong at home, and the diagnostic hour is better spent on the student than on catching up.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for a Diploma science, or is that just convenient for the tutor?
faqs.answer: It works well for theory and for internal assessment writing, and less well for practical technique. A tutor can pull apart an experimental design, question an uncertainty calculation and mark a draft against the criteria without being in the room. What cannot happen remotely is handing a student apparatus. Since the practical work itself is done at school under supervision, the gap is narrower than it sounds for most Diploma students. For Chemistry, ask whether the tutor writes on a tablet, because mechanisms drawn with a mouse are painful to follow.

faqs.question: We have patchy internet in the evening. Does that rule online sessions out?
faqs.answer: It complicates them rather than ruling them out. Audio matters more than video, so a session can continue with cameras off if bandwidth drops, and a tutor who shares written notes afterwards removes most of the risk of a lost explanation. Test the connection during a trial session at the same hour you plan to study, not at midday. If evenings are genuinely unreliable at your address, weekend morning slots or a home tutor for the subjects that allow it is the sensible fallback.

faqs.question: Can we start with online sessions and move to home tutoring later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a fair number of families in the newer Gurugram sectors do exactly that. Starting online gets teaching underway while a home slot is looked for, and the search continues in the background. Moving does usually mean a change of tutor, since the person teaching remotely may live nowhere near Sector 88. Plan the switch for a gap between assessment cycles rather than the middle of an internal assessment, or you will lose a fortnight to the handover.

faqs.question: Is there any support for the extended essay and internal assessments over the summer break?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the long break is when extended essay progress is most achievable, because nothing else is competing for the time. Useful summer work looks like narrowing the research question, testing whether the sources will sustain the word count, and producing a genuine first section rather than another plan. Internal assessment support depends on where the school sits in its cycle. Tutor availability during holidays varies since some travel, so schedules are agreed session by session rather than assumed for the whole break.

faqs.question: My child is in Grade 5. Would you still recommend a screen?
faqs.answer: Usually not as a first choice. A Grade 5 student benefits from someone in the room who can see the page, notice a guess and keep the session moving without a parent hovering. Online can work at that age with an unusually patient tutor and short sessions, and it beats no support at all when nobody suitable is available nearby. Home availability for Primary Years work in Sector 88 is generally easier to arrange than for higher level Diploma subjects, so ask for it directly.

faqs.question: How do we check that a tutor actually knows the IB and not just the subject?
faqs.answer: Ask questions only an IB teacher can answer well. How many cohorts have you taught at this level. What do you look for in the exploration or the practical write-up. Which command terms do students most often misread in this subject. What would you change about my child's last piece of marked work. Vague but enthusiastic answers are a bad sign. Screening covers documents and a markscheme exercise before a profile reaches you, but the first session is still your own check.

faqs.question: What does a session cost, and does the mode change the fee?
faqs.answer: Fees are set by the tutor and quoted before you start. Level and subject scarcity drive most of the difference, with higher level sciences and mathematics at the top and Primary Years support well below. Mode does affect the figure, since a tutor travelling to Sector 88 is committing an hour or more of driving on top of the teaching hour, and that is reflected in the quote. Ask specifically what is included between sessions, particularly marking of drafts, because practice varies.

faqs.question: Do you help students who moved to Gurugram from a different curriculum mid-year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common request in the newer sectors, where families arrive from other cities and other systems. The first month usually goes on the shift in assessment style rather than on content: criterion-related marking, command-term language, and the expectation that a student explains method rather than simply producing an answer. A student arriving from a board syllabus is often ahead on procedural mathematics and behind on writing about it. An honest tutor will say which gap is larger after the diagnostic session.

faqs.question: What if my child likes the tutor but the marks do not move?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor what she thinks is happening, and listen to whether the answer is specific. Marks lag method by several weeks, so a flat score after four sessions is not automatically a failure. What should be visible is different: work started earlier, questions attempted before help is requested, fewer marks lost on command terms. If none of that has moved either, and the tutor cannot name the remaining gaps by topic, change the tutor. Liking someone is not the same as learning from them.

contentBlocks.heading: What Parents in Sector 89 Gurugram Are Actually Deciding This Week
contentBlocks.body:
Most enquiries from Sector 89 arrive with a date attached. A Grade 11 unit test on Friday. An internal assessment draft due before the school closes for a break. A parent meeting where a subject teacher used the word inconsistent and then moved on to the next family.

So the first useful question is not which tutor is best. It is what has to change, and by when.

A week is enough to fix method: how a student reads a question, what they write first, whether they check anything before submitting. A month is enough to rebuild one topic properly, say vectors or acids and bases, along with the study habit sitting underneath it. A term is what a Diploma Programme student needs when the target is the May 2026 or November 2026 session and the gap is broad rather than local.

Families in the Godrej Air and Vatika India Next pockets of Sector 89 often start in the first category and discover within a fortnight that they are in the second. That is ordinary, and it is far better discovered in week one than in March.

IB Gram works backwards from that timeline. Tell an advisor the deadline, the grade, the subject and the level, and the shortlist gets built around the time available rather than around a generic weekly slot.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions, Online Sessions and the Sector 89 Commute Question
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring in Sector 89 is realistic when the tutor already lives or teaches nearby and the slot sits outside the heaviest movement through New Gurgaon. A specialist travelling in from Golf Course Road or DLF Phase 5 for a 7 pm session is also agreeing to a long return trip, and that agreement usually breaks quietly. It shows up as cancellations in week five, not as a complaint in week one.

Be honest about this at the start. It saves a wasted month.

Online sessions solve the geography problem and, more usefully, the specialist problem. Math AA HL at the harder end, Physics option material, or an Economics internal assessment that needs a genuine commentary reader are not evenly spread across the city. Going online widens the pool to tutors who actually teach at that level.

The hybrid pattern suits younger students here: one in-person session a week to hold routine and attention, one online session for revision, doubt-solving or a draft review. Parents of PYP and lower MYP children usually want the in-person anchor. DP students in the months before exams often move fully online, because what helps them is short and frequent contact rather than one fixed ninety-minute block.

Availability in either mode depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed before you commit.

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Subjects Send Sector 89 Gurugram Families Looking for a Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Math AA HL is the most common single request and it usually arrives late. A student who was comfortable through MYP meets proof, calculus and the pace of three papers, and the drop feels sudden to everyone except the teacher. Math AI HL brings a different failure: the modelling questions reward interpretation and written justification, which strong calculators tend to skip.

Physics and Chemistry requests split cleanly into two groups. Some students understand the idea and lose marks in the write-up. Others have a real gap in the mathematics underneath, and no amount of physics teaching helps until that is repaired. A first session should be able to say which group a student is in.

Economics normally arrives as an internal assessment problem: three commentaries, real articles, a hard word limit, and diagram work that has to be accurate rather than decorative. English A requests are usually about analysis and structure, not about reading ability.

Across all of them, command-term language does more damage than content. Explain, evaluate, justify, to what extent, comment on. Each carries a mark expectation, and a student who answers the topic instead of the command term loses marks already earned in understanding.

An IB maths tutor Sector 89 parents keep is usually the one who marks harshly in week one and explains exactly why.

It is a different tutoring geography from the older city. Distances are longer, roads are wider, and a tutor who says fifteen minutes is usually being optimistic about the leg home after 8 pm.

Tutors reaching this area either live within New Gurgaon or travel out from Sector 50, Sector 65, South City 1 and the DLF phases. Nirvana Country, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 turn up regularly in the schedules of tutors who take two or three families in this direction on the same evening. Worth knowing, because a tutor with a nearby cluster stays consistent far longer than one making a single long trip for one student.

For anyone comparing IB tuition near Sector 89 against options deeper inside the city, the honest position is this. Proximity matters a great deal for younger children and for routine. For a DP subject specialist, it matters much less than getting the right teacher.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Need Different Tutors, Not Just Different Timetables
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme runs from ages 3 to 12 and rewards inquiry rather than drill. A tutor who answers a PYP request with a worksheet pack has misread the job. What helps at this stage is reading stamina, number sense, and enough confidence to ask a question in class without waiting to be asked. Younger children in Sector 89 usually do better with shorter sessions held more often.

The Middle Years Programme covers ages 11 to 16 and is where most sudden grade drops appear. The content is not obviously harder. The assessment is. Four criteria per subject, each with its own descriptors, and a student can write a genuinely good answer against the wrong criterion and score badly for reasons nobody has explained. Tutoring at this stage is largely translation work.

The Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, carries the visible pressure: HL and SL choices, an internal assessment in every subject, the extended essay, TOK, and exam sessions to plan around. A DP tutor has to be able to read a draft against criteria and say what specifically to change in it.

IB Gram matches on programme and level rather than subject name, because a strong Grade 10 tutor is not automatically the right person for HL work.

MYP ages 11 to 16: criterion descriptors and command language
DP ages 16 to 19: HL and SL, IA, extended essay, TOK

Level is matched as carefully as subject

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sector 89 Gurugram Enquiry Becomes a Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is deliberately short.

One: you send the grade, programme, subject, level and the deadline that is worrying you. Two: an advisor asks a few follow-up questions, usually about what the school has said and what the last two pieces of marked work looked like. Three: IB Gram checks which screened tutors match that level and can realistically hold your preferred timing, at home in Sector 89 or online. Four: you receive a shortlist rather than a single name, with mode, availability and fee range stated. Five: an introductory session is arranged, and afterwards the tutor should be able to tell you where marks are actually being lost.

None of this guarantees an outcome. It is a process for cutting down the number of wrong starts.

Where it goes wrong is almost always step one. Parents give the subject without the level, or the grade without the deadline, and the shortlist comes back broader than it needed to be. A message reading Grade 11, Math AA HL, IA due in six weeks, evenings after 7 pm produces a far tighter match than one reading needs maths help.

contentBlocks.heading: What the First Four Weeks Should Show You
contentBlocks.body:
Ask for evidence early rather than waiting for a report card. Four weeks is long enough to see whether something is working and long enough that both sides have stopped being polite.

By the end of week one you should know what the tutor believes the real problem is, stated specifically. Not weak in algebra. Something closer to: she loses marks on multi-step questions because she does not write intermediate steps, so an early slip stays invisible until the final line.

By week two there should be a plan you can look at, with the order of topics and the school deadlines marked inside it.

By week four you should be reading marked work in the student's own handwriting that the tutor has annotated. If the only evidence of progress is the student saying sessions are going fine, that is not evidence.

The honest limitation: a student genuinely two years behind in the mathematics underneath a science subject will not show a transformed grade in a month, and any tutor implying otherwise is selling. What you can reasonably expect is a clear map of the gap and a realistic order for closing it.

If it is not working, say so early. Changing tutors in week three costs much less than changing in month three.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Reaches Your Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is about reducing risk. It is not a badge.

Identity is confirmed. Claimed qualifications and teaching background are reviewed against what the tutor says they can teach, at the level they say they can teach it. faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an internal assessment without doing the work for the student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can help the student understand the criteria, discuss whether a research question is actually answerable, review structure, point out where evidence is thin, and mark a draft against descriptors. A tutor must not write sections, supply data or produce the analysis. Schools check for this and IB academic honesty rules are strict. Good internal assessment support usually feels slower than students expect, because it pushes the thinking to happen before the writing rather than during it.

faqs.question: Our daughter says she understands everything in class but the grades do not show it. What is going on?
faqs.answer: This is among the most common patterns and it is usually a writing problem rather than an understanding problem. IB marks attach to command terms and criteria. A student who explains where the question said evaluate has answered a different question. Others hold the concept but omit intermediate steps, so an examiner cannot award method marks. A first session with recent marked work on the table normally identifies which of the two is happening, and it is fixable much faster than a genuine content gap.

November-session students in and around Sector 89 generally plan from the previous term. faqs.question: Which grades and programmes are covered on this page?
faqs.answer: Grade 1 to Grade 12, across the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19. faqs.question: How is IB tutoring different from tutoring for CBSE or ICSE?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps more than the assessment does. IB marks are awarded against published criteria and command terms, with internal assessments carrying real weight alongside the final papers. A tutor trained mainly on board exams will often teach correct content in a shape that scores poorly, because the expected form of an answer differs. This is why matching happens on programme and level rather than subject name alone, and why a strong Grade 10 board tutor is not automatically right for a DP student.

contentBlocks.heading: The 7.40 pm Problem in Sector 90 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
It is 7.40 pm on a Tuesday in Sector 90. The school bus reached the gate at 5.15. Since then there has been a snack, a shower, twenty minutes of arguing about the phone, and a Chemistry worksheet is still lying untouched on the table. The tutor slot is at 8. By 8.20 the student is somewhere between tired and defensive, and very little taught in that hour is going to stay.

This is the real constraint most families here are working against, and it is almost never the one written in the enquiry. The enquiry says needs help with Chemistry. The actual problem is that a school evening contains about ninety usable minutes and three separate demands on them.

Widen out from that one Tuesday and the requirement becomes clearer. An IB tutor in Sector 90 Gurugram has to fit the week a family has, not an ideal one. That may mean a 6.30 pm start instead of 8. It may mean two shorter sessions rather than one long block. It may mean shifting the demanding subject to Saturday morning, when a fifteen-year-old can still think, and keeping weekday time for doubt-solving and marked-work review.

Matching begins with the timetable, then moves to the tutor.

contentBlocks.heading: From First Message to Shortlist for a Sector 90 Gurugram Family
contentBlocks.body:
What happens after an enquiry is fairly mechanical, and knowing the steps helps you supply the right things at the start.

Step one is the brief: grade, programme, subject, level, and the three or four evening windows that genuinely work. Step two is a short conversation, usually about what the last report or teacher comment actually said, because that one sentence often contains the diagnosis. Step three is filtering the screened tutor pool against subject, level and those particular windows, for home sessions in Sector 90 or for online. Step four is a shortlist with mode, availability and fee range set against each name. Step five is an introductory session, after which you should have a plain description of where the marks are going.

The filter that removes most candidates is timing rather than ability. A parent who can offer only 8 pm on weekdays will see a much shorter list than one who can offer 6.30 pm or a Saturday morning. That is not a policy. It is arithmetic, because a tutor covering New Gurgaon fits two or three families into a single evening.

So when a shortlist comes back thin, the thing to loosen first is usually the hour, not the standard.

contentBlocks.heading: Chemistry, Economics and the Subjects That Break First
contentBlocks.body:
Chemistry is where evening fatigue does the most visible damage. Organic mechanisms and equilibrium reward sustained attention, and a student starting at 8.15 pm after a long day will follow the explanation, agree with all of it, and be unable to reproduce any of it on Saturday. Moving Chemistry earlier in the week often achieves more than changing tutor.

Economics fails in a different way. Students who talk fluently about the subject still lose marks because a diagram is unlabelled, a definition is loose, or the evaluation paragraph is opinion with no criteria behind it. The internal assessment commentaries carry a strict word limit that punishes anyone who writes first and edits afterwards.

Math AA HL and Math AI HL requests arrive steadily, mostly around the move into the Diploma Programme, and mostly about pace rather than ability. Physics enquiries tend to follow the first serious problem-solving paper. English A clusters around unseen analysis.

One pattern cuts across all of them. The mark is lost in the last two minutes of a question, not the first ten. Students stop once they have shown they understand and skip the part where the command term asked them to weigh something up. An IB science tutor Sector 90 parents keep is generally the one who reads answers like an examiner instead of a teacher.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP to DP: What Actually Changes at Each Stage
contentBlocks.body:
Parents ask for a tutor for a Grade 4 child and a Grade 12 child in almost the same words, but very little about the two jobs is alike.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages 3 to 12, the tutor is mainly building appetite. Sessions are short, a parent is often nearby, and progress shows up as a child reading for pleasure or volunteering an answer rather than as a number. Loading a nine-year-old with drill at this stage usually buys a worse Grade 6 later.

The Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16, turns everything into criteria. Students are assessed against four strands per subject, and a great deal of frustration comes from writing enthusiastically against the wrong one. Personal project support sits here as well. Parents step back around this point, which is right, and it also means you hear far less about what is going wrong.

The Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, is a project management problem as much as an academic one. Six subjects, internal assessments stacked across two years, an extended essay, TOK, and a fixed session at the end of it. The tutors who help most at this level protect the calendar as carefully as they teach the content.
items: PYP ages 3 to 12: short sessions, appetite before drill
MYP ages 11 to 16: four criteria per subject, personal project
DP ages 16 to 19: six subjects, stacked IA deadlines, EE and TOK

Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next are close enough together that a tutor with one family here will often take a second nearby, and that single fact is the best predictor of whether a weekly slot survives past a month.

contentBlocks.heading: In Person, Online or Split Across the Week in Sector 90 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Three arrangements come up here, and each has a case against it.

Home tutoring gives you presence. A tutor in the room notices the phone, the slouch, the exact moment attention leaves. For younger students that is most of the value. The case against: travel is unpaid time, slots cluster inside a narrow evening band, and a cancelled session is harder to move because the whole trip has to be rebuilt around it.

Online gives you the teacher you want rather than the teacher who lives nearby. Sessions can be shorter and more frequent, screens can be shared for past papers, and a fifteen-minute doubt-solving call the night before a test becomes possible. The case against: a distractible thirteen-year-old is harder to hold online, and a weak connection quietly eats ten minutes of every session.

Splitting the week suits most Diploma Programme students in this sector. One in-person session for teaching, one online for review, marking and questions. It also creates a mid-week checkpoint, which is exactly when a homework backlog is still small enough to fix.

contentBlocks.heading: The Checks Behind a Recommended Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Before a name reaches a parent, a few things get established.

Who the person is, verified rather than assumed. What they have actually taught, at which level, and for how long. Whether the subjects they list match the subjects they can discuss in detail when asked about a specific paper or a specific internal assessment criterion. A tutor comfortable with SL Chemistry may say plainly that they would rather not take HL, and that honesty is useful information instead of a disqualification.

Whether they have marked work against IB descriptors or only taught content. Those are separate skills. The second without the first tends to produce students who understand a subject and underperform in it.

Whether they can genuinely hold the slot they are agreeing to. A tutor with an unrealistic travel plan is a scheduling risk, and scheduling failure is the most common reason a match quietly ends.

References are reviewed where available.

What none of this settles is whether one particular student will work well with one particular adult. That question is answered in the first session and nowhere else. Any platform suggesting its screening removes that uncertainty is overstating what screening can do.
