contentBlocks.heading: Judging Progress Without Waiting for a Report Card
contentBlocks.body:
Report cards arrive far too late to work as feedback. Use three earlier signals instead.

The first is language. Listen to how the student describes a problem after three or four sessions. Vague talk about the chapter being hard should have sharpened into something specific, along the lines of the second part of the question wanting a justification rather than just a calculation. Precision in naming a difficulty usually comes before solving it.

The second is homework behaviour. Students who are getting somewhere begin attempting the hard question before the session instead of saving it for the tutor. That shift is visible from the kitchen table without asking anyone.

The third is the tutor's own record. Ask what was covered, what was marked, and what comes next. A tutor who cannot answer that in a minute is running sessions rather than a plan.

The part nobody enjoys hearing: a student who has disengaged from a subject entirely will need several weeks of repair before any of these signals appear, and adding a second weekly session at that point usually makes things worse. No tutor can promise a grade, and one who does should be declined on the spot.
items: Signal one: the student describes problems more precisely
Signal two: hard questions attempted before the session
Signal three: the tutor can state coverage, marking and next steps
Disengaged students need repair time before signals show
No grade, score or percentage promises at any point

faqs.question: Our son gets home from school after 5.30 pm. When is the best time for a tutoring session?
faqs.answer: For most secondary students, somewhere between 6 pm and 7.30 pm after a short break, with the demanding subjects placed earlier rather than later. Sessions starting after 8 pm work for revision and doubt-solving but are poor for teaching new material, because retention falls sharply once a student is tired. If the only free weekday hour is late, consider moving the hardest subject to a weekend morning and keeping the weekday slot for marked-work review. Tutors in this belt fill early evening slots first, so flexibility helps.

faqs.question: Is one long session a week better than two shorter ones?
faqs.answer: Two shorter sessions usually win, particularly for MYP and DP students. Spacing improves recall, and a mid-week checkpoint catches a homework backlog while it is still small. One long session makes sense when a tutor travels a long distance, or for extended essay and internal assessment work where a single stretch of concentrated writing is genuinely more productive. Weekly cost is broadly similar either way, since fees are set per hour rather than per visit. A good tutor will have a view on which pattern suits the subject.

faqs.question: How do fees work for IB tutoring around Sector 90?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the programme, the level, how scarce the subject is and whether the session is at home or online. HL Diploma subjects cost more than MYP or PYP support, because fewer tutors teach at that standard and preparation takes longer. Home visits carry the tutor's travel time inside the rate. A range is shared before booking so nothing is a surprise at month end. Ask about shorter review sessions as well, since a thirty or forty-five minute online check-in often costs less than a full hour.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP and the grades dropped without the work getting harder. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always the assessment rather than the content. MYP subjects are marked against four criteria with published descriptors, and a student can produce a thoughtful piece that scores low because it addresses the wrong criterion or misses the required form. Investigation tasks are where this shows most often. A tutor working from the actual task sheet and descriptors, rather than from the topic alone, can usually identify the pattern within a couple of sessions. It is fixable, and it does not mean the student has stopped understanding the subject.

faqs.question: Do you provide support for the extended essay and TOK?
faqs.answer: Yes, as mentoring rather than authorship. Extended essay support covers narrowing a research question to something answerable in four thousand words, planning the argument, checking whether the sources will carry the analysis, and reviewing drafts against the assessment criteria. TOK support usually focuses on building the essay and exhibition around knowledge questions instead of general opinion. The school supervisor stays the primary authority on both, and a tutor should work alongside that guidance rather than around it. IB academic honesty rules apply throughout.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, since it simplifies both scheduling and payment. Combinations such as Physics with Math AA, or Economics with Business Management, are common enough that some tutors handle both properly. Be careful with pairings that only look adjacent: strong Chemistry teaching does not imply strong Biology teaching at HL. If a tutor hedges when asked about the second subject at the level you need, take the hedge seriously and match separately. Two well-matched tutors beat one convenient one.

faqs.question: What if the student simply refuses to engage with the tutor?
faqs.answer: Say so early, and describe what the refusal looks like in practice, because the causes differ. Some students resist a specific adult, which a change of tutor solves. Some resist the subject because a gap has become embarrassing, which needs a tutor willing to go back several years without making a point of it. Some are exhausted, in which case adding hours makes things worse and adjusting the schedule helps more. An advisor can rework the match, though no arrangement works with a student who refuses to attend at all.

faqs.question: Do sessions continue during school holidays and exam leave?
faqs.answer: They can, and holidays are often the most productive weeks of the year, because the school workload disappears and a whole topic can be rebuilt properly. Many families switch to shorter, more frequent sessions during breaks. Exam leave is different: the useful work then is timed past papers and mark-scheme review rather than new teaching. Tutor availability during holidays varies, since tutors travel too, so confirm a few weeks ahead rather than assuming continuity. Online sessions tend to survive holiday travel better than home visits.

faqs.question: Which nearby areas do the same tutors also cover?
faqs.answer: Tutors serving this part of New Gurgaon commonly cover the surrounding sectors and the wider Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next cluster, and many travel in from Sector 50, Sector 65, South City 1, Nirvana Country or the DLF phases. Coverage depends on an individual tutor's week rather than on any fixed service boundary. Online tutoring runs across Gurugram and draws on tutors in Delhi, Noida and Faridabad as well. Ask for coverage to be confirmed for your exact address before planning around it.

contentBlocks.heading: What Parents Search For in Sector 91 Gurugram, and What Moves the Grade
contentBlocks.body:
The search box gets typed into with phrases like best IB tutor Sector 91 or IB tuition centre near Sector 91. Reasonable phrases. They simply describe the service rather than the problem.

What almost never gets typed is the sentence that would actually help. My son can do the physics but writes three lines where the mark scheme wants six. My daughter is fine until the question uses the word evaluate. Those are the sentences a tutor can act on in week one.

IB grades move when three things change. The student stops answering the topic and starts answering the command term. Work gets marked against criteria instead of being corrected for right and wrong. And the gap everyone has quietly ignored, usually sitting two years further back, gets named out loud.

None of that can begin until somebody has looked at recent marked work. So the most useful preparation before enquiring about IB tutors in Sector 91 Gurugram is to dig out the last two graded pieces from school and have them to hand.

What follows sets out what the matching process asks for, what each programme needs, and where home tutoring around Vatika India Next and Mapsko Casa Bella is realistic.

Marks move when command terms and criteria are addressed directly
Recent marked work is the fastest diagnostic available

contentBlocks.heading: Math AI HL, English A and the Gap Between Knowing and Scoring
contentBlocks.body:
Math AI HL rewards something students are rarely taught explicitly: explaining why a model suits a situation and where it stops suiting it. Capable students carry out the statistics correctly, present a clean graph, then lose interpretation marks because no sentence about limitations ever appears. Math AA HL has the opposite risk profile, where proof and algebraic fluency form the wall.

English A is the subject parents most often assume needs no tutoring, and it is among the most improvable. The analysis papers want a sustained argument about how meaning is constructed. A student who writes elegantly about what a text says, without touching how it works, can sit in the middle bands for two years without understanding why. The remedy is structural, and structure can be taught.

Physics and Chemistry both punish invisible reasoning. An answer that arrives at the right number by a route the examiner cannot follow forfeits method marks the student had genuinely earned.

Economics reduces to definitions, accurate diagrams and evaluation that weighs something rather than restating it.

Across the whole set, the diagnostic question is not what did you get. It is which criterion cost you the marks. A student who can answer that is already part of the way to fixing it, and any IB maths tutor Sector 91 families work with should be teaching them to answer it.
items: Math AI HL: modelling, interpretation, limitations
Math AA HL: proof and algebraic fluency
English A: how a text works, not only what it says
Physics and Chemistry: visible reasoning earns method marks
Economics: definitions, accurate diagrams, weighed evaluation

contentBlocks.heading: Same Family, Three Programmes, Three Different Requests
contentBlocks.body:
Take a household in Sector 91 with three children: one in Grade 3, one in Grade 9, one in Grade 12. Three requests, and almost nothing transfers between them.

The Grade 3 child sits in the Primary Years Programme, ages 3 to 12. The request is usually reading fluency or number confidence. What works is short sessions, a lot of talking, and resisting the urge to introduce formal exam habits five years early. Progress here is measured in willingness rather than in marks.

The Grade 9 child is in the Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16. The request tends to arrive after a report card with unfamiliar numbers on it. MYP grades come from criterion strands, and a student can work hard against the wrong descriptor for an entire term without anyone noticing. A useful tutor asks to see the task sheet, not just the textbook.

The Grade 12 child is deep in the Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, with internal assessments, an extended essay, TOK and a fixed exam session ahead. The request at this stage is often triage: which subject can realistically gain, which one needs protecting, and in what order to work.

Each of those points to a different tutor profile.
items: PYP ages 3 to 12: fluency, confidence, no early exam drilling
MYP ages 11 to 16: criterion strands and actual task sheets
DP ages 16 to 19: IA, extended essay, TOK and subject triage
One family often needs three different tutor profiles
Programme and level matched before subject preference

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between a Nearby Tutor and the Right Tutor in Sector 91
contentBlocks.body:
There is a real trade-off here and it deserves naming rather than smoothing over.

A tutor living fifteen minutes away can be at your door on a Sunday when a draft is due Monday. That responsiveness is genuine value, particularly for MYP students who need someone physically present to stop the drift. Home tutoring around Vatika India Next, Mapsko Casa Bella, Godrej Air and Godrej Summit is workable when tutor schedules line up, and can be reviewed for a specific address.

A tutor who teaches HL Physics every week to six students, and happens to be sitting in Delhi or Noida, brings something else. They know which past-paper questions are worth an evening and which are not. Online is how you reach that person.

For a Diploma Programme student inside eight months of an exam session, subject depth usually wins. For a Grade 6 student who needs the habit of sitting down at a table, presence usually wins.

The hybrid arrangement takes some of each, and most families here arrive there eventually. One in-person session, one online. Availability in either mode depends on tutor schedules and shifts through the year, so it is better asked about than assumed.
items: Nearby tutors: responsiveness and physical presence
Online tutors: depth at HL and better past-paper judgement
DP students usually gain more from subject depth
Younger students usually gain more from presence
Hybrid arrangements are where most families settle

contentBlocks.body:
Most first messages say some version of the same thing: needs help, falling behind, exams coming. The process exists to convert that into something a tutor can work with.

An advisor asks for four specifics. The grade and programme. The subject and, for Diploma Programme students, whether it is HL or SL. What the school has said, quoted rather than paraphrased wherever possible. And the deadline, mock week or exam session the family is working towards.

Those four turn a vague request into a filter. IB Gram then checks the screened tutor pool for people who teach that subject at that level and can hold a slot that genuinely works, at home in Sector 91 or online. You receive several options rather than one name, each carrying the mode, the availability and a fee range.

An introductory session follows, and its purpose is diagnostic. By the end of it a tutor should be able to describe the problem in terms specific enough that you could repeat them to the school.

If the shortlist does not suit, say why and it gets rebuilt. Wrong first matches happen. Correcting them in week one costs almost nothing.

contentBlocks.heading: Questions Asked of a Tutor Before You Ever Meet Them
contentBlocks.body:
Screening here is a set of questions rather than a certificate.

Can you show us who you are, and does the documentation match the name on the profile. What have you taught, at which level, over what period. Take one internal assessment criterion in your subject and explain what separates a middle band from a top band. Which past papers do you use with students, and why those. Describe a student who did not improve with you, and what you would do differently now.

That last question is the most informative of the set. A tutor who has never had a student fail to improve is either very new or not being straight with you, and either answer tells you something worth knowing.

Qualifications and prior teaching are reviewed. References are taken up where they exist. Subject claims are matched to level, because HL and SL are treated as different jobs here rather than as the same subject at two speeds.

What screening cannot do is guarantee a result, and IB Gram does not claim otherwise. There are no promised grades, no percentages, no numbers attached to outcomes. There is a filtered pool, a stated process, and a first session so you can judge for yourself.

contentBlocks.heading: The Difference Between a Busy Tutor and a Useful One
contentBlocks.body:
Sessions can run for months and look productive while nothing shifts. The pattern is a comfortable one: the tutor explains, the student nods, homework gets corrected, everybody leaves satisfied. Explanation is pleasant to receive and remarkably easy to forget.

A useful session looks less comfortable. The student does the work while the tutor watches, gets stuck, and is left stuck slightly longer than feels kind. Errors are diagnosed out loud rather than quietly fixed. Something gets written under timed conditions at least occasionally, because working speed is a separate skill from understanding and it only develops under some pressure.

Ask for one specific thing at the end of the first month: a piece of the student's own work, marked by the tutor against criteria, with comments a parent can actually read. Not a progress message. Marked work.

And accept the honest limits. Beginning Diploma Programme support in the final term narrows what is possible to exam technique and damage control, which has value but is not a rebuilt subject. Tutoring does not fix attendance, sleep, or a student who does not want to be there. Where one of those is the real issue, an extra weekly hour is an expensive way to avoid the conversation.
items: Explanation feels productive and is easily forgotten
The student should be doing the work during the session
Occasional timed practice, since working speed is its own skill

faqs.question: We do not know which subject is really the problem. Can a tutor help work that out?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a sensible place to start. Bring the last term's marked work across all subjects, and a first conversation can usually identify whether the issue sits in one subject, in a shared skill such as written justification, or in workload management across six Diploma Programme subjects. Sometimes the subject a parent worries about is not the one at risk. An advisor can arrange a diagnostic session in whichever subject looks weakest, and a tutor's read after that hour is far more reliable than a guess made beforehand.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an IB student usually need?
faqs.answer: For a single subject with a specific gap, one session a week plus independent practice is often enough. Two suit a Diploma Programme student rebuilding a subject from some way back, or anyone inside three months of an exam session. More than two hours weekly in one subject rarely helps unless the student is doing very little alone, and at that point the problem is study habit rather than teaching time. Start lower than feels comfortable and increase only if the evidence supports it.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely effective for practical subjects like Physics and Chemistry?
faqs.answer: For the theory, problem-solving and past-paper work that carry most of the marks, yes. Screen sharing suits worked solutions, and annotating a student's own scanned answer works better than either side expects. The real limitation is practical laboratory skill, which cannot be taught remotely and stays with the school. Internal assessment work sits in between: a tutor can help with variables, method design, uncertainties and the write-up, while the experiment itself belongs in the school laboratory under the teacher's supervision.

faqs.question: What should we ask a tutor in the first conversation?
faqs.answer: Ask what they think the actual problem is, and listen for specificity rather than reassurance. Ask how they will know in four weeks whether it is working. Ask which internal assessment criteria they have marked against, if the student is in MYP or DP. Ask about availability across the whole term and not just next week, because consistency matters more than a strong start. A tutor comfortable saying they are unsure about something is usually more dependable than one confident about everything.

faqs.question: Our child starts the Diploma Programme next year. Is it too early to arrange a tutor?
faqs.answer: No, and the months just before the Diploma Programme begins are one of the more useful windows. The transition from MYP catches many students out, especially in mathematics, where the assumed algebraic fluency is higher than the previous year demanded. A few weeks of targeted work over a break can close the gap before it appears in a grade. Subject choice conversations belong here too, since taking a subject at HL because it seemed interesting in Grade 10 is a common and costly decision.

faqs.question: Do tutors follow the school syllabus or use their own material?
faqs.answer: They should work from the school's sequence and task sheets, then supplement where it helps. A tutor running an entirely separate curriculum creates a second workload for a student who already has one, and it makes conversations with school teachers harder than they need to be. Where a school runs ahead of or behind a tutor's preferred order, the school wins, because that is what the student is assessed on next. Past-paper and criterion practice are additions rather than replacements.

faqs.question: What happens if we need to pause sessions for a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Tell the tutor as early as possible, because a slot held open is a slot they are not offering to anyone else. Short pauses around exam leave, family travel or illness are normal and rarely cause difficulty. mainEntity.name: We do not know which subject is really the problem. Can a tutor help work that out?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is a sensible place to start. Bring the last term's marked work across all subjects, and a first conversation can usually identify whether the issue sits in one subject, in a shared skill such as written justification, or in workload management across six Diploma Programme subjects. Sometimes the subject a parent worries about is not the one at risk. An advisor can arrange a diagnostic session in whichever subject looks weakest, and a tutor's read after that hour is far more reliable than a guess made beforehand.

mainEntity.name: How many sessions a week does an IB student usually need?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a single subject with a specific gap, one session a week plus independent practice is often enough. Two suit a Diploma Programme student rebuilding a subject from some way back, or anyone inside three months of an exam session. More than two hours weekly in one subject rarely helps unless the student is doing very little alone, and at that point the problem is study habit rather than teaching time. Start lower than feels comfortable and increase only if the evidence supports it.

mainEntity.name: Is online tutoring genuinely effective for practical subjects like Physics and Chemistry?

acceptedAnswer.text: For the theory, problem-solving and past-paper work that carry most of the marks, yes. Screen sharing suits worked solutions, and annotating a student's own scanned answer works better than either side expects. The real limitation is practical laboratory skill, which cannot be taught remotely and stays with the school. Internal assessment work sits in between: a tutor can help with variables, method design, uncertainties and the write-up, while the experiment itself belongs in the school laboratory under the teacher's supervision.

mainEntity.name: What should we ask a tutor in the first conversation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask what they think the actual problem is, and listen for specificity rather than reassurance. Ask how they will know in four weeks whether it is working. Ask which internal assessment criteria they have marked against, if the student is in MYP or DP. Ask about availability across the whole term and not just next week, because consistency matters more than a strong start. A tutor comfortable saying they are unsure about something is usually more dependable than one confident about everything.

mainEntity.name: Our child starts the Diploma Programme next year. Is it too early to arrange a tutor?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and the months just before the Diploma Programme begins are one of the more useful windows. The transition from MYP catches many students out, especially in mathematics, where the assumed algebraic fluency is higher than the previous year demanded. A few weeks of targeted work over a break can close the gap before it appears in a grade. Subject choice conversations belong here too, since taking a subject at HL because it seemed interesting in Grade 10 is a common and costly decision.

mainEntity.name: Do tutors follow the school syllabus or use their own material?

acceptedAnswer.text: They should work from the school's sequence and task sheets, then supplement where it helps. A tutor running an entirely separate curriculum creates a second workload for a student who already has one, and it makes conversations with school teachers harder than they need to be. Where a school runs ahead of or behind a tutor's preferred order, the school wins, because that is what the student is assessed on next. Past-paper and criterion practice are additions rather than replacements.

introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 92 Gurugram are available for home sessions inside the New Gurgaon societies and online across the rest of the city, covering Grade 1 to Grade 12 across the Primary Years Programme, Middle Years Programme and Diploma Programme. IB Gram takes your child's year group, subject levels and the next three deadlines on the school calendar, then shortlists tutors whose teaching experience fits that specific combination. Start dates depend on tutor availability and the time slot you need.

contentBlocks.heading: What the IB Calendar Looks Like from Sector 92, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Most families start looking for a tutor about three weeks after the term calendar has already made the decision for them. A Diploma student picks up an internal assessment brief in August, sits mocks in late January or February, and submits final coursework well before the May session papers begin. An MYP student has criterion-marked tasks landing every few weeks from the first month of school. Work backwards from those dates and the useful window is narrower than it looks.

So the honest answer to how late is too late depends entirely on what is due. Six weeks before a Paper 1 sitting, a tutor can rebuild exam technique, drill command terms and correct a handful of errors that keep repeating. Six weeks before an IA deadline, a tutor can help structure and sharpen a piece the student has already begun, but cannot start an investigation from nothing unless the student is willing to work at speed. Two weeks out from either, expect triage rather than teaching.

Parents searching for IB tutors in Sector 92 Gurugram usually arrive at one of three moments: a report card that surprised them, a subject the student has quietly stopped attempting, or a DP year that has started and already feels unmanageable. Each of those calls for a different first session. Most of the intake conversation is spent working out which one you are actually in.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Support for Sector 92 Gurugram Families
contentBlocks.body:
The three programmes run on different clocks, and that changes what a tutor is for.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, there is no external exam pressure, so the calendar argument barely applies. What matters is reading fluency, number sense and the habit of asking a question then chasing the answer. A capable PYP tutor works in short sessions, borrows the unit of inquiry the school is already running, and resists handing over worksheet stacks because worksheets are the easiest thing to show a parent at the end of an hour.

The Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, is where most parents here first feel out of their depth. Marks arrive against criteria rather than as a percentage, and a student can be genuinely strong on subject knowledge while losing marks on communication or on critical thinking. Tutoring at this stage is often less about content and more about reading the criterion descriptor properly and rewriting an answer to meet it.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, carries the tightest calendar of the three. Six subjects, HL and SL splits, an internal assessment in nearly every one, with the Extended Essay and TOK sitting on top. A DP tutor is managing a queue rather than marching through a syllabus. Deciding which deadline gets this week's session is half the job, and that call should be made with the parent informed.
items: PYP: inquiry-led reading, numeracy and question-building
MYP: criterion descriptors, task rewrites, concept transfer
DP: HL and SL subject depth, IA direction, EE mentoring, TOK

Past-paper revision built around the school's own mock dates

contentBlocks.heading: Where IB Tutors Travel Around Sector 92 and New Gurgaon
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 92 sits in the newer residential belt of New Gurgaon, and the enquiries reaching us cluster around Vatika India Next, Mapsko Casa Bella, Godrej Air and Godrej Summit. Inside that cluster, travel is trivial. A tutor already teaching a family in one of those societies can often take a second slot in the next tower with almost no dead time, which is why the first name suggested to you sometimes depends on who is already teaching in your building.

Beyond the cluster it gets harder, and this is worth knowing before you set expectations. A large share of experienced IB tutors in Gurugram are based nearer Golf Course Road, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, Sector 50, Sector 65, South City 1 and Nirvana Country. Coming out to Sector 92 on a weekday evening means a long run against the traffic flow. Some will do it for a two-hour block, or for two sessions stacked the same evening. Many will not do it twice a week for a single student.

That constraint is real and pretending otherwise wastes your time. Two arrangements usually fix it. Book the weekend slot at home and run the mid-week session online. Or accept a later start so the tutor travels after the worst of the evening crush. Home tutoring is subject to tutor schedules, and flexibility on mode buys you a better tutor than insisting on home visits alone.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Requests That Come Up Most Often Around Sector 92
contentBlocks.body:
Math AA HL generates the highest volume of requests, and usually not because the student is weak. AA HL asks for proof, algebraic fluency and comfort with abstraction, so a student who coasted through MYP on pattern recognition hits a wall somewhere in the first year. Math AI HL is a different problem. The statistics and modelling content reads as approachable, then the exploration and Paper 3 start demanding judgement about which tool fits which situation.

Physics and Chemistry requests cluster around two dates: the internal assessment and the extended-response section of Paper 2. On the IA, the usual failure is a research question so broad that no amount of data can support a conclusion. A tutor is most useful before data collection, not after, which is precisely the opposite of when most families call.

Economics attracts late requests because the content reads easily and the marks do not follow. Fifteen-mark evaluation answers need a diagram, a real-world link and a judgement with a condition attached to it. That is a trainable skill and it responds fast to focused feedback.

English A support tends to be about the individual oral and the unseen text paper. Students who read widely still lose marks by summarising where they should be analysing.

Across every one of these, the first job is locating where marks are actually leaking. It is rarely where the student believes.
items: Math AA HL: proof, algebraic fluency, abstraction
Math AI HL: modelling judgement, exploration design, Paper 3
Physics and Chemistry: IA research question, Paper 2 long answers
Economics: evaluation structure and real-world application
English A: individual oral, unseen commentary, analysis over summary

contentBlocks.heading: Schools Sector 92 Gurugram Students Commonly Travel To
contentBlocks.body:
Families in these sectors send children a fair distance for IB. Pathways World School in the wider Gurugram region, GD Goenka World School out towards Sohna Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and Lancers International School near Golf Course Road all appear regularly in enquiries from this part of the city. Those are long bus days, and the practical consequence shows up in scheduling more than anywhere else.

A student leaving at seven in the morning and reaching home after four thirty has a shorter evening than a family living close to school. Booking a tutor at five o'clock sounds efficient and often produces a tired hour. Six thirty or seven, after food and a break, tends to hold attention better even though it looks late on paper.

Schools also differ in how they run internal deadlines. Some issue IA briefs early with staggered draft dates. Others compress everything into a shorter run. A tutor who has worked with students from your child's school will usually know that rhythm and plan around it, though we do not treat school familiarity as a substitute for subject depth.

IB Gram operates independently. We are not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to any of the schools named above, and naming them here only reflects where students in this area study.

contentBlocks.heading: How a Tutor Request from Sector 92 Gurugram Is Handled
contentBlocks.body:
The process runs in four steps, and none of them are automated guesswork.

One: the intake call. We ask for year group, programme, exact subject levels, the school, the next three deadlines and what the last two report cards said. A parent describing the problem as maths is fine; the advisor's job is to narrow that to a topic band and a skill.

Two: the shortlist. Tutors are filtered on subject and level first, then on the kind of support needed. Someone excellent at DP exam technique is not automatically the right person for an Extended Essay, and an IA mentor is not automatically good at rebuilding shaky algebra from two years earlier. Location and available slots come in at this point, which is where Sector 92 addresses narrow the field for home sessions.

Three: the first session. It runs as a diagnostic. The tutor works through recent school work, finds where the marks are going, and ends with a written note to the parent naming a starting point and a rough sequence.

Four: the review. After roughly four sessions we ask both sides what is working. Tutor changes at this stage are normal and carry no penalty, because a mismatch found early costs far less than one tolerated for a term.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online and Hybrid Sessions Through the Term
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring in this part of New Gurgaon works well for younger students and for anyone who needs a person physically present to hold attention. A PYP or early MYP child benefits from the desk, the routine and the absence of a screen. Availability depends on tutor schedules, and the pool is genuinely smaller here than nearer the older sectors.

Online is stronger than most parents expect for DP work. Shared documents, annotated past papers, screen-recorded worked solutions the student can replay at midnight before a test, and a specialist who might be teaching from another city entirely. For a rare HL combination or urgent late-evening revision, online usually produces the better match.

But online is worse in two situations, and both matter. A student who has already disengaged will drift on a call in a way they cannot in a room. And handwriting-heavy subjects lose something when the tutor cannot watch the working develop in real time, unless the family sets up a tablet or a second camera on the page.

Hybrid is what most DP families settle into by the second month. One home session for the anchor subject, one online session for a second subject or for pre-exam revision. It is not a compromise so much as a recognition that the two formats are good at different things.
items: Home sessions: routine, attention, better for PYP and early MYP
Online: specialist reach, replayable worked solutions, late slots
Hybrid: one at home, one online, common by the second month
Handwriting-heavy subjects need a second camera or tablet online
Disengaged students generally need a person in the room first

contentBlocks.heading: What the First Four Weeks Should Look Like
contentBlocks.body:
Judge tutoring on process before you judge it on marks, because marks lag by a full assessment cycle and sometimes longer.

By the end of week one you should have a written diagnostic: which topics are shaky, which skill is costing the most marks, and what the tutor plans to do about it in what order. If nobody can tell you that after a session, something is wrong with the match rather than the child.

By week two, the student should be able to explain what they worked on without being prompted. This sounds small. It is the clearest early signal available, and it separates a session that taught something from a session that was merely pleasant.

By week three or four, expect a visible change in behaviour rather than in grades. Attempting the harder question instead of skipping it. Starting an assignment three days out rather than the night before. Asking the tutor a question that has been sitting unasked since last term.

We do not promise grade outcomes and will not attach a number to improvement, because no honest platform can. What we do commit to is a clear starting plan, regular parent updates, and a tutor change if the working relationship is not producing anything by the review point.
items: Week 1: written diagnostic naming topics and skills
Week 2: student can describe the session unprompted
Weeks 3 to 4: behaviour shifts before grades do
Regular written updates to the parent
No grade promises, no improvement percentages

contentBlocks.heading: Checks Completed Before a Tutor Is Shortlisted
contentBlocks.body:
Screening covers four areas, and every tutor recommended to a Sector 92 family has been through all of them.

Identity and documents come first. Government photo identification, current address, and degree or teaching certificates in the subject being claimed. A qualification in a neighbouring discipline does not clear someone to teach Chemistry HL.

Subject and level evidence comes second. Teaching Math AI SL and teaching Math AA HL are separate claims and are checked separately. For DP tutors we look for recent work with the current subject guides, familiarity with command terms, and direct experience of internal assessment criteria rather than a general statement about having taught the IB.

Teaching evaluation is third. Tutors work through a short subject task and explain their approach to a student who has understood a concept but keeps losing marks on the write-up. How someone explains matters as much as what they know, and this stage removes more applicants than the paperwork does.

Ongoing feedback is fourth. Parent reports, session notes and continuation patterns are reviewed. A tutor whose students consistently stop after a few weeks stops receiving recommendations regardless of the qualifications on file.
items: Government photo ID and address confirmation
Degree and teaching certificates checked against the subject claimed
Level-specific evidence, HL and SL treated separately
Short teaching evaluation task with an explanation review
Continuing review of parent feedback and continuation patterns

contentBlocks.heading: Booking IB Tutors in Sector 92 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the calendar. Before you call, note your child's year group, the exact subject levels, and the next two or three dates on the school's assessment schedule. Bring the most recent report or a marked piece of work if one is handy. That single sheet of information cuts the intake call roughly in half and makes the shortlist noticeably more accurate.

The advisor call takes fifteen to twenty minutes. You will be asked what has already been tried, because a family that has been through two tutors needs a different suggestion from a family starting fresh. We then come back with a small shortlist rather than a long directory, with slots, mode and fee range attached to each option. Fees vary by level and by whether sessions run at home or online, and the advisor will give you the range for your case before any commitment.

One honest note to close on. If the exam session is very close and the gap is a whole year of foundations, tutoring will help but it will not rewrite the outcome, and we will say so on the call rather than after you have paid for a month.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the May 2026 session should we start tutoring?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma student aiming at the May 2026 papers, starting by the previous August or September gives a tutor room to cover content gaps and exam technique without competing against internal assessment deadlines. Starting in January still works, though the plan shifts to past papers, command-term precision and repairing the two or three topics costing the most marks. From March onward the work is almost entirely revision strategy. There is no cut-off after which help becomes pointless, but the later you begin, the more you are choosing what to leave out.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting a tutor in the middle of DP Year 2?
faqs.answer: Yes, with realistic aims. Mid Year 2 is a common starting point because mock results have just landed and the picture is suddenly concrete. A tutor at this stage prioritises two questions: which subject shows the widest gap between current performance and what the student needs, and which of those fixes are quickest. Coursework already submitted cannot be reworked, so attention goes to exam papers and to any internal assessment still open. Expect the tutor to decline covering all six subjects. Two, occasionally three, is the honest limit for the time remaining.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an internal assessment the school has already marked once?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help the student interpret the feedback, work out which criterion lost marks and plan a stronger revision, within whatever redraft policy the school allows. What a tutor will not do is write or rewrite the work. IB internal assessment carries an authenticity requirement, and a submitted piece that is not the student's own puts the whole diploma at risk. The useful contribution is teaching the student to read the criterion descriptor and judge their own draft against it, which is a skill they then reuse in every other subject.

faqs.question: Do you have tutors who can come to Sector 92 in the evening?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the day, the subject and where the tutor is starting from. Tutors already teaching inside Vatika India Next, Godrej Air, Godrej Summit or Mapsko Casa Bella can usually add a nearby slot easily. Tutors based around Golf Course Road or the DLF phases face a long evening drive out to New Gurgaon and often prefer weekends or a later start. Home tutoring here is genuinely subject to tutor schedules, so the advisor will tell you what exists for your subject and slot rather than promising coverage first.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the first session?
faqs.answer: The first session runs as a diagnostic, not a lesson from the front of a textbook. The tutor asks the student to work through recent school material, watches where the process breaks, and probes whether the issue is missing content, weak technique or a misreading of what the question wanted. Roughly the last ten minutes go to agreeing a starting point with the student. Afterwards you receive a short written note naming the gaps found and the intended sequence of topics. If that note never arrives, raise it with the advisor immediately.

faqs.question: How are fees decided and what changes them?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by programme level, subject rarity and mode. Diploma HL sciences and Math AA HL sit at the higher end because the pool of tutors who can teach them properly is small. PYP and MYP support sits lower. Home sessions in New Gurgaon carry a premium over online, mostly reflecting travel time rather than teaching quality. The advisor gives you a range for your specific combination before any tutor is introduced. We do not publish a single citywide rate because it would be misleading for most of the subjects families actually ask about.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not the right fit after two or three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell the advisor and ask for a change. This is a normal request and nobody treats it as a complaint. Fit problems are usually about pace or communication style rather than competence: a tutor who explains in a way that suits one student can lose another entirely. It helps enormously if you say what specifically was not working, because that detail shapes the replacement suggestion. A mismatch identified in week two costs a fortnight. The same mismatch tolerated out of politeness costs a term.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP and grades are slipping across several subjects at once. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Slipping across subjects simultaneously usually points at a shared skill rather than several separate content gaps. The common culprits are written communication, poor reading of criterion descriptors, and time management as tasks stack up. Our usual advice is to start with one subject where the student still has some confidence, fix the approach there, then transfer it. Hiring three tutors at once tends to overload a fourteen-year-old and makes it impossible to tell what helped. Start narrow, review after a month, expand only if the pattern holds.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: It works well, provided the setup is right. The student needs a tablet or a document camera pointed at the page so the tutor can watch the working develop rather than only seeing a finished answer. With that in place, online has real advantages for AA HL: the tutor annotates past-paper questions live, saves the annotated file, and records a worked solution the student replays before a test. It also opens up specialists who live nowhere near New Gurgaon. Without a way to see the working, though, online AA HL sessions turn into guesswork.

Starting in January still works, though the plan shifts to past papers, command-term precision and repairing the two or three topics costing the most marks. From March onward the work is almost entirely revision strategy. There is no cut-off after which help becomes pointless, but the later you begin, the more you are choosing what to leave out.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth starting a tutor in the middle of DP Year 2?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with realistic aims. Mid Year 2 is a common starting point because mock results have just landed and the picture is suddenly concrete. A tutor at this stage prioritises two questions: which subject shows the widest gap between current performance and what the student needs, and which of those fixes are quickest. Coursework already submitted cannot be reworked, so attention goes to exam papers and to any internal assessment still open. Expect the tutor to decline covering all six subjects. Two, occasionally three, is the honest limit for the time remaining.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help with an internal assessment the school has already marked once?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tutor can help the student interpret the feedback, work out which criterion lost marks and plan a stronger revision, within whatever redraft policy the school allows. What a tutor will not do is write or rewrite the work. IB internal assessment carries an authenticity requirement, and a submitted piece that is not the student's own puts the whole diploma at risk. The useful contribution is teaching the student to read the criterion descriptor and judge their own draft against it, which is a skill they then reuse in every other subject.

mainEntity.name: Do you have tutors who can come to Sector 92 in the evening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, and it depends on the day, the subject and where the tutor is starting from. Tutors already teaching inside Vatika India Next, Godrej Air, Godrej Summit or Mapsko Casa Bella can usually add a nearby slot easily. Tutors based around Golf Course Road or the DLF phases face a long evening drive out to New Gurgaon and often prefer weekends or a later start. Home tutoring here is genuinely subject to tutor schedules, so the advisor will tell you what exists for your subject and slot rather than promising coverage first.

mainEntity.name: What actually happens in the first session?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first session runs as a diagnostic, not a lesson from the front of a textbook. The tutor asks the student to work through recent school material, watches where the process breaks, and probes whether the issue is missing content, weak technique or a misreading of what the question wanted. Roughly the last ten minutes go to agreeing a starting point with the student. Afterwards you receive a short written note naming the gaps found and the intended sequence of topics. If that note never arrives, raise it with the advisor immediately.

mainEntity.name: How are fees decided and what changes them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fees vary by programme level, subject rarity and mode. Diploma HL sciences and Math AA HL sit at the higher end because the pool of tutors who can teach them properly is small. PYP and MYP support sits lower. Home sessions in New Gurgaon carry a premium over online, mostly reflecting travel time rather than teaching quality. The advisor gives you a range for your specific combination before any tutor is introduced. We do not publish a single citywide rate because it would be misleading for most of the subjects families actually ask about.

mainEntity.name: What if the tutor is not the right fit after two or three sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell the advisor and ask for a change. This is a normal request and nobody treats it as a complaint. Fit problems are usually about pace or communication style rather than competence: a tutor who explains in a way that suits one student can lose another entirely. It helps enormously if you say what specifically was not working, because that detail shapes the replacement suggestion. A mismatch identified in week two costs a fortnight. The same mismatch tolerated out of politeness costs a term.

mainEntity.name: My child is in MYP and grades are slipping across several subjects at once. Where do we start?

acceptedAnswer.text: Slipping across subjects simultaneously usually points at a shared skill rather than several separate content gaps. The common culprits are written communication, poor reading of criterion descriptors, and time management as tasks stack up. Our usual advice is to start with one subject where the student still has some confidence, fix the approach there, then transfer it. Hiring three tutors at once tends to overload a fourteen-year-old and makes it impossible to tell what helped. Start narrow, review after a month, expand only if the pattern holds.

mainEntity.name: Does online tutoring really work for Math AA HL?

acceptedAnswer.text: It works well, provided the setup is right. The student needs a tablet or a document camera pointed at the page so the tutor can watch the working develop rather than only seeing a finished answer. With that in place, online has real advantages for AA HL: the tutor annotates past-paper questions live, saves the annotated file, and records a worked solution the student replays before a test. It also opens up specialists who live nowhere near New Gurgaon. Without a way to see the working, though, online AA HL sessions turn into guesswork.

contentBlocks.heading: A Teacher's Job and a Tutor's Job Are Not the Same in Sector 93, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Confusing those two roles is the single most common reason private tutoring disappoints a family.

An IB classroom teacher is responsible for a subject guide, a room of twenty-odd students, a set of internal deadlines and a moderation process at the end of it. They plan for the middle of the room. They cannot halt a unit because one student never properly understood logarithms two years ago, and they cannot hand over answers, since the work has to be authentically the student's own. None of that is a failing. It is the shape of the job.

A tutor has one student and no syllabus obligation. That freedom is the entire point. A tutor can spend forty minutes on one misconception, go back two chapters or two years, and stay there until the student reproduces the reasoning unaided. A tutor also watches the student work, which a teacher rarely has time for: the teacher sees the finished script, the tutor sees the pencil hesitate.

Parents looking for IB tutors in Sector 93 Gurugram often phrase the request as extra classes. Targeted repair plus supervised practice is the more useful phrasing. Extra classes repeat what already failed to land once.

And where the school teacher is doing the job well, the tutor's brief narrows: fewer topics, more depth, sharper questions for the student to take back into class.

Tutoring works backwards from where marks are lost
Supervised practice, not a second delivery of the same lesson
Authenticity rules mean the student writes their own coursework

contentBlocks.heading: One-to-One at Home Versus One-to-One on a Screen
contentBlocks.body:
The mode question is really a question about what the tutor can observe.

In a room, a tutor sees everything: the page, the pauses, the moment a student writes down a formula they do not trust. Body language carries information that no video call reproduces. For a younger child, or for a teenager who has stopped believing they can do the subject, that presence usually decides whether the hour works. Home sessions in this sector depend on tutor schedules, so availability varies by subject and by day.

On a screen, the tutor loses some of that and gains other things. Annotation on a shared past paper. A recording the student replays at eleven at night before a test. Access to someone who teaches Math AA HL properly but lives in another city. For Diploma students who already know how to sit down and work, online frequently produces the better teacher, not merely the more convenient one.

The honest weakness of online is supervision. A student who drifts will drift more easily on a call. There is a workable fix: ask the tutor to run the session as work-then-check rather than talk-then-set-homework, so the practice happens while someone is watching.

Many families here run one mode for the harder subject and the other for the second, and adjust the balance as exams approach.
items: In-person: reads hesitation, posture, and unspoken confusion
Online: live annotation, replayable recordings, wider tutor reach
Work-then-check format keeps online sessions supervised
Younger and disengaged students usually need a person present
Mode balance shifts as the exam session approaches

contentBlocks.heading: Subjects Where Sector 93 Gurugram Students Ask for a Second Explainer
contentBlocks.body:
Requests concentrate in a handful of places, and each one has a recognisable failure pattern.

Math AA HL comes up constantly. The classroom moves at the pace of a plan, and calculus arrives whether or not the algebra underneath it is secure. A tutor can stop and rebuild that foundation, which is the one thing the teacher cannot do for a single student mid-unit. Math AI HL fails differently: the arithmetic is manageable and the difficulty sits in choosing a model and defending the choice.

Physics students usually understand the concept and lose marks in the write-up, particularly on uncertainty treatment and on explaining rather than describing. Chemistry sits close behind, with organic mechanisms and equilibrium the two topics that most often need a slower second pass.

Economics answers tend to be full of correct content arranged in a way that scores badly. The fix is structural: definition, diagram, application to a named situation, then evaluation that actually weighs something.

English A is the subject where the gap between a confident speaker and a high-scoring one is widest. The individual oral rewards a tight thesis about a global issue, not enthusiasm about the text.

A tutor should be able to name the failure pattern by the end of session two. If they cannot, ask why.
items: Math AA HL: rebuilding algebra under new calculus content
Math AI HL: model selection and justification
Physics: uncertainty handling, explain versus describe
Chemistry: organic mechanisms, equilibrium, a slower second pass
Economics: answer structure; English A: a tight oral thesis

contentBlocks.heading: From Enquiry to First Lesson
contentBlocks.body:
What we ask on the first call is deliberately narrow. Programme and year group. Exact subject and level, since Physics HL and Physics SL are different appointments. The school. What the last marked piece of work said, ideally read out or shared. And what kind of help the student needs, which parents are often surprised to find is a separate question from the subject.

Filtering then happens on that combination rather than on subject alone. Someone who mentors Extended Essays well may be an average exam-technique coach. A tutor who is excellent at rescuing a discouraged fifteen-year-old may not be the person for a confident student chasing the top band. Slot time and travel distance enter last, because getting the wrong tutor nearby is worse than the right tutor on a screen.

What comes back is a small set of options, usually two or three, each with the tutor's relevant experience, available slots, mode and a fee range. Not a directory to sift through.

The first lesson is diagnostic. The tutor is looking for the failure pattern, not covering content. You get a short written summary after it.

Then a check-in around the fourth session, where changing tutors is a normal outcome rather than an awkward one.

Filtering on type of help, not subject name alone
Two or three options with experience, slots, mode and fee range

Check-in near session four, tutor change treated as normal

contentBlocks.heading: How the Tutor's Role Shifts Between PYP, MYP and DP
contentBlocks.body:
In the Primary Years Programme, covering ages three to twelve, the tutor's role is closest to a patient reading and thinking partner. Nobody is preparing for an external paper. The work is fluency, number confidence and the ability to hold a question long enough to investigate it. A tutor who drills a seven-year-old on speed arithmetic here is solving the wrong problem, and parents should push back if that is what they see.

The Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, changes the role again. Assessment is criterion-related, so a student can know the content and still be marked down for how the response is organised or for absent analysis. The tutor becomes a translator between what the student understands and what the criterion is asking for. This is teachable, and it is usually the fastest improvement available at this stage.

In the Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, the tutor turns into something closer to a project supervisor with subject expertise. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and TOK all have their own clocks, and a student rarely fails on ability alone. They fail on sequencing. Alongside content teaching, expect a competent DP tutor to spend real time on what happens this week, what waits until next month, and what to raise with the school supervisor.
items: PYP: reading fluency, number confidence, sustained inquiry
MYP: translating understanding into criterion-shaped responses
DP: subject depth plus supervision of IA, EE and TOK timing

contentBlocks.heading: Who Gets Past Our Screening
contentBlocks.body:
Most applicants do not, and the reasons are worth stating plainly.

Documentation is the first gate. Government photo identification, verified contact details, and degree or teaching certificates that match the subject being offered. Someone with an engineering degree applying to teach Physics HL still has to demonstrate current syllabus knowledge, because the two overlap less than the label suggests.

The second gate is level and assessment evidence. We look for direct experience of the current subject guides, working knowledge of command terms, and familiarity with the internal assessment criteria the student will actually be marked against. A tutor who describes IB experience in general terms but cannot describe how an IA is assessed is not ready for a Diploma student.

The third gate is a teaching evaluation. Tutors talk through how they would handle a student who has memorised a method and applies it in the wrong situation. This removes more candidates than the paperwork does, because subject knowledge and the ability to explain are genuinely separate abilities.

After placement, session notes, parent feedback and whether families continue are all reviewed. Recommendations stop for anyone whose students consistently drift away early, whatever the certificates say.

contentBlocks.heading: What We Will and Will Not Say About Results
contentBlocks.body:
We will not tell you a tutor will move your child from a 4 to a 7, nor put a percentage on improvement. Nobody can honestly forecast that, and a platform that does is selling confidence rather than teaching.

Here is what can be described instead. After the diagnostic session you receive a written note naming the gaps found and the order the tutor intends to address them. From the second week, the student should be able to explain the last session without being asked twice. By the fourth or fifth week, look for changed behaviour: attempting a question that would previously have been skipped, starting an assignment before the night before, bringing a specific question to the school teacher.

Grades move on their own timeline, usually after the next full assessment cycle, and sometimes later than that in subjects where the next graded task is months away.

If none of those earlier signals appear by the review point, the sensible conclusion is a mismatch, not a failure on the student's part. Say so and ask for a different tutor. We would rather make one change early than watch a family quietly lose a term to politeness.
items: No grade promises and no improvement percentages
Written diagnostic note after the first session
Week two: the student can recount the session unprompted
Weeks four to five: behaviour changes precede grade changes
Mismatch at the review point means a tutor change, not persistence

contentBlocks.body:
Bring three things to the call and it will go faster. The exact subject and level. A recent marked piece of work, even a photograph of one. And a sentence on what you think is going wrong, since a parent's instinct about their own child is usually closer to correct than they assume.

The advisor will ask what has already been tried and whether the student agrees there is a problem. That second question matters. A teenager who has been booked into tutoring against their will needs a different opening approach, and it is better to plan for that than to discover it in week three.

You will get back a short list rather than a database, with slots, mode and a fee range for each option. Home sessions in Sector 93 depend on tutor schedules and the day you want. Online sessions can usually be arranged more quickly across every supported IB subject.

If we do not have a good match for a rare subject combination, we will say so rather than offering an approximate one.

faqs.question: My son's school teacher says he is doing fine. Why would we need a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Doing fine in a class of twenty means keeping pace with the plan, which is a different measure from working at the level the student is capable of. A tutor is worth it when there is a visible gap between effort and result, when a specific topic keeps reappearing as a weakness, or when internal assessment work is drifting past its checkpoints. If none of those apply and the student is comfortable and progressing, tutoring is an expense with no clear problem to solve, and we will tell you that on the call.

faqs.question: Will a tutor teach the same way the school does?
faqs.answer: Not identically, and that is usually the value. The tutor follows the same subject guide and the same assessment criteria, so the destination matches. The route can differ, because a method that failed to land in class is unlikely to work better on the second hearing. Where a school uses a specific notation or a preferred approach for coursework, a good tutor adopts it to avoid confusing the student before an exam. Beyond that, a fresh explanation is often exactly what was missing.

faqs.question: Should the tutor be in contact with my child's school?
faqs.answer: Direct contact is rarely needed and schools differ on whether they welcome it. What works better is an indirect route: the tutor helps the student prepare specific questions for the subject teacher or internal assessment supervisor, and the student asks them. That keeps the school relationship where it belongs and builds a habit worth having. If the school does want a conversation, the tutor can join one, but we do not present ourselves to schools on a family's behalf as a matter of course.

faqs.question: How much homework should the tutor be setting between sessions?
faqs.answer: Less than most parents expect, and it should be specific. A tutor who sets thirty problems is transferring work rather than directing it. Six well-chosen questions targeting the exact weakness, with the instruction to attempt them without notes, produce far more useful information for the next session. During internal assessment periods, between-session work often shifts to drafting rather than practice questions. If a student is drowning in school deadlines, a tutor should be reducing the load, not adding to it.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who has taught in an IB school better than a subject expert who has not?
faqs.answer: Usually yes for Diploma work, because classroom experience brings knowledge of how internal assessments are marked, how moderation behaves and what examiners reward in extended responses. A brilliant subject expert without that exposure can teach content beautifully and still leave marks on the table. For younger students, the balance shifts: patience and the ability to explain simply matter more than examining experience. We consider both, and the shortlist notes which kind of background each tutor brings.

faqs.question: We live near Godrej Summit in Sector 93. Can sessions happen at our home?
faqs.answer: Often, though it depends on the subject, the day and which tutors are already working nearby. The Godrej Summit and Godrej Air side of the sector sees reasonable tutor movement, so a well-timed slot is frequently arrangeable. Weekday evenings are the hardest because tutors coming from the older parts of the city face a long drive. Weekend slots and later weekday timings open up more names. The advisor will confirm what genuinely exists for your subject rather than promising coverage in advance.

faqs.question: How do you handle a student who resents having a tutor?
faqs.answer: By not pretending the resentment is absent. The first session should be short, low pressure and mostly about the student talking through where the subject stopped making sense. Tutors who begin by testing a reluctant teenager tend to confirm every fear the student had. It helps if the parent frames the arrangement as temporary and reviewable rather than permanent. Tell the advisor beforehand if this is the situation, because the tutor chosen for a reluctant student is often not the one chosen for a motivated one.

faqs.question: What happens if we see no visible progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Raise it, and be specific about what you expected to see. Sometimes progress is present but invisible because the next graded assessment is weeks away, in which case the tutor should be able to show you the work and name what has changed. Sometimes the diagnosis was wrong and the plan needs rebuilding. Sometimes the pairing simply does not work. All three are fixable, but only if someone says something. A tutor change at week four costs far less than one at week twelve.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics and Chemistry for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking rather than assuming. Tutors qualified across both sciences at Diploma level exist but are less common than people expect, particularly at higher level where the internal assessment expectations differ meaningfully between the two subjects. Where a genuine dual-subject specialist is available, the scheduling and continuity advantages are real. Where one is not, we would rather propose two tutors than stretch one beyond their actual strength, and the shortlist will make that trade-off explicit.

introSummary: IB tutors in Sector 95 Gurugram are arranged around the commute, because most students here travel a long way to school and reach home tired. contentBlocks.heading: Travel Time Shapes Every Tutoring Decision in Sector 95, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Ask a family here how far the school is and you get an answer in minutes, never in kilometres. That habit tells you most of what matters about arranging tutoring in this part of New Gurgaon.

Sector 95 sits out towards the NH-48 side of the city, past the older residential belt, in a group of sectors that grew quickly and are still filling in. IB schools serving these families are mostly not next door. A bus that leaves at half past six in the morning and returns some time after four in the afternoon is ordinary rather than extreme, and by the time a student has eaten and changed, the productive part of the evening is shorter than the calendar suggests.

So the first question we ask is not which subject. It is what time the child gets home and how they look when they do.

A session booked at five o'clock immediately after a long bus ride will often look attentive and teach very little. The same hour at half past six, after food and a proper break, does noticeably more work. Parents searching for IB tutors in Sector 95 Gurugram sometimes want the earliest possible slot to protect bedtime. That instinct is sound and occasionally still produces the wrong booking.
items: School runs measured in minutes, not distance
Bus departures near half past six are common here
Post-commute fatigue is a real constraint on lesson quality
Later start times usually produce better work than early ones
Grade 1 to Grade 12 across PYP, MYP and the Diploma Programme

contentBlocks.heading: How We Build a Shortlist for a Sector 95 Gurugram Family
contentBlocks.body:
Matching runs on four inputs, and slot timing is one of them rather than an afterthought.

The first input is the academic picture: programme, year group, exact subject level, school, and what recent marked work shows. HL and SL are treated separately, and so is the difference between needing content taught and needing exam technique repaired.

The second is the weekly reality. What time does the student reach home, which days carry activities or sport, when do school assignments usually fall due, and how much homework already exists. A tutoring plan that ignores this collapses within a month.

The third is mode. Given the address and the time available, we work out whether a home session, an online session or a combination stands the best chance of actually happening every week for a term.

The fourth is the tutor's own schedule and location, which for this sector genuinely narrows the field on weekday evenings.

What comes back to you is a short set of options with slots, mode and fee range attached. Then a diagnostic first session, a written note on what it found, and a review conversation around the fourth session where changing tutors is a normal outcome.
items: Academic input: programme, level, school, recent marked work
Weekly input: arrival time, activity days, existing homework load
Mode decided from address and available window, not preference alone
Tutor location and schedule considered explicitly for this sector
Diagnostic session, written note, review around session four

contentBlocks.heading: Support Across the Primary, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes
contentBlocks.body:
Younger children in the Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, are the ones most affected by a long bus day. A tired eight-year-old will sit through anything and absorb very little. Sessions for this group are best kept to forty-five minutes, held on days without an after-school activity, and built around reading, number confidence and the inquiry the class is currently running.

Middle Years Programme students, ages eleven to sixteen, can handle a longer session but have the messiest calendars. Criterion-marked tasks arrive across several subjects with no coordination between departments, so a family can go from nothing due to four things due within a week. Tutoring at this stage is often partly about sequencing that pile, and partly about the skill the criteria keep penalising.

Diploma students, ages sixteen to nineteen, carry the heaviest load and the tightest constraints: six subjects, internal assessments in most of them, the Extended Essay, TOK, and mock examinations before the May or November session. For this group the commute matters differently. The bus ride itself becomes usable time for reading or flashcards, and several students we work with treat it that way deliberately rather than accidentally.
items: PYP: forty-five minute sessions on non-activity days
MYP: sequencing clustered criterion tasks across subjects
DP: six subjects, IA workload, EE, TOK and mock preparation
May 2026 and November 2026 exam session planning
Bus time repurposed for reading or recall practice

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing a Lesson Mode That Fits the School Run
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is the default request from families here and it is often the right one, particularly for primary and lower middle years students who need a person at the table. The limitation is supply. A tutor coming from the older parts of the city gives up a large chunk of an evening to reach Sector 95, so weekday home slots are scarcer than parents expect and tend to sit later in the evening.

Online removes the travel problem entirely and opens up tutors who would never take a booking at this distance. For Diploma work it also unlocks narrow specialisms: Math AI HL, a specific science at higher level, a language A that few local tutors teach. The trade-off is that a screen demands more self-discipline from the student, and a tired teenager after a long commute has less of it available.

A third arrangement suits this sector particularly well. Run the main teaching session online mid-week when travel is impossible for everyone, and keep a longer in-person session on Saturday or Sunday morning when the student is rested and a tutor can reach you without fighting the road.

Whichever mode is chosen, protect one thing: consistency of day and time. Sessions that move around every week fail here more than anywhere.

Online opens narrow HL specialisms and removes travel entirely
Weekend in-person plus mid-week online suits this sector well
Screens demand more self-discipline from a tired student
A fixed weekly day and time matters more than the mode chosen

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Subjects Sector 95 Gurugram Parents Ask About Most
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics leads the requests by a wide margin. Math AA HL is the harder ask: the course expects proof, fluent algebraic manipulation and a tolerance for abstraction that many students have never been asked for before. Math AI HL trips people differently, since the content feels friendlier while the exploration and the third paper both demand judgement about modelling rather than recall.

Physics and Chemistry come next, usually at the point where the internal assessment stops being a distant item on a list. The strongest predictor of a good science IA is how narrow the research question is, and that decision gets made weeks before any data exists. A tutor consulted at that stage saves more marks than one brought in to fix the analysis afterwards.

Economics requests arrive later in the year, generally after a first set of essay marks. The content is rarely the problem. Marks are lost on evaluation that states a view without weighing anything against it.

English A tends to be about the individual oral and the analysis of unseen passages, where fluent readers still slip into retelling.

For a student with limited evening time, choosing which two subjects to tutor is more important than the tutoring itself.
items: Math AA HL: proof, algebra fluency, abstraction
Math AI HL: modelling choices in the exploration and Paper 3
Physics and Chemistry: narrow the IA research question early
Economics: evaluation that weighs rather than asserts
English A: oral thesis and unseen passage analysis

contentBlocks.heading: The School Run from Sector 95 Gurugram and What It Costs in Study Time
contentBlocks.body:
Students from these sectors attend IB schools scattered across the wider city and beyond it. Pathways World School in the Gurugram region, GD Goenka World School towards Sohna Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and Lancers International School near Golf Course Road appear regularly among the families who contact us from here. Several of those journeys involve crossing the city in the morning peak.

The consequence is arithmetic rather than opinion. A student spending two hours a day on a bus loses roughly ten hours a week, which is a full working day of study time gone before anyone has opened a book. That does not make the school choice wrong. It does mean the remaining hours have to be used with more deliberation than a family living five minutes from the gate would need.

Practically, this pushes families towards fewer tutoring hours used better: two focused sessions rather than four scattered ones, homework attempted before the session rather than after, and a tutor who sets six targeted questions instead of thirty.

We should state this clearly: IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. No school named here endorses, partners with or is affiliated with us, and these names appear only to describe where local students study.

The immediate neighbourhood is made up of newer residential developments, with Godrej Air, Godrej Summit, Mapsko Casa Bella and Vatika India Next among the addresses that come up repeatedly in enquiries. Within this group, a tutor who takes one booking can often take a second nearby on the same evening, which is the single biggest factor in whether weekday home tutoring is available to you at all.

Look further out and the picture changes. The better lever is timing and mode. Saturday morning at home, mid-week online, and a fixed weekly rhythm the tutor can plan their own week around.
