contentBlocks.heading: Measuring Whether Sessions Are Working
contentBlocks.body:
With limited evening hours, a family here cannot afford to wait a term to find out whether tutoring is useful. So look for signals that appear earlier than grades.

The first is the written note after the diagnostic session. It should name specific topics and a specific skill, not describe the student as needing to build confidence. Vague feedback in week one usually predicts vague teaching in week six.

The second is what happens to homework time. Effective tutoring usually reduces the hours a student spends stuck, because the blockage causing the stalling has been removed. If tutoring is added on top and total study time simply rises, something is off.

The third is the questions the student starts asking, in the session and in class. A student who begins asking why a method works rather than which method to use has moved, whatever the next report says.

Grades follow later, on the school's assessment cycle rather than on ours. We do not forecast them, we do not offer a target score, and we will not quote an improvement figure, because there is no honest basis for any of those numbers.

Homework hours should fall as blockages clear
Better questions in class are an early, reliable signal

No target scores, no forecast improvement figures

contentBlocks.heading: How Tutors Are Vetted Before We Recommend Them
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor proposed to a family in this sector has cleared the same four stages.

Identity and credentials are confirmed first: government photo identification, verified contact details, and academic or teaching certificates matching the subject and level being offered. A certificate in a related field does not qualify someone for Chemistry HL.

Subject depth is examined next, level by level. We look for recent teaching against the current subject guides, comfort with command term distinctions such as explain against describe, and specific knowledge of how internal assessments are marked. General claims of IB familiarity are not sufficient for Diploma placements.

A teaching evaluation follows. Candidates explain how they would work with a student who produces correct answers but cannot say why the method works, and how they would handle a topic the student has already been taught twice unsuccessfully. Clarity of explanation eliminates more applicants here than any documentary check.

Reliability is the fourth stage and it matters especially in this part of the city. A tutor who cancels because the drive was longer than expected causes more damage to a tightly scheduled family than a slightly less qualified tutor who turns up every week. Attendance and punctuality records are reviewed continuously.
items: Photo identification and verified contact details
Certificates matched to the exact subject and level offered
Command term and internal assessment knowledge checked
Explanation task rather than a credentials interview
Attendance and punctuality tracked after placement

contentBlocks.heading: Arranging IB Tutors in Sector 95 Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Before the call, work out two things. What time your child actually walks through the door on a normal school day, and which two days of the week are genuinely free of activities. Those answers shape the plan more than anything else you can tell us.

Then bring the academic detail: year group, exact subject levels, the school, and a recent marked piece of work if you have one to hand.

The advisor call runs about fifteen to twenty minutes and ends with a short list rather than a directory, each option carrying slots, mode and a fee range. Fees depend on level and on whether the session is at home or online, and travel distance is part of why home sessions in New Gurgaon cost more than online ones.

A closing caution. If the only slot that suits your family is one where the student will be exhausted, we will say so and suggest an alternative rather than book it and hope. Home tutoring here remains subject to tutor availability; online sessions can usually be arranged more quickly.

faqs.question: Sector 95 is a long way from the older sectors. Does that limit which tutors we can get?
faqs.answer: For weekday home sessions, yes, and it is better to know that upfront. Tutors based around Golf Course Road, the DLF phases or Sushant Lok give up a substantial part of an evening to reach New Gurgaon, so many restrict themselves to weekends or to longer bookings. Two things widen the choice considerably: accepting a weekend home slot, or taking the teaching online and keeping travel out of the arrangement entirely. Online sessions face no distance limit at all across supported IB subjects.

faqs.question: How long does a typical session run and when can it be scheduled?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes suits primary students, seventy-five to ninety works for middle years, and Diploma sessions are commonly ninety minutes or two hours, especially when internal assessment work is underway. Scheduling depends on tutor availability and on when your child is actually able to concentrate. Weekday sessions in this sector tend to sit between half past six and half past eight. Weekend mornings are easier to arrange and often more productive, since nobody has just come off a two-hour round trip to school.

faqs.question: Our daughter reaches home after half past four. Is a five o'clock session too soon?
faqs.answer: Usually, for anyone below Diploma level. Half an hour is not enough recovery after a long bus journey, and the session tends to become expensive supervised sitting rather than teaching. Half past six or seven, after food and a genuine break, produces better work from the same hour. Diploma students sometimes handle an early start better because the material is more engaging to them, but even then we would rather test it for a fortnight than assume it. Tell the advisor the real arrival time, not the ideal one.

faqs.question: Can we start with home sessions and switch to online partway through the term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and quite a few families do exactly that, usually as exams approach and revision intensity rises. Whether the same tutor continues depends on them offering both formats, which many do. Where a switch means a new tutor, we hand over the session notes and the original diagnostic so the second tutor does not restart from zero. Give a week's notice if you can. Changing mode mid-week with no warning tends to cost a session rather than save one.

faqs.question: Do you charge extra for travel to home tutoring in New Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: Travel is reflected in the home session rate rather than billed as a separate line, and it is one reason home sessions in this part of the city cost more than online ones. The gap widens for tutors coming from further away and narrows when a tutor is already working in your society that evening. The advisor gives you the applicable range before any introduction, so the number is not a surprise later. There is no fee for the initial advisory conversation itself.

faqs.question: Can two siblings in different year groups share one session slot?
faqs.answer: Not the same hour, no. A Grade 6 student and a Diploma student need different tutors, different material and different pacing, and splitting one hour between them shortchanges both. What does work is consecutive slots with the same tutor where the subjects and levels genuinely overlap, which saves travel time and sometimes reduces the combined rate. Where the levels are far apart, two separate arrangements is the honest recommendation even though it is the less convenient answer.

faqs.question: What internet setup do online IB sessions need?
faqs.answer: A stable connection, a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, and headphones so the student is not distracted by household noise. For mathematics and the sciences, add a second device or a document camera positioned over the page, so the tutor can watch the working develop instead of only seeing a typed final answer. A cheap tablet with a stylus does the job well. Without some way of seeing handwritten work in progress, online mathematics sessions lose most of their diagnostic value.

faqs.question: How do you know a tutor is current with the syllabus my child is following?
faqs.answer: We ask for evidence of recent teaching against the present subject guides rather than accepting a general statement about IB experience. That includes familiarity with the internal assessment criteria as they are now written, awareness of command term distinctions, and knowledge of any recent changes to paper structure in that subject. Tutors who last taught a course several years ago are placed only where the content has not shifted meaningfully. If we cannot verify currency for a particular subject, we do not put that tutor forward for it.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue through school holidays and study leave?
faqs.answer: Yes, and holidays are often the most productive stretch available to families here, because the commute disappears and a student can work in the morning when they are fresh. Many use the winter break to get ahead on internal assessment drafts and the summer to repair foundations before a new year begins. Study leave before mocks or the final session usually shifts to shorter, more frequent contact focused on past papers. Availability over holiday periods varies, so book earlier than you normally would.

contentBlocks.heading: The five answers a Sector 99 Gurugram parent needs before booking
contentBlocks.body:
Most enquiries from Sector 99 begin with one sentence: we need an IB tutor. Fair instinct, incomplete request. The families who get a good match on the first attempt tend to arrive with five answers already worked out.

Which programme, and which year inside it, because DP1 in September and DP2 in January are different jobs. Which subject, and at which level, since Math AA HL and Math AI SL share a name and very little else. What the school has actually written on the last report, not the summary you were given verbally at the parent meeting. What time on a weekday is genuinely free once the bus, the activity class and dinner have taken their share. And whether the session belongs at your dining table or on a screen.

Work through those and the field narrows from every tutor in Gurugram to a handful worth a conversation. Skip them and you spend a fortnight interviewing people who were never going to help.

Support here runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12. Planning for the May 2026 and November 2026 exam sessions is already sensible for DP2 students, and useful for DP1 families who would rather not compress everything into one panicked spring.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject requests that come from Sector 99 households
contentBlocks.body:
The subject list that generates most calls from this part of the city is short and predictable: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A.

Mathematics splits the requests almost in half. Math AA HL work is usually about proof discipline and the analysis paper, and students who coasted through MYP algebra hit a wall at calculus and complex numbers. Math AI HL fails differently. The mathematics is more approachable, but the modelling and statistics reward interpretation, and a student who writes down a correct regression without saying what it means in context still loses marks.

Physics and Chemistry requests cluster around two moments: the internal assessment, and the Paper 2 extended response where being partially right earns very little. Economics arrives late, often well into DP2, when a student realises diagrams alone do not carry a fifteen-mark evaluation.

English A is the quietest request and frequently the most urgent. Paper 1 unseen analysis cannot be crammed in the week before.

A tutor matched only on subject name may still be the wrong person. Level, paper and the specific weakness matter more than the label on the timetable.

Physics and Chemistry IA design plus Paper 2 structure

contentBlocks.heading: How a request from Sector 99, Gurugram turns into a shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is deliberately short, and it runs the same way for a Grade 3 numeracy request and a DP2 Physics HL emergency.

One. You send the details: programme, year, subject, level, the report comment if you have it, and two or three time windows that actually work on a school night.

Two. An advisor calls. This is where the request usually changes shape. A parent asking for general maths help often turns out to need internal assessment support in one specific criterion, and a parent asking for exam coaching sometimes has a child who has quietly stopped attempting homework at all.

Three. A shortlist is prepared against those notes. Availability is checked at that point rather than promised in advance, since a tutor free in October may not be free in January.

Four. You speak to the tutor, or run a first session, and decide.

Five. If the fit is wrong, you say so early and the shortlist is revisited.

Nothing here is instant. A specialist match for a rarer combination can take a few days, and a fast answer that ignores level is worse than a slow one that respects it.
items: Send programme, year, subject, level and timing
Advisor call reframes roughly half of all requests
Availability checked at shortlist stage, not promised earlier
A first session before any commitment
Rare subject and level pairs take longer to fill

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sector 99 sits on the Dwarka Expressway side of Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Sector 99 is a residential pocket on the northern, Dwarka Expressway side of the city, and its tutoring problem is geographic before it is academic. The condominium communities here, Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph and ATS Kocoon among them, sit a long way from where most experienced IB tutors already teach.

That older belt runs along Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and the Sohna Road side. Nirvana Country, South City 1, DLF Phase 1 and Phase 4, Sector 50 and Sector 65 all fall inside it. From there, a weekday evening trip up here can eat an hour in each direction, which is why the same tutor may accept an afternoon slot and decline a seven o clock one on the same day.

Two things work in your favour. Movement between neighbouring northern sectors is quick, so a tutor already teaching a family a few towers away is the likeliest home match. And Delhi is close: tutors coming from the Dwarka side sometimes reach this address faster than they reach Sector 54.

Families with a parent commuting to Noida or Faridabad usually end up online for the evening slot.
items: Northern high-rise pocket, off the main tutor belt
Golf Course Road and the DLF phases: an hour each way at peak
Afternoon slots far easier to fill than seven in the evening
Dwarka-side tutors sometimes closer than Sector 54 ones
A tutor already working nearby is the realistic home match

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: what each stage asks of a tutor
contentBlocks.body:
The three programmes need different people, and the common mistake is assuming seniority transfers downward.

Primary Years, ages three to twelve, is the stage most often handled badly. Inquiry-led learning does not respond well to a worksheet pile, and a tutor who converts a Grade 4 unit into drill will produce short-term neatness and long-term boredom. What helps at this age is reading fluency, number sense and the confidence to ask a question in class.

Middle Years, ages eleven to sixteen, is where families first notice the gap between understanding a topic and scoring on it. MYP assessment is criterion-related, so a student can know the science and still lose marks under the communication criterion because the response is thin. A tutor who has read the criterion descriptors is worth more here than one with a stronger degree.

Diploma, ages sixteen to nineteen, is specialist work: subject at level, internal assessment structure, extended essay direction, theory of knowledge argument, and past-paper technique measured against command terms.

Concept-based learning, criterion-related marking and command-term language run through all three. Matching is done against those needs, not on subject name alone.
items: PYP: inquiry, reading fluency and number sense, not drill
MYP: criterion descriptors, especially communication marks
DP: IA, EE, TOK, past papers and command terms
Seniority does not transfer downward

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor is put in front of your child
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a filter, not a ceremony. Four things are looked at, and a weakness in any one of them keeps a profile off the shortlist.

Identity and qualification come first: a government photo identity, the degree or teaching qualification claimed, and confirmation that the person on the call is the person who will teach.

Curriculum evidence comes second, and it is the part most often skipped elsewhere. Having taught mathematics is not evidence of having taught Math AA HL. Having worked in an international school is not evidence of having marked against MYP criteria. Tutors are asked what they have actually taught, at which level, and for how long.

Third, teaching behaviour. A short conversation about how they would handle a student four weeks behind on an internal assessment tells you more than a resume does.

Fourth, reliability. Punctuality, communication with parents, and whether sessions get cancelled.

None of this makes a tutor right for your child. It only removes the people who are clearly wrong. The fit judgment stays yours, which is exactly why a first session before any commitment matters.
items: Photo identity and qualification confirmed
Level-specific teaching history, not subject-level generalities
A scenario question about a late internal assessment
Punctuality and parent communication
Screening filters out; it does not choose for you

contentBlocks.heading: Home visits, online sessions and the Sector 99 clock
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and communities near them, depending on tutor schedules. This sector is reachable, but the honest position is that home slots here are narrower than they are ten kilometres south, and they narrow again after six in the evening.

Online tutoring stays available across Gurugram for every supported IB subject, and for this address it is often the better answer rather than the fallback. A DP2 student needing Math AA HL revision at nine at night will find a stronger specialist online than a tutor willing to drive out at that hour. Screen sharing also suits past-paper work: the question, the markscheme and the student script sit open together.

Home visits earn their keep elsewhere. Younger children who drift on a screen, students who need someone physically present to start work, and families who want a parent within earshot all do better in person.

Hybrid works. One home visit a week for structure, one or two online sessions for drilling. Several families here settle there after a term of trying a single mode.
items: Home slots thin out sharply after six in the evening
Online reaches specialists a car radius cannot
Screen sharing suits past papers and markschemes
In person for younger children and low self-starters
Hybrid: one visit plus one or two online sessions

contentBlocks.heading: The school run from Sector 99 to Gurugram IB campuses
contentBlocks.body:
Children living here attend IB schools spread across the city, and the commute shapes the tutoring timetable more than parents expect.

Pathways World School sits in the wider Gurugram region. Lancers International School is on the Golf Course Road side. Scottish High International School is in Sector 57. GD Goenka World School lies out towards the Sohna Road region. None of these is a five-minute drive from here, and a child on a bus from the far side of the city may not be home before five, tired and with homework untouched.

That has practical consequences. A four o clock session is unrealistic for many households here even though tutors prefer it. Saturday morning becomes valuable. A session starting at half past seven with a child awake since half past five is worth less than a shorter one earlier in the week.

School calendars matter too. Internal assessment deadlines, mock weeks and report cycles differ between campuses, so the plan is built around your school dates rather than a generic term calendar.

Lancers International School, Golf Course Road
Scottish High International School, Sector 57
GD Goenka World School, Sohna Road region
Bus timings, not tutor preference, decide the slot

contentBlocks.heading: Judging progress by week four, and when to change tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks is long enough to judge and short enough that a bad match has not cost a term.

By then you should be able to see three things without asking for a report. The student can describe what the last session covered, in their own words, without prompting. Homework attempts have changed, even if the marks have not. And the tutor has told you something you did not already know about your child work, rather than only confirming what the school said.

If none of that has happened, the fit is wrong. Say so. Changing tutor in week five is ordinary and costs far less than waiting until February.

What should not be promised, by anyone, is a grade. No tutor can guarantee a 7, a points total or a percentage improvement, and a promise of that kind is a reason to be sceptical rather than reassured. What can be described honestly is the process: what will be covered, how often, and what evidence of movement should look like.

Progress in IB is also uneven. A student can improve genuinely and still see a mark drop, because the next unit was harder than the last.
items: The student can recap the last session unprompted
Homework attempted, even while marks lag
The tutor tells you something new about the work
Week five is a normal time to change tutor
Promised grades: a warning sign, not a reassurance

contentBlocks.heading: Starting IB tuition in Sector 99, Gurugram this term
contentBlocks.body:
If the five answers at the top of this page are settled, the next step is a short message carrying them: programme and year, subject and level, the report comment, and two or three workable time windows.

An advisor will call to check the detail, because the written request and the real problem differ often enough that the call is not a formality. A shortlist follows, built against your child level and your household timetable rather than against whoever happens to be free that week.

Availability can be reviewed for home sessions here and in the neighbouring northern sectors, and it depends on tutor schedules in that particular term. Online sessions cover the full supported subject list across Gurugram.

For DP2 students sitting the May 2026 session, the useful window for structured revision is now rather than after the mocks. November 2026 candidates have more room, though internal assessment deadlines will arrive earlier than expected. Younger PYP and MYP students are usually better served by a steady weekly rhythm than by a burst of sessions before reports.

Ask about fees on the first call. They depend on level, subject and mode.
items: Send programme, year, subject, level and timing
Advisor call before any shortlist
Home availability reviewed each term, subject to tutor schedules
May 2026 revision: start before the mocks
Fees vary by level, subject and mode

faqs.question: Is Sector 99 too far north for most IB home tutors?
faqs.answer: Not too far, but the honest picture is that home availability here is thinner than on Golf Course Road or in the DLF phases, and it thins further after six in the evening. Tutors already teaching in the neighbouring northern sectors are the realistic home matches. Afternoon and Saturday slots fill more easily than late weekday ones. If the subject is specialised or the hour you need is late, online will usually produce a stronger match than waiting for a car to arrive.

faqs.question: My daughter takes Math AI HL and her school says she is fine. Why is she losing marks?
faqs.answer: Two different things are being measured. A school comment about being fine usually refers to classwork and understanding. Marks in Math AI HL come from modelling and interpretation as much as calculation, so a student can produce a correct statistical result and still lose marks for not explaining what it shows in context. Ask to see the marked script rather than the grade, then look at where the marks stop. The pattern is often narrower and more technical than the report suggests.

faqs.question: What does a first session usually look like?
faqs.answer: A first session is diagnostic more than instructional. The tutor will typically work through recent classwork or a past-paper question, watch how the student approaches it, and stop at the points where the method breaks rather than correcting silently. Expect questions about the school, upcoming deadlines and what the student thinks is hard. By the end you should hear a plain description of what needs work and roughly how long it will take. If that description does not come, ask for it directly.

faqs.question: How are fees worked out, and what changes them?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the programme stage, the subject and level, the session length and whether the tutor travels. Diploma higher level subjects usually sit above Middle Years support, and a home visit up to this sector carries travel that an online session does not. Frequency also matters: two shorter sessions a week can be priced differently from one long one. Rates are confirmed with the tutor before you start, and it is reasonable to ask what is included and what is billed separately.

faqs.question: Can a Grade 4 PYP child be tutored without turning it into worksheets?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth asking about directly. Primary Years work is inquiry-led, so the useful tutor builds reading fluency, number confidence and the habit of asking questions rather than handing over a stack of practice sheets. Sessions at this age are usually shorter, often thirty to forty-five minutes, because attention runs out before the hour does. A reasonable check after a month: can your child explain something from the last session without being asked leading questions?

faqs.question: We travel to Delhi often for work. Does that disrupt a weekly schedule?
faqs.answer: It is manageable if the schedule is built with the travel in mind rather than around it. Online sessions continue from wherever the student is, which is why families splitting time between Gurugram and Delhi often keep at least one weekly session on screen. Home visits are harder to reschedule at short notice, since a tutor holding a slot in this sector has usually turned down something else for it. Give as much notice as you can and agree a cancellation policy at the start.

faqs.question: What if my son does not get along with the tutor?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than waiting for the term to end. Personality mismatch is common and is not a failure on anyone part: a tutor who suits a confident student can be quite wrong for an anxious one. Ask for a revised shortlist and describe what did not work, since a specific complaint about pace or tone produces a better second match than a general one. Changing in week five costs a few sessions. Changing in February costs the preparation window.

faqs.question: Is there any connection between IB Gram and Scottish High International School or GD Goenka World School?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with Scottish High International School, GD Goenka World School, or any other school named on this page unless specifically stated. Schools are mentioned because they shape the commute and the calendar that families in this sector plan around. Tutors may have taught students from these campuses, but that is a description of experience rather than any endorsement, partnership or approval by the schools themselves.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the November 2026 session should a DP2 student start?
faqs.answer: For a November 2026 candidate, structured subject revision from roughly nine to twelve months out is comfortable, and the more urgent dates sit earlier: internal assessment drafts and the extended essay tend to land well before revision starts to feel pressing. Students who begin later can still make progress, though the plan becomes narrower and more about triage than coverage. A realistic first step is mapping your school deadline calendar, then deciding which subjects need weekly support and which need occasional review.
